negative_highlights: Reported pre-tax loss of $17.4 million for Q4 2024
Consumer loan cleanup included $20.8 million provision and $2.5 million interest reversal
Digital platform margin was only 140 bps (6.47% asset yield vs 5.07% deposit cost)
positive_highlights: Core bank loan pipeline doubled year over year; over 80% from new customers
Panacea loans grew to $435 million and funding to ~$100 million, with 30-40% growth rates
Pre-tax core profitability potential ~$10 million after removing one-time charges and drags
summary: Primis Financial reported a Q4 2024 pre-tax loss of $17.4 million, driven by a $20.8 million provision for the consumer loan book, $2.5 million interest reversal, and $1.25 million fraud losses. Excluding these and other non-recurring items, core pre-tax profit was approximately $6.2 million, with potential closer to $10 million after adjusting for temporary drags. Management repositioned the balance sheet by moving the consumer book to held for sale, watching the Life Premium Finance business, and reducing digital deposit rates, aiming for cleaner earnings and margin expansion to 3.25%-3.50% in 2025. Core bank loan pipeline doubled year over year, and Panacea grew to $435 million in loans with $100 million in low-cost funding.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin decreased to 4.53% from 5.00% quarter-over-quarter.
Nonaccrual loans increased $8.7 million in Q4, with total NPAs at $14.2 million.
Credit card activities generated a $1.1 million pretax loss for 2024.
positive_highlights: Net income up 70.6% to $18.6 million for the year, a record.
Credit card transactions grew 272% to $51.7 million in Q4.
Efficiency ratio improved to 58.1% from 68.1% year-over-year.
summary: GBFH reported Q4 2024 net income of $5.2 million ($0.36 per diluted share), up from $5.0 million in Q3, and full-year net income of $18.6 million ($1.37 per diluted share), a 71% year-over-year increase. Revenue was driven by record SBA originations exceeding $500 million in 2024 and $2 billion cumulative, with loan sales of $98.5 million and gain on sale of $4 million. Credit card transaction volume surged 272% quarter-over-quarter to $51.7 million, with the program achieving breakeven in Q4. Management noted NIM compression from accelerated CD costs but expects repricing benefits in Q1 2025. Nonperforming assets rose to $14.2 million, but most are SBA-guaranteed, and the bank remains confident in working through them.

negative_highlights: Gross margin negatively impacted by promotional pricing, overhead absorption, and product mix
Marketplace challenges with cautious retail and trade channel environment
Company does not expect market to bounce back in Q2
positive_highlights: Revenue came in above analyst estimate
Inventory down about $66 million year-over-year to $201.6 million
Balance sheet remains debt free and dividend maintained
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q1 FY2025 results with revenue above the analyst's estimate but still facing a challenging retail environment, promotional pricing, and competitive pressures. Gross margin was negatively impacted by increased promotional pricing, unfavorable overhead absorption, and product mix. The company highlighted a $14 million acquisition in diving for vertical integration, progress in cost savings, and a debt-free balance sheet, but remains cautious about near-term market conditions.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted from 85% to 83%
SG&A expenses increased $2.9M primarily due to higher compensation and stock-based comp
European revenue remained flat at $1M with a reduction in territories from six to five
positive_highlights: US Heart Failure revenue grew 41% to $14.3M driven by expansion into new territories and accounts
Active implanting centers increased from 178 at end of 2023 to 223 at end of Q4 FY2024
CMS maintained Barostim in APC 1580 for outpatient procedures, preserving ~$45k reimbursement level
summary: CVRx reported Q4 FY2024 total revenue of $15.3 million (up 36% YoY) and US Heart Failure revenue of $14.3 million (up 41%), driven by expansion to 223 active centers from 178 in the prior year. Gross margin was 83%, slightly down from 85% last year, while SG&A expenses rose 19% due to increased headcount and stock-based compensation. Management provided full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $63-65 million with gross margins expected between 83%-84%. The company noted a Q1 seasonality dip is anticipated but expects consistent growth thereafter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down to 35.3% non-GAAP from 38.8% YoY
U.S. Tier 1 demand still muted, expected to be near-term headwind
Africa demand weak due to currency and payment issues, likely modest this year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 26% YoY to $118M, highest in over a decade
Record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $14.8M, up 22% YoY
Operating cash flow of $20.8M, best in at least 7 years
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $118.2 million, up 26.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.82, adjusted EBITDA of $14.8 million (a record) and operating cash flow of $20.8 million, the best in at least seven years. Gross margin improved to 35.3% non-GAAP, but was down year-over-year due to Pasolink mix and a tough comp. Book-to-bill was 1.08 for the quarter, and the company reaffirmed its prior guidance, citing potential upside from U.S. Tier 1 recovery and Pasolink momentum.

negative_highlights: Q4 global retail sales declined 15%, full-year down 7%
Missed original 2024 guidance due to macroeconomic headwinds
LiveWire operating loss of $110 million and only 612 revenue units
positive_highlights: U.S. Touring market share reached 74.5%, highest since 2019
Operating cash flow over $1 billion in 2024, up nearly 40% year-over-year
Achieved $257 million in productivity savings
summary: Harley-Davidson reported Q4 2024 global retail sales down 15%, with North America down 13% and other international regions down 17%, leading to a full-year retail decline of 7%. The company missed original guidance due to cyclical headwinds and high interest rates, but gained market share in the U.S. Touring segment to 74.5%, the highest since 2019. For 2025, management guides to flat retail sales with a positive skew to the second half, and expects double-digit operating margin by 2026, with a 15% target later. LiveWire reported an operating loss of $110 million and 612 revenue units, within revised guidance, with plans to reduce losses to $70-$80 million in 2025.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue declined to $9.9 million from $11.6 million year-over-year
Consumer cannabis adjusted gross margin fell to 26% from 29%
Company cannot break out MedReleaf Australia contribution specifically
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 37% year-over-year, with international medical cannabis up 112%
Adjusted EBITDA grew 316% to a record $23.1 million, ninth consecutive positive quarter
Free cash flow positive at $27.4 million, and balance sheet has no cannabis debt
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported a record Q3 FY2025 with net revenue of $88.2 million, up 37% year-over-year, driven by 51% growth in global medical cannabis and 112% growth internationally. Adjusted EBITDA surged 316% to $23.1 million, net income reached $31.2 million, and free cash flow was positive at $27.4 million. Medical cannabis gross margin improved to 74%, and the company reiterated expectations for continued revenue growth and positive EBITDA and free cash flow in the next quarter.

negative_highlights: FinTech vertical revenue declined 15% year-over-year due to changing client payment support models
DSO increased from 75 days in Q1 to 79 days in Q2, partially offsetting operating cash flow growth
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $140.7M representing the highest quarterly total in IBEX history
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 11.8% driven by offshore growth and site optimization
Raised full-year guidance for both Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA following a strong quarter
summary: IBEX reported record Q2 FY2025 revenue of $140.7 million (up 6.1% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.59 (up 36% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for both Revenue ($525-$535M vs prior $515-$525M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($68-69M vs prior $67-69M), citing strong offshore growth, new logo wins in HealthTech/Travel, and successful AI solution deployments. The company also executed a share repurchase of 3.6 million shares to regain independence from TRGI.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue of $19.6M was down 24.6% YoY, below expectations
FY25 revenue outlook cut to $77-83M from prior expectations
Management and board taking 10% salary/retainer cuts and annual cost reductions planned
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved 490 basis points to 29.4% (second highest in 7 years)
Landed 7 new contracts with $100-200M revenue potential over 5 years
EV Charging revenue up 48% year-to-date and pipeline grew sequentially
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $19.6M, down from $26M year-over-year, with results impacted by project timing delays and reduced lighting distribution activity. Gross margin improved 490 bps to 29.4%, and adjusted EBITDA was slightly positive. Management reduced FY25 revenue guidance to $77-83M and expects double-digit revenue growth and positive adjusted EBITDA in FY26, supported by $100-200M of new contracts and cost reductions. The company is reorganizing into two business units and management/board are taking 10% salary cuts.

negative_highlights: Gross loss of negative 72.7% due to a $19.5 million inventory reserve charge
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $22.1 million from $11.6 million a year ago
Go ESS storage business only 6% of sales, down from 9%, with weak demand and falling battery prices
positive_highlights: Revenue up 86.8% YoY and 21.3% sequentially to $17.3 million, fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth
Excluding inventory charge, gross margin was 40.2% in Q4, up from 36.5% in Q3 (ex-reserve)
Predict Plus platform grew to 140,000 meters under management, ARR above $1 million
summary: Tigo Energy reported Q4 2024 revenue of $17.3 million, up 86.8% year over year and 21.3% sequentially, marking four consecutive quarters of sequential growth. However, the quarter included a $19.5 million inventory reserve charge, resulting in a gross loss of negative 72.7% and an operating loss of $24.1 million. Excluding the charge, gross margin was approximately 40%. The company guided Q1 2025 revenue to $17-19 million and full-year 2025 revenue to $85-100 million, expecting adjusted EBITDA profitability in the second half of 2025. Predict Plus ARR now exceeds $1 million, with 140,000 meters under management.

negative_highlights: Net income from continuing operations fell to $2.7 million from $8.7 million
Cash and cash equivalents dropped to $1.2 million from $3.3 million
Operating cash flow usage increased by $2.1 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24.6% to $16.2 million
Received GMO safety certificate for BBL2-2 corn in May 2024
Gene-editing breakthrough published in Nature
summary: Origin Agritech reported fiscal 2024 revenue of $16.2 million, up 24.6% year-over-year, driven by higher corn seed volume. Net income from continuing operations fell to $2.7 million from $8.7 million, largely due to one-time gains in the prior year and increased G&A and R&D spending. Cash and cash equivalents declined to $1.2 million from $3.3 million, while operating cash flow used increased $2.1 million. Management outlined a three-phase strategy targeting cash flow breakeven by 2026, and highlighted a new GMO safety certificate and gene-editing breakthrough, but did not provide revised revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Soda ash market conditions expected to remain challenging in early 2025
Producer mechanical issues in offshore fields continue to impact volumes
Cash costs of running business remain high at $600-625 million per year
positive_highlights: Offshore segment expected to deliver upwards of 20+% sequential growth in 2025
Marine transportation segment expected to deliver record results in 2025
Management sees significant supply rationalization in soda ash, which could improve prices
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q4 2024 results, highlighting that major offshore projects (Shenandoah and Salamanca) remain on schedule for first production in Q2 2025, which is expected to drive over 20% sequential growth in offshore segment margins. Management guided 2025 adjusted EBITDA to around $700 million and 2026 to around $800 million, with cash costs of $600-625 million. Soda ash market remains challenged, but management sees supply rationalizations (UK, Spain, Poland) as positive for future price recovery. Marine transportation is expected to deliver record results in 2025 due to strong market fundamentals.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $29 million driven by the one-time debt restructuring charge of $41 million
Fourth quarter adjusted ROE was negative 25% due to the non-recurring costs
positive_highlights: Adjusted pretax income of $90 million in full year 2024, up 84% versus the prior year
Total servicing additions increased by 70% over 2023 to reach $25 billion in Q4 alone
Raised adjusted ROE guidance for 2025 to a range of 16% to 18%
summary: Onity Group reported fourth quarter results consistent with prior guidance, delivering adjusted pretax income of $11 million and full-year adjusted ROE of 20%, which exceeded the previous year's result but was in line with current expectations. The GAAP net loss for the quarter included a one-time charge of $41 million related to corporate debt restructuring costs. Management raised its adjusted ROE guidance range for 2025 from prior levels (implied below) to 16% to 18%, citing improved balance sheet positioning and deleveraging progress.

negative_highlights: Ting recorded a $28.2 million one-time restructuring and impairment charge in Q4
Wavelo Q4 revenue down 1.9% sequentially to $9.9 million
2025 guidance includes a $9 million one-time charge for winding down Verizon MVNO agreement
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 19% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $34.9 million in 2024
Ting improved Adjusted EBITDA from a $12.3 million loss to a $1.5 million loss in Q4, with December slightly positive
Wavelo Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 was $13.8 million, well above guidance of $8-10 million
summary: Tucows reported Q4 2024 consolidated revenue up 19% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $34.9 million for the year, up 126% from $15.5 million in 2023. Excluding Ting, Adjusted EBITDA hit $57.4 million, above guidance. Ting reduced Adjusted EBITDA loss to $1.5 million in Q4 from $12.3 million a year ago, turning slightly positive in December. Management guided 2025 Adjusted EBITDA to approximately $56 million before a $9 million one-time Verizon wind-down charge, up 75% over 2024.

negative_highlights: Cash balance remains thin at $405,000, requiring additional financing for acquisitions and growth
Adjusted gross margin declined to 54.1% from 56.6% in the prior quarter
Company withheld revenue guidance citing substantial near-term variability
positive_highlights: Revenue of $3.17 million exceeded guidance and marked fifth consecutive quarter of growth
Adjusted operating loss improved 28.9% quarter-over-quarter, fourth consecutive reduction
Acquisitions of Spacecraft Components and SCP Manufacturing expected to enhance margins and profitability
summary: In fiscal Q1 2025, Mobix Labs reported revenue of $3.17 million, exceeding prior guidance with a 7.3% sequential increase and an 11-fold jump year-over-year. Adjusted gross margin was 54.1%, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to $2.5 million, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of reduced operating losses. The company announced two acquisitions (Spacecraft Components Corp and SCP Manufacturing) and guided to long-term gross margin of 60% and adjusted operating margin of 30%, but withheld near-term revenue guidance due to acquisition-related variability.

negative_highlights: Q4 net sales declined 10% YoY, in line with expectations but down
Expects first-half 2025 revenue to be lighter with a high single-digit decline in Q1
Facing headwinds from USPS rate increase and two more months of large grocer loss
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 48 bps to 8.4% in 2024
Dividend increased by 50% to $0.075 per share quarterly
New client wins including Gallo's Spirit of Gallo and Titleist packaging redesign
summary: Quad reported Q4 2024 net sales decline of 10% YoY, in line with expectations, and full-year adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.4% from 7.9% in 2023. Free cash flow was $56 million, with $71 million from asset sales; net debt leverage reduced to 1.6x. Management expects net sales growth between 2027-2028 and projects a 100bps EBITDA margin improvement by 2028, but faces headwinds from a large grocer loss, a likely USPS rate increase, and early 2025 divestiture of European operations. The dividend was raised 50% to $0.075 per share quarterly.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance is lowered to a range of $30-33 million due to customer inventory burn-down from record H2 volumes, product transitions, and the expiration of a special national mobile hotspot program.
Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) revenue declined slightly YoY in Q4 as customers manage year-end inventory ahead of next-generation product launches expected mid-year.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew >33% YoY with mobile solutions up 59% driven by a large carrier partner and services/other revenue up 62% on SaaS renewals.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 37.4%, representing a 260 bps sequential improvement, while adjusted EBITDA reached an all-time high of $5.4 million (11.2%).
Balance sheet strengthened materially with total debt reduced from >$165M at start of year to $56M by Q4 end and cash position improved to $40 million.
summary: Inseego reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $48.1 million (up >33% YoY) and full-year revenue of $191.2 million (up 14.3%), driven by strong carrier hotspot growth (+59%) and SaaS services expansion (+62%). The company achieved a non-GAAP gross margin of 37.4%, adjusted EBITDA of $5.4 million, and completed the sale of its Telematics business for $52 million cash to reduce debt levels significantly from over $160M in total debt at year-end.

negative_highlights: OpEx guidance implies incremental $14M spending versus $13M revenue increase, though CFO notes 12% expense growth vs. 17% revenue growth
Gross margin guidance of 74% reflects geographic mix and inflation; no expansion this year
positive_highlights: Q4 worldwide sales up 23% YoY and full-year revenue up 22%
International sales up 42% in Q4, driven by strength in Europe and China
New initiatives like LungTraX Detect show early momentum with first patient treated
summary: Pulmonx reported Q4 worldwide sales of $23.8 million, up 23% year-over-year, with record U.S. sales of $15.9 million (up 16%) and record international sales of $7.9 million (up 42%). Full-year revenue was $83.8 million, up 22%. The company guided 2025 revenue growth of 17% at midpoint, below the 20% long-term target but accelerated by new initiatives in the second half of 2025. Gross margin guidance was 74%, with R&D spending increasing for clinical trials. Management remains confident in long-term growth and highlights successful pilot programs like LungTraX.

negative_highlights: Full-year operating margin down 260 bps to 5.7%
Adjusted EPS fell to $3.79 from $4.62
Costume business down 7.5% for the year
positive_highlights: Q4 gross profit dollars up 5% to $35.6 million on net sales up 3%
Initiated quarterly dividend of $0.25 per share
International Disguise business reached all-time high in 2024
summary: Q4 2024 sales were roughly in line with expectations, with toy and consumer products down 1.8% for the full year, slightly better than expected. Gross margin improved 70 bps in Q4, but full-year operating margin fell to 5.7% from 8.3%, and adjusted EPS dropped to $3.79 from $4.62. Management initiated a quarterly dividend of $0.25 and highlighted continued strength in Sonic and international growth, but acknowledged challenges in costumes and cost pressures from tariffs.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth missed the company's own targets, with full-year growth at only 8% despite transformation efforts.
Net Revenue Retention (NRR) for enterprise accounts finished at 99%, which is below past performance and management's confidence level.
Non-enterprise ARR declined 4% to $88 million as the company pivots focus toward high-value B2B/Enterprise segments.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income exceeded $19M for FY2024, a $6M improvement over the loss in FY2023 and nearly double the original forecast.
Operating cash flow reached $26 million for the year, representing a $50 million swing from 2023's negative cash flow.
Non-GAAP sales and marketing expenses improved to 36% of revenue down from 41% in FY2023.
summary: BigCommerce reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $87 million (up 3% YoY) and full-year revenue of $333 million (up 8%), meeting expectations but missing prior growth targets. The company significantly improved profitability with non-GAAP operating income exceeding $19M for the year ($6M loss in FY2023), driven by a ~10% headcount reduction, lower S&M spend at 36% of revenue, and restructuring costs recognized early in Q4. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance to $342-$350 million (up from prior expectations) while maintaining conservative macro assumptions.

negative_highlights: Operating income only up $179,000 in Q4 year-over-year, with lower financial income and higher taxes keeping net income flat
GAAP net income for Q4 declined $344,000 year-over-year
Future grants from Israel Innovation Authority are uncertain beyond first quarter 2025
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $16.3 million, up 16.1% year-over-year; full-year revenue up 82% to $61 million
Record net income of $13.5 million for 2024, with EPS up over 75% on a GAAP basis
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance of 12%–15% growth, indicating continued momentum
summary: RADCOM reported record Q4 2024 revenue of $16.3 million, up 16.1% year-over-year, with full-year revenue of $61 million, up 82% and above guidance midpoint, marking five consecutive years of growth. Operating income for 2024 was a record $9.5 million (16% of revenue), and net income was $13.5 million ($0.83 per diluted share). The company guided to 12%–15% revenue growth for 2025, with a midpoint of $69.2 million, and highlighted new customer wins including Norlys (Telia Denmark) and partnerships like ServiceNow.

negative_highlights: NII per share fell to $0.55 from $0.64 sequentially
NAV per share decreased $0.22 to $19.98
Added seven names to watch list; three-rated investments increased
positive_highlights: NII covered base dividend at 131% in Q4
Non-accruals remain below industry average at 0.9% of fair value
Portfolio weighted average grade stable at 2.1; 87% rated 1 or 2
summary: CCAP reported Q4 2024 NII of $0.55 per share, down from $0.64 in Q3 and $0.61 in Q4 2023, driven by lower base rates and lower non-recurring income. NAV per share declined $0.22 to $19.98. The company declared a regular dividend of $0.42 and special dividends of $0.03 per share. Portfolio quality remained stable with non-accruals at 0.9% of fair value, but watch list names increased. Management anticipates continued pickup in LBO activity in 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth only 3% YoY, modest despite record levels
Net dollar retention of 103% in Q4, but closed the year at 100% indicating sub-100% yearly retention
Management notes gross margin may dip in Q1 due to note weakness in-term AWS credits
positive_highlights: Record total revenue of $45.6M, up 3% YoY; record subscription revenue of $43.4M, up 6% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA of $2.7M, sixth consecutive quarter of profitability and highest in four years
New subscription bookings at highest level since Q4 2022, with four seven-digit deals and 29 six-digit deals
summary: Kaltura reported record Q4 2024 total revenue of $45.6M, up 3% YoY, and record subscription revenue of $43.4M, up 6% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.7M, the sixth consecutive quarter of profitability and the highest in four years, with record gross margin and $4.3M operating cash flow. Management noted record ARR and RPO, accelerating bookings momentum, and raised expectations for 2025 with continued growth and margin expansion, targeting Rule of 30. Guidance and outlook positive, with expansion plans in sales force and AI investments.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 8% and funds from operations down ~19% YoY due to lower Brent prices
Operating costs per BOE up 2% in 2024, impacted by removal of diesel subsidies and higher gas/electricity
2024 net income only $3 million, down from a net loss in 2023 (but still positive)
positive_highlights: Record reserves across all categories and six consecutive years of 1P reserve growth
2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d, up ~35% from 2024 average
Strong reserve replacement ratios of 702% (1P), 1250% (2P), 1500% (3P)
summary: Gran Tierra reported record reserves and highest-ever quarterly production in Q4 2024, with average FY2024 production of 34,710 BOE/d (up 6% YoY) and net income of $3 million (EPS $0.10) versus a net loss in 2023. The company reaffirmed 2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d, up significantly due to Canadian acquisition and development programs. CFO expects operating costs to trend down in 2025, and management is confident in 5-10% production growth into 2026. Management highlighted continued share buybacks (6.7% of shares repurchased in 2024) and plans to allocate 50% of excess free cash flow to debt reduction and 50% to buybacks, with a target net debt of $600M by end 2026 and $500M by end 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 consolidated EBITDA down year-over-year (13.4% margin vs 7.8%)
Q1 guidance flat, with caution on tariff impacts
Arcadia high-end residential demand weak; cost structure being rightsized
positive_highlights: Q4 sales and EBITDA exceeded guidance
Extended Arcadia put option to Sept 2026, easing liquidity concerns
NobelClad Q4 sales were its second strongest in over 10 years
summary: DMC Global's Q4 2024 sales of $152.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $10.4 million exceeded guidance, but profits fell sharply year-over-year due to weak Arcadia residential demand and lower margins across segments. Management guided Q1 2025 sales flat sequentially at $146-154 million and adjusted EBITDA of $8-11 million, citing tariff uncertainty and soft demand. The company extended the Arcadia put option to September 2026, reducing near-term liquidity risk, and is prioritizing free cash flow and debt repayment. Arcadia is being refocused on commercial products with cost cuts, while DynaEnergetics completed a product reengineering and automation phase.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin missed expectations due to higher-than-expected scrap expense related to raw materials and a $1 million inventory reserve.
Q1 guidance midpoint is flat year-over-year, reflecting uncertainty regarding PEPFAR funding freezes affecting international diagnostics revenue (approx. 80% of which is donor-funded).
US academic/research segment exposure faces potential headwinds from NIH plans to reduce indirect research cost funding mechanisms.
positive_highlights: Core revenue grew 10% YoY driven by strong international HIV business order trends and a 14% increase in sample management solutions revenue.
Acquisition of Sherlock Biosciences completed to expand the innovation pipeline with a molecular diagnostic platform for CTNG testing expected by end of 2025.
FDA approval secured for labeling change on OraQuick HIV self-test expanding access to adolescents aged 14 and older.
summary: Q4 total revenue was $37.4 million with core revenue of $36.5 million growing 10% year-over-year to the top half of guidance range. GAAP gross margin contracted to 36.2%, while non-GAAP margins were slightly below expectations due to one-time scrap expenses and inventory reserves related to exiting a business unit. Management provided Q1 revenue guidance ranging from $27.5 million to $31.5 million, noting that the midpoint is flat year-over-year after adjusting for exited businesses.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially due to a prolonged labor market downturn with seasonally adjusted hires down for the 28th consecutive month.
Net loss widened significantly in Q4 to $10.8 million compared to net income of $5.6 million in Q4 2023, driven by revenue contraction.
positive_highlights: Job seeker web traffic grew by 30% in organic visits during 2024, demonstrating product stickiness despite macro headwinds.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $111 million, an 18% year-over-year decline and a 5% sequential decrease driven by soft hiring demand among SMBs. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $14.4 million (13% margin) from $42.4 million in the prior year quarter due to lower revenue volume despite disciplined cost management. Management provided Q1 FY2025 guidance of $109 million at the midpoint, representing an 11% decline versus last year but a sequential improvement over Q4.

negative_highlights: Q4 consolidated revenue declined 2% year-over-year
EPS slightly lower due to FX and discontinued operations
Europe segment operating profit decreased, with Germany revenue weakness
positive_highlights: Operating profit increased 8% year-over-year to $4.9 million
JAX Flight Club revenue grew 19% year-over-year
Q1 2025 revenue expected to grow at a higher pace with 5% incremental membership fee revenue
summary: Travelzoo Q4 2024 revenue was $20.7 million, down 2% year-over-year, but operating profit rose 8% to $4.9 million with a 24% margin. EPS was slightly lower due to FX and discontinued operations, but management expects Q1 2025 revenue to grow at a higher pace with 5% incremental growth from membership fees. Legacy member conversion to paid club membership is on track, with expectations of 50% more paying members by end of Q1. JAX Flight Club grew revenue 19% year-over-year and remains profitable.

negative_highlights: Q1 guidance flat year-over-year due to non-recurring sales and shipment shift
Retail gross margin down 370 basis points in Q4
Recorded $4 million non-cash trademark impairment on Muck
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.19 in Q4
Retail segment highest ever quarterly sales, up 15.3%
Full-year recurring sales up 5.3% and adjusted EPS up 31.6%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q4 sales up 1.7% to $128.1 million, with a strong retail segment up 15.3% and wholesale up 4.5% on a recurring basis. Adjusted EPS rose to $1.19 from $0.98, and full-year recurring sales grew 5.3% with adjusted EPS of $2.54 versus $1.93. The company guided Q1 flat year-over-year due to non-recurring sales and shipment timing, despite momentum in XTRATUF, Muck, and Durango. Management remains cautious on consumer unpredictability and retailer inventory commitments.

negative_highlights: TV Media revenue declined 4% to $5 billion due to affiliate and advertising headwinds.
Q1 adjusted OIBDA is expected to decline year-over-year compared to last year's Super Bowl quarter.
positive_highlights: Paramount+ added 5.6 million new subscribers in Q4, the strongest quarter of sub-growth in two years.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q4 FY2024 results with Paramount+ adding 5.6 million new subscribers and achieving record engagement driven by a strong content slate including 'Landman' and the NFL season. D2C revenue grew 8% to $2 billion, while TV Media revenue declined 4% due to affiliate headwinds and fewer football games. Management raised full-year free cash flow expectations for 2025 despite Q1 being impacted by lapping last year's Super Bowl.

negative_highlights: 2025 revenues and profits expected to decline significantly due to soft bookings market
Q4 tax rate 55% due to non-deductible footprint charges
Bolzoni Q4 revenue down $4M YoY and operating loss below prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 revenues up 4% YoY and adjusted operating profit up 10% YoY

Early 2025 bookings show encouraging signs in EMEA and JPIC
summary: Q4 2024 revenues rose 4% YoY to $1.1B, with adjusted operating profit up 10% to $54M and adjusted EPS of $1.47. Full-year revenues reached $4.3B, up 5%, with adjusted operating profit of $267M (6% margin), the strongest in company history. Guidance calls for a significant decline in 2025 revenues and profits due to soft bookings and higher cancellations, though early 2025 bookings show encouraging signs in EMEA and JPIC. Footprint optimization programs are expected to generate $30-40M annual benefits starting in 2027, but 2025 margins are expected to be below the 7% target.

negative_highlights: China business faces challenging environment, expected only to 'hold serve'
Hyatt integration costs and inventory step-up will affect near-term profitability
Company is not planning significant stock buybacks beyond managing dilution
positive_highlights: Q4 net sales grew 7% sequentially, exceeding expectations
Adjusted diluted EPS increased 14% sequentially
Hyatt acquisition expected to drive strong growth with revenue guidance of $145-160 million for 2025
summary: USANA reported solid Q4 2024 results with sequential net sales growth of 7% and adjusted diluted EPS up 14%, exceeding expectations. The quarter benefited from promotional activities, particularly in the US (up 16% sequentially) and Australia/New Zealand (up 9% YoY). The company completed the acquisition of an 78.8% stake in Hyatt for $405 million, which contributed minimally to 2024 results but is expected to generate $145-160 million in revenue for 2025 (29-42% growth). Management outlined 2025 plans including over 20 product launches, a global convention, and incentive enhancements, while maintaining a cautious outlook for core business growth.

negative_highlights: Cash used in operations and CapEx decreased to $81.4M in 2024 from $99.6M in 2023, still high
Cash burn expected to be lumpy sequentially, though lower on an annualized basis
Gross margins expected to remain lumpy
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue of $24.3M exceeded midpoint of $23.5-25M guidance

Q4 2024 generated gross profit for the first time
summary: Innoviz reported full-year 2024 revenue of $24.3 million, up from $20.1 million in 2023 and above the midpoint of guidance. The company secured an $80 million NRE payment plan, raised $40 million via a registered direct offering, and announced $12 million in annualized cost savings. For 2025, management guides revenue of $50-60 million, implying more than twofold growth, with positive gross margin on an annualized basis.

negative_highlights: 2025 free cash flow guided down to $20-25 million from $47.7 million
Gas Cylinders Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin down 350 bps YoY
Q1 2025 expected to be softer due to order pull-forwards and CNG headwinds
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EPS up 61% YoY to $0.29
Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 12.2% prior year
Four consecutive quarters of margin expansion in Electron
summary: Luxfer reported Q4 2024 sales of $96 million, adjusted EBITDA of $13.8 million (14.4% margin), and adjusted EPS of $0.29, up 61% YoY, driven by defense demand and order pull-ins. Full-year adjusted EPS was $0.99 with EBITDA margin of 13.7%. 2025 guidance calls for flat revenue, adjusted EPS of $0.95-$1.05, EBITDA of $48-52 million, and free cash flow of $20-25 million, reflecting the absence of one-time benefits. Management cited near-term headwinds in clean energy and a softer Q1 2025 due to order pull-forwards, but remains confident in long-term hydrogen and CNG opportunities.

negative_highlights: Q4 gross profit margin contracted to 26.1% from the prior year's 26.8% due to expected price decreases on specific products.
International revenue declined in Q4, partially offsetting gains in North America.
Cash flow from operations decreased significantly to $65.4 million compared to $88.6 million in FY2023.

Operating profit grew 23.1% for the full year, ending with $43.2 million versus $35.1 million prior year.
Company ended FY2024 in a net cash position of $600k after repurchasing shares and paying dividends.
summary: Hamilton Beach Brands reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $213.5 million (up 3.3% YoY) and full-year net income increasing to $30.8 million ($2.20/share). While the company achieved a record gross margin expansion of 300 bps for the year, Q4 margins contracted slightly due to planned price reductions on certain products after cost benefits were realized in late 2023. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations from low single-digits to mid-single digits and reiterated that operating profit is expected to grow faster than revenue driven by expense leverage.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance is flat-to-up (+1%) due to anticipated disruption in H1 from the April 13, 2025 LCD implementation.
Operating expenses increased $12.2 million YoY (up 17%), driven by a 20% rise in SG&A and incremental clinical trial spending for ReNu BLA preparation.
Management expects a challenging operating environment throughout the first half of 2025 before stabilization begins.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $126.7 million beat guidance by exceeding the upper range ($100M-$125M).
Adjusted EBITDA expanded significantly to $18.2 million (up from $7.5m prior year) and exceeded expectations.
Strong brand equity demonstrated as customers adapted quickly to delayed LCD effective dates.
summary: Organogenesis reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $126.7 million (up 27% YoY), exceeding the high end of prior guidance and driving adjusted EBITDA to $18.2 million, which beat expectations by over $2 million. Management provided full-year 2025 financial guidance assuming a delayed LCD effective date of April 13, 2025, projecting revenue between $480 million and $535 million (flat to +11% YoY) with profitability expected to stabilize in the third quarter after challenging first-half conditions. The company highlighted strong execution despite market ambiguity but noted that customer watching behavior remains cautious due to reimbursement uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Product revenue declined quarter-over-quarter primarily due to a drop in product supply sales from global partners ($0.8M vs $7.4M)

positive_highlights: NERLYNX ex-factory bottle sales increased by an approximate 9% quarter-over-quarter to 2,964 bottles

summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $59.1 million, a decline from the prior quarter driven by lower product supply sales to global partners and higher gross-to-net adjustments, though NERLYNX ex-factory bottle sales increased slightly year-over-year due to inventory builds at distributors. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for net revenue between $192M-$198M but explicitly forecast a demand decline of approximately 2% versus the prior year and noted that royalty revenues will be lower in 2025 as China transitions regulatory ownership to Pierre Fabre.

Management remains cautiously optimistic about stabilization and innovation, but faces uncertainty from FDA decision on compounded semaglutide and ongoing subscriber declines.

negative_highlights: Q4 net loss widened significantly to $548 million primarily due to a one-time $570 million estimated loss on the sale of discontinued operations.

Legacy financial guarantee business sold for $420 million, providing capital relief and allowing focus on Specialty P&C growth.

The company successfully closed the Beat acquisition driving significant revenue growth in Cirrata (+93% YoY), while Everspan achieved an underwriting profit with a 96.5 combined ratio despite some program volatility. Management indicated that forward guidance for 2025 will be revisited following the final close of the legacy business sale.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA slightly below guidance range
Jafra U.S. revenue down 17.6% in Q4 due to Shopify Plus adoption issues

Adjusted EPS up 17.3% for the full year

Leadership transition announced with Andres Campos as new President and CEO.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5% QoQ/QoY to $37M with average paid members slightly up.

summary: Codexis reported Q4 2024 revenue of $21.5 million, with product revenue of $9.8 million and R&D revenue of $11.6 million. Management guided 2025 total revenue to $64-68 million, its first combined guidance, expecting double-digit growth across the entire base. The CEO expressed confidence in returning the base pharma business to growth and highlighted progress in advancing the ECO Synthesis platform, with multiple feasibility studies completed and revenue-generating contracts expected in early Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Core income decreased by $12 million year-over-year due to the full retention loss from Hurricane Milton.

Successfully placed a new $200 million catastrophe bond at attractive terms featuring a cascading drop-down feature for subsequent events.
Launched a new apartment program in Florida and wrote 19 new risks totaling approximately $2.3 million of premium.
summary: American Coastal Insurance reported Q4 FY2024 net income of $4.9 million and gross premiums earned growth of approximately 13% year-over-year to $162.7 million, though core income decreased by $12 million due to a full retention loss from Hurricane Milton ($23M) which drove the combined ratio to 91.9%. Management reiterated its 2025 net income guidance range of $70-$90 million and maintained expectations for an underlying combined ratio near 65%, despite pricing decreases of 5-10% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Full-year collaboration revenue growth is expected to decelerate significantly with guidance of only $5-15 million for FY2025.
Management explicitly stated that the Phase 3 INFRONT-3 trial will be powered primarily on symptomatic patients, excluding presymptomatics from primary analysis due to slower progression rates.
positive_highlights: Collaboration revenue surged to $54.2M in Q4, driven by the GSK partnership for Latozinemab and AL101 programs.

Management provided 2025 guidance expecting collaboration revenue between $5-15 million and total R&D/G&A expenses of roughly $175-$185 million / $55-$65 million respectively, indicating a significant reduction in expected spend compared to the prior year's trajectory. The company highlighted strong cash reserves of $413.4 million but noted that future revenue is projected at levels significantly lower than current run rates.

Book value per share fell to -$40.99 from -$32.56, and PREPA resolution remains uncertain with an $800 million claim. summary: LENSAR reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $16.7 million (up 38% YoY) and GAAP net loss of $18.7 million driven by a noncash warrant charge; the company achieved its second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA ($478k). Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to above the prior year's growth rate, citing global expansion in Europe and Southeast Asia.

negative_highlights: Q4 NII declined from $0.58 in Q3 due to base rate declines and repricing

summary: NCDL reported Q4 2024 NII of $0.56 per share, fully covering the $0.55 dividend, and full-year NII of $2.26 per share with ROE of 12.4%. NAV per share rose to $18.18 from $18.15, and the company issued $300 million of unsecured notes in January 2025 to reduce debt costs. Management noted record Churchill platform origination of over $13 billion, a well-managed nonaccrual level of 0.1% of fair value, and expects continued growth in 2025, with no material policy impact anticipated.

positive_highlights: Q4 revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 40% and 28% YoY, exceeding guidance

Full-year revenue rose 30% and contribution ex-TAC rose 24%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 500 basis points to 25%. The company announced the acquisition of Locker, a data collaboration platform, and expects AI measurement to launch in Q2 and AI decisioning in H2 2025. Management noted temporary gross accounting for a few large customers but expressed strong market momentum and a positive outlook.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it will not launch or commercialize any new tests in 2025, limiting near-term pipeline expansion despite robust R&D progress.
Adjusted EBITDA remains a loss of $3.9 million for the quarter and $22.1 million annually; profitability is targeted only for the second half of 2025.
Cash balance decreased to $26.2 million at quarter-end, though management expects cash flow breakeven later in the year.

Gross margin expanded sequentially from 77.0% in Q3 to 78.7% in Q4 as volume scaled.
Pilot program successfully demonstrated the viability of leveraging primary care referral networks via pulmonologists.
summary: Biodesix reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $20.4 million (39% YoY growth) and full-year revenue of $71.3 million (45% YoY), both in line with guidance. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $92-$95 million while maintaining strong margins in the mid-to-upper seventies.

Pharmaceutical-grade ingredient sales up 96% YoY in Q4
summary: ChromaDex reported record Q4 2024 revenue of $29.1 million, up 37% year-over-year, and net income of $7.2 million, versus breakeven a year earlier. Management guided to approximately 18% revenue growth for 2025, with modest gross margin improvement, and highlighted a pending company name change and progress in pharmaceutical-grade Niagen and clinical studies.

negative_highlights: Gross margins declined from 34.4% to 34.1% in Q4 due to negative product mix and lower margin sales.
Adjusted EBITDA margins contracted from 19.3% to 17.5% as operating leverage was offset by increased compensation expenses.
Net income for the full year decreased 19% primarily due to $8.8 million in pretax debt refinancing costs.
positive_highlights: Prepaid segment delivered exceptional performance with a 59% Q4 increase driven by fraud-focused packaging solutions (PACS Gene) and healthcare verticals.
Debit and credit business grew 12% in the quarter, led by eco-friendly contactless cards which now represent approximately 90% of chip card volume.
Free cash flow generation was strong at $34.1 million for FY2024 despite higher capital spending.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q4 FY2024 net sales growth of 22% driven by a 59% surge in the prepaid segment and 12% growth in debit/credit segments. Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $21.9 million, though margins contracted slightly from 34.4% to 34.1%. For full year FY2024, net sales grew 8%, prepaid exceeded expectations with over $100M in revenue, and free cash flow reached $34.1 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 1% full-year and $15 million in Q4 due to a one-time increase of ~$25m in credit losses from the divested direct marketing business.
Reported revenue growth was muted at +6% (organic) because FX, interest, and disposed business headwinds offset underlying performance.
FY2025 guidance for reported revenue is flat to low single-digit (+1.7B-$1.734B), reflecting the ongoing impact of the divestiture.
positive_highlights: Full-year GAAP net income turned positive at $22 million, compared to a loss of $20 million the prior year.

summary: Paysafe reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $420 million (up 1% YoY) and full-year revenue of $1.7 billion (up 6%), though Adjusted EBITDA declined to $103 million for the quarter ($452m full year, down 1%) due to accelerated exits in the divested direct marketing business and associated credit losses. Management provided new adjusted EPS guidance for FY2025 of $2.21-$2.51 per share with revenue growth expected between flat and +2%, citing a one-time portfolio rationalization impact that will normalize margins in 2025.

negative_highlights: Q4 net income slightly down year-over-year due to warrant impact
Full-year combined ratio of 94% above 90% target due to hurricanes
Elevated technology and State Farm investments create near-term margin drag
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 19% to $292 million, exceeding expectations

2025 guidance calls for 30-40% net income growth and 21-29% adjusted EBITDA growth
summary: Hagerty reported Q4 2024 total revenue up 19% to $292 million, with written premiums up 13% and membership/marketplace revenue up 68%. Full-year operating income jumped to $66 million from $10 million, and adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $124 million. Management guided 2025 total revenue growth of 12-13%, adjusted EBITDA of $150-160 million (up 21-29%), and net income of $102-110 million (up 30-40%), despite $11 million in wildfire losses and elevated technology investments. They expect accelerating growth from State Farm Classic Plus conversions and new Enthusiast Plus product, with margin expansion resuming in 2026-2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained at $5.3 million for the quarter

Dixie Medical products have lower gross margins, slightly offsetting gains
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter revenue grew 19% to $21.5 million
Full-year revenue exceeded guidance at $79.9 million
Gross margin improved for RNS products on higher volumes
summary: NeuroPace reported Q4 2024 revenue of $21.5 million, up 19% YoY, and full-year revenue of $79.9 million, up 22% YoY, exceeding original guidance of $73-77 million. Gross margins were stable at 75.4% in Q4, operating expenses rose only 7%, and net loss improved to $5.3 million from $6.2 million a year ago. The company regains capital via a public offering, repurchased KCK shares, and projected cash sufficient to breakeven. Management is confident about ongoing growth, driven by record active prescribers and progress on Project CARE and clinical trials.

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin contracted to 19.2% due to a $2.8 million nonrecurring inventory charge.
Average revenue per customer declined across segments (Lab Essentials -7%, Clinical Solutions -25%).
Management noted recent softening in biopharma demand with customers delaying orders and reducing budgets.

Free cash outflow significantly improved from -$26.7 million in FY2023 to -$13.5 million in FY2024.
Gross margin expanded sequentially to 23.0% in Q4 driven by higher Clinical Solutions mix and reduced headcount.
summary: Alpha Teknova reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $9.3 million (up 18% YoY) and full-year revenue of $37.7 million (up 3% YoY or 11% excluding a one-time prior year order). The company reduced its annual free cash outflow to $13.5 million from $26.7 million in the prior year, finishing below guidance. Management provided FY2025 revenue guidance of $39-42 million (midpoint ~7% growth), noting that while momentum exists, macro uncertainty has caused some customers to delay orders.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 9% year-over-year, and full-year revenue down 7%
Accessories and materials declined 20% for the full year
Active users down 0.7% and 90-day engaged users down 3.1% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up 7% year-over-year to 2.96 million, with 121,000 sequential increase

summary: Cricut reported Q4 2024 revenue of $209.3 million, down 9% year-over-year, with full-year revenue down 7% to $712.5 million. New machine launches (Explore 4 and Maker 4) received positive early feedback, but the company faces pressure in accessories and materials due to private label competition.

summary: Sight Sciences reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $19.1 million (up 2% YoY), driven by a 9% increase in surgical glaucoma but offset by an expected decline in dry eye due to price increases and strategic focus on reimbursement access rather than volume growth. Management initiated full-year 2025 guidance for total revenue between $70-75 million, explicitly factoring in headwinds from new Medicare LCDs restricting multiple MIGS procedures at the same time as cataract surgery and uncertainty regarding TearCare commercial coverage timing. The company expects Q1 2025 revenue to be down low-to-mid double digits compared to the prior year.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 4% YoY due to the conclusion of Emergency Connectivity Fund (ECF) and Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP), which impacted US telecom segment revenues.

US domestic revenue fell 29% for the quarter as legacy mobile broadband customers exited and construction revenue remained lower.
positive_highlights: International segment delivered steady performance with adjusted EBITDA growing 9.7% YoY driven by high-speed data subscriber growth and operational improvements.

Company returned capital to shareholders via $10 million in stock repurchases and maintained dividends of $14.7 million during FY2024.
summary: ATN International reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $680.5 million (down 9% YoY) and full-year revenue of $729.1 million (down 4%), driven by the sunset of US government programs like ECF/ACP, lower construction revenue, and a goodwill impairment charge of $35.3 million that caused a full-year net loss of $26.4 million versus income in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $184.1 million for the full year as US telecom revenues fell, while international segment adjusted EBITDA grew 9.7% YoY on modest revenue growth and margin expansion. Management provided a flat-to-slightly-down outlook for Q1 2025 due to restructuring charges similar in size to last year's first quarter.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 28% YoY to $33.6M

Full-year revenue was $143M and adjusted EBITDA $13.3M. 2025 guidance is $140M-$160M revenue and $13M-$15M adjusted EBITDA, roughly flat to slightly up. Management cites cost actions and diversification, but expects wind tower activity to remain flat through 2026.

positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 17% constant currency, second best-quarter ever

They also announced a transformational agreement with Amazon and an AI partnership with Rabot.

negative_highlights: SMB gross margins contracted to 20.5% due to a one-time $3.5 million inventory write-down for obsolete licenses.

summary: Q1 FY2025 sales grew 26% YoY, with dolls and role play/dress-up up 37% and action play/collectibles up 30%; adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.4 million, a $17.6 million improvement. Gross margin hit 34.4%, driven by product mix and favorable timing. The company remains debt-free with $59.2 million cash, but management is cautious on tariffs, holding some goods and adjusting sourcing; 2025 guidance not explicitly reaffirmed.

negative_highlights: Wholesale sales down 6.3%
Gross margin guidance pressured by tariffs
Inflationary price increases may pressure demand
positive_highlights: Record Q1 gross margin of 41.2%, 210 bps expansion
Adjusted EPS up to $0.73 vs $0.41
Retail segment sales rose 20.5%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $114.1 million, up 1.1% year-over-year, slightly ahead of expectations, with record first-quarter gross margins of 41.2%. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.73 from $0.41 a year ago. Retail segment grew 20.5%, but wholesale declined 6.3% due to planned military reductions. Management reiterated full-year guidance despite tariff uncertainties and plans price increases in June, expecting EPS just below last year's $2.54.

negative_highlights: Operating income down 34% YoY due to member growth investments
Europe revenue up only 1%, operating margin flat at 3%
GAAP operating margin fell to 16% from 26% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue of $23.1 million, highest since pandemic, up 5% YoY; constant currency up 6%
Jack's Flight Club revenue up 20% YoY, premium subscribers up 13%
Expect Q2 revenue growth to double YoY, accelerating trend expected
summary: Travelzoo reported Q1 2025 revenue of $23.1 million, up 5% year-over-year, the highest quarterly revenue since the pandemic, with constant currency revenue up 6%. Operating income fell 34% to $3.7 million due to increased member acquisition investments, and non-GAAP operating profit was $4.3 million versus $6.0 million last year. Management expects Q2 revenue growth to double year-over-year and accelerate through the year as subscription fees are recognized ratably. While North America and Jack's Flight Club led growth, Europe was flat, and management acknowledged near-term EPS pressure from marketing investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 3% YoY due to lower fuel surcharge and tonnage
LTL tonnage per day down 7.5% YoY, though outperforming the industry
Adjusted EBITDA down 3% YoY with lower fuel surcharge, tonnage, and pension income
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.73 exceeded expectations
LTL adjusted OR improved 30 bps sequentially, better than seasonality
Yield ex-fuel accelerated to 6.9% YoY and purchase transportation costs down 53%
summary: XPO reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $2 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $278 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.73, exceeding expectations despite a challenging freight market. LTL margins improved sequentially by 30 basis points to an adjusted operating ratio of 85.9%, with yield ex-fuel up 6.9% year-over-year and purchase transportation costs down 53%. The company lowered outsourced linehaul miles to 8.8% of total miles, a record low, and highlighted ongoing technology and AI investments aimed at further productivity gains. Management expressed confidence in continued above-market yield growth and margin expansion, while noting the uncertain macro environment and expected moderation in CapEx.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 2% due to lower paper, logistics, and agency sales
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 7.2%
Free cash flow was negative $100 million, worse than prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20 per share

Growing In-Store Connect network and new client wins
summary: Quad's Q1 2025 net sales were $629 million, down 2% organically, with adjusted EBITDA down from $51 million to $46 million and margin down to 7.2%. Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20, and free cash flow was negative $100 million due to working capital timing. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite tariff and postal headwinds, noting limited direct tariff exposure and USPS promotional discounts for catalogers.

negative_highlights: First quarter ROA was 66 bps, below the 1% goal
Consumer portfolio charge-offs remain high, with provision additional credit expense
Panacea consolidation reduced operating ROA by 10 bps
positive_highlights: Net interest margin up to 3.15% from 290 bps last quarter
Core community bank loan pipeline about 3 times last year; April loans up $25 million
Expect 24 bps ROA from earning assets, 15 bps from mortgage, 15 bps from tech savings
summary: Q1 FY2025 pre-tax net income was $4.5 million excluding Panacea, or $7.5 million adjusted for one-time items, equating to a 66 basis point ROA. Net interest margin improved to 3.15% from 290 basis points last quarter. Management expects to grow earning assets back to $3.75 billion, add 15 bps to ROA from mortgage growth, and reduce technology spend by 15 bps to exceed a 1% ROA goal. Panacea deconsolidation is possible with a potentially substantial gain, but not guaranteed.

negative_highlights: Sub-servicing additions of roughly flat year-over-year due to lower subservicing additions related to the timing of bulk boardings.
Reverse servicing was up from the prior quarter but remained lower versus the prior year, primarily driven by strong asset gains in Q1 '24 and valuation adjustments on buyout loans.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million exceeded the full-year guidance range of 16%-18% adjusted ROE (actual annualized ROE was 22%).
Originations volume grew 53% year-over-year, significantly outpacing the industry's 8% increase.
Total servicing additions were up $17 billion versus Q1 '24, with owned MSR editions more than doubling.
summary: Onity Group reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million and GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders of $21 million ($2.50 per share), exceeding full-year guidance for both metrics. The company confirmed its full year 2025 financial objectives remain unchanged, citing strong execution in originations volume (up 53% YoY) and servicing UPB growth despite a decline in subservicing additions due to timing of bulk boardings.

negative_highlights: Gas Cylinders sales down 9%, margin down to 6.3% from 9%
Alternative fuel softness drove transportation sales down 23%
FX volatility noted as key sensitivity (~$1M EPS impact per $0.05 move)
positive_highlights: Sales up 8.9% to $90.5M, adjusted EPS up to $0.23
Elektron sales up 31% with 120 bps margin expansion
UGR-E demand expected to more than double in 2025; first European bulk gas module order secured
summary: Luxfer's Q1 2025 sales rose 8.9% to $90.5M, with adjusted EPS of $0.23 up from $0.20, adjusted EBITDA up 9.7% to $11.3M (12.5% margin), and operating cash flow of $5.1M. Elektron grew 31% with margin expansion, while Gas Cylinders fell 9% with margin down. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: EPS $0.95-$1.05, EBITDA $48-$52M, and free cash flow $20-$25M. Management highlighted tariff mitigation, strong defense demand, UGR-E record backlog, and a first bulk gas transportation order, while noting FX and rare earth risks.

negative_highlights: Management suspended full-year guidance citing unpredictability from new reciprocal tariffs imposed in April, reducing visibility into near-term trends.
Gross margin expansion was driven by product mix rather than volume or pricing power as average price decreases offset some gains.
Inventory pull-forward of approximately $32 million occurred due to tariff uncertainty, impacting cash flow and working capital.
positive_highlights: Operating profit improved $3.2 million year-over-year, turning a loss from Q1 FY24 into an operating loss of only $943k for Q1 FY25.
North American consumer markets delivered solid growth led by the U.S., partially offsetting slight international declines.
HealthBeacon contributed $1.5 million in revenue and marked its third consecutive quarter of increasing patient subscriptions.
summary: First quarter revenue was $133.4 million (up 4% YoY) with operating profit improving by $3.2 million to reach a loss of only $943k compared to a prior year loss of $1.2m, driven by HealthBeacon and mix shifts. Management suspended full-year guidance due to new retaliatory tariffs in April reducing visibility into the remainder of 2025. The company is implementing price increases and accelerating sourcing diversification outside China with benefits expected to flow through starting in 2026.

negative_highlights: U.S. growth moderated over past four quarters and came in below expectations
Gross margins lower due to geographic mix
R&D expenses expected to increase with trial enrollment
positive_highlights: Worldwide sales $22.5M, up 20% YoY and 21% constant currency
International revenue grew 39% YoY, driven by China
Added 10 new U.S. accounts, ending quarter with 285 active accounts
summary: Pulmonx reported Q1 2025 worldwide sales of $22.5 million, up 20% YoY (21% constant currency), with strong international growth of 39%, but U.S. growth moderated. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $96-98 million, noting that Q1 likely represents a low point for U.S. growth and expects acceleration in the back half from new initiatives. Gross margin was pressured by geographic mix, and China distributor stocking contributed to international strength.

negative_highlights: DynaEnergetics sales down 16% year-over-year
NobelClad backlog down to $41 million from $49 million
Guidance implies lower Q2 EBITDA and sales, citing tariffs and demand disruption
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales up 5% sequentially to $159.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC up 39% sequentially to $14.4 million
Arcadia adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 14.2% from 9.5% in prior year
summary: DMC Global reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated sales of $159.3 million, up 5% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $14.4 million, up 39% sequentially. Arcadia sales grew 9% sequentially and 6% year-over-year to $65.6 million, while DynaEnergetics sales were flat sequentially but down 16% year-over-year due to pricing adjustments. NobelClad sales were flat sequentially but up 5% year-over-year, with backlog down to $41 million from $49 million. The company guided Q2 sales to $149-157 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10-13 million, citing tariff uncertainty, lower residential demand, and softer energy markets. Management expressed cautious optimism around operational improvements but noted significant external headwinds.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $19 million in Q1 2025
Adjusted EBITDA down from $95 million in Q1 2024
positive_highlights: Production up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ to 46,619 BOE/d
Ecuador wells Iguana B1/B2 averaged 1,684 bbl/d over 30 days
Simonette wells exceed budget type curves by 80%
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q1 2025 production of 46,619 BOE/d, up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ, with a net loss of $19 million (improved from $34 million loss in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million. Capex was $95 million, funded by a heavy capital program, and the company reduced gross debt by $27 million, repurchased shares, and added a new $75 million Colombia facility. Management highlighted record drilling times, strong Ecuador discoveries, and improved Canadian well performance, while maintaining full-year production guidance of 47-53 MBoe/d.

negative_highlights: U.S. Domestic revenue declined 9.5% due to the conclusion of Emergency Connectivity Fund and Affordable Care Program subsidies.
Operating income decreased to $2.7 million, impacted by transaction-related expenses and restructuring costs.

International segment adjusted EBITDA rose 10.6% YoY as the business stabilizes.
summary: ATN International reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $179.3 million, down 4% year-over-year due to the wind-down of government subsidy programs in the U.S., while adjusted EBITDA grew by 2% to $44.3 million driven by international segment performance and cash from operations increasing 55%. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 guidance, expecting revenue flat with last year (excluding construction) and essentially flat adjusted EBITDA, citing ongoing U.S. transition costs but steady progress in international markets.

negative_highlights: Global retail sales down 21%, North America down 24%, citing low consumer confidence
Withdrew 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty; tariff impact estimated at $130M-$175M
HDMC operating income declined 51% on lower volume and higher fixed costs per unit

Q1 bottom line better than expected, with operating margin at 12.1% despite environmental pressures
Tariff impact limited to $9 million in Q1, below initial expectations
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenues down 23%, with HDMC down 27% and wholesale shipments down 33%. Operating income fell 51% at HDMC, but HDFS grew 19% to $64M. EPS was $1.07. Retail sales down 21% globally and 24% in North America. Management withdrew full-year 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty, citing a potential $130M-$175M tariff impact. They remain committed to reducing dealer inventory by ~10% year-end and expect productivity savings of $100M in 2025. LiveWire reduced its full-year operating loss guidance to ~$59M from $70-80M.

negative_highlights: Continued market challenges and cautious retail environment
Diving business still very challenged
Tariffs will impact business despite U.S. manufacturing
positive_highlights: New Humminbird products (MEGA Live 2, Xplore) demand exceeding expectations
Jetboil new orders outpacing expectations
Inventory down $69 million year-over-year
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q2 FY2025 results reflecting continued market challenges and a cautious retail environment. Gross margin improved slightly to 35% due to cost savings, despite marketplace discounting. Operating expenses decreased $7.7 million year-over-year. Inventory was down $69 million to $180 million. New products in fishing and camping are exceeding expectations, but overall demand remains soft and tariffs are expected to impact the business.

negative_highlights: Tariff exposure estimated at up to 2-2.5% of COGS in near term, pressuring gross margins
Q4 gross margin not expected to accelerate due to tariff and software mix
International revenue down 5% year-over-year on tough APAC comp
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million, second consecutive quarterly record

Initial sales of ProVision Plus software to Pasolink customers
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $112.6 million, up 1.6% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million (up 17% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.88 (up 13% YoY). Gross margins improved to 35.8% non-GAAP, driven by software and regional mix, but management expects Q4 margins to be pressured by tariffs and a softer software quarter. The company reiterated full-year guidance within the $430-$470 million range and expects to approximate consensus revenue and EBITDA, citing tariff uncertainty and a cautious Q4 outlook.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss of $25 million, though improved from $38 million YoY
Servicing fee income fell from $124 million to $104 million due to 2024 bulk sales

positive_highlights: Pull-through weighted lock volume up 15% YoY to $5.4 billion
