negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from prior expectations due to a one-quarter delay in hiring primary care and associate sales reps.
Sales force contraction reduced Q1 test volumes compared to the previous quarter as new territories were not yet staffed.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $6.2 million, with breakeven now targeted specifically for the fourth quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% year-over-year driven by lung diagnostics (up 16%) and development services (up 61%).
Gross margins expanded 80 basis points sequentially/annually to reach 79.4%, demonstrating operational leverage.
SG&A expenses decreased year-over-year despite adding sales headcount, reflecting successful cost containment.
summary: Biodesix reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $18 million (up 21% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 79.4%, but adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $6.2 million due to sales force reconfiguration delays. Management revised full-year revenue guidance down to $80-$85 million, citing that commercial expansion is approximately one quarter behind plan following the shift from pulmonology-focused reps to primary care and associate support roles.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin of ~15.6% missed the full-year guidance target range of 17%-18%.
GAAP net loss was $2.1 million (EPS -$0.06) compared to a GAAP profit in Q1 FY2024, primarily due to one-time gains and pre-opening costs stripping out non-recurring items.
Recent macroeconomic pressures caused customer traffic reductions of 10-11% in April and May following strong January/February performance.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales declined only modestly by 0.7% in Q1, a significant improvement from the -5.6% decline seen for all of FY2024.
Gift card redemption rates have stabilized around 60-65%, outperforming the industry average, with management noting increased premium menu sales among gift card users.
summary: In Q1 FY2025, GEN Restaurant Group reported total revenues of $57.3 million, a 13% year-over-year increase driven by new store openings and same-store sales improvement to -0.7%, though this was below the full-year prior period decline of -5.6%. Adjusted EBITDA margin came in at approximately 15.6%, missing the annual guidance target range of 17%-18% due to higher costs associated with six new restaurant openings and pre-opening expenses totaling $2.6 million.

negative_highlights: Company reported a working capital deficit of approximately $9.4 million.
No revenue guidance provided for the current or upcoming quarters; first commercial revenue expected only in Q4 FY2025.
Ovaprene interim assessment is safety-only with no primary endpoint analysis, meaning sample size cannot be increased if efficacy data looks weak.
positive_highlights: G&A and R&D expenses decreased significantly by 14% ($2.3M) and 31% respectively compared to the prior year quarter.
Company secured a non-dilutive grant of up to $10.7 million in November 2024 specifically for Ovaprene Phase 3 enrollment expansion.
Received positive feedback from industry peers regarding the 'dual path' strategy (503B compounding while seeking FDA approval).
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a comprehensive loss of approximately $4.4 million for Q1 FY2025, with G&A and R&D expenses decreasing by 14% and 31% respectively due to reduced stock-based compensation and headcount. The company ended the quarter with roughly $10.3 million in cash but maintains a working capital deficit of approximately $9.4 million. Management provided no financial guidance for Q2 or full-year revenue, instead focusing on strategic updates regarding upcoming product launches via 503B compounding expected to begin generating revenue in Q4.

negative_highlights: Dropping one rig for May–August and pausing completions due to macro uncertainty and weak oil prices.
Tariffs on tubular goods could increase AFE by ~2%, though offset by other savings.
First quarter capital spend reached 38% of full-year budget, higher than planned, due to pulling forward activity.
positive_highlights: Production averaged over 53,000 Boe/d, beating guidance and consensus, up ~6% vs Q4.
EBITDA nearly $200 million, up ~10% QoQ on similar oil price.
Drilling efficiencies: spud-to-spud dropped from 14 to 11 days, >20% faster; simul-frac expected to be a 'dollar bill' step change in cost.
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q1 2025 production of over 53,000 Boe/d, beating guidance and consensus, up ~6% sequentially, with EBITDA near $200 million, up ~10% QoQ. The company is taking proactive steps to manage activity in a volatile market by dropping one rig for four months and pausing completions, while still expecting to complete the same number of wells as originally guided. Guidance was narrowed with the floor raised to 48,000 Boe/d, and management highlighted significant drilling efficiencies (spud-to-spud down to 11 days) and expects further cost savings from simul-frac operations. Capital spend was 38% of the full-year budget in Q1, but the company still generated positive free cash flow.

negative_highlights: Terminating SEEG distribution, which reduces product portfolio
Operating expenses up 8% due to R&D investments
Cash burn of $7.5M in the quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 24% YoY to $22.5M, exceeding expectations
Gross margin expanded to 77% due to RNS manufacturing efficiency
Full-year guidance raised to $93-97M
summary: NeuroPace reported Q1 2025 revenue of $22.5 million, up 24% year-over-year, with RNS System sales growing 26% (29% ex-NAUTILUS). Gross margin expanded to 77% from 73.6%, and net loss narrowed to $6.6 million from $8.9 million. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $93-$97 million, representing 16-21% growth, and remains on track for cash flow breakeven by end of 2027. Management announced termination of SEEG distribution to focus on higher-margin RNS business, with minimal 2025 revenue impact.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenues declined slightly by approximately 1% year-over-year.
GAAP net loss increased to $6.7 million due to a $4.3 million non-cash accounting charge related to dust storm damage at Texas facilities reducing crop yield.
Retail branded sales in Canada were down 22% as the company intentionally shifted away from lower-margin value SKUs.
positive_highlights: International medicinal export sales grew 285% year-over-year, contributing significantly to margin expansion.
Canadian cannabis gross margins expanded to 36%, up from 25% in Q1 last year and within the targeted range of 30%-40%.
The Vanguard transaction will generate $40 million in cash proceeds while retaining a minority stake in an attractive produce opportunity.
summary: Consolidated revenues of $77 million were roughly in line with the prior year's $78 million, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $6.7 million ($0.06/share) from a prior-year loss due to lower produce sales and non-cash accounting charges rather than operational deterioration. The company announced a definitive agreement to privatize its majority fresh produce division into Vanguard Foods LP for $40 million cash, retaining 37.9% ownership while keeping Canadian cannabis assets (Delta, D1) and Texas facilities (Marfa I, Monahans). Management highlighted strong international medical export growth of 285% year-over-year in Canada but noted that retail branded sales were lower due to a strategic shift away from low-margin value offerings.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened significantly from prior year income due to market rate compression and dry docking costs increasing by $5.2M YoY
GAAP EPS declined from $0.25 per share in Q1 last year to a loss of $0.03 per diluted share this quarter
Cash flow turned negative with net cash used in operations of $4.3 million compared to prior period inflows
positive_highlights: TCE rates remained a premium of approximately 33% over prevailing market averages despite sector-wide declines
Total shipping days rose 24.6% year-over-year to 5,210 driven by the addition of SSI handy fleet vessels
Management authorized a new $15 million share repurchase program in addition to declaring a quarterly dividend
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported an adjusted net loss of $2 million and GAAP net loss of approximately $2 million for Q1 FY2025, down from prior year income due to a 37% decline in average market TCE rates. Despite the revenue miss driven by lower charter hire expenses ($14.8M EBITDA vs implied higher prior), management raised guidance expectations slightly via new share repurchase authorization and maintained dividend continuity at $0.05/quarter while integrating SSI fleet synergies.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 2% YoY, with Gearing revenue down 28% and Industrial Solutions down 29%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.4% reflects low utilization and lower-margin mix.
Gearing segment posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.2 million due to soft demand and operational inefficiencies.
positive_highlights: Orders increased 5% YoY to $30.5 million, with industrial solutions setting a record for bookings and backlog.
Heavy Fabrication revenue up 15% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up sequentially and YoY.
Reiterated full-year guidance with expected Q2 revenue improvement.
summary: Broadwind reported Q1 2025 revenue of $36.8 million, down 2% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 million (6.4% margin). Orders rose 5% YoY to $30.5 million, driven by wind repowering adapters and gas turbine demand, while gearing and Industrial Solutions revenue declined due to softness and supply chain delays. The company reiterated full-year 2025 guidance of $140-$160 million revenue and $13-$15 million adjusted EBITDA, citing improved momentum in Q2.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 47% from 52% due to intangible amortization
Program revenue declined $1.4 million YoY
Operating expenses up due to noncash charge and acquisition-related costs
positive_highlights: Revenue up 59% YoY to $11.8 million, ahead of internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 50% YoY
Reiterated full-year revenue guidance and on track for AVCAD production
summary: 908 Devices reported Q1 2025 revenue of $11.8 million from continuing operations, up 59% year-over-year driven by handheld device sales. Adjusted gross margin improved 75 basis points to 54% despite a higher mix of international distributor sales. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $4.6 million from $5.3 million a year ago. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance, expects positive adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2025 and cash flow positivity in 2026, with the company citing strong demand in handheld markets and progress on the AVCAD program.

negative_highlights: Total expenses increased by $21 million YoY, including $15.5 million in acquisition-related costs and transactional fees.
Everspan gross premiums written declined 10% to approximately $87 million due to the non-renewal of a personal alliance reinsurance program.
Organic growth excluding acquisitions contracted by 2%, primarily driven by pullbacks in ESL and note weakness in-term medical business.
positive_highlights: Insurance Distribution and Specialty Program premium grew 70% YoY to $318 million, driven largely by the Beat acquisition contributing over $20 million in revenue.
Cirrata segment produced adjusted EBITDA of $12 million on a 29.5% margin compared to $5 million at a 28.7% margin last year.
Everspan loss ratio improved nearly 9 percentage points (to 66.9%) following the de-emphasis of assumed programs.
summary: Ambac reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $63 million (up 27% YoY) and a net loss from continuing operations of $16 million ($0.58/share), driven by the Beat acquisition offsetting headwinds in ESL/medical lines and higher expenses at Everspan. Management provided no specific numerical guidance for future quarters, instead setting long-term targets to generate $80-90 million adjusted EBITDA by 2028 while awaiting regulatory approval for a legacy business sale.

negative_highlights: Cash burn remained at approximately $4 million during the quarter despite lower OpEx compared to prior year.
Only ~50% of AYA patients currently complete full adherence, indicating room for improvement in patient support programs.
G&A expenses increased quarter-over-quarter due to noncash stock compensation.
positive_highlights: Net product sales grew 18% year-over-year to $8.8 million, marking the second consecutive quarter of growth.
PEDMARK launched commercially in Germany and UK with Norgine; Scottish Medicine Consortium accepted PEDMARQSI for use in Scotland.
Adherence numbers improved as Fennec HEARS program was redesigned for home administration settings.
summary: Fennec reported Q1 FY2025 net product sales of $8.8 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase and a second consecutive quarter of growth compared to $7.4 million in the prior period. The company noted that cash operating expenses were approximately $33 million for the full year, with Q1 specifically seeing lower watching and marketing spend due to the elimination of European pre-commercialization activities from 2024. Management expressed confidence in continued momentum entering H2 2025 as new commercial initiatives mature.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue declined 4% YoY primarily due to FX headwinds and lower interest revenue; excluding these factors, underlying EBITDA would have been down roughly flat or slightly negative.
Attrition in the SMB segment was higher than expected (reducing revenue by ~12%), partially offsetting growth from new customers which contributed only 2% to total revenue.
Gross margin declined 190 basis points YoY due to a shift toward lower-margin ISO channel sales and reduced interest income, with Merchant Solutions margins compressing significantly.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 5%, slightly better than expected, driven by double-digit growth in e-commerce (verticals like North America iGaming) and a ramping enterprise sales organization that signed over 100 new contracts.

Processing volume for Merchant Solutions increased 11% to $34.3 billion while Digital Wallet volumes rose 5%, indicating strong underlying demand despite reported revenue headwinds from FX and interest rates.
Adjusted EBITDA of $95 million was slightly ahead of expectations due to timing of cost items falling into Q2, resulting in a margin that beat the prior period's normalized run rate.
summary: Paysafe reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $401 million (a 4% decline vs prior year) and Adjusted EBITDA of $95 million ($95M), which management noted was slightly ahead of expectations when excluding inorganic impacts from the divestiture. Management reiterated full-year guidance, citing Q1 results as 'slightly ahead' but acknowledging that underlying organic growth (excluding FX/interest/divestiture) would have been flat to down 3% without those one-offs. The company highlighted strong e-commerce and iGaming volume growth tempered by higher attrition in SMB.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA decreased by approximately $2.4 million compared to the prior quarter due to higher lease operating expenses and G&A costs
C48 well production underperformed initial expectations at ~100 barrels of oil per day, requiring a pivot from D-Sand to C-Sand completion
Capital program reduced with three Beta projects deferred resulting in capital savings of approximately $50 million
positive_highlights: C54 well completed with outstanding early results showing an IP20 of approximately 800 barrels of oil per day over first 20 days
Beta field production increased by approximately 35% since early 2024 after offsetting asset base decline
Completed three Haynesville acreage transactions generating $9.2 million in total net proceeds while retaining a 10% working interest
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $19.4 million and production of 17,900 BOE/day, a slight decrease from the prior quarter due to gas imbalance adjustments in East Texas and adverse weather. Management lowered its annual production guidance range for 2025 to 19,000-20,500 BOE/day following a comprehensive review of uncommitted capital budget triggered by material reductions in oil prices. Consequently, the company elected to temporarily defer three development projects at Beta and is exploring additional cost savings opportunities.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue guidance unchanged at $50-60 million, despite record quarter
Revenue expected to be back-end loaded with margin fluctuations; tariffs impact limited but uncertain
No explicit product shipment record confirmed; first Fabrinet units only expected in about a month
positive_highlights: Q1 revenues of $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x YoY, a record
Gross margin of ~40%, also a record versus 8.9% prior quarter
NRE payment plan expanded to ~$95 million; cash at $85.4 million
summary: Q1 2025 revenues were a record $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x year-over-year, with record gross margin of ~40%, driven by NRE payments and LiDAR sales. The company expanded its NRE payment plan from ~$80 million to ~$95 million, ended Q1 with $85.4 million in cash, and maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million (more than twofold YoY growth). Management highlighted a new manufacturing partnership with Fabrinet, accelerated LiDAR shipments to Volkswagen for robotaxi deployments, and expanding collaboration with NVIDIA. They expect first Fabrinet product unit shipments within a month and continue to target 1-3 new programs in 2025.

negative_highlights: Israel Innovation Authority grant declined to $25,000 from $209,000 year-over-year
Gross margin may vary with mix; expected range 72%-76%
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year
Raising full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance to 15%-18%
Highest-ever non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million and $4.4 million positive cash flow
summary: RADCOM reported record Q1 2025 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million (19% of revenue) and cash flow of $4.4 million, ending the quarter with $99.1 million in cash and no debt. The company raised its full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance from 12%-15% to 15%-18% year-over-year, citing strong momentum and strategic partnerships with ServiceNow and Nvidia. Management highlighted expanding agentic AI capabilities and a renewed tier-one North American contract.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5 million from $1.8 million
Tissue Health Plus segment adjusted EBITDA loss deepened to $2.0 million
SG&A expenses increased 32% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 26% year-over-year to $23.4 million
Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up $1.5 million to $2.7 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $23.4 million, up 26% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair products up 28% and bone fusion up 18%. Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%, and Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.7 million from $1.2 million. The company reaffirmed its growth expectations, narrowed THP cash investment guidance, and remains on track to launch the THP pilot in Q2. Net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expense.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased moderately due to a reporting change including fuel gross at Camarillo and startup costs, obscuring underlying operational efficiency.
Management explicitly identified new competition as its 'biggest concern today' in response to analyst questions about replicators of the model.
positive_highlights: Revenues surged 133% year-over-year driven by full quarter operations at the newly acquired Camarillo campus and ramp-up in Phoenix, Dallas, and Denver.
Management reaffirmed prior guidance to achieve consolidated cash flow breakeven before year-end as leasing accelerates on new campuses over summer/fall.
Nashville occupancy remains strong at 92% (above 100% utilized space), demonstrating demand for the home basing model.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenues increased significantly by 133% YoY and 20% sequentially primarily due to the incorporation of operations from the Camarillo campus acquisition in December 2024. Operating expenses rose moderately, driven largely by a reporting change that now includes fuel gross at Camarillo rather than net, alongside startup costs for new headcount at Phoenix, Dallas, Denver, and APA locations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach consolidated cash flow breakeven by the end of FY25 as leasing ramps up on three new campuses.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply to $7.5M from $17.1M YoY, partly due to a one-time 2024 Roche license
Net loss widened to $20.7M from $11.5M in Q1 2024
A $2.5M pharma biocatalysis order slipped into April, missing the top of Q1 guidance
positive_highlights: Product gross margin expanded to 55% from 49% YoY
First ligase order delivered to a large pharma customer in Q1, with additional orders expected
Three CDMOs validated ligase performance in-house, supporting scalability
summary: Codexis reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.5 million, down from $17.1 million in Q1 2024, with product gross margin up to 55% from 49%. Net loss widened to $20.7 million from $11.5 million, and cash stood at $59.8 million. The company reiterated its 2025 revenue guidance of $64–68 million, noting revenue timing was affected by a $2.5 million payment shifting to April. Management highlighted early commercial progress in its ECO platform, including first orders for its ligase products and upcoming presentations at TIDES USA.

negative_highlights: Cash only $8 million, sufficient into Q3; need $15 million more
EMA approval contingent on additional GLP studies that may impact EU timeline
Phase 2 MB-106 first patient relapsed after over 600 days of complete remission
positive_highlights: First patient treated in Phase 3 MIRACLE trial with 38 sites selected
EMA approved trial in all nine EU countries
FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients
summary: Moleculin Biotech reported Q1 2025 progress with its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin (naxtarubicin) in relapsed/refractory AML, including first patient treated, 38 sites selected, EMA approval for nine EU countries, and WHO recognition of the generic name. The company has roughly $8 million cash, enough into Q3, and needs about $15 million to reach Q1 2026 funding. FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients. Final data from the MB-107 soft tissue sarcoma trial is expected soon. The company remains confident in achieving the 45-patient interim readout by end of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margins were softer than a year ago due to revenue mix changes, specifically the inclusion of $1 million in NYC COVID-related spoilage revenue which had no margin.
Card issuing revenues were slightly down compared to the prior year quarter primarily because the New York City COVID program provided over $1 million in revenue that is not recurring.
positive_highlights: Record numbers in first quarter revenues driven by significant increases in processing volume across all segments.
Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially, rising from $500,000 in Q4 2024 to $700,000 in Q1 FY2025.
PayFac business continues strong growth trajectory with revenues up 25% and now accounting for approximately 59% of total card revenues.
summary: Usio reported record Q1 FY2025 revenues with a 5% increase year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA rising to $700,000 from the prior quarter's $500,000. Processing volume surged significantly across segments: total processing up 34%, ACH volumes up 36%, card transactions up 65%, and PayFac revenues up 25%. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of 14% to 16% growth.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it does not currently provide financial guidance for future quarters.
Cash balance declined to $40 million from $41.7 million at year-end despite recent capital raise.
No specific revenue figures were reported as the company is pre-revenue in its clinical stage.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased to $8.5 million from $10.6 million in Q1 FY2024 due to lower operating expenses of $9.1 million versus $10.1 million previously.
Successfully initiated the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 registrational trial with FDA approval and added Mayo Clinic sites, targeting approximately 350 patients.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $8.5 million ($0.21 per share) for Q1 FY2025, representing an improvement from the prior year quarter due to lower operating expenses and increased tax benefits. The company raised approximately $11 million in new capital earlier this month but did not provide financial guidance or raise its operational outlook. Management highlighted the initiation of the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 trial for Versamune HPV plus pembrolizumab, noting that enrollment is ongoing and specific timelines are pending.

negative_highlights: Israeli revenue declined 56% YoY, partly due to supply delays and the Oranim deal cancellation.
Cash balance remains low at $1.4 million, with reliance on credit facilities and future financing.
Revenue growth was modest at 4% YoY, as German gains were mostly offset by Israeli declines.
positive_highlights: Achieved net profit of $0.2 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million, a ~$3M improvement YoY.
German revenue grew 569% YoY, now 62% of total revenue; 12 new strains launched in Q1 alone.
Gross profit up 94% YoY, aided by a 56% reduction in operating expenses.
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q1 2025 revenues of $12.5 million, up 4% YoY, with a net profit of $0.2 million versus a $6.0 million loss a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6 million, improving from a $2.2 million loss in Q1 2024. German revenue surged 569% YoY to offset a 56% decline in Israel, while gross margin improved 87 percentage points. Operating expenses fell 56% YoY, driving the profitability turnaround.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to shipment deferrals in the Aero and Architecture divisions caused by customer hesitation regarding tariff impacts.
Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated quarter-over-quarter from negative $4.8 million to negative $5.5 million, widening the loss despite margin expansion.
Management explicitly stated that 2025 will not be a positive free cash flow year; FCF is expected to turn positive only in 2026.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6% driven by operational efficiencies in Safety Tech (margin up from 12.8%) and Architecture segments.
Total purchase order backlog increased significantly to $36 million, indicating strong underlying demand despite timing delays.
Secured first tranche of a new debt facility with Mizrahi Bank at favorable terms ($370 bps interest rate reduction), enhancing liquidity.
summary: Gauzy reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $22.4 million (down from $24.7M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $5.5 million (worse than the prior quarter's -$4.8M). Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6%, driven by Safety Tech, while Aero revenue grew but margins contracted due to shipment timing shifts related to tariff uncertainty in March/April. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance of $130-$140 million revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: China tariffs expected to impact gross margin by approximately $1 million in the back two quarters
Physical Playboy Club development is projected as a one-to-two-year project, not immediate revenue
Licensing business excluding Byborg still grew but at a slower pace of over 50% YoY
positive_highlights: Licensing business revenue surged 175% year-over-year
Honey Birdette is ahead of plan for Q2 with an easy comparable base
Byborg deal includes a $20 million annual minimum guarantee plus additional payments
summary: PLBY Group reported Q1 FY2025 results where the licensing business grew significantly by 175% year-over-year to positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 million (excluding one-time personnel costs). Management highlighted strong performance in Honey Birdette with an easy comparable base and noted that Byborg contributed a significant portion of growth, though excluding it still showed over 50% YoY improvement. The company expects continued benefits from new deals in gaming and hospitality starting in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $22 million was driven by a single underperforming contract with prior year claim impacts.
Total revenue declined 4% YoY due to the intentional reduction in membership base from exiting unprofitable plans.
One specific payer partner remains an outlier requiring collaborative resolution for performance issues.
positive_highlights: Three of four markets achieved breakeven or better performance, with the outlier being a single payer partner.
PMPM funding increased by 8% to $1,063 due to improved disease burden capture and favorable contract terms.
Utilization metrics trended positively including a 21% decrease in ED visits per 1,000 and an 11% drop in high-cost claims >$20k.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $373 million (4% YoY decrease) and membership fell 8%, both in line with expectations but reflecting an intentional strategy to exit unprofitable plans. Adjusted EBITDA reported a loss of $22 million, driven by a single outlier payer partner responsible for roughly one-quarter of the business that is being actively remediated; excluding this specific impact, the rest of the business operates at or near breakeven. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance despite these headwinds and noted positive trends in utilization metrics (e.g., ED visits down 21%) and PMPM funding (+8%).

negative_highlights: NII per share down $0.10 QoQ to $0.45
Non-accruals increased to 3.5% of debt at cost
Tariff uncertainty tempering near-term M&A activity
positive_highlights: New investments at 565 bps spread, above recent quarters
Portfolio weighted average interest coverage improved to 2.0x
97% floating-rate assets vs. 55% floating-rate liabilities
summary: Q1 FY2025 NII was $0.45 per share, down from $0.55 in Q4, driven by lower base rates, non-recurring income runoff, reduced Logan JV dividend, and higher non-accruals. Non-accruals rose to 3.5% of debt at cost (1.8% at fair value) with four new first-lien names. Management called this quarter 'reflective of our earnings baseline,' cited tariff-driven M&A slowdown, and noted potential tailwinds from SPV facility repricing and full-quarter portfolio impact. GAAP EPS was $0.11, NAV per share $19.62.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $2.2 million missed the outlook, primarily driven by front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid growth in Q4 and early Q1.
Loss from operations widened to a loss of $500,000 compared to income of $3.8 million in the prior year quarter.
Wayfair gross originations declined significantly (approximate volume of $17M) due to category challenges within home furnishings and mattresses.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 15.4% YoY to $64.2 million, beating the outlook for 11% growth.
Revenue of $71.9M came in slightly above expectations at a 10.6% increase year-over-year.
KPay originations surged 57% and now represent approximately 35% of total gross originations.
summary: Katapult reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $71.9 million (up 10.6% YoY) and gross originations growth of 15.4%, both slightly beating guidance; however, adjusted EBITDA was $2.2 million, missing the outlook due to front-loaded lease depreciation from strong Q4/Q1 origination volume. Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance for at least 20% gross originations growth and revenue growth of at least 20%, while projecting breakeven adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

negative_highlights: Cash position remains low at $2.6M end of quarter
Revenue guidance not provided; described as lumpy
Dependence on future financing and cost control; macro environment described as difficult
positive_highlights: Revenue up 44% year-over-year to ~$0.25M, including first human product sales
Operating expenses down 35% and cash used in operations down 48% year-over-year
Licensing discussions with over 10 companies, seven with combined market value over $600B
summary: VolitionRX reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of almost $0.25 million, up 44% year-over-year, including first-ever human product sales. Operating expenses fell 35% and cash used in operations dropped 48% to $4.3 million. Management reiterated full-year cash flow neutrality goal, emphasized confidential licensing discussions with over 10 companies, and noted a new $6.25 million convertible loan after quarter-end. Revenue remains lumpy; no FY2025 guidance provided.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year.
Net loss widened to $737K in Q1 '25 vs. $573K prior year.
Year-over-year comparisons hurt by $1.2M prior-year contract and EMEA transition.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 10% sequentially to $1.6 million in Q1 '25.
Gross margin healthy at 82.6%; SG&A reduced 23% year-over-year.
Cash increased to over $3 million, and debt more than halved to ~$762K.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue fell to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year due to a large financial services customer's contract timing, though revenue rose 10% sequentially. The customer upgraded to a one-to-many biometric solution, contributing $690K in Q1 and expected to generate ~$3M over two years starting Q1 2026. Gross margin dipped to 82.6%, and net loss widened to $737K due to higher share count, while cash rose to $3.1M from warrant proceeds. The company is shifting to BIO-key branded products in EMEA and highlights expanding recurring revenue over $6M.

negative_highlights: Q1 2026 global cannabis revenue expected to be slightly lower sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA projected to be sequentially below Q4 due to lower high-margin international revenue
Poland experienced regulatory headwinds impacting prescription volumes
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue up 34% YoY with record global medical cannabis and plant propagation revenue

summary: Aurora Cannabis reported record fiscal 2025 results: net revenue up 27% to $343 million, global medical cannabis revenue up 39% to $244.4 million, adjusted EBITDA of $49.7 million, and positive free cash flow of $9.9 million. Q4 net revenue rose 34% to $90.5 million, with record adjusted gross profit of $54.2 million and adjusted EBITDA up 619% to $16.7 million, while cash at $185.3 million and no cannabis debt. Management guided Q1 2026 global cannabis to be slightly lower sequentially due to temporary international declines (notably Poland), but expects improvement in later quarters.

Fulfillment reliability improved to nearly 100% for franchisee demand during the holiday season following the in-house packaging transition.
The company expects profitable contribution from e-commerce in fiscal '26 after resolving fulfillment inefficiencies.
summary: RMCF reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $8.9 million (up from $7.3M YoY) but a net loss of $2.9 million ($-0.37/share), widening the deficit compared to last year's $1.6M loss due to higher raw material costs and brand refresh expenses. FY2026 guidance is for 5% revenue growth to ~$84M, with flat to slightly lower EV charging revenue, and management expects to approach or achieve positive adjusted EBITDA for the year.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was essentially flat, masking a decline in product sales of approximately $0.6 million driven by the loss of a large specialty market customer.
Franchise and royalty fees were up only modestly ($1.7M vs $1.1M) despite higher same-store sales at existing locations.

Costs and expenses decreased to $6.5 million from $8 million last year due to lower G&A costs.
summary: Total revenue was $6.4 million for Q1 FY2026, essentially flat year-over-year due to the loss of a large specialty market customer that reduced sales by nearly $500,000. Despite this volume decline and dropping product sales from $5.3M to $4.7M, the company achieved positive EBITDA of $2 million compared to negative $1.4M last year due to pricing adjustments and lower G&A costs. Management expressed cautious optimism about a business transformation entering an execution phase but noted they are not currently planning to raise capital.

negative_highlights: Q3 throughput was limited to just under 1,500 tonnes per day due to scheduled maintenance and downtime before the plant reached full capacity.
The company still operates with a negative working capital ratio at quarter end, requiring focus on rightsizing payables in Q4.
Joint venture agreement remains less favorable than peers (55-45 split), which management cites as an ongoing factor impacting share price appreciation.
positive_highlights: Production increased substantially quarter-over-quarter as operations accessed higher-grade ore blocks, producing just under 4,700 ounces in Q3 versus lower prior periods.
Processing cost per tonne improved to below $15 due to economies of scale from the expanded plant capacity and optimized fleet usage.
Agreement with Bank of Tanzania secured a reduced royalty rate of approximately 4% on domestic sales compared to 7.3% for exports, providing immediate cash flow benefits.
summary: TRX Gold reported Q3 FY2025 results with revenue of $12.5 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $4 million, driven by production of just under 4,700 ounces at an average gold price over $3,100/oz. Management highlighted a strong quarter-on-quarter improvement in financial metrics as the company transitioned from low-grade oxide material to higher-grade sulfide ore following the completion of Stage 1 stripping. The CEO reiterated that the business is self-funding growth and focused on normalizing working capital ratios while executing plant optimizations.

negative_highlights: Active customer count declined due to acquisition slowdown before comp plan changes
Q3 operating margin expected to be pressured by convention and rollout investments
China growth partly driven by tariff-related note-ups, not sustainable demand
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 11% year-over-year

summary: USANA reported Q2 FY2025 net sales up 11% year-over-year and adjusted EPS up 36%, ending the quarter debt-free with $151 million cash. The company repaid its line of credit used for the Hiya acquisition. Despite a drop in active customers partly due to compensation plan changes, management expressed optimism about growth initiatives, including new partnerships and product launches, and reaffirmed fiscal 2025 guidance while noting Q3 margin pressure from planned investments.

summary: JAKKS Pacific reported Q2 2025 sales down 20% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.3 million versus $12.3 million last year, and adjusted EPS of $0.03 versus $0.65. The quarter was hit by tariff-driven order cancellations and delayed retail resets, but first-half sales were down only 3% overall, with international sales up 33% and Europe up 65%. Management is cautious about the second half, citing ongoing tariff uncertainty and later shelf resets, but highlighted strong gross margins of 32.8%, a new credit facility, and continued dividend.

summary: BeFra reported Q2 2025 consolidated revenue growth of 5.1% YoY and EBITDA up 3.5% YoY to MXN 679 million, with margin at 19.1%, rebounding from a weak Q1. Betterware Mexico returned to sequential growth (+4% QoQ) and achieved its first net associate growth since Q1 2021, while Jafra Mexico grew revenue 10.9% YoY with EBITDA margin at 21.2%. Guidance for 2025 is maintained at 6-9% revenue and EBITDA growth, implying acceleration in H2. Management highlighted pricing, product, and incentive initiatives as key drivers, despite a still challenging macro environment.

summary: Primis Financial reported Q2 2025 net income of $8.4 million or $0.34 per share, including a $7.5 million pretax gain from PFH, offset by new mortgage team support and consumer program reversals. Core pretax pre-provision earnings were about $8.4 million, with core net interest margin expanding to 3.15% and noninterest-bearing deposits up 19% annualized. Management expects run-rate PPNR to grow to over $13 million heading into 2026, aided by tech savings of $1.5 million per quarter starting in Q3 and continued margin expansion to mid-3.20% by year-end.

Membership fees grew to $3 million and are expected to reach about 25% of revenue next year. Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in coming quarters as membership fees are recognized ratably, with profitability to increase over time. Despite near-term EPS pressure, they will continue aggressive member acquisition as long as payback remains favorable.

summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $105.6 million, up 7.5% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.55 versus $0.17 last year, more than tripling. Gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 41.0%, driven by higher wholesale margins and a favorable retail mix. The company raised its full-year 2025 guidance: revenue growth now 4-5% (up from low single digits) and EPS up ~10% to $2.79 (vs prior down slightly), despite expecting ~$11 million of tariff headwinds. Management cited strong execution across XTRATUF, Muck, and other brands, and is ahead of schedule shifting production to lower-tariff facilities like the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico.

The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $100-105 million and expects Q3 revenue of $29-31 million and adjusted EBITDA of $2-4 million. While U.S. revenue was only 17% of total, with Europe leading growth, management expressed confidence in sustaining growth and gaining share despite market challenges.

The company raised its full-year 2025 EPS guidance to $0.97–$1.05 and EBITDA to $49–$52 million, citing defense and aerospace momentum, while noting softness in autos and clean energy.

Guidance for retail in North America is expected to turn positive in the second half, supported by easier comps. Management also confirmed a new small-displacement motorcycle entry price below $6,000 launching in H1 2026.

They noted cautious optimism in the market, no significant client pullback due to tariffs, and highlighted growth in data-driven marketing solutions and In-store Connect. Asset sales and acquisitions (Sacramento plant sale, Enru purchase) were completed in the quarter.

summary: Q2 2025 revenue was $23.9 million, up 15% YoY and 13% on a constant currency basis, with international revenue a record $9.1 million, up 32% YoY. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance from $96-98 million to $90-92 million, attributing the shortfall to timing rather than strategic changes and citing record StratX referrals in June/July as early signs of improvement.

The company signed a mandate for a $200M prepayment facility and expects closing in Q3 2025, while maintaining 2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d. Management highlighted strong results from Cohembi, Costayaco, and Simonette, and expressed confidence in ramping production in H2.

The rebrand is described as an intermediate step with potential disruption during the transition period before full efficacy is realized.

ARR reached nearly $355 million with a 9% increase in average revenue per enterprise account.
summary: Commerce reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $84.4 million (up 3% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $4.8 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company executed a corporate rebrand to 'Commerce' and announced new partnerships with Perplexity, Google Cloud, PROS, and Accenture focused on AI-driven commerce capabilities. While Q2 results were solid, management noted that material revenue benefits from these strategic shifts are expected in early 2026 rather than the current year.

summary: Genesis Energy reported Q2 2025 results in line with expectations but guided to the low end of prior adjusted EBITDA guidance due to delayed producer well remediation and slightly delayed first oil from Shenandoah and Salamanca. Shenandoah achieved first oil last week with initial wells expected to exceed predrill expectations and ramp to 100,000 barrels per day by end of September; Salamanca remains on track for first oil by end of Q3. Management reaffirmed 2026 outlook and expects free cash flow generation to begin in Q3, with focus on deleveraging and potential capital returns to unitholders.

summary: OneWater Marine reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $553 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.79, missing the prior year's $1.05 despite outperforming an industry that declined over 15%. Gross profit fell to $129 million due to lower new boat volumes and promotional pressure, while SG&A expenses rose 6% to $92 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of $1.8 billion-$1.85 billion but lowered adjusted EBITDA ($65M-$80M) and EPS ($0.50-$0.75) outlooks citing macro uncertainty, tariff impacts on consumer confidence, and margin pressure.

negative_highlights: Book value declined 2.4% from the prior quarter due to broad market weakness following Liberation Day volatility in April.

Arc Home contributed a loss of approximately $0.13 per share ($130,000) for the quarter due to pipeline losses from April volatility.

Acquired an additional 21.4% stake in Arc Home (total ownership now 66%) with minimal dilution expected to be earnings accretive starting in 2026.
Completed two securitizations and closed two new residential mortgage warehouse facilities designed to reduce mark-to-market risk.
summary: MITT reported a GAAP net loss of $1.4 million ($0.05 per share) and an economic return on equity that was essentially flat at negative 0.5% for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. Book value declined modestly by 2.4% to $10.39 per share due to mark-to-market losses from April volatility and commercial loan maturities placed on nonaccrual, though these were partially offset by gains on securitizations and a post-quarter refinancing that reduced debt costs by over 50 bps. The company increased its quarterly dividend by 5% to $0.21 per share.

Management revised its full-year outlook downward, now expecting EBITDA neutrality for the second half of 2025 rather than profitability.

Management noted strong demand for new fishing innovations and Jetboil products, but cautioned on fourth-quarter tariff costs and a still-weak watercraft market. Management reiterated full-year FY2025 guidance for revenue between $160M-$170M and adjusted EBITDA between $16M-$18M without raising or lowering expectations.

summary: CVRx reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $13.6 million (up 15% YoY) and a net loss of $14.7 million ($0.57/share), beating the prior year's EPS but missing on top-line growth relative to recent trends due to sales force ramp-up costs. Management narrowed full-year guidance, expecting total revenue between $55M-$57M (down from previous expectations) and operating expenses of $96M-$98M, citing slower productivity gains for new hires than anticipated. The company raised its full-year 2025 outlook, now expecting revenue growth of 13-14%, net income of $112-120 million (up 43-53%), and adjusted EBITDA of $162-172 million (up 30-38%). Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 annualized adjusted ROE guidance range of 16% to 18%, maintaining it despite a quarter that missed expectations relative to last year's performance.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 53% year-over-year from $12.4 million to $19 million

Content licensing revenue surged by over $8 million YoY driven by AI training demand
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $19 million (up 53% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $3.1 million from a loss of $1 million last year. Management raised full-year 2025 adjusted free cash flow expectations to an implied range consistent with Q3/Q4 performance, citing strong growth in AI data licensing and new international distribution deals. The company maintained its no-debt balance sheet with $30.7M liquidity.

NobelClad backlog fell to $37 million from $41 million due to tariff-driven lost business
Third-quarter guidance implies sales down $5-13 million sequentially and EBITDA down $1.5-5.5 million

DynaEnergetics adjusted EBITDA margin rose 210 bps sequentially and 190 bps YoY to 13.4%

Arcadia sales declined 11% YoY, DynaEnergetics declined 12%, while NobelClad grew 6% but saw backlog fall to $37 million from $41 million. The company cut total debt by 17% to $59 million. Third-quarter guidance is soft at $142-150 million sales and $8-12 million EBITDA due to tariff uncertainty, high interest rates, and weak energy activity.

Subscriber growth may be flat to declining in Q3 due to natural attrition, and Q2 benefited from pull-forward of accessories demand
positive_highlights: Operating income grew 14% and EPS grew 22% YoY
Total gross margin expanded to 59% from 53.5%, with Products gross margin up to 32.4% from 23.3%
Paid subscribers grew 7% YoY to over 3 million, with new user engagement (cuts in first 30 days) improving
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 2% to $172.1M, with operating income up 14% and EPS up 22%. Platform revenue grew 4% to $80.7M, and Products grew 1% to $91.4M, with connected machines down 10% but accessories and materials up 12% due to tariff-driven pull-forward of shipments. Paid subscribers reached 3+ million, up 7% YoY, while ARPU rose 2% to $53.84. Gross margin expanded significantly, particularly in Products, up to 32.4% from 23.3%. Management cited moderation in engagement erosion but remains cautious on tariff impacts and subscriber seasonality, guiding to potential flat/declining subscriber count in Q3.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 49% from 54% due to amortization and warranty costs
Adjusted gross margin down 220 basis points to 56% driven by higher warranty costs
Operating expenses increased to $21.5 million from $14.7 million due to noncash charges
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% YoY to $13 million, above internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 45% YoY and 15% QoQ
Record XplorIR units shipped in Q2, with 164 devices placed
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 2025 revenue of $13 million, up 14% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA loss improving 45% year-over-year and 15% sequentially. The company highlighted record XplorIR placements and strong legislative tailwinds, while maintaining its goal of adjusted EBITDA positive by Q4 2025. They launched VipIR, acquired KAF Manufacturing, and completed facility consolidations to reduce costs.

negative_highlights: Infrastructure gross margin compressed year-over-year by approximately 230 basis points to 17.9% due to project timing shifts and inflationary pressure.

Spectrum segment faced headwinds from network cancellations and ad sales softness despite new launches.

Life Sciences revenue surged 88.2% to $3.2 million driven by R2 growth outside North America and consumable sales.
Company successfully completed early settlement of indebtedness refinancing transactions extending debt maturities.
summary: INNOVATE reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated revenues of $242 million, a decrease of 22.7% year-over-year compared to $313.1 million in the prior period. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $22 million ($1.67 per share), down from net income of $14.1 million ($1.03 per share) last year, driven primarily by a 23.6% revenue decline and margin compression at the Infrastructure segment. Management highlighted successful debt refinancing extending maturities but noted that first-half results were impacted by project timing issues in infrastructure and network cancellations in spectrum.

negative_highlights: Second quarter total revenue missed guidance range ($51.8M vs $56M-$61M) driven by softness in May and June across key verticals
National advertising revenue per attendee declined to $0.36 from $0.45 year-over-year despite a 24% increase in attendance
Local and regional advertising revenue fell significantly, down approximately 35% year-over-year due to cautious advertiser sentiment
positive_highlights: Third quarter revenue guidance raised to a range of $62 million to $67 million based on strong early Q3 pacing ahead of last year's levels
Programmatic advertiser volume grew by more than 50% quarter-over-quarter with approximately 70% of advertisers being new to NCM
Self-serve platform revenue increased more than 30% year-over-year signaling strong adoption

Management raised third quarter revenue guidance to a range of $62-67M (up from prior expectations) citing strong early Q3 pacing ahead of last year's levels despite tough box office comparisons. The company reinstated its dividend at $0.03 per share and continued share repurchases, while highlighting growth in programmatic volume (+50% qoq) and self-serve revenue.

negative_highlights: Dividend reduced from $0.21 to $0.15 per share due to FAD coverage dropping to 79%.
Occupancy fell primarily due to the expiration of a lease at Aurora, Illinois and rejection of a master lease at East Orange, New Jersey.
positive_highlights: Successfully retenanted the Beaumont, Texas facility with CHRISTUS Health as of May, ending negative cash flows after nearly two years.
summary: Global Medical REIT reported Q2 FY2025 results with a significant dividend cut from $0.21 to $0.15 per share due to declining cash flow coverage dropping from 110% in Q1 to 79% in Q2. Occupancy declined to 94.5% driven by the expiration of an Aurora, Illinois lease and the rejection of a master lease at East Orange, New Jersey following Prospect Medical's bankruptcy. Management raised full-year CapEx guidance expectations due to leasing activity but emphasized strategic priorities including refinancing debt maturities in late 2025 and potential asset recycling.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue fell to $7.9 million from $11.5 million due to strategic shift
Plant propagation adjusted gross margin dropped to 6% from 18% due to nonrecurring quality issue
Q2 free cash flow expected to be impacted by significant cash outflows
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 209% to $10.8 million from $3.5 million

summary: Aurora Cannabis reported strong Q1 FY2026 results with net revenue up 17% to $98 million, global medical cannabis revenue up 37%, and international revenue up 85%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 1,000 basis points to 52%, and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $10.8 million. The company achieved positive free cash flow of $9.2 million and ended with $186 million in cash, with no cannabis debt. Management raised no explicit full-year guidance but issued Q2 guidance for 8-12% global medical cannabis growth and continued positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: CHMP referral raises questions on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox
International orders expected to remain lumpy
US government RFP timing uncertain, with negotiation expected to take months
positive_highlights: Product revenues of $79M in Q2, fulfilling $70M of outstanding orders

Pretax operating income of $46M and net income of $35M, with no debt
summary: Q2 2025 product revenue was $79 million (oral TPOXX $53M, IV TPOXX $26M), fulfilling $70M of prior-year orders, with $26M in remaining IV TPOXX orders targeted for 2026 delivery. Pretax operating income was $46 million for the quarter, net income $35 million, and fully diluted EPS $0.49. The U.S. government committed $27 million in incremental development funding under the BARDA 19C contract ($14M manufacturing, $13M pediatric). The CHMP initiated a referral on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox, while management remains confident in the smallpox indication.

negative_highlights: Revenue essentially flat at $19.6 million vs $19.9 million
EV charging revenue fell to $2.7 million from $3.8 million, citing project timing
EV financing uncertainty and tariff concerns noted
positive_highlights: Gross margin reached 30.1%, highest in about six years
Third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
New $6.5 million Boston Public Schools EV charging expansion win
summary: Orion reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $19.6 million, roughly flat year-over-year, with LED lighting up 1% and maintenance up 21%, offset by a decline in EV charging due to project timing. Gross margin expanded 850 basis points to 30.1%, and net loss narrowed to $1.2 million from $3.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA positive for the third consecutive quarter. CEO stated confidence in achieving FY2026 revenue of about $84 million and positive adjusted EBITDA. Guidance was reiterated, not raised.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 19% year-over-year, with volumes down across all product lines
Q2 bookings fell to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, driven by tariff-related demand deferrals
Q2 adjusted operating profit down to $5 million, with tariff-driven costs of $10 million

Bookings declined to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, and backlog fell from $1.9 billion to $1.7 billion. The company maintained its full-year guidance but emphasized heightened economic uncertainty, tariff volatility, and a cyclical demand trough, while planning to increase production in H2 to meet an expected demand uptick.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.9 million ($0.03 per share) caused by hedge maturity and reduced NIM.
NAV declined approximately $6.2 million (or 2.7%) relative to March 31, ending the quarter at a lower book value.
positive_highlights: Earnings available for distribution (EAD) remained positive at $0.10 per share despite GAAP losses, supporting dividend sustainability.
Servicing costs came in lower than estimates due to deboarding fees from the prior quarter and a drop in loan count following the Mr. Cooper acquisition integration.
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $0.9 million ($0.03 per share) for Q2 FY2025, driven by the maturation of a large hedge and lower dollar roll income, resulting in an NAV decline of approximately 2.7%. Book value per common share decreased to $3.34 from $3.58 at quarter-end. Management maintained leverage around 5.3x while raising $9 million via ATM programs.

Management reiterated full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $20-25M and operating expenses of $85-90M, noting that xPloration contributions are currently small but additive.

negative_highlights: Total company revenues were down slightly due to a specific loss of approximately $2 million in card issuing revenue from one large account losing a downstream customer.

Card issuing and Output Solutions revenues were impacted by specific headwinds: loss of an amusement park client in card issuing and soft ad hoc work/transition pricing in output.

ACH revenues grew over 30% for the second consecutive quarter with total payment dollars up 19%. Card processing volume increased 69% in transactions and PayFac revenue rose 17%.
Adjusted EBITDA remained positive at just over $500,000 despite lower top-line revenues.

Management adjusted full-year revenue guidance down to a range of 5%-12% growth citing prolonged implementation delays at two large national accounts.

negative_highlights: Policy acquisition costs increased $10.3 million (74.8% year-over-year)

Risk appetite for adding new exposures is limited during the third quarter

Combined ratio of 60.6%, significantly below the stated target of 65%
summary: American Coastal Insurance Corporation reported Q2 FY2025 results with revenue growing 26% year-over-year and pretax earnings increasing 51%. Net income was $26.4 million while core return on equity reached approximately 42%, driven by a step-down in quota share ceding that increased net premiums earned despite higher acquisition costs. The company achieved a combined ratio of 60.6% against its target and received an upgrade to BBB- with a Positive outlook from Kroll Bond Rating Agency.

Management maintained its full-year 4-wall margin guidance range of 17% to 18%, citing operational efficiencies like AI tools and automation expected to improve results starting in Q3, despite a sharp downturn in April through June that recovered slightly in July.

SeQure Dx integration is on track to meet annual revenue expectations of approximately $2 million.

Management lowered its full-year 2025 guidance for core business revenue from an expected 8-15% growth range ($35M-$37M) to flat-to-down 10% ($29.5M-$32.5M), citing headwinds including a large customer's manufacturing reorganization and capital equipment purchasing hesitancy.

Gross originations fell to $48 million from $166 million, reflecting a deliberate slowdown, with portfolio fair value down slightly to $2 billion. Credit quality improved with nonaccruals dropping to 0.2% of fair value, and NAV dipped to $17.92 per share. Management sees positive momentum in the second half with a stronger pipeline and completed rotation to core middle market assets.

Adjusted net loss was $8 million, improved from $138 million last year. Book value per share declined to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99. Management emphasized persistent PREPA uncertainty and noted a newly transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to a custodian to enhance marketability, while still considering the sale process. Guidance is not applicable, but tone is cautious and forward-looking about PREPA resolution.

summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2025 net product revenue of $49.2 million (up from $43.1M in Q1) and GAAP EPS of $0.12 per share, driven by a sequential increase in NERLYNX bottle sales to 2,608 units despite new prescription declines of approximately 3% quarter-over-quarter. Management provided full-year net revenue guidance of $192-198 million (raised from prior expectations) and Q3 net income guidance of $2-4 million, while noting that demand growth is currently stronger in the specialty distributor channel than the specialty pharmacy channel.

negative_highlights: M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, the sharpest decline ever
10% workforce reduction announced, with cost savings only starting in Q3
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guided down sequentially due to one-time benefits in Q2

First three AI deals closed, with 100+ qualified AI pipeline opportunities

EE&T revenue grew 7% YoY, its highest since Q1 2022, while M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, its sharpest ever. The company announced a restructuring that will cut ~10% of workforce, with expected savings of $2.6 million in 2025 and $8.5 million annualized, but reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects strong Q4 with M&T sequential growth.

Q3 revenue outlook is reduced to a range of $15.1-$15.6 million reflecting near-term weakness.
CIB gross margin contracted from Q2 2024 levels attributed to product mix changes.

Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to a range of $66-$71 million due to customer forecast reductions driven by global tariff impacts.

Phase III data not available until 2026

Phase III enrollment is on track, with top-line results expected mid-2026 (C-BEYOND) and end of 2026 (C-FORWARD). Cash balance is $379.7 million, with runway through 2027, and the company repurchased 4.6 million shares under a $25 million buyback. Market research shows 76% of high U.S. DAA prescribers extremely likely to prescribe the regimen.

negative_highlights: Advanced Wound Care revenue fell 25% YoY due to LCD delay uncertainty and aggressive competitor pricing tactics.
Gross margins contracted from 78% last year to 73%, impacted by lower revenue over fixed costs and product expiration write-downs.

positive_highlights: Surgical & Sports Medicine segment delivered strong growth of 16% YoY with $8.1M revenue.
Company exited Q2 with 'fair amount of momentum' despite challenging market conditions.
New in-licensed products are well-positioned to drive recovery and margin expansion in the second half of 2025.
summary: Q2 net product revenue was $100.8 million, down 23% YoY due to a 25% decline in Advanced Wound Care ($92.7M) driven by LCD delays and aggressive competitor pricing, partially offset by a 16% increase in Surgical & Sports Medicine ($8.1M). Management updated full-year 2025 guidance downward significantly, narrowing the net revenue range to $480-$510 million (flat to +6%) and lowering profitability expectations due to expected margin compression from product mix shifts.

negative_highlights: Residential market flat over past two quarters; outlook depends on macro factors
Noncash tax provision of $206,000 reduced reported EPS
Telco contract timing depends on customer installation pace
positive_highlights: Revenue up 55% YoY to $3.5 million, with hardware up 89% and monitoring up 19%
Gross margin expanded to 75% from 73%; operating income up 267%
Uplisted to NASDAQ; R&D up 17% supporting new product launches

Gross margin expanded to 75%, operating income rose 267% to $947,000, and fully diluted EPS was $0.28 (excluding noncash taxes, EPS would be $0.36). The company uplisted to NASDAQ, launched next-generation Omni and OmniPro monitors, and reiterated a 20% average annual revenue growth target over the next 3-5 years. Management highlighted a $5.4 million telecom contract with $4.1 million recognized to date, strong cash flow, and a debt-free balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.4 million due to the recognition of multi-year movie payments in this single quarter.
Q2 results did not yet reflect direct conversion impacts from the recent F1 Movie release, which occurred near the end of the period.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year with operating cash flow increasing 10% YoY to $6.3 million.
Expensify Travel revenue accelerated significantly in July and is outperforming initial expectations for Expensify Card.
Brand awareness among the core demographic (ages 18-54) increased over 50%, with a massive 350% increase among ages 18-24 following F1 exposure.
summary: Expensify reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $35.8 million (up year-over-year) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $1.4 million due to a one-time movie accounting charge; management raised annual free cash flow guidance from the prior range of $17-21 million to $19-23 million, citing increased confidence as the quarter progresses.

Management provided specific guidance for the third quarter with booked days at $14,272 per day but offered no forward-looking revenue or EBITDA targets. The company executed share buybacks totaling ~338,000 shares and sold a strategic endeavor to preserve balance sheet strength amidst geopolitical uncertainty.

Northeast/Mid-Con segment delivered a 900 basis point improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin with double-digit sequential revenue growth.

While the Rockies segment rebounded strongly, the Southwest segment saw a 10% sequential revenue decline due to customer-initiated completion holidays in the Permian basin. Management maintained Q3 guidance for low-to-mid-single-digit sequential revenue growth despite ongoing rig count volatility.

negative_highlights: Mobile revenue declined year-over-year due to record promotional activity from the prior period (2024) rather than current weakness.
$10 million-plus enterprise deal removed from Q3/Q4 forecast is contingent on congressional E-Rate funding which remains in limbo.
positive_highlights: FWA revenue surpassed mobile hotspot revenue for only the second time in company history due to strong adoption of the new FX4100 product.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to an 11.7% run rate, marking the highest level in a decade.
Secured renewals with two large Tier 1 carriers and won a major new Tier 1 carrier relationship for both mobile and FWA products.
summary: Inseego reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $40.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $4.7 million (11.7% margin), representing sequential growth driven by strong FWA volumes from the new FX4100 launch, a large channel deal, and consistent services revenue at roughly $12 million. Revenue declined in the U.S. market (-0.4%), and Shower Systems revenue fell -11.2%, offsetting gains elsewhere.
Operating loss widened from a $0.5M gain to a $0.8M loss as lower margins were compounded by increased operating expenses related to growth initiatives.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 5.5% year-over-year to $31 million driven by growth in Sanitaryware (up 4.3%), Bath Furniture (up 2.7%), and Covered Bridge cabinetry (up 67.7%).
Order pipeline is recovering following the initial tariff-induced pause, with management expressing confidence that momentum has returned.
Strategic investments in new programs and global sourcing diversification are progressing to fuel future organic growth.
summary: FGI reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $31 million (up 5.5% YoY) and gross profit of $8.7 million, but GAAP operating loss widened to $0.8 million from a prior year gain due to margin compression and growth investments. Gross margins declined 240 bps to 28.1%, primarily driven by tariff impacts that caused an industry-wide pause in orders during the quarter. Management maintained full-year guidance of revenue between $135M-$145M, citing a recovering order pipeline despite ongoing uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are 'cautious' regarding how the new biomarker approach will translate into enrollment trends due to competition.
The company halted its previously announced evorpacept colon cancer program, indicating a strategic pivot away from that indication.
positive_highlights: New data from ASPEN-06 confirms CD47-high expression as a predictive biomarker, showing an ORR of 65% versus 26% in the control arm for HER2-positive gastric cancer patients.
Cash runway guidance was extended to Q1 FY2027 following capital prioritization and closure of legacy trials (ASPEN-03 through ASPEN-07).
The Phase II breast cancer study design has been amended to pursue a CD47 biomarker-driven strategy, with interim data expected in Q3 2026.
summary: The company reported strong clinical progress in Q2 FY2025, presenting new data from the ASPEN-06 trial identifying CD47 expression as a predictive biomarker for evorpacept efficacy (ORR of 65% vs 26% control). Management announced that ALX2004 is on track to dose its first patient later in Q3 and completed the Sanofi partnership study phase. Financially, management revised guidance extending cash runway into Q1 FY2027 by halting legacy trials like ASPEN-03/04/06/07.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly from approximately $4.9M due to discontinuation of consulting services and equity-based fees dropping from ~$108k to ~$72k
Recorded a substantial impairment expense of approximately $19.9 million on investments deemed other than temporary
positive_highlights: Secured a broker-dealer license for subsidiary Netcapital Securities to participate in larger Reg A capital raisings
Portfolio company MAGFAST raised over $10 million through multiple offerings on the funding platform
summary: Netcapital reported full year fiscal 2025 revenues of $869,460 and a net loss of approximately $28.3 million compared to prior years' figures of roughly $4.9M revenue and $4.9M loss respectively. The company incurred an impairment expense of approximately $19.9 million due to investment write-downs and discontinued its equity-based consulting services, resulting in an operating loss of $8.3 million versus a previous year's loss of $3.4 million. Management highlighted the acquisition of a broker-dealer license for Reg A participation but offered no specific financial guidance or turnaround metrics.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased moderately due to payroll setup costs for three new campuses that generated only $200k in revenue during the quarter.
Management declined to provide precise monthly guidance on ground lease signings or specific variance percentages against forecasts, citing schedule variability.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue growth accelerated significantly with an 82% increase year-over-year reaching $6.6 million.
Cash flow from operations turned positive at $2.2 million for the Obligated Group subsidiary.
Pre-leasing pilots at Dulles and Bradley achieved signed leases above target revenues, validating a new leasing strategy.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 82% year-over-year to $6.6 million in Q2 FY2025, driven by the acquisition of Camarillo and higher volumes at existing campuses. The company reaffirmed guidance for cash flow breakeven on a consolidated basis by the end of the year as three new campuses ramp up leasing. Management highlighted that actual revenues are expected to exceed original CBRE projections due to stronger-than-anticipated rents, fuel margins, and occupancy optimization.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance for 2025 maintained at $64-68 million, implying significant back-half weighted performance
Management notes continued lumpiness in Pharma Biocatalysis revenue due to unpredictable order timing
Gross margin improvement to 72% is not expected to be sustained at that magnitude for the full year
positive_highlights: Revenue in Q2 2025 was $15.3 million, nearly double the $8 million reported in Q2 2024
Operating loss halved year-over-year, with net loss improving to $13.3 million from $23.8 million
Customer engagements for ECO Synthesis exceed 30, with growing interest approaching 40
summary: Codexis reported Q2 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, up from $8 million in Q2 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 72% from 45%. Net loss narrowed to $13.3 million from $23.8 million year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $64-68 million, with growth expected in the second half from ligase and ECO Synthesis. They reported over 30 (approaching 40) customer engagements for ECO Synthesis and are exploring options to expand capacity, including a potential Codexis-owned GMP facility to capture more value from early-phase projects.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to hardware mix
Operating loss of $5 million in Q2 2025
SG&A reduction partially offset by higher R&D costs
positive_highlights: Revenue up 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million
Secured major IAM deployment with National Bank of Mozambique
Closed $600,000 follow-on orders from defense ministry, total project over EUR 3 million
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue increased 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million, with hardware revenue up $458,000, but gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to product mix. SG&A was reduced 13.5% year-over-year, partially offset by higher R&D, and the company reduced its note payable from $1.5 million to $447,000. Management highlighted new defense contracts, including a first phase deployment for an international defense agency, a 3-year PortalGuard deployment with a Middle East police force, and $600,000 of follow-on orders. Despite a $5 million operating loss in Q2, management expects expense run rate to normalize and sees strong growth opportunities in defense and EMEA in the back half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 15.5% from 16.9% YoY due to front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid growth.
Write-off rate increased by 50 basis points year-over-year to 9.8%, though management noted this remained within the targeted 8-10% range.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 30.4% year-over-year to $72.1 million, beating the top end of the 25-30% outlook range.
Revenue increased 22.1% YoY to $71.9 million, surpassing the 17-20% guidance band for the ninth consecutive quarter of growth.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $300,000 in Q2, exceeding the breakeven expectation and marking a significant step toward profitability.
summary: Katapult reported Q2 FY2025 gross originations of $72.1 million (30.4% YoY growth) and revenue of $71.9 million (22.1% YoY), both exceeding their respective guidance ranges. The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA of approximately $300,000 against a breakeven outlook while raising its 2025 gross originations forecast to 20-25%. Management highlighted strong top-of-funnel activity with applications up over 91% YoY and reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of at least 20%.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $20.1 million missed expectations due to shipment timing dynamics, resulting in a gross margin contraction from 27% YoY.
Operating loss widened significantly to -$8.7 million compared to -$3.9 million in the prior year quarter.
Production disruptions occurred for two or three weeks in June due to regional conflict and tariff announcements.
positive_highlights: Record backlog of purchase orders totaling roughly $86 million expected for delivery in FY2025, with a specific spike to $43 million near-term.
Full-year revenue guidance reaffirmed at $130M-$140M despite Q2 timing misses.
Adjusted EBITDA is projected to be positive for the full year 2025 as top line ramps above the ~$31M break-even point.
summary: Gauzy reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $20.1 million and a gross margin contraction to 21.4% due to timing shifts in shipments from the second half into this quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $130M-$140M, citing a record backlog of $43M (approx $86M total expected delivery) and expects adjusted EBITDA to be positive by year-end driven by H2 ramp-up above the ~$31M break-even threshold. The company raised approximately $15 million in debt financing during the quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin only 16% in Q2, with fluctuation expected
Cash burn still $7.3 million in quarter; annualized burn remains
ATM program of $75 million launched, indicating financing need
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 46% YoY; first-half revenue exceeded all of 2024
Raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million
Signed SOW with top-5 OEM; shipping units, targeting 2027 SOP
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $9.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with first-half revenue of $27.1 million exceeding all of FY2024. Cash burn fell to $7.3 million from $20.7 million in Q1, and the company raised its NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million. Management launched the InnovizSMART non-automotive product and signed a development agreement with a top-5 OEM for a 2027 L3 program, while maintaining full-year revenue guidance of $50-60 million. The company is ramping production at Fabrinet and expects 10x unit shipments in Q3 versus Q2.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss only improved 43% due to continued THP investment
THP strategic alternatives process initiated, limiting ability to communicate
Additional EUR 2 million OsStic milestone payments remain uncertain in timing
positive_highlights: Surgical net revenue up 28% YoY to $25.8 million

THP pilot program initiated and CarePICS acquisition completed
summary: Sanara MedTech's Surgical segment grew net revenue 28% YoY to $25.8 million, with soft tissue up 28% and bone fusion up 25%.
