Management initiated a formal strategic alternatives process for THP and guided second-half THP cash investment down to $5.5-$6.5 million. The company remains on track for OsStic launch in Q1 2027 after BMI completed two milestones.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin rate declined approximately 200 basis points to 34% YoY due to Motif integration costs and external white-label brand impacts.
Temporary disruptions in on-time-in-full (OTIF) service levels for Motif brands caused a 30 bps decline in overall market share versus Q2, though normalized by mid-June.
Net loss of $6.3 million due to non-cash fair value changes in derivative liabilities associated with BAT top-up rights and preferred shares.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $110.2 million gross sales and $70.8 million net revenue, representing significant year-over-year growth.
International business scaled significantly with $7.4 million in revenue (up 208% YoY) driven by exports to Germany, Australia, and the U.K.
Operational efficiency realized synergies of $4.2 million ($15M annualized target on track), including capacity additions yielding an extra 14,000 kg annually.
summary: Organigram reported record Q3 FY2025 results with gross sales of $110.2 million (up 73% YoY) and net revenue of $70.8 million (up 72% YoY), driven by acquisitions and international expansion, though adjusted gross margin rate decreased to 34%. Management maintained guidance for full-year margins around 35%, citing temporary drag from Motif integration costs that are expected to normalize in Q4 as synergies flow through.

negative_highlights: No Israel Innovation Authority grant received in Q2, versus $180,000 in prior year
FX headwinds from shekel strength noted, not hedged
Guidance kept at 15-18% growth, implying deceleration from Q2's 19.3%
positive_highlights: Revenue up 19.3% YoY to a record $17.7 million
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to nearly 20% of revenue
Cash at record $101.6 million, debt-free
summary: RADCOM reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $17.7 million, up 19.3% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.4 million (19.5% of revenue) and non-GAAP net income of $4.2 million ($0.25 per diluted share). Cash reached a record $101.6 million, with positive operating cash flow of $2.6 million. The company maintained full-year revenue guidance of 15-18% growth and noted progress on NVIDIA and ServiceNow partnerships, with some customers moving to lab deployments.

negative_highlights: Guest value perception declined unexpectedly after March menu launch
Company comp traffic down 2.5% in Q2; July started at -0.9%
Full-year guidance lowered; no longer free cash flow positive in 2025

Portfolio closures are removing negative-cash-flow restaurants and boosting nearby sales
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $126.4 million, down 0.7% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 1.5% but traffic down 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6 million from $9.2 million, and restaurant contribution margin contracted to 12.8% from 15.5%, pressured by $1.7 million in menu-rollout costs. Management cut full-year guidance to revenue of $487-$495 million and comp sales growth of 2.5%-4%, and no longer expects positive free cash flow in 2025. Recent weekly sales trends improved to +5% following the Duos value launch, but overall results missed internal expectations.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased year-over-year primarily due to higher net interest expenses and debt repayment costs
Cash balance decreased significantly to $31.9 million compared to $41.7 million at December 31, 2024
positive_highlights: VERSATILE-002 median overall survival remains steady at 30 months with no new safety signals
Enrollment in VERSATILE-003 Phase III trial is complete and the company is right on schedule for patient accrual
Colorectal cancer cohort of PDS01ADC met criteria to expand from Stage 1 to Stage 2 following positive results
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $9.4 million ($0.21 per share) for Q2 FY2025, an increase from the prior year's loss due to higher interest expenses and debt repayment costs offset by lower personnel spending. While clinical programs advanced with positive data presented at ASCO 2025 and enrollment in the VERSATILE-003 Phase III trial proceeding on schedule, management noted a cash balance of $31.9 million down from year-end levels.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% sequentially due to mix and tariffs
Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 1.4% from 15% sequentially
Revised FY25 non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9M on tariffs and mix
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $18.4M and 135 units delivered
Lowest operating loss since going public at $7.1M
Positive free cash flow of $4.6M, highest in company history
summary: Xos reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $18.4 million on 135 units, up from $5.9 million on 29 units in Q1, and highest quarterly deliveries in history. GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% last quarter due to product mix and tariffs, but operating loss hit a record low of $7.1 million and free cash flow was positive at $4.6 million. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50.2-$65.8 million and unit deliveries of 320-420, but revised non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9 million due to mix and tariffs. The convertible note repayment was amended to extend through 2028, and the company highlighted growth in powertrain orders from Blue Bird and increased interest in the MDXT.

negative_highlights: Deal activity constrained due to tariff and regulatory uncertainty
NAV per share declined 0.7% sequentially to $19.55
Watch list 14% of portfolio, gap to nonaccruals narrows versus peers
positive_highlights: NII exceeded dividend with 110% base dividend coverage
NAV per share outperformed average public BDC since IPO
Portfolio yield stable at 10.4% and interest coverage improved to 2.1x
summary: CCAP reported Q2 2025 NII of $0.46 per share, or $0.48 excluding $0.02 of one-time accelerated amortization, up from $0.45 in Q1. NAV per share declined 0.4% to $19.55, largely due to a special dividend, with stable portfolio yield at 10.4% and debt-to-equity at 1.23x. Deal activity was constrained, gross deployment was $58 million with net realizations of $35 million, and the company announced a $20 million stock repurchase program. Management noted watch list at 14% of portfolio at fair value, nonaccruals at 2.4%, and no Q3 supplemental dividend.

negative_highlights: Working capital deficit of approximately $12.6 million at the end of Q2.
R&D expenses decreased due to contra-expenses (nondilutive funding) rather than operational efficiency alone.
Technical difficulties prevented a live Q&A session with analysts.
positive_highlights: Received $17.6 million in net proceeds from stock sales and grants after quarter end, significantly strengthening liquidity.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a working capital deficit of approximately $12.6 million at quarter end but received an additional $17.6 million in net proceeds from stock sales and grants after the period close to strengthen its balance sheet. G&A expenses decreased slightly year-over-year, while R&D expenses dropped 71% due to nondilutive funding awards offset by new development costs for HPV and LARC programs. Management reiterated a Q4 2025 launch timeline for DARE to PLAY Sildenafil cream via a 503B facility but noted technical difficulties prevented the standard Q&A session.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat year-over-year and below expectations
Net loss more than doubled to $15.7 million
Operating expenses jumped to $15.4 million from $9.3 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 73% from 64% year-over-year
Full-year guidance reaffirmed at 70-75% revenue growth
CAPTAIN trial fully enrolled with 212 patients; TULSA-AI BPH software on track for Q4 launch
summary: Profound Medical reported Q2 2025 revenue of $2.2 million, flat year-over-year, with a net loss widening to $15.7 million ($0.52/share) from $6.9 million ($0.28/share) in Q2 2024. Total orders were over $3 million, and gross margin improved to 73% from 64%. Management acknowledged revenue was below expectations due to delays in capital sales but reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 70-75% over 2024. Key milestones include full enrollment of the CAPTAIN trial (212 patients) and pilot launch of TULSA-AI BPH software with 60-90 minute procedure times.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered from a midpoint of -$15 million loss to a range of -$69 million to -$39 million loss.
Membership declined by 9% year-over-year due to the intentional rationalization of underperforming payer and provider partnerships.
A single major national payer caused late data delays and quality measure adjustments that negatively impacted Q2 results.
positive_highlights: Normalized medical cost trends remained materially flat YoY despite unit cost increases of 6% to 7%, demonstrating effective operational execution.
Per member funding improved by 10% on a normalized basis, driven by better burden-of-illness documentation and contract renegotiations.
Operating expenses decreased $3 million (13%) compared to the prior year quarter due to strategic workforce rationalization.
summary: P3 Health Partners reported Q2 FY2025 revenue of $356 million (down 6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $17 million ($8 million normalized), missing expectations due to a net $9 million in prior period adjustments. Management revised full-year 2025 guidance for an adjusted EBITDA loss range of $39 million to $69 million, citing headwinds from the single underperforming payer and noncore assets while noting that core business fundamentals are stabilizing.

negative_highlights: Sales decreased by $4.7 million in Brazil and $1.2 million with Pfizer due to timing differences.
R&D expenses increased significantly by 100% (or $3 million) year-over-year as the company prepares for a Phase II trial of PRX-115 starting later this year.
Management explicitly warned that current bulk orders from Chiesi are not indicative of end-user demand and may show quarters with no orders due to inventory destocking in early launch phases.
positive_highlights: Revenues from note goods increased 16% year-over-year to $15.4 million, driven primarily by an $8 million increase in sales to Chiesi for Elfabrio.
Cost of goods sold decreased significantly by 38% (or $3.6 million) compared to the prior year period due to lower Pfizer and Brazil volumes.
Net income swung from a loss of approximately $2.2 million in Q2 FY2024 to a profit of approximately $164,000 in Q2 FY2025.
summary: Protalix reported Q2 FY2025 revenues of $15.4 million from watching goods and $0.2 million from license/R&D services, representing a 16% year-over-year increase driven by sales to Chiesi but partially offset by timing-related decreases in Brazil and Pfizer sales. Net income turned positive at approximately $164,000 compared to a loss of $2.2 million last year due to lower cost of goods sold ($5.9M vs $9.5M) and reduced SG&A expenses. Management provided no updated financial guidance for the full year or next quarter; instead, they reiterated long-term royalty expectations exceeding $100 million by 2030 while noting that current bulk orders do not reflect end-user demand due to early-phase inventory destocking.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 21% year over year to $1.7 million
Gross margin dropped to 55.5% from 67.2% due to under-absorption
Operating loss widened to $2.9 million from $2.3 million
positive_highlights: Pediatric revenues increased 23% year over year
Back order resolved in first week of July; building finished goods inventory
Reimbursement increase to $1,639 per day supports outpatient heart failure growth
summary: Second-quarter revenue was $1.7 million, down 21% year over year, due to a temporary sterilization vendor back order that has since been resolved. Pediatrics grew 23%, while heart failure and critical care declined 53% and 35%. Gross margin fell to 55.5% from 67.2%, and operating loss widened to $2.9 million. The company terminated REVERSE-HF to reallocate funds and plans a manufacturing transition, while noting progress in outpatient heart failure with improved reimbursement.

negative_highlights: Cash balance $2.3 million, down from $3.3 million at end of 2024
Revenue remains lumpy; no 2025 revenue guidance
Operating expenses still high relative to revenue
positive_highlights: Revenue up 15% in first half year-over-year
First human product revenue recorded (Nu.Q NETs)
Cash used in operations down 30% in first half
summary: VolitionRx reported Q2 2025 revenue of over $400,000, with first-half revenue up 15% year-over-year, including first human product sales (Nu.Q NETs). Operating expenses down 9% in the quarter, and net cash used in operating activities down 30% in the first half. Cash at end of quarter was $2.3 million, with additional $1.2 million from a registered direct offering after quarter end. Management reiterated goal of cash neutrality for the year, dependent on licensing deals, and highlighted progress in over 10 licensing discussions and upcoming interim lung cancer data at ESMO. The tone is optimistic about future milestones but cautious on revenue guidance, noting lumpiness.

positive_highlights: Net revenues grew 10% sequentially and 33% year-over-year to reach a record quarterly high of $9.7 million.
summary: Fennec reported Q2 FY2025 net revenues of $9.7 million, representing a 33% year-over-year increase and a 10% sequential gain driven by the addition of 14 new accounts and expansion within existing ones. Management highlighted significant commercial momentum with three consecutive quarters of growth but declined to provide specific Q3 guidance or active prescriber counts due to competitive sensitivities. Full-year cash operating expenses are expected to remain consistent at roughly $33-34 million, similar to FY2024.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down from $34 million to $26.3 million year-over-year
Capital markets income down from $14.6 million to $11.3 million YoY
XBT product net outflows continue, though slowing
positive_highlights: Fee-paying AUM up 26% QoQ to $6.6 billion
CoinShares Physical highest fees on record at $6.8 million
Treasury unrealized gains of $7.8 million

Fee-paying AUM rose 26% quarter-over-quarter to $6.6 billion, driven by strong price recovery and $170 million inflows into CoinShares Physical, which offset XBT outflows. The company highlighted positive momentum into H2, including new all-time highs in July and progress on U.S. expansion and product pipeline.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 1.1% year-over-year
Gross margins contracted (GAAP 34.2% vs 35.3% prior year)
Material weaknesses in controlled environment identified
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA for third consecutive quarter
Backlog up 11% year-over-year to $323 million
Tariffs minimal impact due to mitigation, moved $1.5 million supply purchases from China
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $115.3 million, down 1.1% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 (up 15.3%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $15.1 million, up 26.7%. Backlog rose 11% to $323 million. Fiscal 2026 guidance implies roughly 4% revenue growth at the midpoint, with management citing conservatism due to lumpy project demand; they also disclosed material weaknesses in internal controls.

negative_highlights: Fintech vertical revenue share decreased to 10.6% as exposure declined from 13.7%.
Nearshore region revenue contracted by 3%, shifting business volume to offshore locations.
Adjusted EBITDA margin ticked down slightly in the full year due to increased SG&A expenses related to India expansion and Workday implementation.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue surged to a record $147.1 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase.
Full fiscal year adjusted EPS hit a new high of $2.75, up 31% from the prior year.
Free cash flow reached a quarterly record of $23 million in Q4 and $27.3 million for the full year.
summary: IBEX reported record Q4 FY2025 revenue of $147.1 million (up 18% YoY) and full-year revenue of $558.3 million (up 9.8%). Adjusted EPS reached a record $2.75 for the year, with adjusted EBITDA hitting $72 million. Management provided FY2026 guidance expecting revenue between $590M-$610M and Q1 FY2026 revenue of $143M-$146M.

Loss per share deteriorated significantly, rising from a loss of $5.10 to a loss of $1.27.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased approximately 34% year-over-year to $190 million, exceeding prior period performance.
CEO noted a strategic shift toward scalable revenue models is taking shape in FY2026.

Management highlighted revenue growth driven by portal fees and equity-based services but did not provide forward guidance or raise expectations despite the top-line beat.

positive_highlights: Received a nonbinding LOI from USXM for a potential $285 million project debt facility to fund Phase 1 construction

Management noted cash burn continues with total debt rising to $7.8M after adding new borrowings, though they expect margins to improve as cocoa prices ease from recent highs.

Mexican consumer environment described as sluggish and volatile
Year-to-date EBITDA still below last year's level due to a difficult Q1

summary: In Q3 FY2025, revenue grew 1.4% year-over-year, EBITDA increased 22% with margin expanding 362 basis points to 21.4%, and adjusted net income rose 71%. Management highlighted solid profitability, strong free cash flow conversion at 77% of EBITDA, and declining leverage (1.97x to 1.8x). Betterware Mexico sales decreased 5.3% due to softer demand, while Jafra Mexico grew 8% with EBITDA up 31%. summary: SSP reported Q3 FY2025 results that met expectations with Local Media revenue down 27% YoY due to the absence of political advertising and Scripps Networks revenue flat at $201 million despite a 41% jump in CTV. Management provided cautious guidance for Q4, expecting Local Media revenue to decline approximately 30% (driven by lack of politics) while anticipating core network revenue growth of ~10%. The company highlighted successful asset sales totaling $123M and significant debt paydowns improving leverage from 6x in the prior year.

negative_highlights: Q3 2025 product revenue only $0.9 million; net loss per share $0.09
EMA raised questions on TPOXX efficacy in mpox; CHMP decision pending
Government shutdown may delay CDC analysis for PEP program, affecting FDA submission timeline
positive_highlights: Product sales for 9 months outpaced prior year: $86 million vs $54 million
Cash balance strong at $172 million with no debt, more than 4x annual operating expense run rate
Management expects multiple international sales in 2026
summary: SIGA reported Q3 2025 product revenues of only $0.9 million, a quiet quarter after a strong Q2 with $79 million; nine-month product revenues were approximately $86 million versus $54 million in the prior year. The company noted $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders for IV TPOXX expected for delivery in 2026. Management is actively engaged with the U.S. government on future procurement and remains encouraged despite the government shutdown, and expects multiple international sales in 2026. The EMA's CHMP will meet next week regarding the TPOXX referral, and management expressed confidence in their responses.

negative_highlights: Vessel operating expenses increased approximately 57% year-over-year due to the addition of the SSI fleet and higher loan days.
Total general and administrative expenses rose significantly from $6 million to approximately $9.8 million, driven by consolidation costs and timing of incentive compensation recognition.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased approximately $4.9 million year-over-year to $28.9 million, reflecting strong TCE premiums of ~10% over market indices.
Shipping days surged by 22% YoY following the integration of 15 Handysize vessels acquired from SSI at the end of last year.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 17.1%, up from 15.7% in the prior period, supported by a 13% decrease in voyage expenses per day.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q3 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $28.9 million (up ~$4.9M YoY) and GAAP net income of $12.2 million ($0.19/share), driven by a 22% increase in shipping days from SSI integration despite higher vessel operating expenses. Management booked approximately 1,710 Q4 days at an average TCE of $16,537/day and reiterated that broader dry bulk market pricing remains buoyant for the quarter ahead. The company maintained its disciplined capital allocation approach with continued share repurchases ($2M in Q3) and a declared quarterly dividend.

negative_highlights: Mobile revenue declined year-over-year reflecting record carrier promotions from Q4 FY2024 that will normalize in future quarters.
Q4 guidance for total revenue ($45M-$48M) and adjusted EBITDA ($4M-$5M) is lower than the sequential growth rate achieved in Q3, acknowledging seasonality.
positive_highlights: FWA shipment volumes were up more than 50% year-over-year driven by T-Mobile and a new Tier 1 carrier win.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sequentially to 12.5%, the third highest in over a decade, aided by strong FWA mix.
Software services revenue remained consistent at $12 million, providing stable high-margin recurring revenue.
summary: Inseego reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $45.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.8 million, both beating guidance with a second consecutive quarter of sequential growth in each metric. Management raised full-year expectations by citing strong mobile volume gains from new carrier ramps and FWA expansion into MSOs/MSPs despite Q3 being a record for fixed wireless. The company highlighted the launch of premium FX4200 hardware and Inseego Connect SaaS updates as key drivers, while noting that non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be modestly lower in Q4 due to higher mobile mix.

negative_highlights: Cash OpEx increased to $12.4 million due to higher bonus payouts tied to strong performance, though this is a one-time variance.
Management noted that Q3 revenue was lower than the prior quarter's managed services spike as business normalizes.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 22% year-over-year to $26.1 million, significantly ahead of consensus estimates.
Adjusted EBITDA improved over $2 million sequentially from the prior period to reach $5.1 million.
Gross margin expanded substantially YoY to 67.2%, driven by favorable product and channel partner mix.
summary: OptimizeRx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $26.1 million (up 22% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $5.1 million, beating consensus estimates. Management raised full-year guidance to revenue between $105M-$109M and adjusted EBITDA between $16M-$19M, while also providing initial FY2026 outlooks with revenue expected at $118M-$124M. Gross margin expanded 410 bps YoY to 67.2% driven by product mix and channel partner shifts.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined significantly due to a timing issue where leads remained strong but conversion lagged, resulting in Q3 revenue lower than anticipated.
A noncash impairment charge of $4.6 million was recorded related to unused Salesforce technology components for operations and clinical needs.
The closure of the London facility resulted in an additional loss of approximately $2.3 million.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales performance in Q4 is improving compared to year-to-date trends, suggesting stabilization ahead.
Pilot programs for skin tightening are expanding to multiple centers with higher conversion rates observed among GLP-1 patients.
Management has generated over $3 million in annualized cost savings and repaid nearly $18 million of debt year-to-date.
summary: Third quarter revenue declined 17.8% year-over-year to $35 million due to a timing issue and challenging consumer sentiment for considered purchases rather than demand destruction. Management lowered its full-year 2025 revenue guidance from the prior range of $160M-$170M to approximately $153 million, while reiterating EBITDA at the low end of the previous guide ($16M). The company closed an unprofitable London center and recorded a noncash impairment charge related to Salesforce components.

negative_highlights: Total net sales were lower versus $50 million in Q3 FY2024 due to a reduction of 19 retail locations since July.
Management explicitly tempered expectations for gross margins in the fourth quarter, anticipating compression relative to durable activity and tariff impacts (estimated at ~1% of sales).
Revenue growth is expected to slow sequentially in Q4 as durable equipment sales volume increases from $7M to $13M.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA returned positive at $1.3 million compared to a loss of $2.4 million last year, marking an inflection point after restructuring costs were removed.
Gross margins expanded significantly to 27.2% from 21.6%, driven by proprietary brands growing their share of cultivation and gardening revenue to 31.6% (up from 23.8%).
Operating expenses decreased 31.5% year-over-year as the company closed underperforming stores, reducing total locations to 24.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $47.3 million (up 15% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA returning to positive $1.3 million after a restructuring-driven loss in the prior year period, exceeding its own guidance of $41 million but missing consensus expectations due to store count reductions from 63 to 24 locations. Gross margins expanded to 27.2%, driven by proprietary brand mix shifting to 31.6% and lower operating expenses, though management explicitly warned of expected margin compression in Q4 due to higher durable sales volume (up to $13M) and tariff impacts.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group revenue declined 4.6% YoY, missing the prior year's political advertising boost which inflated Q3 FY2024 results.
GAAP operating loss of $116M due to a one-time $29 million FCC license impairment charge and lower broadcast margins (down from 77M income in prior year).
Free cash flow turned negative at -$33M compared to +$73M last quarter, driven by timing differences in political revenue recognition.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue grew 13.5% YoY to $342M, significantly beating guidance of high single digits.
Podcasting revenue increased 22.5% YoY with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding from 33.2% to 38.1%.
Management announced an additional $50 million in annual cost savings beginning in 2026.
summary: Consolidated revenue was down 1.1% YoY at the high end of guidance (low single digits), while Digital Audio Group revenue beat expectations with a 13.5% increase driven by podcast growth; however, Multiplatform and Audio & Media Services groups missed due to political advertising headwinds in Q4 prior year comparisons. Adjusted EBITDA was $205M, slightly above the midpoint of guidance but flat YoY, impacted by a one-time FCC license impairment charge that caused GAAP operating loss. Management raised 2026 cost savings expectations and reiterated confidence in digital growth despite macro uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Core Simoa organic revenue declined 36% YoY due to smaller project sizes driven by the weak grant environment.
Spatial revenue fell 9% YoY, with U.S. academic revenue down ~30% and pharma revenue down 23%.
Full-year guidance tightened on gross margins (45%-47%) compared to prior expectations due to accounting reallocations.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat revenue guidance of $38-42M, driven by a partial quarter contribution from Akoya ($17.2M).
Integration synergies realized at $67 million against an $85 million target within three months post-closing.
Sequential improvement in Accelerator and Instrument revenues signaled gradual recovery despite academic weakness.
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue was $40.2 million (up 12% YoY), driven by a partial quarter of Akoya and integration synergies realized at $67M against an $85M target, though core Simoa organic revenue declined 36%. Management maintained full-year guidance for total revenue between $130-135M but tightened gross margin expectations to 45%-47% due to accounting reallocations from the Akoya integration. The company expects cash flow breakeven in 2026 and ends with approximately $120M in cash.

negative_highlights: New bookings did not show the expected sequential increase in Q3
Revenue guidance lowered due to ~$0.5 million delay from two customer projects
M&T gross retention still lower than usual, though improving
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, a record, marking ninth consecutive quarter of profitability
Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 70% from 68% YoY
Closed five AI deals for ContentLab and Genie, with pipeline supporting Q4 pickup
summary: Kaltura reported Q3 2025 revenue of $43.9 million and subscription revenue of $42 million, with record adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, the ninth consecutive profitable quarter. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 70% from 68% YoY, and non-GAAP net profit was $2 million. The company announced the planned acquisition of Ethof.ai for up to ~$27 million and a share repurchase of 14.4 million shares from Goldman Sachs at a 25% discount. New bookings remained soft in Q3, with a pickup expected in Q4, and two customer projects caused a ~$0.5 million revenue recognition delay into next year.

negative_highlights: Quarterly growth included a 600 basis point headwind from a lost advertiser
Political advertising created temporary distortion in reported growth
Majority of $250 million opportunity still undecided
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 7% YoY, above the midpoint of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA of $16 million exceeded the high end of guidance
Flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors as advertising platform
summary: Viant reported record Q3 2025 results with revenue up 7% and contribution ex-TAC up 12%, both above the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA reached $16 million, up 9% and above the high end of guidance. Excluding political advertising, revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 19% and 22% respectively. The company highlighted a flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors and raised full-year guidance.

negative_highlights: U.S. Cannabis segment posted a small negative adjusted EBITDA due to regulatory headwinds and unregulated hemp competition.
Netherlands recreational cannabis gross margin declined slightly sequentially, attributed to start-up ramp dynamics rather than structural issues.
Produce sales decreased 10% YoY primarily because of commissions paid following the privatization of a portion of that business.
positive_highlights: Canadian cannabis gross margin expanded sequentially to record levels at 56%, well above the high end of the targeted 30-40% range.
Adjusted EBITDA from Canadian operations reached an all-time quarterly record of $26.6 million, more than tripling YoY performance.
International medical exports surged over 750% YoY to $16.3 million as the company solidified its position in Germany.
summary: Village Farms International reported record Q3 FY2025 results with consolidated net sales increasing 21% YoY to $66.7 million and adjusted EBITDA rising 309% YoY to $20.7 million (41% margin). Canadian cannabis gross margins expanded significantly to 56%, driven by improved pricing, higher yields, and a shift toward high-margin SKUs following portfolio realignment. The company reaffirmed its long-term target range of 30-40% for the sweet spot while noting current performance exceeded expectations due to supply constraints.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4% YoY, with handheld revenue down 5%.
Approximately $4 million of Q4 revenue potentially impacted by government shutdown delays.
Gross margin decreased slightly to 53% due to product mix and unabsorbed precision machining costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million was the lowest in company history, down 53% quarter-over-quarter.
Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY, and Explorer shipments set a record with 30% sequential growth.
Cash position strong at $112 million with no debt.
summary: 908 Devices reported Q3 2025 revenue of $14 million, down 4% YoY but up 8% sequentially, with gross margin at 53% on a GAAP basis and 58% on an adjusted basis. Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY to $4.8 million, representing 36% of total revenue. The adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $1.8 million, the lowest in company history, but management flagged an estimated $4 million of Q4 revenue at risk due to the U.S. government shutdown, while reaffirming full-year guidance. Explorer and Viper showed strong traction, with Explorer placements up 30% sequentially and Viper expected to ramp in 2026.

negative_highlights: October SAAR slowed significantly to 15.3 million units compared to Q3 strength.
Management expects modestly lower fourth-quarter revenues than the third quarter due to current market sluggishness.
Pricing environment remains weak with limited spot volume opportunities and OEM contract renewals showing mixed results.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24.9% YoY driven by market share gains and the Brothers acquisition (up 21%).
Adjusted operating ratio improved 250 bps to 96.3%, demonstrating operational efficiency despite a $1.9M restructuring charge.
Sister hauls increased to 11% of revenue, reducing empty miles through unified systems.
summary: Proficient Auto Logistics reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $114.3 million (up 24.9% YoY) and adjusted operating ratio improvement to 96.3%. Management raised full-year top-line growth guidance to a range of 10-12%, but warned that fourth-quarter revenues will be modestly lower than Q3 due to softness in October volumes, despite expecting seasonal strength later in the year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $32 million due to a combined increase in intangible amortization, interest expense, and legacy litigation costs.
Everspan's net written premium declined significantly year-over-year from $33 million to $18 million following the proactive nonrenewal of auto programs.
Loss ratio deteriorated materially to 84.5% in Q3 FY2025 compared to 74.4% last year, driven by adverse development on runoff commercial auto.
positive_highlights: Insurance distribution segment revenue increased by 80% year-over-year to $43 million driven by strong organic growth.
Adjusted EBITDA for the insurance distribution segment reached a record $6 million, up from $2.1 million in the prior period.
Corporate G&A expenses decreased slightly on an absolute basis ($27.2M vs $26.6M) despite one-time M&A and exit costs.
summary: Octave Specialty Group reported a net loss of $32 million ($0.67 per share) for Q3 FY2025 compared to an $18 million loss in the prior year period. While insurance distribution revenue surged 40% organically, overall results were weighed down by higher intangible amortization and interest expenses following a legacy business exit. Management provided cautious guidance on Everspan's premium outlook for 2026, projecting growth north of $400 million but noting modest sequential increases rather than aggressive expansion.

negative_highlights: CFO transition announced (Hadar leaving, incoming CFO Hod Cohen)
Gross margin may vary based on revenue mix; expected to sustain at ~77% in Q4 only
R&D grant expected to decline to ~$50k in Q4
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year
Record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% of revenue)
Positive cash flow of $5.1 million and record cash balance of $106.7 million
summary: RADCOM reported record Q3 2025 revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year, with record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% margin) and record non-GAAP EPS of $0.29. Cash flow from operations was $5.1 million, ending cash at $106.7 million. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 15-18% and targets double-digit growth for 2026, citing strong pipeline and new partnerships (NVIDIA, ServiceNow, 1Global) expected to contribute initial revenue in 2026.

Prelude Therapeutics reported strategic progress in Q3 FY2025, including an exclusive option agreement with Incyte for its JAK2V617F program, with $60 million upfront (including $25 million stock purchase) and potential $100 million option exercise payment plus milestones up to $775 million. Management highlighted two lead programs on track for IND filings in 2026: a JAK2V617F selective inhibitor (IND Q1 2026, Phase I in H1 2026) and a KAT6A selective degrader (IND mid-2026, Phase I in H2 2026). Preclinical data show differentiation over existing therapies, but no financial results (revenue, EPS) were provided, and clinical data readouts for KAT6 will likely not come until 2027. The tone is confident and forward-looking, emphasizing pipeline progress and business development.

negative_highlights: THP discontinued after failing to find strategic partner
Q4 growth expected to decelerate due to tough comparison and prior saline shortage benefits
Sequential EBITDA margin flat
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 22% YoY to $26.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million YoY
Distributor network expanded from 300 to 400+ in trailing twelve months
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q3 FY2025 surgical net revenue of $26.3 million, up 22% year-over-year, driven by soft tissue repair product sales up 24% to $23.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million and operating cash flow was $2.2 million. The company announced discontinuation of Tissue Health Plus (THP) after failing to find a strategic partner, with expected cash costs of $5.5–$6.5 million in H2 2025 and no material cash spend after 2025. Management expects slower growth in Q4 2025 due to a tough comparison and one-time benefits from last year's saline shortage, but remains confident in the surgical business.

negative_highlights: Management tempered full-year FY2025 guidance for gross originations (now 20-23%), revenue (18-20%), and adjusted EBITDA ($8-9M) citing macroeconomic uncertainty.
Write-offs as a percent of revenue increased to 9.9%, up 60 basis points from the prior year quarter, though within target range.
Gross margin contracted slightly to 19.7% compared to 19.8% in Q3 FY2024.
positive_highlights: Gross originations grew 25.3% YoY, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of growth in this metric.
Revenue delivered $74M (up 22.8%), representing the tenth consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth.
Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $4.4 million, exceeding the previously guided range of $3-3.5 million.
summary: Katapult reported Q3 FY2025 gross originations of $64.2 million (up 25.3% YoY) and revenue of $74 million (up 22.8%), both within the company's outlook range, while delivering positive adjusted EBITDA of $4.4 million above its guidance. Management highlighted strong application growth but noted a minor headwind from recent underwriting tightening and comped against robust Q4 2024 results when setting forward expectations. Consequently, management tempered full-year FY2025 outlooks for gross originations (now 20-23%), revenue (18-20%), and adjusted EBITDA ($8-9 million) due to macroeconomic uncertainties.

negative_highlights: Core revenue declined YoY as instrument and license sales were adversely impacted by customers consolidating programs due to the depressed funding environment.
Management expects a drag on growth through the first half of next year from key customers rationalizing their pipelines.
Gross margin contracted in non-GAAP terms (81% vs 85%) reflecting lower volume and product mix shifts toward less expensive instruments.
positive_highlights: Signed four strategic platform licenses (SPLs) this year, bringing the total signed SPL count for FY2025 to 4 and cumulative portfolio to 32.
SeQure DX is fully integrated with growing customer interest in its unique off-target risk assessment assays.
Vertex's CASGEVY program showed strong momentum with cell collections doubling year-over-year, driving royalty revenue.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q3 FY2025 core revenue of $6.4 million and total revenue of $6.8 million, both missing prior year levels due to timing shifts into Q4 and a challenging operating environment affecting key customers. Management reiterated full-year guidance for flat-to-10% decline in core revenue but highlighted significant restructuring actions including a 34% workforce reduction expected to generate $17M-$19M in annualized savings starting in late 2025.

negative_highlights: Subscription, retail, and wholesale combined revenue declined year-over-year despite sequential improvement.
Net loss widened to $3.7 million due to a non-cash stock-based compensation charge of approximately $7 million.
G&A expenses increased significantly by 52% YoY primarily due to the one-time SBC charge and secondary offering costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 46% year-over-year to $18.4 million, exceeding prior guidance.
Adjusted free cash flow surged 88% YoY to $4.8 million for the seventh consecutive quarter of positive FCF.
Licensing revenue increased over 40% YoY driven by AI training data demand and new partnerships.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $18.4 million (up 46% YoY), exceeding guidance with adjusted free cash flow rising to $4.8 million (+88%). Licensing drove the majority of growth at $8.7M, while subscription revenue declined sequentially despite sequential improvement over prior quarters; net loss was $3.7M driven by a one-time stock-based compensation charge of ~$7M and secondary offering expenses. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance to an implied range of $70-72 million based on Q4 expectations, while maintaining no-debt balance sheet with over $29M liquidity.

negative_highlights: Automotive gross margin declined sequentially to 43.2% from Q2's 50.5%, attributed to product mix and manufacturing line transition expenses.
Cash balance decreased quarter-over-quarter, ending at $93.5 million compared to $102.7 million in Q2.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations at $17.3 million versus a guided range of $15.1 million to $15.6 million.
GAAP gross margin expanded sequentially and came in above guidance at 63% (vs. Q2's 63%).
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to $4.3M, better than the guided range of a $7.4M-$6.8M loss.
summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $17.3 million, beating the guidance range of $15.1M-$15.6M and marking a sequential increase from Q2's $17.1M. GAAP gross margin expanded to 63%, exceeding the guided range of 58%-60%. Management raised full-year revenue expectations to $69.4M-$70.1M (midpoint ~$69.75M) and provided Q4 guidance of $18.2M-$18.9M, projecting seven consecutive quarters of growth.

negative_highlights: Management noted they have been slower or slightly delayed in terms of campus delivery compared to original projections four years ago, though this was met with additional equity.
Construction costs remain higher than originally forecasted when the bond deal was issued four years prior.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenues grew 78% YoY and 11% sequentially, reaching $7.3 million.
Operating expenses decreased moderately as one-time non-recurring startup costs from Q2 did not carry into the quarter.
Company is less than $1 million away from breakeven on a cash flow for operations basis.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 11% sequentially to $7.3 million in Q3 FY2025, driven by the acquisition of Camarillo Campus and higher activity at existing sites. Operating expenses dropped slightly due to one-time startup costs from prior quarters not recurring, bringing the company within less than $1 million of breakeven on a cash flow basis for operations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach 23 airports by year-end despite recent project modifications.

negative_highlights: Cash burn was $14M in the quarter, though expected to decline sequentially
No specific margin or profitability metrics disclosed
Guidance reiterated rather than raised for full-year revenue
positive_highlights: Q3 revenue $15.3M; year-to-date $42.4M, up 2.3x vs prior year
Major commercial vehicle OEM selected Innoviz for level 4 autonomous trucks
NRE payment plans raised above $110M for 2025-2027
summary: Innoviz reported Q3 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, with year-to-date revenue of $42.4 million, up 2.3x from the prior year. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million, more than double YoY, and raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million, already within range. The company announced a new level 4 autonomous trucking OEM win, ramped production at Fabrinet, and highlighted continued momentum in level 4 programs with VW/MOIA and non-automotive Innoviz Smart deployments. Innoviz Three was unveiled with a 60% smaller form factor and planned behind-windshield integration.

negative_highlights: Prior year net reserve development was unfavorable by approximately $1 million for the first nine months of the year.
Management expects underlying loss ratios to increase slightly (by about one point) over the next 12 months due to inflation and Citizens book impacts.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written surged 49% YoY to $239 million, driven primarily by voluntary market growth rather than Citizens takeouts.
Underlying loss ratio remained favorable at approximately 17.4% on a gross basis for the year-to-date period, aligning with expectations despite inflationary pressures.
Combined ratio improved substantially from 94% in Q3 '24 to 79% in Q3 '25 due to scale benefits and stronger ceding commissions.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported a strong Q3 FY2025 with gross premiums written increasing 49% to $239 million and net income available to common shareholders reaching $13 million ($0.67 EPS). The combined ratio improved significantly to 79%, driven by favorable non-cat losses (underlying loss ratio of ~17%) and disciplined expense management, though the company noted some immaterial unfavorable reserve development offsetting prior year gains. Management raised guidance for future profitability by confirming a plan to gradually reduce quota share reinsurance usage in 2026 while expanding voluntary growth into middle-aged homes and new states.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue growth decelerated to just 1% YoY
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance cut to $89-$90 million
Operating leverage remains elusive with net loss of $14 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%
International revenue grew 15% YoY
Added 9 new U.S. centers in the quarter
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $21.5 million, up 5% YoY (4% constant currency), with U.S. revenue up only 1% and international up 15% (9% constant currency). Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%, but net loss remained at $14 million (EPS -$0.34) and adjusted EBITDA loss was $8.2 million. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $89-$90 million (from a prior range not in the transcript) and acknowledged slowing U.S. growth and lack of operating leverage. Newly returned CEO and CFO are conducting a bottom-up review to realign spending and extend cash runway, but provided no specifics.

negative_highlights: DBMG gross margin compressed year-over-year by approximately 510 basis points to 13.6%.
Spectrum segment adjusted EBITDA decreased $700,000 due to softness in ad sales and customer terminations.
positive_highlights: Infrastructure adjusted EBITDA increased by $2.6 million ($19.8M total) driven by revenue growth in commercial structural steel fabrication.
summary: Consolidated revenue increased 43.3% to $347.1 million and adjusted EBITDA rose to $19.8 million in Q3 FY2025 compared to the prior year period. The Infrastructure segment drove growth with a 45.4% revenue increase, while Life Sciences grew modestly at 3.3%. However, margins compressed significantly across segments due to macro headwinds and project timing shifts.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6M from $12M a year ago
GAAP net loss of $107M due to noncash charges including $35M impairment and $30M tax valuation allowance
International real estate business placed in administration with ongoing wind-down support through 2027
positive_highlights: Revenue up 10% year-over-year to $57M, with 95% recurring management fees
International added over $600M in new assets during the quarter, including a $240M mandate
Zero-based budgeting delivering savings, with $20M in recurring annual savings expected by 2026
summary: AlTi Global reported Q3 2025 revenue of $57M, up 10% year-over-year, with 95% recurring revenue, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $6M from $12M a year ago. The quarter included large noncash charges: a $35M impairment of the arbitrage fund intangible, $16M receivable write-off, $30M tax valuation allowance, and a $20M loss from discontinued operations (international real estate). The CEO cited continued cost-cutting, with $20M in annual gross savings expected by 2026, and strong new asset flows ($1.2B international YTD, $1.1B US through September), but net loss widened to $107M.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was significantly impacted by $2.5 million in litigation expenses related to China and domestic arbitration.
The company is not currently utilizing its stock buyback authorization as the priority remains deleveraging and extending debt maturity until May 2028.
Honey Birdette growth strategy relies on raising third-party capital rather than using internal cash flow, indicating a need for external investment to accelerate expansion.
positive_highlights: Licensing revenue grew 61% year over year, driven by six new deals signed in the quarter bringing total YTD to 14.
Honey Birdette comparable store sales increased 22% year over year with gross margins expanding 700 bps from 54% to 61% due to reduced promotions and full-price item growth of 15%.
The Great Playmate Search exceeded expectations with approximately 130,000 unique users signing up for a multimillion-dollar annualized business potential.
summary: Playboy reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $29 million and net income of $500,000, marking the first quarter of positive net income since going public. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.1 million inclusive of $2.5 million in litigation expenses (excluding which it would have been $6.6 million). Management raised guidance for licensing revenue growth and highlighted strong underlying trends after normalizing prior-year one-time items.

negative_highlights: Total revenues were adversely impacted primarily by continued weakness in card issuing along with a decline in interest income
Adjusted EBITDA declined incrementally on a sequential basis from $500,000 in the second quarter to $368,000 this quarter
Some government-related programs and SNAP payments were pushed out or put on hold due to federal government shutdown concerns
positive_highlights: Record quarterly overall transaction volume of 16,200,000 representing an 8% increase from a year ago
ACH revenues up strongly for the third consecutive quarter with electronic check transactions growing sequentially in all periods reported
Penless debit offering set all-time records with growth over the same period in 2024 of 96% for transactions processed and 87% for dollars processed
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenues were relatively unchanged year-over-year due to weakness in card issuing and a decline in interest income, though the quarter saw record processing volumes across all channels including an ACH volume up 8% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA was $368,000, down sequentially from Q2 but remaining positive with operating cash flow of $1,400,000 and share repurchases totaling approximately $750,000 year-to-date. Management noted that the current quarter includes one-time non-recurring items in last year's comparison which will normalize going forward.

negative_highlights: No financial results or guidance provided in the call
Phase III readouts not expected until mid-2026 and end of 2026

positive_highlights: Enrollment for CBEYOND on track to complete next month; top-line results mid-2026
