Management highlighted strong commercial execution with number one market share in MAT-P contracted capacity segments under Resolution 400/2025. The quarter was capital intensive due to the $301 million CapEx including the transfer of Piedra del Aguila shares and the acquisition of Patagonia Energy S.A.

negative_highlights: Net loss before tax hit $13.3 million, primarily driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on derivative instruments unrelated to operations.
Graphite-related expenditures totaled approximately $2.3 million in Q1 as the company transitions from development to commercial execution.
Germanium recovery initiative with Teck Metals is still a cooperation agreement requiring feedstock threshold work, with no cash payments or offtake revenue expected within 12 months.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $19.6 million supported by consistent zinc sales volumes.
Zinc production of 14.2M payable pounds was delivered in line with the mine plan and cost guidance.
Commenced first end-to-end domestic natural flake graphite concentrate shipments from the U.S. demonstration facility.
summary: Titan Mining reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $19.6 million (up 22% YoY) and a net loss before tax of $13.3 million driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on derivatives rather than operational performance. The company delivered zinc production in line with guidance, maintained cost discipline within the $0.98/lb C1 cash cost range, but incurred approximately $2.3 million in graphite-related expenditures and a net loss that masks underlying robust operating capacity.

negative_highlights: Net income dropped significantly due to elevated Citizens takeout activity in Q1 FY25 moderating, resulting in a lower comparable quarter.
Expense ratio increased structurally from 12% to 37.6% YoY as the company retained more premium and associated expenses while reducing quota share ceding commissions.
Combined ratio widened materially due to higher loss ratios (37.3%) and expense levels compared to the prior year period which benefited from non-recurring Citizens dynamics.
positive_highlights: Voluntary customer growth of approximately 9 million homes driven by double-digit policy increases across nearly every channel (agents +9%, alliances +40%).
New business production in Tri-County HO-3 policies surged to a quarter of voluntary Florida new gross written premium, up from low single digits last year.
Reinsurance market conditions improved with strong engagement and anticipated meaningful reduction in risk-adjusted pricing at the June 1 renewal.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $19.9 million ($1.02 diluted EPS) and gross premiums written of $220 million (up 3.7% YoY), though these results are structurally lower than the prior year due to a lack of Citizens takeout activity which benefited Q1 FY25. Management highlighted strong voluntary growth in Tri-County and middle-aged homes, with policies in force growing 14% YoY, but noted that expense ratios increased significantly as they retained more premium via reduced quota share ceding.

negative_highlights: Company remains pre-revenue with no commercial sales reported.
Cash balance of $21.7 million must fund ongoing clinical trials and manufacturing validation without income offsetting burn.
No specific guidance provided for future cash runway or revenue timing.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $7.3M from $8.5M due to lower clinical and manufacturing costs ($3.5M R&D vs $5.8M prior year).
VERSATILE-003 trial amendment reduces patient count by ~100 (from 350 to 250) and shortens duration, lowering external costs.
PDS01ADC stage I data published in JCO Oncology Advances showing encouraging results for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
summary: PDS Biotechnology reported a net loss of $7.3 million ($0.13 per share) for Q1 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $8.5 million loss driven by lower R&D and G&A expenses totaling $6.5 million versus $9.1 million previously. Management highlighted significant clinical progress including a trial amendment to reduce patient count from 350 to 250 and costs for PDS0101, alongside positive data publication for PDS01ADC in colorectal cancer; however, the company has no commercial revenue as it remains pre-revenue with cash of $21.7 million.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially in every product service line except tech services, primarily due to Winter Storm Fern causing a revenue loss of over $5 million.
Rockies segment posted an operating loss of about $3.8 million and Southwest region reported an operating loss of $3.4 million driven by reduced oil-directed activity.
positive_highlights: Northeast Mid-Con segment revenue increased 28% year-over-year to $52.5 million with Adjusted EBITDA quadrupling compared to the prior year period.
Dry gas revenue in the Northeast region was up approximately 45% year-over-year driven by sustained activity in Haynesville and Marcellus Utica basins.
summary: First quarter revenue was $145 million, down approximately 6% year-over-year and at the lower end of guidance due to Winter Storm Fern delays pushing over $5 million into Q2 and customer budget resets. Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to about 8%, reflecting typical seasonality and weather-related white space in the Rockies segment which saw a revenue decline of roughly 19%. Management maintains full-year CapEx at approximately $40 million but notes it is tracking below that framework, while forecasting sequential Q2 revenue improvement driven by seasonal rebounds.

negative_highlights: Cross-Industry Business (CIB) revenue declined sequentially as demand was pulled into Q4
Management explicitly stated CIB growth will not occur until the second half of the year
Automotive segment margin contracted to 46.2% from 48.4% in prior-year quarter
positive_highlights: Revenues exceeded top-end guidance at $16.9 million
GAAP gross margin expanded to 62.2%, significantly above the guided range of 57%-59%
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5M, better than anticipated
summary: Valens reported Q1 FY26 revenues of $16.9 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($16.3M-$16.7M), with GAAP gross margin expanding to 62.2% versus a guided range of 57%-59%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5 million compared to an anticipated loss between $4.4M and $7.9M, though the company noted Q1 revenue was lower than Q4 due to seasonality and demand digestion in its Cross-Industry Business (CIB). Management provided unchanged full-year guidance of $75M-$77M but issued a specific warning that CIB growth will accelerate only starting in H2 2026, implying the first half remains soft.

negative_highlights: Net income decreased 2.3% YoY due to a one-time equity tax impact and higher funding costs
NIM on loans contracted significantly as the central bank raised rates by 200 bps in Q1, with further hikes expected later in the year
Full-year ROE guidance lowered after adjusting for the equity tax and building in a tougher interest rate environment
positive_highlights: Completed sale of MFG for $464 million to strengthen capital position
Banco de Bogotá acquired Itaú's personal banking business, hold COP 3.2 trillion in mortgage lending and positioning it third in the housing market
Aval Fiduciaria ROE reached 33% with net income of COP 22 billion
summary: Grupo Aval reported Q1 FY26 net income of COP 336 billion, a decrease of 2.3% YoY due to the impact of an equity tax and higher funding costs from central bank rate hikes. Gross loans grew 6% YoY while deposits increased 11.7%, but NIM compressed as liability repricing outpaced asset growth in this quarter. Management lowered full-year ROE guidance by roughly 20 basis points after stripping the one-time equity tax impact, citing a tougher interest rate environment and electoral uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined by 130 basis points due to increased marketing and IT investments ($6M) and higher credit loss expense.
Merchant segment adjusted EBITDA decreased year-over-year, reflecting a decline in underlying gross margins driven by business mix shifts toward lower-margin ISO channels.
SMB revenue growth was modest at 2%, with management noting limited expectations for significant contribution from this segment through the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 10% year-over-year with organic growth of 8%, offsetting the prior period's business disposal impact.
Adjusted EPS increased 21% due to a reduced share count and strong top-line performance in iGaming (up 20%).
Unlevered free cash flow rose 17% year-over-year to $67 million, with net leverage improving from 5.5x to 5.2x.
summary: Paysafe reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $442.7 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 21%, driven by strong iGaming performance during the NFL playoffs and a one-time licensing data deal contributing $7M. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue, EBITDA, and EPS despite Q1 margins being pressured by higher marketing/IT investments ($6M increase) and credit losses ($10M). The company generated $67 million in unlevered free cash flow (up 17% YoY) while reducing net leverage to 5.2x.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $26.1 million in Q1 FY2026 compared to a net loss of $20.8 million in the prior year quarter
Commercial expenses increased significantly to $15.8 million from $10.4 million due to launch-related personnel and operational costs
Only 300 prescriptions were captured through late April, representing an early-stage partial quarter with limited revenue generation
positive_highlights: CARDEMYST launched within two months of FDA approval as an aggressive goal was successfully met
Express Scripts secured national preferred formulary coverage early in the launch quarter, covering approximately one-quarter of commercially insured lives with quality access
Over 400 unique prescribers wrote prescriptions for CARDEMYST by late April, indicating broad initial adoption
summary: Milestone Pharma reported its first partial quarter of commercial sales for CARDEMYST in Q1 FY2026 with $0.2 million in product revenue and a net loss of approximately $26.1 million ($0.20 per share). The company successfully launched the drug within two months of FDA approval, capturing roughly 300 prescriptions by late April after securing an early formulary win with Express Scripts covering about one-quarter of commercially insured patients. Management noted that while launch execution is on track and prescriber reception is positive, financial results reflect a pre-revenue phase driven largely by commercial expenses.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly refused to provide formal guidance for full-year revenues or EBITDA, citing early-stage variability and a lack of visibility into future project completions.
Operating expenses increased significantly in tandem with new campus openings, including non-cash accruals related to ground leases signed at the end of 2025 that are not yet operational.
Denver APA phase I is only 44% leased six months post-opening and described as lagging compared to other campuses.
positive_highlights: Revenues surged 56% sequentially and 76% year-over-year driven by new campus openings including Opa-locka phase II which opened mid-quarter at 68% pre-leasing occupancy.
Assets under construction increased $75 million to over $352 million, indicating accelerating investment pace.
Re-lease escalation rates averaged 23%, up from the prior quarter's 22%, demonstrating strong pricing power independent of CPI.
summary: Q1 FY26 revenues increased 76% year-over-year to an annualized run rate of $35 million, driven by new campus openings and occupancy gains at Opa-locka phase II (opened mid-quarter) and Denver. However, management explicitly declined to provide full-year guidance for the Obligated Group due to early-stage variability in project cadence, noting that significant cash flow generation is expected only from 2027 onwards.

negative_highlights: Total at-risk membership declined from approximately 118,000 in Q1 2025 to 106,000 in Q1 FY2026 due to deliberate portfolio exits.
Underlying adjusted EBITDA excluding prior-year items was only $8 million for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung from a loss of $22 million in Q1 2025 to $26 million in Q1 FY2026, exceeding internal expectations.
MA funding rates improved approximately 15% year-over-year due to contract restructuring and rate progression.
Medical cost trend remained flat compared to the full year 2025 baseline despite industry guidance of 7% or higher.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $386 million (up from $373M in Q1 2025) with adjusted EBITDA of $26 million compared to a loss of $22 million last year. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook range to $20-$60 million, citing structural contract improvements and favorable prior-year development ($17M). The company reduced its at-risk membership base by exiting non-economic arrangements while maintaining flat medical cost trends.

negative_highlights: OpEx increased by approximately $6 million year-over-year due to SG&A expansion supporting PEDMARK growth.
German milestone payment from partner Norgine is not anticipated for this quarter or near term despite launch efforts in multiple markets.
Cash position decreased slightly during the quarter, with Q2 cash expected to be lower than Q1 before recovering in H2 2026.
positive_highlights: Net product sales surged 73% year-over-year to $15.1M driven by record new patient enrollments in March and April.
Fennec HEARS full-service hub accounted for over 50% of total Q1 demand, with conversion rates hitting the 80% benchmark for the first time.
Commercial footprint expanded significantly via Project Ignite to reach a target base increasing from ~1,300 to over 5,000 healthcare professionals.
summary: Fennec Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 FY2026 net product sales of $15.1 million, a 73% year-over-year increase from $8.8 million in the prior period and representing six consecutive quarters of growth since new leadership took over. Management highlighted record patient enrollments in March and April as their highest demand month ever, with Fennec HEARS driving approximately 50% of total Q1 demand by itself. While OpEx increased to roughly $14 million due to expanded marketing and headcount for Project Ignite, the company maintains a predominantly fixed cost base and expects meaningful operating income growth in subsequent quarters.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses surged from $1.4 million in Q1 2025 to $5.6 million in Q1 2026
Cash and cash equivalents declined significantly from $12.6 million at year-end to $7.2 million by March 31, 2026
No current revenue generated; all income comes from discontinued operations or non-dilutive government contracts
positive_highlights: Secured first FDA precedent gastrointestinal study protocol from NIAID to fully fund BLA enabling programs
Completed 200-fold manufacturing scale-up at Velocity Bioworks within budget and specifications
Net loss per share improved to $2.23 despite higher absolute losses due to increased weighted average shares
summary: Valion Bio reported a net loss of $6.2 million for Q1 FY2026 compared to a prior year loss of $1.5 million, driven by the integration of Velocity Bioworks which added approximately $3.8 million in SG&A and $1.9 million in R&D expenses. The company did not provide specific revenue guidance or financial targets due to its transition from Tivic Health Systems and lack of current commercial sales for entolimod. Management highlighted significant non-dilutive federal funding milestones, including a new NIAID agreement and Department of War engagement, but noted that third-party CDMO revenue remains in the early pipeline development stage.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences revenue fell 48.4% YoY due to decreases in Glacial FX and Rx unit sales in North America
Spectrum segment faced headwinds from advertising demand softness, network cancellations, and a $900k revenue decline
Company stated it is working with lenders on strategic alternatives as it focuses on fixing its capital structure
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 33% YoY to $364.8 million
Infrastructure segment adjusted EBITDA rose significantly, with gross margin compression of only ~140 bps despite higher activity
DBM Global backlog remained stable at $1.8 billion while increasing revenue compared to the prior year quarter
summary: Innovate reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $364.8 million (up 33% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $19.7 million (up from $7.2m), driven by a strong Infrastructure segment but offset by significant declines in Life Sciences (-48.4%) and Spectrum segments. While the company raised guidance for its core DBM Global infrastructure business, it explicitly stated that near-term performance at other units remains challenged due to demand softness and network cancellations.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth impacted by lower average note price from powertrain mix
Operating expenses increased sequentially from $7.1M to $9.0M
Management cautions margins will not hold at this level every quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue nearly doubled YoY to $11.2 million
Record GAAP gross margin of 38.6%
Strong Hub demand with new data center and defense opportunities
summary: XOS reported Q1 2026 revenue of $11.2 million, nearly double the prior year's $5.9 million, with 95 units delivered versus 29 a year ago. GAAP gross margin hit a record 38.6%, up from 20.6% in Q1 2025 and a loss in Q4 2025, driven by a favorable mix of higher-margin hub and powertrain sales. Management highlighted strong demand for the Hub, including a new deployment with MacAllister Caterpillar for a hyperscaler data center project, and expects full-year 2026 margins to be meaningfully better than 2025. They also noted continued cost discipline and a pipeline expansion into public sector and defense applications.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue was flat sequentially, equivalent only to the prior quarter
Net loss widened to $1.3 million ($0.02/share) primarily due to a non-cash stock-based compensation charge of $2.2 million
Q1 sequential decline in total revenue is attributed to strategic trade-offs prioritizing durable licensing relationships over maximizing upfront recognition
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow reached $1.3 million for the ninth consecutive quarter
Licensing revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $6 million driven by new pilot agreements with large-scale partners
Gross margin expanded from 53% in Q4 2025 to 56% in Q1 FY2026
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $15.2 million (slight YoY increase) and adjusted EBITDA of $0.9 million, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive results but missing prior expectations due to deliberate strategic choices favoring long-term licensing structures over immediate quarterly recognition. Management provided forward guidance for H1 2026 revenue between $35M-$41M (up from implied Q1 levels) and full-year FY2026 revenue between $75M-$80M, alongside adjusted EBITDA of $16M-$20M. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.085 per share while executing a small buyback.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it does not have a full year of cash runway without anticipated revenue inflows.
No product revenue was recorded in Q1 FY2026 as commercial launches are targeted for later in the fiscal year.
DARE to PLAY nationwide dispensing is delayed until summer due to state-specific 503B facility registration requirements.
positive_highlights: Ovaprene Phase III interim data showed a pregnancy rate consistent with expectations and improved tolerability compared to previous reviews.
Two consecutive positive DSMB reviews for Ovaprene reinforced safety signals over prolonged use.
DARE to PLAY received enthusiastic reception at ACOG, with providers writing prescriptions on the spot.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported Q1 FY2026 results with no product revenue recorded as the company remains in a pre-commercial phase for its key assets like DARE to PLAY and Flora Sync LF5 (launching June). Management highlighted positive interim data from the Ovaprene Phase III trial, including two consecutive DSMB reviews and improved tolerability metrics. The company ended the quarter with $18.5 million in cash but explicitly stated it does not have 12 months of capital runway without anticipated revenue inflows.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined approximately 8.8% due to fuel price impacts and reduced discretionary spending
Cost of goods sold as a percentage of restaurant sales increased significantly to 38%, up from 33.6%
Company suspended construction on six additional stores and slowed new openings to only 5-7 for the full year
positive_highlights: Same-store sales decline improved sequentially to -8.8% from Q4's -11.7%
Cost of goods sold margin expanded via a $1 price increase, though COGS % rose to 38%
Retail CPG division secured commitments for an estimated run rate exceeding 2,000 supermarket locations by end-2026
summary: In Q1 FY26, the company reported a net loss of $7.5 million ($0.22 diluted EPS) and an adjusted net loss of $4.5 million ($0.14 diluted EPS), driven by same-store sales declines of approximately 8.8% due to macroeconomic pressures like high fuel prices in California. Management guided for full-year revenues between $215-$225 million, a significant slowdown from prior growth plans, and restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margins targeting 15%-15.5% in the second half of the year following initiatives including menu streamlining and new retail partnerships.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenues of $7.1 million were below expectations due to NRE milestone shifts.
Gross margin approximately -22% due to revenue mix and lower fixed cost absorption.
positive_highlights: Record number of units shipped in Q1, about half of 2025 total shipments.
Reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $67-$73 million.
Entered defense market with multiple partnerships and prepayment received.
summary: Innoviz reported Q1 2026 revenues of $7.1 million, with some NRE milestones delayed to later quarters but POs in place. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance of $67-$73 million, expecting 27% YoY revenue growth. Record unit shipments and entry into defense/homeland security were highlighted, with new partnerships including Kela and a large holding group. Gross margin was -22% due to revenue mix and low absorption, but fixed cost absorption is expected to improve with volume ramp.

negative_highlights: NII down from $0.45 to $0.38 per share due to non-accruals and lower base rates.
NAV fell from $19.10 to $18.27 per share, driven by market and credit-specific markdowns.
Non-accruals increased to 5.7% of cost (from 4.1%) with 5 new health-care non-accruals.
positive_highlights: Fee reductions: base management fee cut from 1.25% to 1% and incentive fee from 17.5% to 15%.
Portfolio stress concentrated: 86% of investments rated 1 or 2, interest coverage improved to 2.2x.
Attractive new investment spreads: new platforms at ~500 basis points with 93% lead/agent.
summary: Q1 FY2026 was a challenging quarter for CCAP: NII fell to $0.38 per share (down from $0.45), NAV decreased to $18.27 from $19.10, and non-accruals rose to 5.7% of cost. Management reduced base and incentive fees, reset the regular dividend to $0.34 per share, and approved special dividends to manage spillover. Deployment remained modest at $115 million with net deployment of $22 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 11% YoY to $2.1 million due to lower Bitcoin prices
Net loss widened to $10.1 million from $5.4 million in Q1 2025
Bitcoin price weakness drove a $7 million fair value adjustment
positive_highlights: Bitcoin production up 19% sequentially to 26.1 BTC; March production of 9.6 BTC was a record
Energized hash rate reached 790 PH/s, highest in company history
Curtailment and energy sales generated $368,000 in Q1, supporting margin
summary: LM Funding reported Q1 2026 revenue of $2.1 million, down 11% year-over-year due to lower Bitcoin prices, but Bitcoin production rose 19% sequentially to 26.1 Bitcoin with record energize hash rate of 790 petahash. The company posted a net loss of $10.1 million, largely due to a $7 million non-cash fair value adjustment. Management highlighted operational improvements and a recovering Bitcoin treasury value post-quarter, while acknowledging softer Bitcoin environment and seasonal headwinds ahead.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses increased to $8 million due to investments in people and leadership expansion.
Net loss widened significantly to $8.4 million compared to the prior year quarter, even after adjusting for one-time non-cash gains previously reported.
Cash on hand declined from $0.3 million at December 2025 to just $0.1 million as of March 31, 2026.
positive_highlights: Gross margin remained stable at 80.7% despite lower absolute gross profit.
Management reported an 11% sequential revenue increase from February to March within the quarter, indicating improving momentum.
The company strengthened its balance sheet by reducing debt and raising $3.3 million in equity alongside a new convertible debt tranche.
summary: Banzai reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $2.7 million, a decrease of 4% sequentially and 20% year-over-year due to one-time prior period items. The company posted an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.9 million and net cash used in operations was $5.5 million. Management highlighted recent cost reductions but noted revenue remained relatively flat on a run-rate basis compared to Q4.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they do not provide specific guidance on quarterly revenue or backlog conversion cadence due to operational dependencies like store readiness.
Revenue recognition is staggered over approximately five-year contract terms, meaning current deployments will take years to fully reflect in financial reports.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 114% year-over-year driven by Smart Cart deployments and the start of retail media revenue streams.
Contracted backlog expanded to $195 million, providing visibility into future deployment activity through late 2027.
Secured a firm proposal for a non-dilutive $30 million bank credit facility directly aligned with customer contracts.
summary: A2Z reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $3.3 million, representing a 114% year-over-year increase driven by Smart Cart deployments to over 2,500 units and the commencement of retail media revenues. The company expanded its contracted backlog to more than $195 million (approx. 19,000 carts) for deployment through late 2027 while securing a new non-dilutive $30 million bank credit facility linked to customer contracts. Management highlighted strong operational metrics including daily utilization rates above 95% and over one million transactions processed.

negative_highlights: Revenue fulfillment pace affected by severe weather conditions, customer facility readiness delays, and installation timing issues
Inventory increased due to anticipated manufacturer price increases/tariffs and larger industrial installations expected in Q4
positive_highlights: Record revenue for the three months ended March 31
Gross margin expanded sequentially from approximately 23% (FY2019 baseline) to 32.5%
SG&A expenses declined sequentially driven by G&A reductions and facility consolidation
summary: EVI Industries reported record revenue and gross profit for the three months ended March 31, alongside a sequential decline in SG&A expenses driven by G&A reductions despite Belenky acquisition costs. Management noted that while fulfillment pace was impacted by severe weather and installation delays, these were temporary disruptions rather than demand deterioration, with significant backlog remaining to be fulfilled later. The company highlighted operational improvements including a 9% increase in field service appointments and enhanced technician productivity.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased to $6.3 million from $5.8 million, with net cash used in operating activities rising to $5.3 million
Revenue remains lumpy and no 2026 revenue guidance provided
License deals are still in discussions with no closed agreements
positive_highlights: Revenue up 300% year-over-year to approximately $1 million in Q1 2026
Mayo Clinic trauma study showed Nu.Q H3.1 levels over 37 times higher in VTE patients vs healthy
Feline lymphoma assay achieved 86% sensitivity at 97% specificity, expected to unlock $5M milestone
summary: Q1 2026 revenue was about $1 million, up from $0.2 million a year earlier, largely due to a $0.7 million catch-up in deferred revenue recognition from the Nu.Q Vet agreement with Heska. Operating expenses rose to $6.3 million from $5.8 million, partly from severance and higher R&D costs, while cash increased to $3.1 million after ATM and convertible note proceeds. Management highlighted key clinical and product milestones, including Mayo Clinic trauma biomarker data, feline cancer assay results, and the milestone payment trigger pending publication, but reaffirmed not providing revenue guidance and noted lumpy revenues. Licensing discussions are progressing with multiple parties, though no deals have been closed yet.

negative_highlights: Non-cash loss on warrants of $2.3 million
Fleet utilization at 85% in Q1 2026
Middle East conflict disrupting Strait of Hormuz
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income up 358% to $5.5 million
Voyage revenues up 34% to $11.6 million
Aframax TC rate up 106% to $77,500
summary: C3is reported Q1 2026 adjusted net income of $5.5 million, up 358% YoY, with voyage revenues up 34% to $11.6 million and adjusted EBITDA up 130% to $6.9 million. The Aframax TC rate rose 106% to $77,500 and fleet TC rate rose 98.6% to $32,000. Cash increased 82% to $27 million, and the company remains debt-free. Management noted strong tanker and dry bulk markets, delivered the first of two product tankers in Q2, with the second expected in Q3, and sees continued growth opportunities.

negative_highlights: Shares currently suspended from Nasdaq, trading on OTC Markets.
Financial statements subject to adjustment pending audit completion.
Net loss though improved, still negative in Q1.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 34% to $2.1 million, beating prior-year levels.
Hardware revenue increased more than 100%.
Management expects profitability and cash flow positive in Q2.
summary: BIO-key reported Q1 2026 revenues up 34% year-over-year to $2.1 million, with hardware revenue more than doubling and license fee revenue up 24%. Gross margin held at 82% in both periods, and net loss improved to $165,036, or $0.15 per share, from $736,545, or $1.57 per share, in Q1 2025. Management expects to be profitable and cash flow positive in Q2 and projects first-half revenues of about $5 million. The company is pursuing Nasdaq relisting after a suspension, with an appeal hearing on June 16, 2026.

negative_highlights: Paying MAU down 9% sequentially, driven by reduced UA spend
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $13 million, including litigation costs
Debt of $130 million matures by end of this year, with strategic alternatives under review
positive_highlights: Revenue up 33% year-over-year to $29 million
Adjusted EBITDA loss excluding litigation improved 15% quarter-over-quarter to $7 million
Jury awarded $420 million in damages against Papaya, potentially up to $1.2 billion
summary: In Q1 FY2026, GAAP revenue was $29 million, up 33% year-over-year but down 3% sequentially (up 2% normalizing for tax accrual release). Adjusted EBITDA loss was $13 million, worse than Q4's $10 million loss but improved from $17 million loss a year ago; excluding litigation expenses, loss narrowed to $7 million, a 15% sequential improvement. Paying MAU declined 9% sequentially to 128,000 due to reduced UA spend, but ARPPU increased 7% and GMV grew. The jury awarded $420 million in damages against Papaya, with potential total award up to $1.2 billion, but collectability and timing remain uncertain. Guidance was not provided, and management's outlook is mixed: they expect PMAU to be flat to up with better unit economics, while RZR remains profitable for a third consecutive quarter.

negative_highlights: Cash flow was negative $1.5 million in the quarter, mainly due to annual bonus payments
Revenue guidance of 8%-12% growth implies a slowdown from Q1's 12% growth rate
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $18.6 million, extending recent positive trajectory
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 20.1%, up from 19% a year ago
Multi-year renewal with a Tier-1 customer expands RADCOM ACE into additional AI-driven use cases
summary: RADCOM reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $18.6M, up 12% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 20.1% from 19% in the prior year. Non-GAAP net income rose to $4.7M ($0.28 per diluted share), up from $4.1M ($0.25) a year ago. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of 8%–12% growth and highlighted a Tier-1 renewal, the launch of RADCOM Neura AI agent suite, and new ServiceNow connector. Executives expect some new customer revenue to materialize in Q4 2026, with partner-driven opportunities potentially closing by end of 2026 or early 2027.

negative_highlights: Reported net profit declined compared to last year due to a non-operating foreign exchange loss of approximately USD 4.3 million.
North America same-store sales fell by 5.1% YoY, attributed to extreme cold weather in January and February affecting customer traffic.
Cash reserves decreased from $270 million at the end of 2025 to $214 million due to investments in store expansion.
positive_highlights: Operating profit surged 70.7% year-over-year to USD 13.99 million due to operating leverage release from revenue growth.
Haidilao restaurant same-store sales grew by 4%, with East Asia leading at +10.6% and Southeast Asia adding one new store.
Other business revenues (Red Pomegranate project) exploded 166.7% YoY to USD 14.4 million, diversifying the revenue structure.
summary: Super Hi reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of USD 226 million (up 14.2% YoY) and operating profit of USD 13.99 million (up 70.7% YoY), driven by an 8.4% increase in Haidilao restaurant sales to USD 204 million. Operating margin expanded significantly from 4.1% to 6.2%, while net profit was impacted by a non-operating foreign exchange loss of approximately USD 4.3 million, resulting in reported net income of only USD 4 million. Management maintained guidance implicitly through strong execution and raised no specific new targets but emphasized strict quality controls over rapid expansion.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 31.9% YoY
Gross profit down from RMB 8.1M to RMB 5.5M
Cash decreased to RMB 13.4M
positive_highlights: Net loss improved 43.8% YoY
G&A expenses down 69.8% YoY
Biotech stack includes BBL2-2 biosafety certificate
summary: Origin Agritech reported H1 FY2026 revenue of RMB 49.2M, down 31.9% YoY, with a net loss improved by 43.8% to RMB 14.4M. Gross profit fell to RMB 5.5M, while operating expenses dropped 43.9% due to cost discipline. Management highlighted progress in GMO licensing, AI-assisted breeding, and commercial launch, expecting conversion to results in H1 FY2027.

negative_highlights: Packaged product sales were roughly $1.5 million below expectations, disproportionately impacting e-commerce revenue.
The company deliberately exited a specialty markets customer relationship which negatively impacted quarterly results by nearly $1.5 million.
Net loss increased to negative $0.38 per share from negative $0.37 per share in the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Gross margin mix achieved the highest level in over two years due to price adjustments, production process reviews, and SKU rationalization.
Newly remodeled stores are showing encouraging performance trends, with Corpus Christi generating a $10%-15% sales increase post-reopening.
Franchise development pipeline strengthened significantly with 40 queued Area Development Agreements (ADAs) representing vertical market opportunities.
summary: Total revenue for the fourth fiscal quarter was $6.8 million compared to $8.9 million in the same period last year, while net loss widened to $3.4 million from a negative $2.9 million prior year due to underperformance of packaged assortment and deliberate exit of low-margin specialty markets. Management acknowledged that results fell short of expectations primarily because their boxed product offerings did not align with guest preferences for smaller pieces and greater variety. The company stated it expects to have reconfigured items on shelves by Labor Day following consumer research.

negative_highlights: EV charging segment revenue declined to $14.4M from $16.8M
Net loss of $3.2M for FY2026 though narrowed
Solar asset write-off and earn-out expense hit Q4
positive_highlights: Revenue beat target: $86.3M vs $84M goal
Gross margin up to 32.6% from 25.4%
Sixth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
summary: Orion Energy Systems reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $25.7 million, up from $20.9 million in Q4 FY2025, and full-year FY2026 revenue of $86.3 million, exceeding the $84 million target. Adjusted EBITDA was positive for the sixth consecutive quarter, with FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.2 million versus a loss of $2.9 million in FY2025, and the company achieved its first full-year positive adjusted EBITDA in some time. Gross margin improved significantly to 37% in Q4 and 32.6% for FY2026, aided by a $1.3 million contract amendment payment. For FY2027, management guided to revenue of $95-97 million with positive adjusted EBITDA, and highlighted new data center product entry and strong backlog as growth drivers.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted net income fell to CAD 5.6M from CAD 16.3M, due to higher SG&A and lower FX/interest
Canadian federal reimbursement change effective April 2026 expected to hit FY2027 revenue and margins
Consumer cannabis revenue dropped to CAD 3.6M from CAD 8.2M as segment wound down
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue +10% YoY; global medical +14%, international +19%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA +32% to CAD 54 million; net revenue exceeded guidance
Acquired EU GMP Safari Flower Company to expand capacity; strong cash position
summary: Aurora reported Q4 FY2026 net revenue of CAD 84.8 million, up 10% year-over-year, with global medical cannabis revenue up 14% and international revenue up 19%. Adjusted gross margin was 60% (medical at 66%), adjusted EBITDA came in at CAD 9.2 million, and adjusted net income was CAD 5.6 million, down from CAD 16.3 million a year ago due to higher SG&A and lower interest/foreign exchange gains. Full-year net revenue rose 11% to CAD 321 million, above the guided range by CAD 8 million; adjusted EBITDA grew 32% to CAD 54 million; cash stood at CAD 165 million with no debt. Management exited certain lower-margin Canadian consumer markets, divested Bevo, and acquired Safari Flower Company; FY2027 guidance reflects a regulatory change in Canada that will impact top line and margins, but tone remains confident on international growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $6.8M to $38.6M due to one-time charges including digital asset fair value losses, legacy biotech impairment (Compedica), and legal costs associated with the strategic pivot.
Balance sheet showed substantial doubt at period end with only ~$700k cash on hand against ~$13M current liabilities before subsequent financing events improved liquidity to $10.3M by July 2026.
Fiscal year results reflect a company in transition rather than an operating business, as the primary revenue drivers (anchor compute contract and GAMEE) were signed/acquired after March 31st.
positive_highlights: Signed first enterprise offtake agreement: two-year contract with $32.2 million total value ($16.1M annual) and an upfront payment of $7.5 million received, bringing the company to full live status on ALPHA-01 cluster.
Acquired GAMEE for a 60% controlling interest adding 120 million registered users to the ecosystem with revenue growth continuing into the new fiscal year.
Secured qualified pipeline exceeding $200 million in annualized opportunities across AI research labs and sovereign entities, indicating strong demand despite early stage.
summary: Alpha Compute Corp reported a net loss of approximately $38.6 million for fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, driven by transition costs and legacy impairments rather than the new AI compute business which generated negligible revenue in this period due to timing differences with its first enterprise contract signed after year-end. Management clarified that reported results do not yet reflect the full scale of operations as significant contracted revenue from the anchor customer ($16.1M annual) and GAMEE acquisition sit entirely within the current fiscal year starting April 1st, leading to a going concern disclosure at period end despite subsequent cash improvements.

negative_highlights: Stock price decline noted by management despite strong fundamentals, attributed to market dynamics rather than operational issues
Processing costs per ton increased over $25 due to reagent usage for recovery optimization before normalization is expected in future quarters
No dividend or buyback declared; capital remains reinvested into expansion projects
positive_highlights: Record quarterly production exceeding 7,400 ounces driven by metallurgical upgrades and higher gold prices
Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $21 million with gross margins near 60%
Full-year guidance of 25k-30k oz already achieved as of Q3 end
summary: TRX Gold reported a record Q3 with revenue of $33 million and adjusted EBITDA of nearly $21 million, driven by gold production exceeding 7,400 ounces (up ~60% YoY) at an average realized price over $4,700/oz. Management confirmed the company has already achieved its full-year guidance range of 25,000-30,000 ounces and expects to produce towards the top end in Q4 following record throughput of 1,690 tons/day. The quarter featured significant operational improvements including recovery rates nearing 85% and normalized mining costs.

negative_highlights: First industry-scale facility is a few months later than originally planned
Non-cash, non-strategic impairment recorded in the quarter
Silver yield is not yet proven; pilot validation is pending
positive_highlights: Ended quarter with $31.4 million cash and no debt
Mining asset sale expected to bring $20 million in August and eliminate $1.4 million annual costs
Solar panel recycling revenue in June and July about double May's rate
summary: Comstock ended Q2 2026 with approximately $31.4 million cash, no debt, and total working capital of $39.9 million. The company expects an additional $20 million in August from the sale of legacy mining assets to Mackay Precious Metals, which will also eliminate reclamation liabilities and $1.4 million in annual costs. Metals recycling revenue ramped in June and July, with solar panel recycling revenue of $2.6 million for the first half, and the first industry-scale facility is set to begin continuous operations in August, initially at 25% capacity. Management guided to at least 25% capacity for four months and highlighted a 1-ton-per-day metal recovery pilot targeted by year-end to validate silver extraction.

negative_highlights: Organic EBITDA decreased due to deliberate gross margin investment in JAFRA Mexico
Non-recurring expenses related to Tupperware transaction hit net income
Tupperware Brazil still declined 7% YoY in June
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth accelerated to 4.1% Q2 FY26 from 0.3% in Q1 FY26
Tupperware direct note revenue grew nearly 30% YoY in first month
Raised quarterly dividend to MXN 250 million, 26th consecutive quarter
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Betterware reported organic revenue growth of 4.1% YoY, accelerating from 0.3% in the prior quarter, with total revenue up 16.8% including the first month of Tupperware. Organic EBITDA decreased due to deliberate gross margin investment in JAFRA Mexico and non-recurring acquisition expenses, but normalized EBITDA margin was approximately 19.3%. The company raised its quarterly dividend to MXN 250 million and highlighted accretive Tupperware results, with pro forma EPS 36% higher. Guidance was not provided, but management expressed confidence in continued growth across all brands.

negative_highlights: Outdoor seasonal business down 12% in Q2 and 17% year-to-date, described as a structural headwind.
Gross margin at 32.3% was slightly lower than 32.8% a year ago.
No new toy introductions in the second half to support holiday theatrical releases.
positive_highlights: Net sales up 17% YoY to $139.2 million in Q2.
Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million, with 12-month trailing Adjusted EBITDA at $37.8 million.
Tariff refunds of $6.8 million recognized as non-operating income.
summary: Q2 net sales were $139.2 million, up 17% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million from $2.3 million. Adjusted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.03 last year. Management noted an operating loss of $142,000, improved from a $2.8 million loss, and reiterated a front-loaded year with no new toy introductions in the second half. Tariff refunds of $6.8 million were recognized as non-operating income, but excluded from non-GAAP metrics.

negative_highlights: Specific reserve build of $5.3 million on largest office CRE credit
Core net charge-offs rose to 53 bps from 6 bps last quarter
Core OpEx burden expected to remain elevated in Q3 before normalizing

Net interest margin expanded to 3.45% from 2.86% a year ago
Non-performers declined 36% quarter-over-quarter
summary: FRST reported Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $9.4 million or $0.38 per share, up from $2.4 million a year ago, with revenue exceeding $50 million for the first time. Net interest margin expanded to 3.45%, up from 2.86% a year ago, and non-performers declined 36%. Management highlighted $6.1 million in expected earnings improvements from core consolidation and expressed confidence in continued operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Franchise same-store sales spread to company comps grew to ~600 bps; management cites variability
Portfolio optimization includes 30-35 company-owned restaurant closures in 2026
Debt reduction target of only ~$10 million for 2026, though progress noted
positive_highlights: Restaurant-level margin expanded by >400 bps YoY to over 17%, highest in 5 years
Adjusted EBITDA up ~80% in Q2, more than doubled in H1
Full-year 2026 guidance raised for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA
summary: Noodles & Company reported its strongest second quarter as a public company, with restaurant-level margins expanding by over 400 basis points to over 17%, the highest in five years. Adjusted EBITDA grew about 80% in Q2 and more than doubled in the first half. Comparable sales have been positive and increasingly positive for 18 months, with Q2 company-owned comps far exceeding the Black Box index and Q3 quarter-to-date company-owned comps up approximately 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA, and expects year-end debt at or below 3x EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income decreased by $0.3 million quarter-over-quarter due to lower mortgage gains.
Non-interest expense guided higher to $20-$21 million per quarter going forward.
Management noted price competition on loans and disciplined pricing may temper loan growth.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 119% year-over-year to $6.7 million, with EPS of $0.57 up 129% from prior year.
Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9% and gross revenue increased 16% YoY.
No loan charge-offs for the second consecutive quarter; classified and criticized loans slightly down.
summary: First Western Financial reported Q2 2026 net income of $6.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.57, up 119% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9%, and loans grew for the fifth consecutive quarter with total deposits up 12.6% YoY. Management raised guidance for quarterly non-interest expense to $20-$21 million and expects improved balance sheet growth and NIM expansion in the second half.

negative_highlights: NPLs increased due to KRW 130 billion in exposures related to the Chung Hong group workout.
SG&A expenses rose QoQ by KRW 42.8B (up 15%) primarily due to one-off voluntary retirement costs, though recurring SG&A declined.

Non-interest income hit a record high of KRW 628.9 billion in Q2, up 20% YoY driven by capital market performance and fee businesses exceeding KRW 700B quarterly for the first time.
CET1 ratio strengthened to 13.71%, providing ample buffer above the 13% threshold required for aggressive buybacks.
summary: Woori Financial Group reported Q2 FY26 net income of KRW 1 trillion and 4.6 billion (up 66% QoQ), driven by record non-interest income of KRW 628.9 billion which increased 20% YoY. The group maintained a stable NIM at 1.51% despite rising market rates, supported by ALM optimization and core deposit expansion. Management raised the full-year share buyback target to KRW 350 billion (the largest in history) and approved an additional KRW 221 per share dividend.

negative_highlights: Broadscale application delayed, no 2027 GA at target specs
R&D resources shifted from Broadscale, slowing its development
Nine out of ten sales conversations hit sample-type limitation (tau brain-only)

summary: Nautilus reported its first revenue in Q2 FY2026 from Baylor College and Michael J. Fox Foundation, driven by proteoform assays. However, Broadscale application GA is delayed beyond 2027 due to insufficient assay improvements, and R&D resources are being reallocated to proteoform applications. The company expects tau and AKT1 general availability in mid-2027, with further oncology assays and ~20 proteoform assays by mid-2028.

negative_highlights: Reported operating loss of $2.8 million versus prior year profit

Cash balance fell to $7.6 million, partly from share repurchases and lower merchant payables
positive_highlights: Management expects 2027 EPS incremental benefit of $1.20 from membership investments

Advertising revenue improved in June and July, indicating demand recovery

Management accelerated membership spending, driving marketing costs to $4.6 million, which they expect to produce higher revenue and margins in future periods. They estimate 2027 EPS of $1.20, but clarify this is incremental benefit, not a projection. Q3 revenue growth is expected as demand improves, though international conflicts remain a temporary drag.

Customer bankruptcy drove $1.1 million accounts receivable write-off

XTRATUF became the largest brand, expected to surpass $100M for the year
B2B Lehigh continued strong growth with substantial new account additions
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $118.4 million, up 12% year-over-year, with wholesale up 7.9%, retail up 21.8%, and contract manufacturing up 17.2%. GAAP EPS was $1.83, up from $0.48, partly due to a $15 million net IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Full-year guidance was raised modestly, reflecting strong demand and pre-book orders, but management remains cautious on tariff and consumer uncertainty. XTRATUF is expected to exceed $100 million in sales for the year, up 30% over last year.

DynaEnergetics margin down from 13.4% to 8.4% on pricing/mix, only benefiting from tariff refund
NobelClad sales decreased 17% YoY on weak oil and gas

Arcadia sales up 9% YoY and 19% sequentially, EBITDA best in over a year
Q3 guidance implies sequential improvement across all segments

DynaEnergetics was flat YoY but improved sequentially with a $1.5 million tariff refund; NobelClad sales fell 17% YoY but rose 15% sequentially. Q3 guidance is $158-168 million sales and $10-13 million EBITDA, with no tariff refunds assumed. Management emphasized continued end-market headwinds and discussed the upcoming put/call option on the remaining 40% Arcadia stake.

negative_highlights: Distilling Solutions sales down 42% with brown goods down 59%
Ingredient Solutions gross margin only 10.1% due to waste starch costs
RNDC bankruptcy created financial impact and ongoing distributor transitions
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA and EPS ahead of expectations
Branded Spirits ex other products up 3%, premium plus up 5% vs industry declines
Penelope up 13%, Yellowstone up 54%, Everclear up 13%
summary: Q2 FY2026 sales fell to $124.4M with adjusted EBITDA of $27.6M and adjusted EPS of $0.72, both above expectations though down YoY. Branded Spirits sales ex other products rose 3% with premium plus up 5%; Ingredient Solutions grew 2%, while Distilling Solutions sales dropped 42% due to oversupply. Management guided to higher putaway in H2, raised digital A&P to 15%, and rationalized 52 brands representing 47% of SKUs.

negative_highlights: Cost pressures persist, notably in ink due to Middle East supply chain issues
USPS postage increase up to 10% for mailing clients effective July 12
Global shipping and logistics costs elevated due to Strait of Hormuz security concerns
positive_highlights: Net sales increased compared to the second quarter of 2025
Strong free cash flow generated in the second quarter
Packaging business expected to grow in 2026; new Salt Lake City facility to open in Q4
summary: Quad's Q2 FY2026 results were in line with expectations and full-year guidance is reaffirmed. Net sales increased versus prior year, and strong free cash flow supported returning $13 million to shareholders. The company is expanding its packaging business with a new Salt Lake City facility and growing its in-store retail media network with new retailer wins and expansions. Management continues to manage cost pressures from ink and postage, while pursuing long-term growth initiatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 5% YoY, with U.S. down 4%
International revenue down 6% due to China suspension
Second consecutive quarter of revenue decline; expects typical Q3 seasonality
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million from $8.4 million
Gross margin expanded to 78% from 72% YoY
China registration renewed, shipments expected to resume by early 2027
summary: Pulmonx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $22.8 million, down 5% YoY and 6% constant currency, in line with expectations. U.S. revenue declined 4% YoY but rose 7% sequentially, with 12 new treating centers; international ex-China grew 9% constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million, and net loss narrowed to $10.1 million. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at $90-$92 million, while operating expense guidance was reduced to $109-$111 million.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined to 3.78% due to funding costs and loan yield compression
Provision expense increased by $2.8 million sequentially, driven by higher non-performing assets
Credit card transactions declined to $84.2 million following operator restrictions on card usage
positive_highlights: SBA originations reached $131.4 million with retained yields of 8.01%
Gain on sale income rose to $9.3 million from $5.1 million in the prior-year period
New BVNKROLL partnership with AXES expected to drive scalability
summary: In Q2 FY2026, GBank reported strong SBA loan production of $131.4 million, with $61.3 million retained at an average yield of 8.01%, and gain on sale income rose from $5.1 million to $9.3 million for the first six months. However, net interest margin fell to 3.78%, and provision expense increased $2.8 million due to elevated non-performing assets, including SBA hotel loans and retail credit card delinquencies. Management provided no formal guidance but noted near-term allowance levels may remain elevated while fundamental credit quality is better than reported due to SBA guarantees. The company also highlighted new gaming fintech initiatives, including a BVNKROLL partnership with AXES and a Visa Prepaid Card planned for Q4 launch.

negative_highlights: GMV lines down modestly sequentially in Q2 vs Q1
Cash flow positivity not expected until mid-2027
Revenue growth expected to soften from triple-digit rates
positive_highlights: Revenue up 108% YoY and 136% for the first half
Non-GAAP operating income turned positive to +$400,000 from -$2.7M loss
Operating cash burn cut 52% YoY
summary: PSQH reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 108% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income turning positive at +$400,000 versus a -$2.7M loss a year ago. The company divested EveryLife for $5.5M in cash and is affirming full-year 2026 revenue of about $32M with positive non-GAAP operating income, targeting operating cash flow positivity in 2027. Payments volume grew 153% YoY, while credit GMV grew 32% YoY. Management emphasized disciplined cost cuts and a focus on core fintech operations.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs in franchise finance remained elevated at $11.6 million
Linked quarter revenue declined due to lower gain on sale revenue
Average loan balances down 1% sequentially due to paydowns
positive_highlights: Non-performing loans declined sequentially to 1.58% from 1.63%
Total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million
Fintech fee revenue up 222% trailing twelve months
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q2 2026 net income of $2.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share, with total revenue up 23% year-over-year to $41.1 million and pre-provision net revenue up 28% to $15 million. Provision for credit losses declined sequentially to $13.4 million from $16.3 million, while total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million (78 bps of performing loans). Management highlighted a credit inflection point, with SBA charge-offs down nearly 50% sequentially and expectations for continued credit improvement and stronger H2 origination volumes.

negative_highlights: Customer caution and conservative spending due to elevated oil and gas prices
EMEA margin pressure due to timing lag between surcharge implementation and input cost increases
North America PPS volume was a slight detractor due to tough comparison
positive_highlights: Automation revenue increased 139% year-over-year on a constant currency basis
Consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency, with North America up 8.5% and Europe/APAC up 15.4%
Gross margin improved 150 basis points versus prior year
summary: Ranpak reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency (14% reported), with automation revenue surging 139% year-over-year constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% constant currency to $19.1 million, with gross margin up 150 bps year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year automation revenue target of ~$60 million and automation adjusted EBITDA breakeven by year-end, while noting macro uncertainty and a temporary European surcharge to offset input costs.

negative_highlights: July completion factor of 91% below winter storm lows
Weather disruption impacting Q3 start
Integration costs and duplicative overheads persist until early 2028
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.89 and revenue up 8% sequentially on 7% higher block hours
Full-year guidance raised on block hours, revenue, and adjusted EBITDAR
Integration ahead of schedule with FAA approval on first revision cycle
summary: Republic Airways reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $41 million ($0.89 per diluted share) on revenue of approximately $571 million, up 8% sequentially as block hour production rose 7%. The company raised full-year guidance: block hours to ~880,000 (from at least 865,000), revenue to >$2.1 billion (from >$2 billion), and adjusted EBITDAR to $395-$405 million (from >$380 million). July weather has hurt completion factor to 91%, but management remains confident, citing strong partner demand and ahead-of-schedule Mesa integration. Integration benefits are expected to materialize in late 2027 into 2028.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell note weakness in of expectations at $3.0 million versus prior year's $3.9 million
Gross margin declined significantly from 49.9% to 46.4%
Operating loss widened to $1.2 million compared to $687,000 in the same quarter last year
positive_highlights: Still a preferred supplier to Shopify despite overall retail decline
No going concern issue raised by auditors
Industrial scanning business grew to ~10% of Q2 revenue with direct enterprise sales gaining traction
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.0 million, a decline from the prior year's $3.9 million and missing expectations due to challenges in its retail scanning business. Gross margin contracted to 46.4% from 49.9%, driven by underutilized manufacturing capacity, resulting in an operating loss of $1.2 million compared to a smaller loss previously. Management confirmed continued cost-cutting measures including headcount reductions and highlighted the growing industrial segment which contributed approximately 10% of revenue.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 4% due to lower unit volumes and a difficult prior-year comparison for pre-owned revenue which was up 18%
Service parts and other revenue declined 13%, primarily reflecting the impact of the Ocean Bio-Chem sale
Full-year guidance narrowed with expectations that same-store sales will be down low to mid-single digits
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24% driven by favorable product mix and exiting brands with lower margins in prior year
Adjusted net leverage improved significantly from 5.8x trailing EBITDA at the end of last year to 3.7x, achieving the target under four times ahead of schedule
Same-store sales declined only 2%, outperforming an industry that is down high single digits
summary: Revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $531 million while gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24%. Management updated and narrowed full-year guidance for revenue ($1.75B-$1.8B) and adjusted EBITDA, citing a challenging retail environment where the industry is expected to be down high single digits.

negative_highlights: Credit and occupancy loss guidance assumes 25 basis points, though year-to-date actuals at 10 basis points
Rising interest rates and macro uncertainty noted as risks
positive_highlights: Record quarterly investment volume of over $500 million
AFFO per share up 7.4% year-over-year and guidance raised
Occupancy at record 99.8%, recapture rate 105%
summary: Agree Realty reported record Q2 2026 investment volume of over $500 million across its three platforms, with acquisitions of $451 million at a 7% cap rate and 73% investment-grade tenants. Core FFO per share rose 7.5% to $1.13 and AFFO per share rose 7.4% to $1.14. Full-year AFFO guidance was raised to $4.57-$4.59 and investment volume guidance to $1.6-$1.8 billion. Occupancy set a record at 99.8%, and the company executed 1.6 million square feet of leases in the first half at a 105% recapture rate.

negative_highlights: Temporary loss of ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict
Global diesel and chemical supply constrained; Strait closure removing ~3M bpd refining capacity
Cash opex held flat year-over-year only by offsetting inflation with cost savings
positive_highlights: Earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B despite 10% upstream production loss
Guyana production ~900k bpd and Errea Wittu FPSO on schedule; capital recovery accelerated two years
Chemical margins up ~180% QoQ; specialty products record earnings; cumulative cost savings $16.3B
summary: ExxonMobil reported exceptional Q2 results despite losing ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict, with industry-leading earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B. Upstream production outside the Middle East hit a two-decade high, chemicals margins surged ~180% QoQ, and specialty products posted record earnings. Guyana's Errea Wittu FPSO on track, and the company achieved $16.3B cumulative structural cost savings since 2019. Guidance implies continued momentum with free cash flow expected to double by 2030 versus 2025.

negative_highlights: Management declined to comment on individual shareholder note, which has pressured the stock
Utility corridor developments are capital-intensive, though planned in advance
No significant impact from AI-related cost increases, but noted only slight revenue reduction from non-strategic asset sales
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 23% and net income up 37% YoY, both second-quarter records
Gross margins expanded across all segments (residential 45% to 48%, hospitality 39% to 42%, commercial 57% to 65%)
Repurchased $32.7 million of stock, reducing share count to lowest in ~30 years
summary: The St. Joe Company reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $158.9 million, up 23% YoY, and net income of $40.5 million, up 37% YoY, both record highs for the quarter. Gross margins expanded across all segments: residential to 48%, hospitality to 42%, and commercial to 65%. The company allocated $32.7 million to buybacks, $24 million to capex, and repaid $10.9 million in debt, with share count at a 30-year low. Management emphasized long-term capital allocation, continued demand from in-migration, and no near-term constraints from power development.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets up nominally to ~$1.07 billion due to rate delays
Realized losses expected to rise to $20-30 million per quarter
Distributable earnings guided at $0.15-0.17 per share for next few quarters
positive_highlights: Year-to-date agency volume up 30% year over year
$135 million additional liquidity from CLO unwind with reduced pricing and enhanced leverage
Cost-cutting measures expected to save ~$10 million annually
summary: Arbor Realty Trust reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $0.15 per share, in line with guidance, but noted $0.02 per share of one-time financing drag and higher specific reserves. Non-performing assets remained around $1.07 billion, with $90 million resolved in July and $105 million contracted for August. The company closed a $375 million convertible offering, used $114 million to watch back stock at 50% of book value, and cut annual expenses by ~$10 million. summary: Stoke Therapeutics reported significant progress in its phase III EMPEROR study for zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome, with enrollment completed at 162 patients in just 10 months and no treatment discontinuations. The company is on track for a phase III readout in Q3 2027 and plans a rolling NDA submission starting Q1 2027. Long-term OLE data show durable seizure control and statistically significant improvements in cognition and behavior through four years, with a strong safety profile. The company has a pro forma cash position of approximately $420 million, providing runway to a potential U.S. launch by early 2028. Additionally, STK-002 for ADOA has completed dosing of the first cohort and is advancing to higher doses, with early results expected in the first half of 2027.

positive_highlights: First-ever FDA approval of a PROTAC degrader, VEPPANU

summary: Arvinas reported Q2 2026 with cash of $567.9 million, down from $685.4 million at end of 2025. The FDA approved VEPPANU (first PROTAC degrader) and it was out-licensed to Rigel Pharmaceuticals. The KRAS G12D program ARV-806 is deprioritized for partnering. Clinical milestones: ARV-393 phase I data expected by end of 2026, ARV-027 healthy volunteer data in H1 2027, ARV-102 trials now expected to begin in 2027. Financials include a one-time revenue recognition from Pfizer collaboration and a $52.7 million liability for VEPPANU closeout.

summary: Marqeta reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with net revenue up 17% to $176M, gross profit up 17% to $122M, and TPV up 32% to $120B. Adjusted EBITDA grew 31% with a 21% margin, and the company achieved its second consecutive quarter of GAAP net income at $8M. Management highlighted continued diversification from Block, with non-Block TPV growing over 2x faster, and raised expectations for the remainder of 2026 based on strong execution and product momentum.

summary: Match Group reported Q2 FY2026 with total revenue down 1% year-over-year and Adjusted EBITDA up 14% year-over-year, beating expectations. Tinder DAU improved to -4% year-over-year, with MAU still declining 7% but improving sequentially, and payers expected to return to growth by Q4 next year. Hinge MAU grew 13% globally with 22% revenue growth, while E&E faces headwinds from Azar's App Store removal. Management raised the outlook for Adjusted EBITDA to at or above the high end and is confident in a Tinder turnaround, with MAU expected flat by Q4 next year and 2027 Tinder revenue up year-over-year.

summary: Gartner's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.7 billion, up 3% as reported and 2% FX neutral, with EBITDA of $466 million up 6% and adjusted EPS of $4.37 up 24% year-over-year. Contract value grew 2% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1, and free cash flow rose 9% to $378 million. Management raised full-year EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow guidance, and expects CV growth to continue accelerating. The company is optimistic about AI-driven demand and its Business and Technology Insights transformation.

summary: Addus HomeCare reported Q2 2026 revenue of $377.4 million, up 8% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $1.73, up 16.1%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.9% to $49.2 million, with margin expanding to 13%. Personal care same-store revenue grew 6.8%, driven by 2.2% same-store hour growth; hospice same-store revenue rose 11.1%, while home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved sequentially. Management raised expectations for personal care organic growth to 6-6.5% for 2026 and remains optimistic about eliminating the 80/20 rule and M&A pipeline.

summary: BP reported a 'good quarter' with net debt down $3 billion sequentially and financial obligations down $7 billion since Q1. However, operational performance fell short and cost reductions have not yet flowed to the bottom line; management guided to $18 billion in structural costs by end of 2026, from $22 billion in 2025. BPX production grew to 545,000 boe/d, with a new basin production record. Management emphasized 'Fit to Grow' strategy, portfolio simplification, and balance sheet strengthening, but acknowledged past impairments and slower cost progress.

Excluding that benefit, comparable EPS was $1.90. Light Duty sales were flat YoY on tough comps, Heavy Duty grew ~7%, Specialty Vehicle declined 1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3%-5% net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $8.50-$8.80, reflecting lower tariff environment and pricing actions. Heavy Duty margin improved 150 bps ex-refund, but freight market remains challenged.

Revenue grew 9% to $312 million, with gross margin steady at 30.6% and EPS rising to $1.42 from $1.32. The company is aggressively expanding capacity, planning a new facility and expects strong performance into FY2027.

Plans for leadership transition and increased MGM ownership were reiterated.

Active customers grew 11% year-over-year to exceed 3 million, and the 115,000 quarterly growth is the highest in four years. Gross margin was 56.6%, including a 160 basis point benefit from tariff refunds; adjusted EBITDA rose to $27 million from $23 million, with EPS of $0.26 versus $0.14 in the prior year. Management expects double-digit revenue growth for the full year and noted July sales up 18% year-over-year.

International/offshore revenue rose 11% sequentially, while NAM land fell 4% sequentially due to Canada seasonality. The company closed the TCO Group acquisition for $95 million and guided Q3 revenue to $260-270 million and adjusted EBITDA to $51-57 million, implying sequential growth. Management cited strong subsea momentum, Mexico activity, Saudi market share gains, and expects U.S. land growth in the back half.

Q3 combined revenue guidance of $255 million midpoint implies over $1 billion annualized run rate.

summary: Q2 revenue was a record $201 million, up 18% sequentially and 62% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, up over 120% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, driven by strength across all end markets, especially compute and communications. Q3 guidance calls for FPGA revenue of $210-230 million and combined revenue of $245-265 million, including two months of AMI, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.54-0.58, which implies roughly 100% year-over-year EPS growth. The acquisition of AMI closed in late July and is expected to be accretive to EPS starting in Q4, with AMI expected to exit 2026 at a revenue run rate of more than $200 million and grow 25% in 2027. New product revenue is expected to exceed 25% of total revenue this year, and the company described a 'rule of 105' based on 62% growth and over 40% EBITDA margin.

The company completed redemption of convertible debt and ended with $21M cash and 314 Bitcoin. Q3 guidance is $8.5M-$10M, with the high end dependent on licensing deals. Supply constraints persist, especially memory, and the company targets breakeven as revenue scales.

The company advanced its continuous manufacturing pilot line, completed the stage one ISO 9001 audit, and received a milestone payment from SK On, while negotiating a new collaboration agreement. Management expects to announce a joint venture for commercial electrolyte production in South Korea by year-end.

The company beat prior-year profitability, driven by improved volumes, pricing, and mix, and reaffirmed expectations for sequentially higher adjusted EBITDA in Q3. The order book is up over 50% year-over-year, with record aerospace and defense shipments and a near doubling of industrial backlog. Management guided to slightly higher Q3 adjusted EBITDA sequentially and year-over-year, with price increases announced effective August, fully realized in 2027.

summary: DuPont reported Q2 FY2026 organic sales growth of 4%, operating EBITDA margin up 80 basis points to 24.6%, adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.88, and free cash flow conversion of 127% for the quarter. The company raised full-year guidance again: organic growth to slightly ahead of 4%, operating EBITDA midpoint to $1.760B, and adjusted EPS midpoint to $7.24 (up $0.15). Management also announced a Q3 $250M share repurchase and expects full-year free cash flow conversion ahead of the 90% target. Strength was driven by healthcare, aerospace, industrial water, semiconductor, and electric vehicle battery applications, with continued momentum expected in the second half.

summary: Bruker returned to organic revenue growth in Q2 2026, with reported revenue up 5.2% to $838.5 million and organic growth of 2.8% (3.4% excluding U.S. tariff refunds). Non-GAAP EPS of $0.49 was up 53% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin up 350 bps to 52.1% and operating margin up 510 bps to 14.1%, aided by cost savings and tariff refunds. Management raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance despite trimming top-line guidance due to FX and tariff timing, while reiterating $140 million of annualized cost savings and expecting additional $20 million in 2027 from a new operating structure. Bookings showed strength in biopharma (up >20% organic) and deep tech (semiconductor and energy research both up >50% organic), though U.S. academic order weakness persists and some revenue is pushed to Q4 and 2027 due to long lead times.

Management maintained full-year guidance despite PFB segment margin disappointment, citing strong backlog and operational improvements, with steeper Q4 ramp expected. Orders exceeded $1B for the third consecutive quarter, up 10% YoY.

Global same-store sales rose 1.5%, with iLottery wagers up 22% in the first half. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance, expects accelerated H2 growth, and highlighted a 3.24x leverage ratio, ahead of target, with over $400 million annual free cash flow potential.

USFS local case volumes grew 2.6% in Q4 with 130 bps sequential improvement on a two-year stack, and international posted 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted operating income growth (up 15.7%). Management guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS growth of 9%-11% and reiterated expected close of Restaurant Depot acquisition by Q3 FY2027, with $250 million cost synergies and day-one EPS accretion.

The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60 from $4.15-$4.70, citing strong performance in biofuels, crush volumes up ~5%, and momentum in Nutrition (especially flavors). CFO noted strong cash flow of $1.8 billion in H1, and management discussed expansion of U.S. crush capacity, natural colors opportunities, and potential share repurchases.

summary: ACADIA reported Q2 2026 total revenues of $308 million, up 17% year-over-year on an adjusted basis, with DAYBUE at $125 million (up 30%) and NUPLAZID at $183 million (up 10%). The company raised DAYBUE full-year guidance to $480-$510 million, reaffirmed NUPLAZID guidance at $760-$790 million, and expects total 2026 revenue of $1.24-$1.3 billion. Strong DAYBUE STIX uptake (40% of U.S. patients) and a positive CHMP opinion for trofinetide support the raised outlook. The phase II remlifanserin readout is expected in September-October, with Fast Track designation received.

summary: PSEG reported Q2 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $0.86, up from $0.77 a year earlier, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $4.28-$4.40 per share. The utility segment (PSE&G) grew earnings on infrastructure and energy-efficiency investments, while PSEG Power benefited from higher realized market prices and nuclear output, partially offset by the end of ZEC programs. Management announced an expected base rate case filing by year-end 2026 and cited regulatory clarity from PJM and New Jersey proceedings, including the Power in New Jersey Act enabling new nuclear development.

The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.1B-$2.2B and adjusted EBITDA to $437.5M-$455M, citing a 'transmission demand super cycle' and strong order flow. Net leverage improved to 3.85x, and management expects meaningful free cash flow generation in 2026.

Evergreen net inflows were $640 million with positive flows in 10 of 12 products, though one non-U.S. multi-strategy equity fund saw elevated redemptions. Management expects five key strategies to be in market over the balance of fiscal 2027 and early 2028, and highlighted strong fundraising momentum including a $3.8 billion direct equity fund close.

summary: Lime reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $304 million, up 23.6% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $84 million (28% margin). Average operational fleet grew 22.1% to 408,000 vehicles, and MAU grew 22.1% to 5 million. RVD of $8.20 grew 1.2% reported but mid-single digits on a same-market basis. Management highlighted the early success of LimePrime, which launched globally in February and now represents a double-digit percentage of the user base, though it is weighing on near-term adjusted gross margin (52.1% vs. 55.7% last year) due to upfront investment. The company reaffirmed expectations for a record year with strong growth and profitability, and planned meaningful cash flow generation.

The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: sales growth now expected 14%-16% (up from 10%-14%), adjusted EBITDA $330-$340 million (up from $315-$330 million), and EPS $9.30-$9.80 (up from $8.85-$9.50). AST sales rose 21.8% with strong semiconductor demand, and Sealing Technologies grew 15.3% overall (5% organic) despite soft commercial vehicle and European markets.
