RDS segment showed strong growth with adjusted EBITDA up 10.4% and margins healthy. New business wins contributed 4.5 points of growth, including about 1 point from the Win the Pro focus, and the company remains confident in its long-term 8-12% growth target.

Management highlighted a new Chief Commercial Officer, AI-driven productivity gains, and continued regulatory tailwinds.

positive_highlights: Record revenue of $217.8M, up 8% sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 53%, up from ~50% in Q1
Second straight guidance raise; CapEx guidance raised $100M
summary: WaterBridge reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $217.8 million (up 8% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of $115.8 million (up ~12% sequentially), with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 53%. Management raised full-year 2026 volume and Adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second consecutive quarter and raised CapEx guidance by $100 million to $530-$590 million. The quarter included the closing of the Ranger acquisition, announcement of the NDB Landfill acquisition, and acceleration of the New Devon project. Speedway Phase I launched on schedule in July with volumes expected to ramp toward ~100,000 barrels per day and exit the year above that.

negative_highlights: Constant currency revenue declined 6.3%, with adjusted decline of 3.6% excluding Byte and dealer inventory reductions.
OIS segment revenue fell 13.2% as reported; SureSmile declined double digits.
EDS volumes declined in Americas and EMEA, with continued distributor inventory reductions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS flat at $0.52 despite revenue decline, aided by $0.17 tariff refund benefit.
Operating cash flow more than doubled to $99 million from $48 million.
Wellspect revenue grew 7.1% as reported on new product strength.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 4.1% as reported (6.3% constant currency), with adjusted EPS flat at $0.52, supported by $44 million in tariff refunds. The company maintained its 2026 outlook of $3.5-$3.6 billion net sales and adjusted EPS of $1.40-$1.50, excluding tariff refunds. Management expects Q3 earnings to be below Q2, with improvement weighted to Q4 as investments ramp.

negative_highlights: Hedging limited participation in higher oil prices during the quarter.
Natural gas differentials remain highly negative at -$8.14 per Mcf due to takeaway constraints.
Capital spending guidance raised for 2026 to $158-$178 million, above previous plan.
positive_highlights: Sequential production increased 3% to 19,990 BOE/d, within guidance.
Realized oil price increased 38% to $95.45 per barrel.
Leverage improved to 1.7x and liquidity increased to $226 million after equity offering.
summary: Ring Energy reported Q2 2026 production of 19,990 BOE/d, up 3% sequentially, with realized oil prices up 38% to $95.45/barrel, but hedges limited upside. The company completed an equity offering, reducing debt to about $360 million and leverage to 1.7 times. Management raised second-half 2026 oil sales guidance midpoint by about 2% and lowered LOE midpoint guidance slightly, while increasing full-year 2026 capital spending to $158-$178 million. Initial 2027 guidance shows BOE volume growth of about 10% and a ~10% midpoint reduction in capital spending.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance of $330-$415 million remains wide and unchanged.
R&D expenses increased from $72M to $79M due to ATTC investments.
Recent quarter's FRUZAQLA U.S. growth not highlighted; previous Medicare impact noted.
positive_highlights: ELUNATE and SULANDA grew over 40% in China, driving strong product sales.
FRUZAQLA ex-U.S. in-market sales grew 70% on rapid geographic expansion.
Company remains profitable with $16 million net income and $1.4 billion cash reserve.
summary: HUTCHMED reported strong H1 2026 results with oncology revenue of $162 million, up 23% year-over-year, and China product sales growth led by ELUNATE and SULANDA at over 40%. FRUZAQLA ex-U.S. in-market sales grew 70%, and the company remained profitable with net income of $16 million. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $330-$415 million, with management confident of at least beating the lower end and potentially exceeding the high end with business development and milestones. The company advanced its ATTC pipeline with two assets in Phase I and a third IND cleared, and expects key data readouts from SAFFRON and SANOVO in H2.

negative_highlights: Ironton production of 4.5 million pounds was down from the prior quarter
Compounding asset runs only five days a week, with 24/7 expected in Q4
Breakeven target remains second-half, indicating still not achieved
positive_highlights: Revenue grew for the sixth consecutive quarter, up substantially from a year ago
New Jersey approved PureFive as recycled content, accelerating brand qualifications
Turnaround completed ahead of schedule and below budget; new daily throughput record in June
summary: PureCycle reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $4.5 million, up substantially year-over-year, with production of 4.5 million pounds of PureFive and about 5 million pounds of feedstock processed. The company completed a major turnaround ahead of schedule and below budget, set a new daily throughput record in June, and brought compounding in-house. Management reiterated the second-half Ironton breakeven target, citing accelerated customer qualifications following New Jersey's approval of PureFive as recycled content and commercial production of Procter & Gamble's Downy caps, with Tide caps and Vicks ZzzQuil lids scheduled for Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Second half revenue may not fully reflect underlying demand due to NRDL-related commercial dynamics
XACDURO growth constrained by supply constraints
positive_highlights: Net product revenue grew 11% sequentially to $105.8 million, with business commercially profitable
zoci potential best-in-class ADC, with confirmed ORR 38.2% in extrapulmonary NEC vs ~18% for current regimens
Cash at $717.5 million, providing flexibility for investments
summary: Q2 2026 net product revenue grew 11% sequentially to $105.8 million, with the commercial business remaining profitable. Management emphasized pipeline progress, including zoci moving toward global pivotal trials and expected U.S. accelerated approval in 2028, plus ZL-1503 first-in-human data later this year. They guided for stable operating expenses and expect a return to meaningful growth in 2027, with potential first U.S. product launch in 2028. The tone is confident but acknowledges near-term revenue impact from NRDL dynamics and supply constraints.

July 4th holiday described as a 'dud' and industry demand down mid-to-high single digits
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 9% to $0.58, a record second quarter

Leverage back to 2.99x, record operating cash flow of $236M
summary: Somnigroup (formerly Tempur Sealy) reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.8 billion, adjusted EPS of $0.58 (up 9% YoY), and adjusted EBITDA of $297 million. North America margins expanded sharply (gross +680 bps, operating +400 bps) on synergies, but Mattress Firm margins fell on financing and investments. Full-year EPS guidance was $2.85-$3.15, implying mid-single-digit industry decline and low-single-digit like-for-like growth for most segments; management noted a weak July 4th period and ongoing ERP challenges at Dreams, but reaffirmed confidence and highlighted the Leggett & Platt deal on track to close in Q3.

negative_highlights: Supply constraints and capacity challenges spreading broadly
Lead times stretching, causing expedite requests to go unsupported
positive_highlights: Net sales beat high end of guidance, up 38% YoY to $1.485B
June quarter book-to-bill well above 1, strongest bookings quarter in ~4 years
September quarter EPS guidance up 165.7% YoY and 22.4% sequentially at midpoint
summary: Microchip reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $1.485 billion, up 13.2% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.76, $0.07 above the midpoint, with gross margin at 63.8%, operating margin at 35.1%, and strong free cash flow. Data center sales soared 97.8% year-over-year, with full-year 2026 data center sales expected to reach ~$1 billion, up 69%. September quarter guidance is for net sales up 8% sequentially and non-GAAP EPS of $0.91-$0.95, with gross margin forecast at 66%-67%, above the long-term target of 65%. Bookings were the strongest in about four years, and distribution inventory correction is complete, with lead times stretching due to capacity constraints.

negative_highlights: Tobacco segment operating income fell from $35.7 million to $3.5 million year-over-year
Consolidated net loss of $5 million versus net income of $8.5 million in prior year
Ingredients segment operating loss of $700,000 with persistent consumer headwinds and high fixed costs
positive_highlights: Full-year customer demand expectations consistent with fiscal year sales plan

summary: In Q1 FY2027, Universal Corp reported consolidated revenue of $524 million, down 12% year-over-year, and an operating income of $2.3 million versus $33.8 million in the prior year, driven by a steep decline in tobacco segment operating income from $35.7 million to $3.5 million due to oversupply and delayed customer watching. The ingredients segment posted a $700,000 operating loss as consumer headwinds and high fixed costs persisted. Management maintains full-year customer demand is consistent with plan, with second-half-weighted shipments expected, and sees less risk of large inventory write-downs. The company noted a net loss of $5 million versus a net income of $8.5 million last year, but highlighted net debt reduction of $52 million and a $1.1 billion liquidity position.

negative_highlights: Atera launch is expected to moderate Xenium and Visium sales, with some customers delaying orders
Q3 consumables expected to step down sequentially due to Atera order timing

Atera order flow exceeds initial expectations, with 40+ instruments planned for H2
Xenium and Visium consumables grew sequentially after Atera launch
summary: Revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $151 million, or $149.4 million excluding non-recurring settlement revenue, up 3% YoY. Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with strong growth in Chromium and Xenium utilization. The company launched Atera, a new spatial platform, and reported very strong early order flow exceeding initial expectations, with 40+ instruments expected to ship in the second half, mostly in Q4. Management raised guidance, expecting a sequential step-up in Q3 to Q4 revenue driven by Atera instrument sales and consumables, while noting some near-term cannibalization of Xenium and Visium orders.

negative_highlights: Restaurant margin decreased 66 basis points to 16.4%

Diluted EPS decreased 0.7% to $1.85. Commodity inflation guidance was lowered to approximately 5% for the full year, and the company plans a 1% menu price increase in Q4. Development remains on track with 35 company openings planned for 2026.

Management highlighted continued scaling, new product introductions (Hellcat, Blue Ops Variant 7), and strong demand, expecting a 'dramatic' revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4. Cash stood at $325.6 million, and they reaffirmed a focus on profitability in 2027.

Full-year revenue guidance raised by $6M
AI adoption: active AI users nearly half of prescribers, prompt volume up 25% QoQ, Scribe users up 10x in July
summary: Doximity reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $157M, up 7% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $75M (48% margin), both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $6M to $671-$681M, while maintaining EBITDA guidance at $309-$329M as it accelerates AI investments. AI Search launched late April, with first cohort onboarded and majority of contracted revenue expected to be recognized in Q3. Q2 guidance implies 1% YoY growth due to tough comparison, with stronger growth expected in Q3.

Organic net sales down 2% with U.S. spirits and Chinese white spirits weak
Impairment charges of $1.5 billion and restructuring charges of $0.9 billion
positive_highlights: Organic operating profit increased 2% despite a 2% organic sales decline
Free cash flow rose 16% to $3.2 billion, reducing net debt by $1.4 billion
Europe, LAC, and Africa delivered strong growth, with India up 7%
summary: Diageo reported a mixed fiscal 2026: organic net sales declined 2% (down ~0.5% ex-Chinese white spirits), but organic operating profit grew 2% and EPS pre-exceptionals rose 0.7% to $1.653. Free cash flow rose $463 million to $3.2 billion, net debt fell to $20.5 billion, and leverage improved to 3.1x from 3.4x. North America suffered an 8.4% organic sales decline with tequila down 21%, while Europe, LAC, and Africa grew. Management announced a $1.2 billion restructuring plan (over two years) with around $1 billion in savings, and will provide fiscal 2027 guidance at the Capital Markets Day.

Atera instrument placements concentrated in Q4, creating back-half weighted uncertainty
Xenium and Visium consumables growth likely to moderate as customers await Atera
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $151M, up 3% YoY ex-settlement
Total consumables revenue up 7%, with double-digit growth in Chromium consumable reaction volumes
Atera order flow exceeding expectations; ordering above 40 instruments
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $151M, or $149.4M excluding $1.6M non-recurring settlement revenue, up 3% YoY. Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with double-digit growth in Chromium consumable reaction volumes. The company highlighted exceptionally strong early order flow for the new Atera spatial platform, exceeding the prior 40-instrument guidance, and announced the acquisition of Proteintech Genomics to enhance proteomics capabilities. Management guided to sequential consumables revenue step-down in Q3 due to Atera transition, then a step-up in Q4 largely driven by Atera instrument shipments.

One-time hedge loss from Two Harbors-related hedging, causing equity drain
Two Harbors transaction failed, leading to litigation and a hedge loss
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA over $180 million in Q2, with about $40 billion of business
Equity to increase from $1 billion to roughly $3 billion, non-funding debt-to-equity down to 1.2x
Oaktree partnership seen as strategic, with shared vision on housing and MSR expertise
summary: UWM reported Q2 Adjusted EBITDA over $180 million on about $40 billion of business, with management emphasizing consistent profitability despite a tough mortgage market. The company announced a $2 billion-plus capital raise with Oaktree (including $550 million from Mat Ishbia) and decided to suspend its dividend to retain equity and strengthen the balance sheet. Management acknowledged a one-time hedge loss and a failed Two Harbors MSR acquisition, but positioned the Oaktree partnership as a strategic long-term win. Guidance outlook is forward-looking, with expectations for a significantly better mortgage market in the next few years.

negative_highlights: Capex came in below guidance midpoint due to timing, not full-year change
Galvan divestiture reduces production base, though proceeds used for debt

positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow of $467 million, above expectations
Raised second half production guidance and lowered G&A by $50 million
Reduced net debt by $1.1 billion and redeemed 2027 notes
summary: SM Energy beat expectations in Q2 FY2026, generating $467 million adjusted free cash flow, $1.4 billion adjusted EBITDAX, and $2.19 adjusted EPS. The company raised its second half production outlook, lowered G&A guidance by $50 million, and reduced net debt by $1.1 billion, with 95% of merger synergies actioned. Management emphasized integration progress, buybacks, and a strong balance sheet, positioning 2027 for full earnings power.

Pharmacy channel reached 10% of U.S. sales in first full quarter of PayGo
FDA submission for Mobi Tubeless completed; launch expected in second half
summary: Tandem reported record Q2 sales of $255 million, up 6% YoY, with 33,000 pumps shipped worldwide (10%+ YoY growth). Gross margin improved to 57%, up 5 points YoY, and the company reiterated full-year guidance despite infusion set supply constraints. Pharmacy channel adoption reached 10% of U.S. sales in the first full quarter of PayGo, and management expects continued momentum into 2027 with the Mobi Tubeless launch.

Raised full-year revenue and margin guidance
summary: VSE reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $449 million, up 65% year-over-year with 14% organic growth, and record adjusted EBITDA of $86 million, up 98%, with margin expanding 320 bps to 19.2%. The quarter benefitted from the PAG and NorthStar acquisitions, and management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 61%-64% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.7%-19%. Integration and synergy capture are underway, with leverage at 2.4x and improving cash generation expected in the second half.

negative_highlights: Quiet quarter with limited near-term financial catalysts

positive_highlights: Received upfront Moderna settlement payment of $950 million, with ~$772 million to Genevant

LPP study enrolling extremely well with high enthusiasm
summary: Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2026 with R&D expense of ~$200 million, non-GAAP adjusted G&A just under $100 million, and cash of just under $4 billion before receiving the $772 million Moderna settlement payment. The company is on track for a brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September, with patient enrollment completed in the phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study. Management expects a busy second half with multiple data readouts and remains committed to a slow and steady launch approach. Share repurchases accelerated, with ~$200 million in the quarter at an average price in the high $20s.

Initiated phase II FORGE trial in FSHD.
summary: Scholar Rock's Q2 2026 results show a strong cash position of $492 million, including $63 million from ATM sales, with no revenue or EPS reported since apitegromab is pre-launch. The company has submitted its BLA with two fill-finish facilities, maintaining a September 30 PDUFA date, and has initiated the phase II FORGE trial for FSHD. Enrollment in OPAL is robust, and commercial readiness is advanced.

negative_highlights: Nelson Labs segment income down 0.6% on a constant currency basis
Nelson Labs margin declined versus prior year due to higher costs
Nelson Labs 2026 revenue growth expected only low single digits
positive_highlights: 8% constant currency revenue growth, above guidance

summary: Sotera Health reported strong Q2 2026 results with 8% constant currency revenue growth and 8.7% constant currency adjusted EBITDA growth, beating expectations. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for constant currency revenue growth to 5.25%-6.75% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 5.75%-7.25%, and improved adjusted EPS guidance to $0.95-$1.01. All segments grew, with Sterigenics up 7% cc, Nordion up 16.7% cc, and Nelson Labs up 5.4% cc, and the company reached its target leverage range of 3x. New CEO Alton Shader struck a confident tone, highlighting broad-based momentum and strategic focus on growth.

negative_highlights: CAG GMV declined 1% due to project timing
Q4 retail GMV and revenue expected to decline sequentially

positive_highlights: GAAP EPS up 39% and Adjusted EBITDA up 30% YoY
Record GMV in Retail and GovDeals segments
CAG take rate up 270 bps driving 13% direct profit growth despite GMV decline
summary: Liquidity Services reported strong Q3 FY2026 results with GMV up 10% to a record $453 million, revenue up 8% to $129.6 million, GAAP EPS up 39% to $0.32, and Adjusted EBITDA up 30% to $22 million, marking the 10th consecutive quarter of YoY EBITDA growth. Retail and GovDeals segments achieved record GMV and profitability, while CAG GMV declined 1% but direct profit rose 13% on a 270 bps take rate improvement. Guidance for Q4 projects GMV of $450-$455 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $22-$25 million, positioning FY2026 for the highest annual Adjusted EBITDA in 13 years.

negative_highlights: Latin America organic sales down 3% in Q4
Agriculture vertical remains soft in FY2027 guidance
Oil and gas vertical expected flat in FY2027

FY2026 adjusted EPS up 18% to $32.31, with adjusted segment operating margin up 120 bps to 27.3%

summary: Parker-Hannifin reported record Q4 FY2026 results with sales up 10% (organic up 8%), adjusted segment operating margin up 110 bps to 28.0%, and adjusted EPS up 21% to $9.27. Full-year sales hit $21.5 billion with organic growth of 6.6% and adjusted EPS of $32.31, up 18%. Management raised the long-term margin target to 30% by FY2031 and initiated FY2027 guidance of 7% organic sales growth at the midpoint, with all market verticals guiding positive for the first time. Order rates accelerated across segments, with total orders up 19% on a 3-month basis and Aerospace backlog up 15% to a record $8.5 billion.

negative_highlights: Ravenswood will ramp up toward higher production only after 2028
Cerro Lindo saw a step down in silver contribution in April
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow per share up 42% year-over-year

Fifth consecutive annual dividend increase
summary: Triple Flag reported a strong Q2 with nearly 29,000 GEOs sold, $117 million adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow per share up 42% year-over-year. The company announced a settlement with Steppe Gold, closed the Ravenswood acquisition, raised 2026 guidance to 100,000-110,000 GEOs, and increased its dividend for the fifth consecutive year. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, citing multiple development projects and a strong balance sheet with over $1.1 billion in liquidity.

negative_highlights: Third-quarter per-unit margins expected to be slightly lower due to moderated commodity prices
Full-year capital expenditure now expected toward high end of $850M-$1B range
Crude oil and NGLs throughput expected to decline low double digits for 2026
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $737 million, up 19% year-over-year
Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA midpoint by $250 million
New Powder River Basin agreements add ~270,000 acres with substantial minimum volume commitments
summary: WES reported record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $737 million, up 19% YoY, driven by Delaware Basin throughput, the Brazos acquisition (closed mid-June), and higher commodity prices. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint by $250 million to $2.85 billion, and increased DCF and FCF guidance midpoints by $200 million. Management highlighted new Powder River Basin G&P agreements adding 270,000 dedicated acres with MVCs, and expects increased throughput from customers accelerating activity into H2 2026. Q2 distribution held at $0.93 per unit.

Protocol modification increased enrollment target by 19 patients, potentially adding timeline risk.
No financial performance metrics (revenue, EPS) were disclosed in the transcript.
positive_highlights: Enrollment in pivotal catheter study surpassed halfway point ahead of schedule, targeting early Q4 completion.
Raised $57.5 million net proceeds, ending quarter with over $100 million cash on hand.
EU feasibility data showed 96% freedom from AF at one year and 1.7% serious adverse event rate.
summary: Pulse Biosciences reported Q2 FY2026 results, highlighting significant progress in its nPulse cardiac catheter pivotal study, which surpassed halfway enrollment ahead of schedule and is expected to complete in early October, three months earlier than originally planned. The company raised $57.5 million in net proceeds through an ATM program, ending the quarter with over $100 million cash on hand, and amended its study protocol to increase enrollment target to 164 patients. Vybrance disposable sales rose sequentially to $434,000 from $400,000. Management expressed confidence in the technology's differentiated efficacy and workflow advantages, and announced a partnership with the Clayman Thyroid Center.

Advanced Wound Care net product revenue fell 61% compared to last year

summary: Total revenue declined 58% year-over-year to $42.8 million in Q2 FY26, driven by a 61% drop in Advanced Wound Care sales due to CMS policy changes and market contraction. Management updated its full-year 2026 guidance downward from an expected decline of 45%-52% YoY to a range of 62%-68%, citing a more measured recovery pace than previously anticipated. The company executed two restructurings in Q1/Q2 reducing annual operating expenses by over $32 million, though GAAP net loss widened significantly due to valuation allowance charges.

Early commitments pacing meaningfully ahead of last year; confident in 1M+ lives target
summary: Progyny reported record Q2 2026 revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA, with revenue up 5.3% reported and 11% excluding a former client's transition agreement. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year. Management highlighted strong watching season momentum with early commitments ahead of last year and retention de-risked for 2027, reiterating the target of adding 1 million or more lives. The company announced a new $200 million share repurchase program and continued to generate strong cash flow, with over $50 million in operating cash flow for the fourth time in five quarters.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% constant currency, EPS up 16%
FY2027 guidance above consensus, dividend +10%

summary: ResMed reported Q4 FY2026 revenue growth of 8% constant currency, non-GAAP EPS up 16%, and gross margin expansion. For FY2026, they achieved 10% headline revenue growth, 180bps operating margin expansion, and over $1.6 billion in free cash flow. They announced a 10% dividend increase, accelerated buybacks, and raised FY2027 guidance that beats consensus. The company also closed the Noctrix acquisition, plans to divest MatrixCare, and reaffirmed tariff relief for their products.

summary: Haemonetics reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $339 million, up 6% reported and organic, and adjusted EPS of $1.14, up 4% year-over-year. The company raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to 5%-8% reported and 4%-7% organic, while reaffirming operating margin expansion of 50-100 basis points. MedSurg grew 6%, apheresis grew 6% organic, and interventional technologies returned to 3% organic growth. Free cash flow conversion was 75% for the quarter, with $50 million debt repaid during the quarter and another $50 million after quarter end.

summary: TPL reported record quarterly total revenue of ~$246M, up 31% YoY, with record net income and free cash flow of $156M. Oil and gas royalty production averaged ~39,700 BOE/d, up 20% YoY, and produced water royalty volumes rose 15% YoY. The company reaffirmed FY CapEx guidance of $65-75M and highlighted progress on data center/power initiatives, including a $100M land acquisition in Shackelford/Jones County and completion of a desalination facility. Management expressed confidence in near-term deal announcements despite a sequential decline in water sales volumes due to weak gas prices.

Management guided Q3 revenue to $365-370 million and full-year revenue to $1.460-1.470 billion (narrowed lower at the top end), with Q3 Adjusted EBITDA expected at $70-75 million and full-year at $315-325 million, reflecting continued investments.

The company raised $60 million at $30 per share in May, ending the quarter with $229 million cash and over $367 million in working capital. Management reiterates strong demand and supply constraints through 2027, citing the Drone Dominance Gauntlet and other government programs, but acknowledges infrastructure buildout is needed and that Q3 will not show top-line impact from these investments.

The company reiterated full-year guidance and guided Q3 production above 35 MBOE/d midpoint, with management expressing confidence in the balance sheet and litigation upside.

negative_highlights: Shop occupancy declined 70 bps sequentially to 91.7%, partly due to tenant recaptures.
Same-property leased occupancy down 40 bps year-over-year to 96.3%.
Unexpected Wren Kitchens bankruptcy impacted occupancy, though settlement income was received.
positive_highlights: FFO as adjusted up 10% to $0.40 per share, exceeding internal expectations.
Raised full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 at midpoint to $1.50-$1.54.
New lease cash spreads year-to-date nearly 30% and expected to exceed 20% for the year.
summary: Urban Edge Properties reported a strong Q2 2026 with FFO as adjusted of $0.40 per share, up 10% year-over-year, and same-property NOI growth of 3.2%. The company raised its full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 to $1.50-$1.54 per share and increased the low end of same-property NOI guidance to 3.25%. Leasing activity remains robust with new lease cash spreads of 13% in the quarter and nearly 30% year-to-date, though shop occupancy dipped to 91.7% due to strategic recaptures and the Wren Kitchens bankruptcy. Capital recycling continued with acquisitions in Virginia and Massachusetts funded by asset sales, and management expressed confidence in continued rent growth driven by limited supply and strong demand.

negative_highlights: Sustaining capital at Gibraltar elevated at CAD 48 million in H1 2026
Gibraltar cathode production lower due to SX/EW electrical issues
Florence C1 cost of $4.72/lb not indicative of future; fixed costs high during ramp-up
positive_highlights: Revenue of CAD 331 million was the highest ever for Trekor
Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million
Florence generating positive operating margins and ~CAD 10 million EBITDA in Q2
summary: Trekor reported record revenue of CAD 331 million in Q2 FY2026, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million. Florence produced over 5 million lbs of cathode in its first full production quarter, while Gibraltar produced 30 million lbs; the company maintained annual guidance. Management expressed confidence in ramp-up progress and highlighted strong copper prices and a contracted negative TC of -CAD 140/t for 2027, while noting cost pressures and higher sustaining capital.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital usage
Brokerage gross margin declined 70 bps sequentially due to fuel price headwinds
Last mile expected to weaken in Q3
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $40 million exceeded the high end of outlook
Truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, highest growth in four years
Managed Transportation awarded ~$100 million in freight under management in Q2 and another $100 million in July
summary: RXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $40 million (above the high end of guidance), and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Brokerage volume grew 2% YoY, with truckload spot mix up 900 bps sequentially to 42% and truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, the largest gain in four years. Last mile stops grew 3%, and managed transportation won ~$100 million in freight under management. Management guided to continued brokerage volume and gross profit per load growth in Q3, but expects weakening in last mile. Free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital, expected to convert strongly in Q3.

negative_highlights: Quarter described as 'quiet' with no major business updates
Launch pace for brepocitinib expected to be 'slow and steady'
Continued litigation uncertainty with Pfizer and BioNTech
positive_highlights: Phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study enrollment initiated ahead of schedule
Received $950M upfront payment from Moderna settlement, with $770M to Genevant
Cash position strong at ~$4B before receiving settlement funds
summary: Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2027 with $200M R&D expense, ~$100M non-GAAP G&A, and cash just under $4B before receiving $772M from Moderna's settlement. The company initiated Phase III for cutaneous sarcoidosis ahead of schedule, with top-line data expected in 2028. Management reiterated readiness for brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September and expects a busy second half with multiple readouts. They continue share repurchases, having bought back ~$200M in the quarter at average high-$20s per share.

negative_highlights: Customer environment remains challenging, with persistent pressure on industry foot traffic.
Higher sales force costs are expected to continue for the next couple of quarters, creating a headwind.
Healthcare case volumes eased from Q1 in both one- and two-year stack basis.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to a record $604 million and margin expanded 29 bps to a record 5.7%.
Independent restaurant case growth of 5.1% was the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains.
Pronto sales outlook raised to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates.
summary: US Foods delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $604 million, up 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%. Adjusted EPS grew 21%. Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains. The company raised Pronto sales guidance to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates. Management remains confident in achieving over $300 million in cost savings by 2027, with $50 million already realized in H1 2026.

negative_highlights: Net sales growth of 4.1% was driven by pricing, with volumes slightly lower
Elevated tariff costs (Section 232) and inflation persist, partially offset by refunds
Softer new residential construction activity expected in Q4
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440 bps to a record 27.1%
Raised annual adjusted EBITDA guidance for the third consecutive quarter
WMS adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 650 bps to a record 28.1%
summary: Q3 FY2026 was a record quarter: net sales grew 4.1% to $395.9M, adjusted EBITDA rose 24.3% to a record $107.4M with margin expansion of 440 bps to 27.1%, and adjusted EPS increased 47.1% to $0.50, partly helped by a one-time tax benefit. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $367M-$372M and narrowed net sales growth to 2.8%-3.5%, while lowering SG&A and tax rate guidance. WMS led growth with sales up 10.3% and EBITDA margin up 650 bps to 28.1%, and specialty valves are seeing traction in industrial water/data centers.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS growth in Q4 was only 6.1% due to a lower tax provision in the prior year.
FY2026 EPS was negatively impacted by $120M in additional interest and tax expense.
Revenue guidance includes $500M acquired growth, implying organic growth lower than total.
positive_highlights: Record performance with revenue growth of 17.6% in Q4 and 10.9% for FY2026, exceeding expectations.
EBITDA margin expansion of 110 bps to 12.3% and free cash flow per share up 68%.
Raised fiscal 2027 guidance with revenue growth over 11%, EBITDA margin in high 12% range, and at least $900M free cash flow.
summary: CACI reported Q4 and FY2026 with record revenue, EBITDA margin, and free cash flow. Q4 revenue was $2.7B (+17.6% YoY, 11.6% organic), EBITDA margin 13% (up 150 bps), adjusted EPS $8.91 (+6.1%), and free cash flow $233M. Full-year revenue grew 10.9%, EBITDA margin 12.3%, free cash flow $735M (up 68% per share), and contract awards exceeded $10B. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue growth of 11.3%-13.4%, high-12% EBITDA margin, adjusted EPS of $32.96-$33.86, and free cash flow of at least $900M. Executives highlighted strength in electronic warfare, space, and counter-UAS, with the $500M Domestic Shield award and a classified counterspace win. Leverage reduced to 3.7x and expected to reach low-3s by June 2027.

negative_highlights: NAV declined 10.4% due to the portfolio sale at a 5% discount plus transaction costs
Quarterly NAV fell 2.1% due to markdowns at Pluralsight, PVHC, and Zilliant
Net investment income per share of $0.22 was modest relative to dividend of $0.17
positive_highlights: Net leverage reduced to ~0.4x pro forma, significantly improving financial flexibility
Non-accruals declined to 1.6% at fair value from 2.8% in Q1
Strong repayment activity totaling $111.6 million in Q2
summary: Q2 FY2026 results showed adjusted NII of $0.21 per share, NAV declined 2.1% to $6.58 due to portfolio markdowns, and non-accruals improved to 1.6% at fair value. Management announced a major portfolio sale to a continuation vehicle at a 5% discount, reducing NAV by 10.4% but cutting net leverage to ~0.4x, and initiated a strategic review with KBW. Repayment activity was strong, and the Domo sale is expected to repay $69 million in Q4.

negative_highlights: Reported diluted EPS only $0.09 due to $23 million in charges from fraudulent loan repurchases
Net income down 10% in capital markets segment due to mix shift to brokered lending
Additional $12-16 million expected in Q3 for Fannie Mae review completion
positive_highlights: Transaction volumes up 3% YoY to $14.4 billion, debt financing up 8% to $12.5 billion
Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19, excluding repurchase-related charges
GSE market share up 350 basis points to nearly 15% year to date
summary: Walker & Dunlop's Q2 FY2026 core business grew modestly with transaction volumes up 3% to $14.4 billion and adjusted core EPS up 3% to $1.19, but reported diluted EPS was $0.09 due to $23 million in charges related to fraudulent loan repurchases. Management confirmed Freddie Mac's investigation is complete and expects $12-16 million additional charges in Q3 for Fannie Mae, with no further repurchases expected. Guidance for the year was not formally revised but management expressed confidence in core earnings excluding these charges, with GSE market share up to 15% and $114 billion in remaining GSE capacity.

negative_highlights: Natural gas prices fell significantly due to widening regional differentials
Adjusted G&A increased to $2.7M, though low among peers
Uncertainty around new Cherokee test well and potential stacked pay opportunity
positive_highlights: Revenue up 48% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up 49% YoY
Net income nearly doubled to $27M, driven by 22% oil production growth
Continued shareholder returns with $5.05 per share in dividends since 2023
summary: SandRidge reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 48% YoY to $51M, adjusted EBITDA up 49% to $34M, and net income of $27M ($0.72/share). Production grew 11% YoY (22% oil growth), driven by higher oil prices and the Cherokee drilling program. The company announced a bolt-on acquisition in the Cherokee Play, continues to pay dividends, and maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt. Guidance for 2026 remains intact with $76-97M capex and 10 wells planned.

negative_highlights: Europe delivered only mid-single-digit growth, with traffic pressured by macro and tourism slowdown
Full-year outlook remains prudent on Europe due to macroeconomic uncertainty
Tariff and higher labor/material costs partially offset margin expansion
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 13%, ahead of mid to high single-digit outlook
Gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%
Full-year outlook raised after Q1 over-delivery
summary: Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, exceeding the mid-to-high single-digit outlook, with Asia up 25%, North America up 13%, and Europe up 5%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%, and AUR increased 15%. The company raised its full-year outlook while maintaining caution on Europe due to macro uncertainty. New customer acquisition was 1.5 million in DTC, and core product sales grew mid-teens.

negative_highlights: Content licensing revenue experienced lumpiness and was a drag in Q2
Traditional search-driven traffic continues to decline, impacting digital ad revenue
Digital revenue mix slightly ticked down to 47.4% in Q2
positive_highlights: Digital-only ARPU reached another record high, increasing 34% year-over-year
Free cash flow increased 11% year-over-year to approximately $20 million
Second consecutive quarter of positive net income and digital-only subscription revenue growth
summary: USA TODAY Co. reported Q2 2026 with positive net income for a second consecutive quarter, $20 million free cash flow (up 11% year-over-year), and record digital-only ARPU (up 34% year-over-year). Digital-only subscription revenue grew for the second consecutive quarter and digital other revenue also grew, but content licensing was lumpy and search-driven traffic declined. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, expecting improved revenue trends, EBITDA and margin expansion, and fourth consecutive year of free cash flow growth, with a goal of becoming majority digital in the back half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Marketing optimization expected to be a headwind in Q3 vs Q2
G&P results slightly offset by commodity price sensitivity
Still some price-related shut-ins returning in Q3
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 38% year-over-year, record quarter
Permian volumes up 450 MMcf/d sequentially, tracking ahead of expectations
Guidance raised to top end of range; dividend up 25%
summary: Targa Resources reported record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.603 billion, up 14% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, driven by record Permian volumes of 7.2 Bcf/d, record NGL transportation and fractionation volumes, and record LPG exports. Management raised expectations to the top end of the $5.7-$5.9 billion full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range, suggesting near $1 billion growth over 2025. Marketing optimization outperformed by ~$250 million in H1, though some of that is expected to moderate in H2. Dividend increased 25% to $1.25 per share, with $80 million of buybacks in Q2.

negative_highlights: Full-year royalty revenue guidance lowered to a range of $19-22M from the prior expectation of $20-23M due to potential generic market share thresholds in China
Commercial new patient starts declined 6% quarter-over-quarter despite overall demand growth
positive_highlights: Net product revenue increased quarter-over-quarter by $11.6M driven by higher demand and inventory decrease of approximately $1.3 million
Full-year 2026 net income guidance raised to a range of $17-20 million, exceeding the prior expectation of $16-19 million
Company is now debt-free after making its final quarterly principal loan payment of $11.1 million
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2026 net product revenue of $53.6 million (up from $42M in Q1) and GAAP EPS of $0.16 per share, turning a loss to profit driven by demand growth and inventory drawdowns. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for net NERLYNX revenue ($205-209M vs prior $202-206M) and net income ($17-20M vs prior $16-19M), while slightly lowering royalty expectations due to potential generic competition in China. The company is now debt-free following a loan payoff, with R&D expenses increasing significantly as Phase II trials for alisertib progress.

negative_highlights: Occupancy in July was down 65 bps year-over-year
Move-in rates per square foot were down 4.4% on average
L.A. fire ECRI restrictions impacted seven properties, with -2% same-store revenue growth in Q2
positive_highlights: FFO as adjusted per share up 17.6% year-over-year, beating expectations
Same-store operating margins up 150 bps year-over-year, second consecutive quarter of margin improvement
Raised full-year guidance for same-store revenue, NOI, and FFO per share
summary: SmartStop Self Storage reported Q2 FY2026 FFO per share of $0.49, up 17.6% year-over-year, with same-store NOI growth of 3.7% and 150 bps margin expansion. The company raised its full-year same-store revenue and NOI guidance and FFO guidance to $1.98-$2.04 per share, citing better-than-expected momentum. They also introduced the Deca Initiative, aiming for a $10 billion capitalization level, and increased capital deployment guidance to $55-$75 million. Management expressed confidence in the acquisition pipeline and recovery from L.A. fire restrictions.

negative_highlights: CMS may delay shared savings cash settlement until November, affecting year-end cash flow timing
Guidance implies significant deceleration in practice collections growth in 2H (from ~13% to ~3%)
Full cash taxpayer status expected to limit free cash flow conversion to 70-80% of EBITDA
positive_highlights: Practice collections up 12.4% year-over-year to $970 million
Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% and margin expanded 310 basis points
Raised 2026 guidance across practice collections, care margin, and EBITDA
summary: Privia Health reported strong Q2 results: practice collections grew 12.4% to $970 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $37.4 million with margin expanding 310 bps to 28.3% of care margin. Implemented providers grew 10.1% and attributed lives grew 19.2%. The company raised its 2026 guidance across most metrics, citing strong first-half performance. Management remains confident in long-term growth and margin expansion, despite minor CMS cash timing delays.

negative_highlights: Revenue per episode decreased 1.9% as expected due to Southeast mix
Senior living margins face lumpiness in Q3/Q4 from new acquisitions
Hospice faces administrative costs from new program integrity measures
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 35.8% to $298M, beating prior year
Adjusted EBITDA grew 48.2% to $24.3M
Guidance raised for full-year revenue and adjusted EPS
summary: Q2 2026 showed strong results with revenue up 35.8% to $298M and adjusted EBITDA up 48.2% to $24.3M, driven by acquisitions and operational excellence. Adjusted EPS rose 33.3% to $0.36. Management raised full-year guidance, citing momentum and better-than-expected acquisition transitions. Home health and hospice segments delivered strong same-store growth, while senior living showed stable improvements.

negative_highlights: APT spreads narrowed significantly beginning in late June due to earlier-than-expected takeaway capacity
O&M guidance raised to $875-$885 million
Management expects to be at lower end of $0.08-$0.12 APT second-half range
positive_highlights: Year-to-date EPS up 14.5% to $7.33
Added nearly 51,000 customers over 12 months, with 12 new industrial customers equivalent to 18,000 residential customers
Rate increases contributed $227 million to operating income
summary: Atmos Energy reported fiscal 2026 YTD EPS of $7.33, up 14.5% year-over-year, and reaffirmed full-year EPS guidance of $8.40-$8.50. Strong rate increases and customer growth drove operating income, but APT spreads narrowed sharply in late June/July as new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected, leading management to guide toward the lower end of the $0.08-$0.12 second-half APT range. O&M guidance was raised to $875-$885 million, and capital spending remains on track at ~$4.2 billion.

negative_highlights: Comparable sales declined 6.2% in Q2
Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $0.2 million
Q3 guidance lowered due to Cyclospora outbreak impact
positive_highlights: Transaction comps improved sequentially each month, flat in June
Wraps drove 200 basis points comp uplift and ~500 basis points transaction improvement
New York and Seattle returned to positive transaction comps in Q2
summary: Sweetgreen reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $192.7 million, up ~4% YoY, but comparable restaurant sales declined 6.2%, with adjusted EBITDA near breakeven at a loss of $0.2 million. Management noted sequential monthly improvement in transactions, with flat transaction comps in June, but flagged the impact of a Cyclospora outbreak and a jalapeno recall on outlook. Guidance for Q3 was lowered, reflecting recovery assumptions, and the company emphasized disciplined investment and menu innovation like wraps, which lifted transactions but created a check drag.

negative_highlights: Colombia subscriber figures include normalization effect from reporting harmonization
Chile remains highly competitive with aggressive pricing and elevated churn
Q2 EFCF benefited from timing; management cautioned on H2 forecasting
positive_highlights: Service revenue $2B, +5% organic YoY, strongest since 2021
Adjusted EBITDA $1B, first time above $1B in a quarter
Guidance raised: EFCF from ≥$900M to ~$1.1B, leverage below 2.5x
summary: Millicom delivered record Q2 FY2026 results: service revenue of $2 billion, up 5% organically YoY (strongest since 2021) and 60.1% reported; adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion (first time surpassing that milestone) with organic growth of 9.1% YoY; record equity free cash flow of $327 million, up 50%+ YoY. Management raised FY2026 equity free cash flow guidance from at least $900 million to around $1.1 billion and improved the year-end leverage target to below 2.5x. The board approved an additional interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in two installments.

negative_highlights: Combined non-political advertising down 5.8% YoY
TEGNA distribution revenue declined on subscriber losses, partially offset by rate growth
Litigation and regulatory overhang continue with trial scheduled for July 2027
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $1.99B, up 62.2% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA $633M, free cash flow more than doubled to $238M
Reiterated confidence in record 2026 financial performance
summary: Nexstar reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $1.99 billion, up 62.2% YoY (including TEGNA), with adjusted EBITDA of $633 million and free cash flow of $238 million, more than doubling YoY. Advertising revenue grew 81.5% to $862 million, driven by TEGNA and political, while combined non-political advertising fell 5.8%. The company reaffirmed legacy distribution guidance, raised no forward revenue targets, and remains focused on debt repayment, having repaid $409 million in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Scrap margin declined to 26% from 38% sequentially, with normalization expected toward 15-20%
Gold price volatility and stabilization noted as a headwind to scrap profitability
Expenses rising sequentially due to growth initiatives and minimum wage increases
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 48% to $65.6 million, EPS up 47% to $0.47
Core pawn revenue up 24%, core pawn gross profit up 28%
PLO at record $382 million, up 31%; Latin America PLO up 33%
summary: EZCORP reported a strong fiscal Q3 2026 with adjusted EBITDA up 48% to $65.6 million and adjusted diluted EPS up 47% to $0.47. Core pawn revenues grew 24% and core pawn gross profit rose 28%, with same-store core pawn gross profit up 13%. Latin America and SMG contributed significant growth, and management raised no formal guidance but expressed confidence in continued momentum. Scrap margins normalized sequentially as expected, and the company completed full ownership of SMG.

negative_highlights: CW laser production success not yet declared; process still being locked down
Utilization rates driving longer lead times for internally manufactured products
Mix shift from small laser devices could pressure profitability near term
positive_highlights: Record book-to-bill of 1.6 to 1 and highest quarterly bookings ever
All three end markets grew sequentially; data center up ~40% and at record revenue
Gross margin expanded 120 bps to 59.7%
summary: MACOM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $342.2 million, up 18.4% sequentially and 35.8% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $1.40. All end markets grew sequentially, led by data center (up ~40%) to $137.6 million, with I&D and telecom also up. Book-to-bill was a record 1.6:1, and gross margin expanded 120 bps to 59.7%. The company expects continued growth with data center and defense strength, launching CW laser production potentially in late calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: TV revenue and segment profit declined due to timing of episodic deliveries
Reported diluted loss per share of $0.10
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% YoY to $777 million
Motion picture segment profit reached $105 million, a record first quarter
Leverage improved to 4.3x, hitting target earlier than anticipated
summary: Lionsgate Studios reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $777 million, up 48% year-over-year, with adjusted OIBDA of $79 million and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Motion picture revenue more than doubled to $587 million, driven by Michael and The Housemaid, achieving record first-quarter segment profit. The company hit its mid-4x leverage target early, ending net debt at $1.5 billion, and reaffirmed fiscal 2027 growth outlook, citing a $1.5 billion backlog and upcoming Hunger Games release. TV revenue declined on timing but management expects significant growth later in the year.

negative_highlights: Gross margin decreased 60 basis points to 29.3% due to mix, shrink, and freight
Adjusted EBITDA decreased 7.6% to $22.5 million including a $2 million insurance recovery
FY2026 comp sales guidance lowered to 1.5%-2% from 1.5%-2.5%
positive_highlights: Daily comparable store sales growth accelerated to 1.2% from 0.5% in Q2
Opened six stores YTD with record opening day sales, including second-best ever in Wisconsin
Npower penetration increased 200 basis points to 84% of net sales
summary: Natural Grocers reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $334.7 million, up 1.8% YoY, with daily comparable store sales growth of 1.2%, accelerating from 0.5% in Q2. Gross margin declined 60 basis points to 29.3% due to mix, shrink, and freight, and adjusted EBITDA fell 7.6% to $22.5 million. EPS was $0.48, down from $0.50, and guidance for FY2026 comp sales and EPS was narrowed/lowered. The company opened three stores in Q3, including its first in Wisconsin, and launched a DoorDash partnership.

negative_highlights: Trading gains down $14.8 million year-over-year due to lower fair value on Babcock & Wilcox investment
Other income excluding interest expense fell to $8 million from $88 million in Q2 2025
Targus consumer products segment reported a $6 million loss in Q2
positive_highlights: Operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, best core operating quarter in nearly three years
Debt reduced by $497 million since December 2024, net debt down to $285 million
Added five senior producers and reactivated key institutional accounts
summary: BRC Group reported Q2 2026 net income of $18.5 million and operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, the best core operating quarter in nearly three years. Total revenues were $239 million, up $14 million year-over-year, driven by a $30 million increase in management fees from carried interest in SpaceX funds. The company reduced total debt by $497 million since December 2024 to $1.277 billion, with net debt down $87 million to $285 million. Management highlighted reactivated institutional accounts, a strong capital markets pipeline, and expects to comfortably cover $306 million in upcoming senior note maturities with cash and investments.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $33.6 million in Q2.
Results weighed by $10.7 million acquisition-related costs.
ASM acquisition closing subject to final procedures.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $25M from uranium with 57% gross margin.
Conditional $725 million loan from Office of Strategic Capital announced.
Uranium inventory cost declined to $33.92/lb from ~$36/lb Q1.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $25 million from uranium, with a 57% gross margin and production cost of $23/lb. Net loss of $33.6 million included $10.7 million in transaction costs. Management highlighted conditional $725 million government loan, progress on ASM acquisition closing late August, and announced VAC acquisition expected to close early 2027. Continued investment in rare earth expansion and maintained strong balance sheet with ~$1 billion liquidity.

negative_highlights: Pull-ahead of $25-30 million masks underlying mid-single-digit organic growth
Material costs expected to be significant year-over-year headwind for remainder of year
Residential demand performing modestly worse than anticipated; organic residential sales flat
positive_highlights: Record first-quarter revenue above $1 billion, up 21% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 230 bps to 35.8%, second highest in history
Stormwater storage products grew 18% in the quarter
summary: ADS reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1 billion, up 21% YoY, with organic growth of 9% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35.8%, the second highest in company history. Results benefited from $25-30 million of demand pulled forward ahead of price increases; excluding that, organic growth was mid-single digits. Management maintained full-year guidance of $3.35-3.55 billion sales and $1.0-1.05 billion EBITDA, citing dynamic inflation and a tepid demand environment. Non-residential end markets beat expectations, while residential demand was modestly worse.

negative_highlights: Issued policies declined 12% YoY, full-year expected down mid-single digits
New life licenses still below prior year levels
Expense growth expected to accelerate to 10%-12% in Q3
positive_highlights: ISP revenues up 21%, pre-tax income up 31% YoY
AUM reached record $140 billion, up 16% YoY with $397 million net inflows
Adjusted operating EPS up 17% to $6.41
summary: Primerica reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating revenues up 8% YoY and adjusted net operating income up 11%, with adjusted operating EPS up 17% to $6.41 including a $0.15 tax benefit. The ISP segment grew revenues 21% and pre-tax income 31%, with record AUM of $140 billion and $397 million in net inflows. Term Life premiums grew 3.4% but issued policies declined 12%, and the company guided full-year issued policies down mid-single digits. Management raised ISP sales guidance to 10%-15% growth for 2026, while maintaining full-year expense growth of 7%-8%.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 22% YoY
Net loss $171 million including $103 million deferred tax allowance
Second quarter costs included planned outages and Middle East related input costs
positive_highlights: TiO2 volumes at highest level since Q2 2022, high end of guidance
Sequential price improvement of 5% for TiO2 and zircon, driven by base pricing
Recommendation to reinstate India anti-dumping duties on Chinese TiO2
summary: Tronox reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $868 million, up 19% YoY, driven by strong TiO2 and zircon volumes, with TiO2 volumes at the high end of guidance and zircon exceeding expectations. Adjusted EBITDA was $73 million, down 22% YoY due to exchange headwinds, pricing, and costs, but within guided range. Pricing improved sequentially for both TiO2 and zircon, and the company expects further sequential price increases and EBITDA of $95-$115 million in Q3, with positive full-year free cash flow. Management highlighted anti-dumping progress, including India and a context reinstatement of duties on Chinese TiO2, and noted cost headwinds from Middle East conflict and input costs.

negative_highlights: Moody's negative outlook persists, though management expects improvement
Batch Zero timeline is uncertain and may extend beyond February 2027
positive_highlights: Q2 adjusted EPS rose 30% YoY to $1.16
Oncor's incremental capital opportunities firming with $10 billion upside
summary: Sempra reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16, up from $0.89 in Q2 2025, with GAAP EPS of $1.21. The company affirmed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30 and 2027 guidance of $5.10-$5.70, along with long-term EPS growth of 7%-9%. Management highlighted strong Texas demand, with 44 GW of Batch Zero load requests (140% increase over current peak), and Oncor's incremental capital opportunities totaling $10 billion.
