Over $1.4 billion in closed acquisitions YTD, $800 million locked up, all expected to close by year-end
summary: Q2 FY2026 was exceptionally strong with total portfolio same-store NOI growth of 13.2% year-over-year and 12.7% for the first six months. Same-store occupancy held at 90.7% for Trilogy and SHOP same-store NOI grew 20.5% year-over-year. Management increased full-year guidance and highlighted over $1.4 billion in closed acquisitions year-to-date with $800 million more expected by year-end, none of which is reflected in revised guidance. Net debt to EBITDA stood at 2.5x, indicating continued deleveraging.

negative_highlights: Increased variability among portfolio companies, with some struggling more than expected
Some companies are being more conservative with dividend income due to economic uncertainty
Lower middle market investments decreased by $31 million due to elevated repayment activity
positive_highlights: Annualized ROE of 18.9% in Q2 2026
Realized gain of over $46 million from Centre Technologies exit
Supplemental dividend of $0.30 per share and regular dividend increased 3.9%
summary: Main Street Capital reported strong Q2 2026 results with an annualized ROE of 18.9%, significant NAV per share increase driven by net fair value gains, and another material realized gain from the Centre Technologies exit of over $46 million. The company declared a $0.30 supplemental dividend and raised regular monthly dividends by 3.9% to $0.265 per share for Q4 2026. Management remains optimistic about future realizations and portfolio growth, though notes increased variability among portfolio companies and a cautious dividend income outlook from some companies.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 2.7% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA declined 3.7% YoY
Tech & Shopping declines persist due to search AIO headwinds
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 13% YoY, driven by reduced share count
Stock up approximately 45% YTD and 65% over the past year
AI-authored code doubled; 24% more code shipped on lower headcount
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 2.7% YoY to $286.7M, slightly better than expected, while adjusted EBITDA fell 3.7% to $76.8M, with margins of 26.8%, an improvement from prior guidance. Adjusted EPS grew 13.2% to $1.03 due to aggressive buybacks. The company completed the sale of its connectivity business for $1.2B, expects to pay ~$200M in taxes and repay $149M in convertible debt, and continues to repurchase stock. AI-authored code roughly doubled and now over half of new code, while Tech & Shopping revenue decline improved to -5% from -13% in Q1.

negative_highlights: Additional $44 million losses on Gordie Howe project
Operating cash flow negative $317 million due to tax payment
Legacy project funding remains, with $94 million future funding expected
positive_highlights: Revenue up 9% YoY to $4.3 billion
Adjusted EBITDA up to $149 million from $96 million
New awards over $6 billion, backlog nearly $27 billion
summary: Fluor reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 9% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up to $149 million from $96 million and adjusted EPS of $0.91 versus $0.43. New awards exceeded $6 billion, backlog grew to $26.9 billion, and management raised expectations for full-year book-to-bill above 1. The quarter included $44 million in additional losses on the Gordie Howe project, and guidance implies a small step-up in second-half EBITDA, with most of it already in backlog.

negative_highlights: Q2 Adjusted EBITDA declined to $72M from $76.9M year-over-year.
Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes declined 0.9%.
Credit card fees increased $3.3M due to elevated fuel prices.
positive_highlights: First-half Adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $123M.
Merchandise margin expanded 110 bps to 34.7%.
USPP acquisition expected to add ~$30M annual Adjusted EBITDA and be accretive upon closing.
summary: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $72M, down from $76.9M in the prior year, but first-half Adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $123M. Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes fell 0.9% while merchandise margin expanded 110 bps to 34.7%. Announced a strategic acquisition by subsidiary APC to acquire U.S. Petroleum Partners for $205M plus $30M in earnout stock, expected to add ~280 million gallons and ~$30M annual Adjusted EBITDA, closing later this year. Management reiterated confidence despite a challenging consumer and fuel price environment.

negative_highlights: adjusted EPS growth only 1% due to share issuance
increased depreciation, amortization, and property tax expenses negatively affected EPS
customer growth slowing from peak levels
positive_highlights: adjusted net income up 5%, adjusted EPS up 5% for the quarter
capital guidance increased by $100 million to $550-$600 million
announced $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project, largest in company history
summary: Chesapeake Utilities reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income up 5% and adjusted EPS of $1.05, also up 5% year-over-year (1% EPS increase). The company raised full-year 2026 capital guidance by $100 million to $550-$600 million and announced the $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project. Management reaffirmed long-term growth and expects to provide 2027-2031 capital and earnings guidance in February 2027. Customer growth remains above national averages but showed signs of slowdown.

negative_highlights: Facing headwind from higher lube oil prices in the quarter, costing roughly $1.5 million per month
Power Infrastructure margins expected to improve as legacy business is repriced, implying current levels are below target
Only 50% contracted for 2027 compression deliveries, with 2028 contracting just beginning
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $217 million, up 22% year-over-year, a new company record
Compression Infrastructure adjusted gross margin at 70%, up 170 bps year-over-year, second consecutive quarter at or above 70%
Raised full-year adjusted EBITDA, margin, and discretionary cash flow guidance
summary: Kodiak Gas Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $391 million, up 21% year-over-year, and record adjusted EBITDA of $217 million, up 22%. Compression Infrastructure grew revenue 7% year-over-year with adjusted gross margin of 70% and fleet utilization at 98.2%. The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA, margin, and cash flow guidance reflecting improved visibility. Power Infrastructure segment generated $33 million revenue with 64.5% margin, and management highlighted a growing project pipeline, including a limited notice to proceed for a West Texas data center supply deal.

negative_highlights: Traditional premiums grew only 0.9% constant currency due to in-force management actions
Other one-time items contributed $0.83 per share, partially masking underlying earnings power
Exposure to capped cohorts reduced by 25%, reflecting actions that lower current premiums
positive_highlights: Record pre-tax adjusted operating income of $761 million, or $8.89 per share
Strong investment results: new money yield 6.02% and VII annualized return 15%
Raising dividend by 5.4% and maintaining $2.2 billion excess capital
summary: RGA reported a record second quarter 2026 with pre-tax adjusted operating income of $761 million or $8.89 per share, driven by strong investment income and favorable claims. New money yield was 6.02% above portfolio yield of 4.96%, and VII returned 15% annualized, well above the 7% plan. Management raised the dividend by 5.4% and affirmed the 8%-10% EPS growth and 13%-15% ROE intermediate-term targets, expressing confidence in meeting or exceeding them.

negative_highlights: LOE per BOE increased to $10.27 from $9.57 in Q1, prompting higher full-year guidance
Waha basis hit record low, with gas realization of $1.12 per Mcf
Annual production volumes now expected at the lower end of guidance due to timing
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDAx increased to $79.6 million from $75.4 million a year ago
Added 21.9 net undeveloped locations at entry costs supporting returns above 25% threshold
Gas realizations expected to improve as Permian takeaway capacity ramps, with Q3 gas sales projected above $30 million
summary: Granite Ridge reported Q2 2026 production of 32,044 BOE/d and Adjusted EBITDA of $79.6 million, up from $75.4 million a year ago. GAAP EPS was $0.23, up from $0.19, while adjusted EPS was $0.09. Guidance for full-year LOE was raised to $8.25-$9.25 per BOE, and production is expected to trend toward the lower end of the range. Management reiterated its 2027 free cash flow inflection with strong exit production nearing 40,000 BOE/d and improving gas realizations.

negative_highlights: NII declined to $0.45 per share from $0.47, with non-accruals and higher financing costs as drags
Non-accruals increased to 2.9% of portfolio at cost with three new names
NAV per share remains within 2.5% of inception NAV, pressured by mark-to-market on underperformers
positive_highlights: Approximately 95% of the portfolio performing in line with underwriting case
JV accretion contributed $0.03 and is expected to grow
Share repurchases added $0.05 to NAV per share during the quarter
summary: In Q2 FY2026, MSDL reported net investment income (NII) of $0.45 per share, down from $0.47 in the prior quarter, and declared a dividend of $0.45 per share. The decline was driven by new non-accruals (three credits added) and higher financing costs, partially offset by Capstone JV accretion. Credit quality remained stable with ~95% of the portfolio risk-rated 2 or better, but non-accruals rose to 2.9% of portfolio at cost. Management expressed confidence in the dividend level and expects the JV to ramp, but acknowledged persistent market headwinds.

negative_highlights: Q2 adjusted EPS down CAD 0.10 year-over-year
New Mexico Gas earnings lower due to higher O&M and depreciation
Higher corporate interest expense from temporarily carrying both new and maturing financing
positive_highlights: Year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.06 consistent with last year's very strong performance
Approval and expected close of New Mexico Gas sale with $650-$700 million after-tax proceeds
Operating cash flow up 8% excluding working capital
summary: Emera reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of CAD 0.69, down CAD 0.10 year-over-year, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.06, consistent with last year. The company is on track for compound annual adjusted EPS growth above the 5%-7% target through 2026 and within that range through 2030. The New Mexico Gas sale received regulatory approval and is expected to close later this month, with after-tax proceeds of CAD 650-700 million. Management highlighted strong performance at Peoples Gas and progress on data center opportunities in Tampa Electric, while noting lower earnings at New Mexico Gas and higher corporate interest costs.

negative_highlights: Leisure room availability constrained by strong group mix and renovations.
Guidance for ice! remains conservative due to limited visibility.
Back-half RevPAR growth expected to be occupancy-driven, impacting flow-through.
positive_highlights: Same-store hospitality beat expectations with ~$7M adjusted EBITDAre outperformance.
Group ADR up 7.5% YoY, ~3 points above expectations.
Entertainment adjusted EBITDAre up nearly 30% YoY to a new quarterly record.
summary: Ryman Hospitality reported another standout quarter with same-store RevPAR and total RevPAR exceeding expectations by ~2.5 points each, and adjusted EBITDAre outperforming by ~$7 million. Group ADR grew 7.5% YoY, catering contribution per group room night rose nearly 13%, and bookings for future periods hit a record ADR of ~$310. Management raised the midpoints of full-year guidance for same-store hospitality by $10 million and JW Desert Ridge by $1 million, and remains on track for 2027 targets. The entertainment segment posted record adjusted EBITDAre, up nearly 30% YoY.

negative_highlights: SG&A up to $103.1M from $93.4M due to commissions and FX
Q3 gross margin guidance of ~40.8% implies sequential decline
No additional tariff refunds assumed in guidance
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 47% to $0.88, above prior year
Adjusted gross margin up 524 bps to 45%
Raised full-year guidance on strong orders and backlog
summary: Interface reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with currency-neutral net sales up 4% YoY, exceeding expectations, and adjusted EPS of $0.88, up 47%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 524 basis points to 45%, partly from $15.6 million in tariff refunds and operational improvements. Management raised full-year guidance, citing strong order momentum (orders up 5% currency-neutral) and backlog up 22% year-to-date. Healthcare billings grew 19% on top of 28% prior-year growth.

negative_highlights: Unrealized losses in corporate other due to lower debt spreads and higher rates
Recourse borrowing rate unchanged at 5.5%, but overall debt-to-equity rose to 9.2:1
Agency MBS now a smaller part of portfolio, reflecting rotation away from that strategy
positive_highlights: GAAP EPS of $0.43 and ADE of $0.60 per share, well above dividend
Annualized economic return of 13.6% and book value increased
Longbridge originations up 38% year-over-year with record prop reverse volumes
summary: Ellington Financial reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with GAAP net income of $0.43 per share and adjusted distributable earnings of $0.60 per share, exceeding the dividend. Book value increased and annualized economic return was 13.6%. Longbridge originations rose 38% year-over-year, with record proprietary reverse mortgage volumes and strong securitization execution. The company maintained momentum with portfolio growth, expanding credit hedges, and a pending acquisition, while also enhancing disclosures.

negative_highlights: MFS continued elevated outflows due to industry pressure
New business CSM margin dipped due to competitive pricing
Medicaid membership down 9% from deliberate contract exits
positive_highlights: Underlying EPS up 13% to CAD 2.02, above 10% target
Canada record underlying net income up 23%
Asia underlying net income up 21% and sales up 20%
summary: Sun Life reported strong Q2 2026 results with underlying EPS up 13% to CAD 2.02, above their 10% medium-term target, and underlying ROE at 19.1% approaching the 20% target. Record Canada earnings (up 23%), strong Asia growth (up 21%, sales up 20%), and U.S. improvement (underlying up 15%) drove performance. Management raised no guidance but reinforced medium-term targets, noting margin expansion expected in asset management and continued progress in dental and MFS outflows.

negative_highlights: Lapping headwinds from AWS and Dayforce total approximately $19M over next four quarters
FDE hiring costs initially will hit R&D before revenue generation, pressuring margins near-term
Healthcare vertical investment will follow government playbook, implying multi-quarter ramp before returns
positive_highlights: Second consecutive quarter of ARR re-acceleration, with broad-based strength
Enterprise pipeline and >$500K deals growing strongly, FedRAMP opportunity significant in Q3
365Talents integration exceeding pipe targets, enabling wins like largest telecom and automotive safety supplier
summary: Docebo reported Q2 2026 with ARR re-acceleration for the second consecutive quarter, driven by broad-based strength across net new, expansion, and international. Management expressed high confidence in second-half acceleration, supported by lapping AWS and Dayforce headwinds (approx. $19M over next four quarters) and a strong FedRAMP pipeline. The company is investing in a foundational FDE team for agentic workflows and a healthcare vertical, following the prior government playbook. Cash position is $45M with $90M debt, and the SIB is expected to have minimal share tenders at current stock price; no major acquisitions planned in next 12 months.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered to $158-$162 million
Engineering orders delayed or lost, including a coating line order due to Tesla litigation concerns
Memorialization hit by record-low death rates and escalating input costs (copper, steel, fuel)
positive_highlights: Memorialization nine-month adjusted EBITDA up 4.4% to $130 million
Strong customer interest in DBE testing and new mass production machine
Strategic partnership with Linx to expand Axian product reach
summary: Matthews International reported a difficult Q3 FY2026 with adjusted EBITDA guidance cut to $158-$162 million, citing engineering order delays, softer memorialization volumes, higher input costs, and Propelis synergy delays. Revenue in Memorialization was $208 million, up 2.1% YoY, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $42.2 million from $42.8 million. The company returned $25 million of Propelis preferred equity and announced a strategic partnership with Linx Printing Technologies, while evaluating strategic alternatives for OLBRICH and expecting DBE-related ramp in 2027.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow negative $23 million in Q2
North American volumes expected lower in H2 due to Riverdale loss and Eastover outage
Middle East conflict pressuring energy, chemicals, and transportation costs
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled sequentially to $60 million
Price and mix favorability of $32 million in Q2, with more realization expected
Eastover projects expected to deliver $55 million annual benefits
summary: Sylvamo's Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA roughly doubled sequentially to $60 million, with a 7% margin and adjusted operating earnings of $0.03 per share, but free cash flow remained negative at -$23 million. Management guided to a significant second-half improvement with $75-$85 million benefit from price and mix, but lowered expectations for North American volumes due to Riverdale supply loss and a longer Eastover outage, and cited ongoing Middle East conflict cost pressures. Eastover strategic investments remain on schedule and are expected to generate $55 million in annual benefits by 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue outlook lowered due to softer demand in North America and APAC
North America revenue declined 9% with wholesale and DTC pressure
Traffic softened from late May across key regions
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income exceeded outlook
EMEA revenue increased 12% (10% constant currency) driven by distributor strength
Bouncy Tee exceeded expectations at full $65 retail price
summary: Under Armour reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.1 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with North America down 9% and APAC down 7% (constant currency down 10%), while EMEA grew 12% and Latin America grew 8%. Adjusted operating income exceeded outlook despite the revenue miss. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook but maintained adjusted operating income expectations, citing softer consumer demand and a more promotional marketplace. SKU reductions and full-price product launches like the Bouncy Tee were highlighted as progress, though the tone was cautious.

negative_highlights: Permian competition intense; bid outs at nearly 2x paid prices
MidCon rig count down 24% due to weak natural gas prices
Gas-weighted basins like Haynesville saw production decline 11%
positive_highlights: Record revenues surpassed $100 million for the first time
Distribution increased 15% to $0.47 per unit
Closed Mesa acquisition and announced second drop-down
summary: Kimbell Royalty Partners reported a record Q2 2026 with oil, natural gas, and NGL revenues exceeding $100 million for the first time, and record consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $84.9 million. Average daily production hit 25,830 BOE/d, with run-rate increasing to 26,967 BOE/d after the Mesa acquisition. Distribution raised 15% to $0.47 per unit, and guidance for 2026 is affirmed, with an update expected after the drop-down acquisition closes. Management remains active in M&A, noting Permian competition is intense but that they are selective and disciplined.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue declined 13.6% YoY due to collection timing.
Revenue per visit normalized down from prior-year peak.
In-network progress remains slight and not material.
positive_highlights: Net income surged 3,100% to $112.6M in H1 2026.
Same-hospital visits grew 6.3% in Q2 2026.
Cash flow from operations up 40% to $109.7M.
summary: Nutex Health reported H1 2026 revenue of $427.2M, down 6% YoY, with net income jumping to $112.6M from $3.5M, driven by lower arbitration costs and the HaloMD amendment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 2% to $147.5M and cash flow from operations increased 40% to $109.7M. Q2 same-hospital visits grew 6.3%, but total revenue fell 13.6% due to collection timing and prior-year IDR adjustments. Management is optimistic about legal rulings and the CMS final rule, while in-network progress remains slight. Pipeline expansions are planned for late 2026 and 2027.

negative_highlights: Recorded $1.1 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge on the Scripps Networks business due to linear viewing trends and Nielsen methodology changes.
Local media distribution revenue declined 13% year-over-year due to service blackout periods during negotiations with Comcast (March-May) and DIRECTV (May-July).
Scripps Networks revenue down 13%, attributed partly to a sudden change in Nielsen measurement methodology which management estimates impacted about 50% of the reported softness.
positive_highlights: Signed first NBA agreement with Detroit Pistons and NHL partnership with Nashville Predators, adding material value to core advertising revenue.
Completed station swap with Gray Media expanding presence in the Mountain West and acquired a second Big Four station for Lexington duopoly.
Successfully renewed 70% of paid TV subscriber households following carriage disputes with Comcast and DIRECTV.
summary: The E.W. Scripps Company reported a Q2 loss of $12.68 per share driven by a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $1.1 billion and restructuring costs of $36 million. Revenue declined across segments, with Local Media down 1% to $317M due to carriage disputes affecting distribution revenue (-13%) and Networks down 13%. Management raised the annualized run-rate savings target for their transformation plan from prior guidance to $100 million by year-end.

negative_highlights: Catastrophe losses of $50M, including $46M from Middle East conflict
Combined ratio deteriorated to 95% from 86.8% year-over-year
Bermuda casualty deep dive resulted in $16M reserve charge
positive_highlights: Net income of $144M and 21% annualized ROE
Gross premiums written up 17%, with International up 22%
AM Best upgraded Hamilton Select to A
summary: Hamilton reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $144M (21% annualized ROE) with a combined ratio of 95%, pressured by $50M catastrophe losses, mostly from the Middle East conflict. Gross premiums grew 17% overall, with International up 22% and Bermuda up 12%. The company raised a modest $16M reserve charge on casualty lines and maintained full-year low double-digit growth guidance, while noting competitive property pricing but stable casualty rates.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income per share guidance lowered from $0.50 to a range of $0.15-$0.20
Everspan adjusted EBITDA guidance reduced to $6M due to higher acquisition costs on newer programs
Market softening observed in wholesale large property with rates down 10%-20% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Insurance Distribution revenue surged 77% driven by organic growth of 44% and the ArmadaCare acquisition
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 13% a year ago to approximately 26%
Everspan loss ratio improved 640 bps to 61.4%, with active programs running at about 59%
summary: Octave Specialty Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with Insurance Distribution revenue growing 77% to $58.4 million and adjusted EBITDA rising four-fold to $10 million. The company revised its full-year guidance, raising organic growth expectations to 25%+ (from 20%) but lowering total adjusted EBITDA guidance from $40M to $39M ($6M for Everspan) due to higher acquisition costs and interest expense adjustments.

negative_highlights: No explicit forward guidance provided
M&A decisions on Mataripe and ethanol still pending
Equatorial margin well still awaiting results
positive_highlights: Record recurring net profit and gross profit in company history
Production up 15% YoY, exceeding target by 200,000 bpd
Adjusted EBITDA of $20 billion, up 70% QoQ
summary: Petrobras reported record Q2 2026 results, with recurring net profit and gross profit at all-time highs, despite Brent not being at its historical peak. Production reached 2.7 million barrels of oil per day, up 15% YoY, and refinery utilization surpassed 100%, helping reduce imports by 40% and increase exports by 12%. Adjusted EBITDA was $20 billion, up 70% QoQ and nearly double YoY. Management highlighted production capacity still to ramp up (270,000 bpd) and reaffirmed capital discipline, with no change to guidance.

negative_highlights: Cash of approximately $26 million restricted due to contractual dispute, though company expects it to be lifted
Mill availability impacted by unplanned maintenance on ball mill gearbox and primary crusher work
Mining costs per ton increased year-over-year due to lower tons mined and higher fresh rock exposure
positive_highlights: First-half production of just over 69,000 ounces, near the upper end of indicated range
Strong safety record: 11 million hours without lost time injury, 456 incident-free days
Exploration budget expanded to $25 million, drilling on track for 2027 MRMR update
summary: Galiano Gold reported Q2 fiscal 2026 production of 34,400 ounces, bringing first-half output to 69,000 ounces, near the upper end of guidance. Revenue was $156.6 million, adjusted EBITDA $78.5 million, adjusted EPS $0.09, with AISC of $2,473 per ounce, within guidance. Full-year guidance was maintained at 140,000-160,000 ounces and $2,300-$2,600 AISC. The company continued investing in Nkran Cut 3 pre-stripping and exploration at Esaase and Abore, with a planned hedge roll-off and higher-grade ore expected to improve results in 2027 and beyond.

negative_highlights: Effective tax rate increased to 20.4% from 17.8%
Other operating income fell 32.2% due to lower government grants and no licensing fees
Agricultural machinery engine sales declined 18.9% YoY
positive_highlights: Revenue up 13.9% YoY and net profit up 53.2% YoY
AIDC engine sales at 1,800 units in H1, full-year target 3,500 units
Dividend raised to $0.87 per share from $0.53
summary: In H1 2026, revenue grew 13.9% YoY to RMB 14.7 billion, with engine unit sales up 10.9%. Gross profit rose 36.5% to RMB 2.5 billion, and operating profit increased 58.9% to RMB 988.2 million. Net profit attributable to shareholders surged 53.2% to RMB 560.6 million. Management noted strong demand for high-horsepower engines, with AI data center sales reaching 1,800 units, and reiterated a full-year AIDC volume target of 3,500 units. The company raised its 2025 dividend to $0.87 per share and is planning capacity expansion to 5,000 units for high-horsepower engines.

negative_highlights: Cement volumes down 1.4% YoY, industry dispatches down 5%
Consolidated EBITDA margin contracted 97 bps to 20.2%
Railroad EBITDA margin turned negative at -5.2% vs +9.8% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue up 2.1% YoY to ARS 238.1 billion despite lower volumes
EBITDA per ton in dollars up 14% YoY to $32.1
Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.3x from 1.47x at end of 2025
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Loma Negra reported cement volumes down 1.4% YoY and consolidated revenue up 2.1% to ARS 238.1 billion. Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.5% to ARS 48.2 billion, with margin down 97 bps to 20.2%. Net profit improved to ARS 7.5 billion from ARS 0.5 billion a year ago, helped by lower financial losses. Management noted soft April volumes due to heavy rains, maintained a cautiously optimistic outlook for H2, and highlighted new RIGI projects and road concessions as potential supports.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $25.6 million in Q2 from $30 million in Q1
Full-year shipment guidance lowered by 1 million tons at midpoint
Cost guidance raised $7 per ton at midpoint, tied to higher diesel and supply costs
positive_highlights: Q2 met segment cost per ton decreased to $103.07 from $107.98 in Q1
New Wildcat low-vol mine in production, ramping up in Q3/Q4 to shift mix
Thermal byproduct realizations increased to $79.36 per ton from $69.41
summary: AMR reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $25.6 million, down from $30 million in Q1, with 3.5 million tons shipped. The company lowered its full-year shipment guidance by 1 million tons to a range of 14.2-15.4 million tons and raised its cost guidance midpoint by $7 to $103-$107 per ton, citing higher diesel and supply costs, weaker met coal markets, and reduced DTA terminal capacity due to storm damage. Management noted continued weak global steel demand and tightness in the Australian PLV spread, while highlighting the ramp-up of the new Wildcat low-vol mine as a positive mix shift.

negative_highlights: Network revenue down if excluding one-time revenue from prior year
Payment and Revenue Integrity segment missed consensus due to timing
NSA revenue uptick concentrated in one client, volume growth uncertain
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 6.6% YoY, highest quarter in 15 quarters
Bookings in H1 2026 up 150% YoY, surpassing full-year 2025 bookings
Operating cash flow up 51% YoY, levered free cash flow up 49%
summary: Claritev reported Q2 2026 revenue of $257.5 million, up 6.6% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $155.8 million (60.5% margin), with operating cash flow up 51% to $93 million. Bookings were strong at $30 million ACV in Q2, bringing H1 to $70 million, up 150% YoY, and the company raised its full-year bookings target to $100 million. Guidance was raised, and management expressed confidence in achieving at least 50% ACV bookings growth for the year.

negative_highlights: Significant curtailments in Q2 due to Waha economics
Oil-weighted spending skewed but production expenses down 4% YoY
Management notes perceived undervaluation versus peers
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 17% sequentially; free cash flow up over 400% from Q1
Repurchased ~3% of shares outstanding at $20.37; board increased repurchase authorization to ~$243 million
Guidance reiterated; D&C capital $850-900 million expected to sustain production
summary: NOG reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA up 17% sequentially, free cash flow up over 400% from Q1, and record natural gas volumes up 35% year-over-year. Despite Waha curtailments, the company reiterated capital spend and production guidance, citing cost tailwinds and activity pickup. Management highlighted strong free cash flow of $159 million, a 3% share repurchase, and a raised buyback authorization. They remain confident in asset value, with internal estimates of $7 billion+ versus a $4.6 billion enterprise value.

negative_highlights: Second-half margin outlook pressured by Middle East conflict and moderating pricing/FX
Aftermarket remains flat; no significant inflection yet
India JV impacted by Middle East conflict
positive_highlights: Record Q2 sales of $528M, up 16.4% YoY
Adjusted EPS of $0.82 vs $0.75 year ago
Koch Filter integration 95% complete, growth initiatives underway
summary: Atmus delivered record Q2 FY2026 sales of $528 million, up 16.4% year-over-year, driven by the Koch Filter acquisition and Power Solutions growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million (20.7% margin), and EPS was $0.82, beating prior-year $0.75. The company narrowed full-year EBITDA guidance to 19.75%-20.25% and maintained EPS guidance at $2.85-$3.00, while noting second-half headwinds from Middle East conflict and moderating pricing/FX.

negative_highlights: Total telecom revenues down 6% YoY (4% ex-divestitures)
Legacy copper and cable revenue pressures, cable revenue down ~10% YoY
Full-year revenue guidance lowered to $1.000-1.025B
positive_highlights: Fiber service address delivery of 66,000 in Q2, first-half record 106,000

negative_highlights: Base business net sales declined by $10.2 million (2.9%) driven primarily by a volume decrease of $15.5 million.
GAAP EPS was negative at -$0.05 due to approximately $9.7 million in acquisition, divestiture-related expenses and restructuring costs.
Management noted softness in College Inn consumption and the need to improve performance across retail branded channels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $60.4 million (up from $58M) driven by the acquisition of College Inn/Kitchen Basics, divestitures, and tariff refunds.
Base business net sales are on track with plan for YTD FY26 at approximately flat compared to prior year ($711.4M vs $711.2M).
Spices & Flavor Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% due to improved cost environment and tariff refunds.
summary: B&G Foods reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $383.3 million (down 9.7% YoY) and a GAAP loss of $4 million ($0.05/share), though adjusted metrics beat prior year with Adjusted EBITDA rising to $60.4 million on the back of divestitures, acquisitions, and tariff refunds. Management reaffirmed full-year FY26 guidance for net sales between $1.735 billion-$1.775 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $275 million-$290 million despite a challenging industry backdrop involving inflationary pressures in vegetable oil and spices.

negative_highlights: High-powered laser shipments remain significantly behind customer demand despite increased signals, creating a supply constraint relative to the fastest-growing segment.
Convertible note equity conversion resulted in a $7.8 billion non-cash GAAP charge, turning reported net income into a loss of $7.2 billion for Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion, marking eight consecutive quarters of top-line growth with three straight quarters above 20% sequential expansion.
Non-GAAP gross margin crossed the 50% threshold in Q4 at a revenue level well below the original target run rate, driven by mix and pricing power.
Q1 FY2027 guidance raised to $1.225-$1.275 billion with operating margins of 39.5%-40.5%, achieved more than one quarter ahead of schedule.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion and non-GAAP EPS was $3.23, significantly beating the high end of guidance due to strong components ($649M) and systems ($357M) performance driven by AI demand. Management raised Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance to a range of $1.225-$1.275 billion (midpoint $1.25B), noting they are hitting this target more than one quarter ahead of schedule, and projected non-GAAP operating margins between 39.5% and 40.5%. Gross margin expanded to 50.4%, crossing the previously targeted threshold at a much lower revenue run rate.

negative_highlights: Net asset value per share declined $0.23 to $16 due to realized and unrealized losses totaling $0.26 per share.
Realized loss of $9.4 million recognized on the liquidation of investment in Sundance, alongside other rotation-related losses.
Non-accrual rate increased 20 basis points to 2.7% driven by additions for 4over and Diverzify.
positive_highlights: New floating-rate loan originations averaged 566 basis points over SOFR, reflecting a wider pricing environment than the prior quarter.
Debt-to-equity ratio remained within target range at 1.17x despite leverage increases from delayed realizations rather than deliberate moves.
Watch list held steady at approximately 5.5% of fair market value with no material deterioration in credit quality overall.
summary: KBDC reported net investment income of $0.42 per share and EPS of $0.16 for Q2 FY2026, slightly below the prior quarter's NII but in line with expectations given a lower dividend coverage ratio relative to NAV decline. The company maintained its target debt-to-equity range at 1.17x while rotating out of broadly syndicated loans into higher-yielding private credit assets averaging 566 bps over SOFR. Management noted modest deal flow pickup and stable watch list levels, though realized losses from Sundance and unrealized marks on specific positions weighed on NAV.

negative_highlights: Calendar shift reduced reported organic revenue by approximately 2%, masking underlying growth that would have been higher.
Nexus contribution in Q3 was described as a 'small amount' with full ramp-up expected to occur primarily in the fourth quarter and fiscal 2027.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 9% to $5B with underlying growth excluding calendar shift estimated at +2%; AOI margins expanded nearly 20 bps driven by supply chain efficiencies.
Client retention reached record levels of approximately 98%, reflecting strong service execution and client relationships across the portfolio.
Aramark Nexus contributed late-quarter revenue from a top global hyperscaler, with scope increasing 40% to an estimated $140M-$160M annually per site.
summary: Aramark reported Q3 FY26 organic revenue growth of 9% to $5 billion and adjusted operating income (AOI) expansion of nearly 20 basis points to a margin that drove AOI up 18%. Management raised the fiscal 2026 organic revenue guidance range from prior levels to an increase of 9%-10%, while reaffirming AOI growth expectations of 12%-17% and adjusted EPS growth of 20%-25%. The quarter was driven by record client retention at approximately 98%, strong new business wins totaling $1.6 billion year-to-date, and the initial ramp-up of Aramark Nexus operations.

negative_highlights: Negative revenue adjustment of $136 million related to exiting Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail contracts
Adjusted loss per share was $0.63 due to one-time charges including a non-cash impairment of $75 million
Volume headwinds in Northern Europe, China, and Middle East affecting Harsco Environmental
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased by over 20% compared to last year
Harsco Environmental revenues grew on a like-for-like basis with improved pricing and volumes
Rail aftermarket revenue growth offset lower original equipment sales
summary: Total revenue was $187 million but included a negative adjustment of $136 million for exiting rail contracts; excluding this, revenues were higher than the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA increased by over 20% to $34 million driven by Harsco Environmental and aftermarket volumes at Rail, though adjusted loss per share was $0.63 due to one-time exit charges of roughly $190 million in accrued liabilities. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite better-than-anticipated first-half performance, citing uncertainty from Middle East geopolitical pressures.

negative_highlights: Live streaming revenue declined YoY to CNY 1.1 billion amid softer user spending and industry-wide competition.
Sales and marketing expenses increased sharply by 58% YoY (to RMB 91M) primarily due to promotional efforts for Goose Goose Duck Mobile.
Interest income dropped significantly from RMB 59 million to RMB 26 million, reflecting lower cash balances.
positive_highlights: Game-related services revenue surged 54% YoY to CNY 638 million due to publishing success (Goose Goose Duck) and advertising growth.
Gross margin expanded 120 bps sequentially to 14.7%, driven by the shift toward higher-margin game publishing and in-game item sales.
Non-GAAP operating income turned positive at RMB 16 million, a significant improvement from RMB 0.4 million last year.
summary: HUYA reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of CNY 1.74 billion (up 11% YoY), driven by a 54% surge in game-related services and advertising to CNY 638 million, while live streaming revenue declined slightly year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 14.7%, narrowing the operating loss to RMB 7 million as higher-margin publishing contributions offset slower core streamer performance. Management raised its share repurchase authorization from $50M-$100M and highlighted strong monetization in their new title, Goose Goose Duck Mobile.

negative_highlights: IDI real estate vertical declined modestly due to industry headwinds including limited inventory and elevated interest rates.
Gross revenue retention decreased slightly by two percentage points to 95% compared to the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached a record $26.7 million, up 23% year-over-year with four of five verticals hitting all-time highs.
Adjusted gross margin expanded two percentage points to a new high of 86%, driven by operating leverage and scale.
Added a record 447 IDI customers in Q2, surpassing the previous quarterly record of 400.
summary: Red Violet reported a record Q2 FY2026 with revenue of $26.7 million (up 23% YoY), adjusted gross margin expanding to a new high of 86%, and cash flow from operations reaching $10.6 million. The company added a record 447 IDI customers in the quarter, including significant growth across four verticals while FOREWARN expanded into home healthcare with over 25,000 new users. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 'high 30s' following this exceptional performance.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased to $41.2M due to employment costs and one-time restructuring charges related to the April efficiency initiative
Net loss widened slightly to $39.1M compared to $37.8M in Q1, though still better than prior year
positive_highlights: Q2 net revenue of $45.7M, representing substantial growth over the prior quarter and year-ago period
Gross margin expanded significantly to 55% from Q1's 6%, driven by volume increases at Nucleus facility
Full-year guidance raised to $140-$150 million based on strong H2 momentum
summary: Autolus reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $45.7 million, a significant increase from the prior quarter and year-ago period, driven by strong adoption in over 80 U.S. centers and early launch momentum in the UK. Management raised full-year guidance for AUCATZYL to $140-$150 million (from an original range of $120-$135 million) citing improved gross margins that expanded to 55% from Q1's 6%. The company also announced a new strategic financing with Perceptive Advisors providing up to $250 million in notes.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to the absence of robotic system deliveries in Q2.
Operating loss increased quarter-over-quarter despite sequential revenue growth, indicating high fixed cost burn during a transition period.
Catheter supply remains constrained by contract manufacturer output (Osypka AG), limiting ability to capture full demand and impacting near-term margins.
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue grew significantly to $6.2 million (up 70% sequentially), driven by the launch of MAGiC and a new portfolio of robotically navigated catheters.
Management expects recurring revenue gross margins to expand from current levels in Q2/Q3 toward mid-70s as manufacturing volumes ramp up.
GenesisX received its first U.S. purchase order from an academic medical center, demonstrating progress on compatibility with non-modified X-rays.
summary: Stereotaxis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.7 million, a year-over-year decline due to the lack of robotic system deliveries but an increase sequentially from Q1 driven by catheter sales. Gross margin was 58%, with operating loss widening slightly to $4.6 million compared to $4.0 million in the prior year quarter. Management provided specific guidance for recurring revenue growth ($7M in Q3, $8M in Q4) and system revenue stabilization at approximately $3M per quarter in H2, while explicitly stating that full-year visibility is limited by supply constraints on catheters.

negative_highlights: Year-over-year revenue declined significantly from $4.1 million due to lower product and service sales.

Gross margin contracted sequentially by 130 bps (from implied higher levels) driven by the shift in mix toward services/consumables which have different margins, though absolute gross profit improved slightly or held steady relative to prior year context of instrument-heavy quarters; specifically noted as a decline from Q2 2025.
Management explicitly stated that caution among academic customers regarding grant funding delays is not expected to end by the balance of 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue showed sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 ($3.1M vs $2.8M) indicating early recovery momentum.
New Chief Commercial Officer Tony Bazarko has already engaged with ~20% of North American customers and is refocusing the organization on large accounts.
SECURE-SG100K study completed 10,000 samples in May; preliminary data expected to drive future buyback commitments.
summary: Seer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 million, a decrease from the prior year's $4.1 million and an increase sequentially from Q1's $2.8 million due to macroeconomic headwinds in academic funding and elongated sales cycles. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range of $16-$18 million despite the challenging environment, citing positive trends in customer interest for H2 driven by new commercial leadership and upcoming data releases.

negative_highlights: June advertising yield was reduced by a shift in film slate composition toward R-rated titles and budget shifts for the FIFA World Cup.
Unlevered free cash flow turned negative at -$2.1 million due to one-time operational transformation costs.
Management paused dividend payments and share repurchase programs following the announcement of the acquisition.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 12.7% year-over-year to $58.4 million driven by a 19.3% increase in attendance.
Adjusted OIBDA improved significantly, reaching $2.1 million compared to the prior period.
Local advertising revenue surged 48.4% YoY to $9.5 million due to sales force rebuilding and premium inventory expansion.
summary: NCMI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58.4 million (up 12.7% YoY) and adjusted OIBDA of $2.1 million (a three-fold increase), with results falling within the company's guidance range despite June headwinds from film mix shifts and FIFA World Cup budget reallocation. The CEO announced a definitive agreement to acquire Captivate, valuing it at an enterprise value of $275 million for approximately 48,000 combined digital screens across theaters, offices, and residential properties. Management stated they are pausing dividend payments and share repurchases pending the transaction's closing in H2 FY26.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed expectations due to extended protest periods and low-margin material volume impacting near-term dynamics.
Preliminary FY2027 outlook includes a specific revenue impact of approximately 3% from NASA's workforce insourcing directive.
Company is exiting several domestic-based operations representing roughly 1% of total revenue that are no- or low-margin.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased to $290 million with record quarterly margins of 8.3%, up 60 bps year-over-year.
Net bookings reached $3.9 billion, resulting in a trailing twelve-month book-to-bill ratio of 1.3x.
Raised full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $50 million to the range of $1.115B-$1.14B.
summary: Third quarter revenue of $3.5 billion came in slightly below expectations due to protest delays and low-margin material volume, though adjusted EBITDA hit a record $290 million with margins expanding to 8.3%. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($1.115B-$1.14B) and EPS ($2.40-$2.50), while maintaining free cash flow expectations, despite acknowledging a preliminary FY2027 revenue headwind of approximately 3% from NASA workforce directives.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue was at the low end of guidance due solely to a delayed seven-figure customer contract extension.
A commercial ASIC design targeting Intel 18A is being removed from H2 forecast with potential shift to 2027.
Mature product revenue growth slowed, expected to be flat for full year FY26 compared to prior years.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 46.8%, significantly above the midpoint outlook.
Net loss narrowed to $1.1 million (vs $1.5M prior year), with cash balance increasing to $13.5 million.
Government contract ceiling increased to $89 million, expected to drive significant Q4 revenue.
summary: QuickLogic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $5.5 million (up 48.7% YoY), which missed the midpoint of guidance due to a delayed contract extension and an uncertain commercial ASIC design targeting Intel 18A, leading management to narrow full-year growth outlook to 70%-80%. Management forecast flat Q3 revenue but raised confidence in securing new contracts for late-stage negotiations and government work. The company expects non-GAAP profitability and cash flow positive operations for the second half of FY26.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined to $102.9 million from $113.1 million in the prior year, primarily due to the closure of the U.K. cast roll facility.
Q2 results reflect a one-time decline rather than organic weakness; however, revenue is down compared to the same period last year.
positive_highlights: Customer orders increased approximately 50% versus the prior year to $144 million, indicating accelerating demand across segments.
Backlog grew from Q1 levels ($38.5M) to $39.9 million in Air and Liquid Systems alone (total backlog implied higher), reflecting record order activity.
Adjusted EBITDA improved 22% sequentially versus Q1 of the current year as restructuring impacts fade.
summary: Ampco-Pittsburgh reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $102.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9.8 million (margin expanding to 9.5%), representing a significant sequential improvement as the impact from prior U.K. facility closure flows through results. Customer orders surged by approximately 50% year-over-year, with backlog growing substantially to $385.4 million driven by strong demand in Air and Liquid Systems and recovering roll shipments in Forged and Cast Engineered Products. Management expects a significantly stronger second half of the year despite normal seasonal outages.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened slightly to $29.7 million due to increased operating expenses associated with scaling commercial support and project development.
Adjusted EBITDA remains a loss of $17 million, though the company notes this is an inflection point as it transitions from build-to-transfer models.
positive_highlights: Revenue doubled year-over-year driven by Australian project progress and new US contracts.
Backlog increased approximately $650 million quarter-over-quarter to roughly $2 billion, more than doubling from a year ago.
Raised full-year revenue guidance range significantly while narrowing the gross margin outlook to 20%-25%.
summary: NRGV reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.4 million (up 104% YoY) and GAAP gross margin expanding to 31%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $270-$310 million from the prior $225-$300 million, citing strong backlog growth to roughly $2 billion. The company highlighted its largest-ever contract (1.25 GW) and improved liquidity with cash ending at $148 million.

negative_highlights: Results were essentially flat versus expectations due to late Q2 white space and volatile commodity prices muting customer response.
Drilling-focused revenue mix (approx. 23%) limited incremental margins compared to higher-margin service lines like completions.
Company elected PIK interest on senior notes for the second quarter, adding $8.2 million to principal rather than paying cash.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 68% sequentially to approximately $19 million due to operating leverage and WolfPack contribution.
Q3 revenue guidance raised significantly with a midpoint of $182 million implying mid-single digit growth in the base business excluding acquisitions.
WolfPack acquisition integration progressing smoothly, contributing $3.4M in June with an annual run rate of ~$41 million.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $167.3 million (up 15.6% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA was $18.7 million, with results coming in at the midpoint of guidance despite late June white space. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to a range of $176-$188 million ($182m midpoint), citing improved activity levels driven by WolfPack integration and seasonal normalization. The company announced a proactive $125 million backstop equity rights offering designed to reduce leverage, improve liquidity, and strengthen the balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was an outflow of CAD 3.9 million due to working capital investments supporting scale and inventory buildup
Canadian vape share gains were limited to a single month (June) before declines reversed, indicating early-stage recovery rather than sustained trend yet
positive_highlights: Record net revenue of CAD 105.8 million driven by Sanity Group contributions exceeding EUR 24.5M in Q1 post-acquisition
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 37% (up 300 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA reached record CAD 13.4 million
Sanity revenue for the full quarter exceeded EUR 25M, meeting acquisition expectations with growth expected in Q4
summary: OrganiGram reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of CAD 105.8 million (up 49% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 37%, driven by Sanity Group contributions which exceeded EUR 25M expectations for the full quarter. Adjusted EBITDA hit a new high of CAD 13.4 million, while Canadian share recovery in vapes and pre-rolls offset slightly lower domestic market share due to portfolio rationalization. Management raised guidance expecting revenue above CAD 350M for FY26 and meaningful margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Reported adjusted EBITDA margin diluted by 60 bps due to elevated metal cost inflation, specifically regarding hafnium prices rising from ~$5k/kg to $12.5k-$13k/kg.
Turbo Wheels division reported an Adjusted EBITDA fall of $0.6 million YoY largely attributable to the sale of Ivostud business.
CapEx expected to remain at elevated levels during this investment phase, impacting near-term cash flow conversion.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34% YoY to a record $269 million, with Engine Products growing 39% overall (Europe +49%, North America +29%).
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 180 bps QoQ to 17.8%; excluding metal pass-through impact, the underlying organic margin expansion was robust.
Signed fourth strategic partnership with an aerospace OEM underpinning a new greenfield superalloy site in Alabama.
summary: DPC Holdings reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $269 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $48 million (up 33%), driven by strong growth in Engine Products segments. Adjusted EPS was $0.05, representing a significant recovery from the prior year's loss as net income moved into profit. Management initiated full-year guidance for revenue between $1 billion-$1.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $182 million-$187 million.

negative_highlights: Loan growth expectations lowered significantly for the year, with real growth now projected between 10% and 15%.
Net fee income is expected to decline between 5% and 8% in real terms due to softer activity.
Cost of risk remains elevated at a run rate around 5.6%, though guidance suggests it will stay within the challenging range of 5.3%-5.8%.
positive_highlights: Attributable net income turned positive at ARS 13 billion, a swing of more than ARS 31 billion from Q1 loss.
Structural ROE reached 14.4% after incorporating full quarterly salary savings and excluding extraordinary severance charges.
NIM expanded sequentially by 250 bps to 20.3%, driven by funding costs declining faster than asset yields.
summary: Grupo Supervielle returned to profitability in Q2 FY2026 with attributable net income of ARS 13 billion and adjusted net income of ARS 36 billion following a loss in the prior quarter. Management updated full-year guidance, lowering real loan growth expectations to 10%-15% from previously higher targets due to subdued retail demand, while raising NIM guidance to 17%-19%. The rightsizing program is largely complete with structural ROE reaching 14.4%, though management notes margin pressure in the second half as asset repricing begins.

negative_highlights: Reported net income declined year-over-year due to approximately $3.3 million in transaction costs associated with the Flatrock acquisition.
The second quarter effective tax rate was elevated at 30.9% compared to a full-year expectation of roughly 25%-26%, driven by discrete state tax items.
positive_highlights: Rental revenue reached a record $49.4 million, up approximately 25% year-over-year.
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 61.1%, an increase of roughly 36 basis points despite inflationary cost pressures.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised from the prior range of $92.5M-$97.5M to a new record high of $103M-$108M.
summary: NGS reported record Q2 FY26 results with rental revenue of $49.4 million (up ~25% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 61.1%. The company increased full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $103-$108M from the prior range of $92.5-$97.5M, driven by a Flatrock acquisition contribution that added roughly half a month in Q2 and contracted organic growth raising expectations for 2026 deployments.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not providing clear production guidance for H2 of the year due to a desire to maintain flexibility after deferring deliveries.
The company confirmed it is not interested in spot sales, preferring to protect inventory for future opportunistic pricing or loan repayment.
Shirley Basin operations were limited until late June as they awaited regulatory authorization from the state.
positive_highlights: Production increased significantly to 141,000 pounds (up 26% YoY) following the installation of a sand filtration system that removed flow constraints at Lost Creek.
Shirley Basin is now in full operation with six of ten production columns online and first shipments imminent after receiving regulatory authorization.
Cash cost per pound remained low at $40.20, including ad valorem and severance taxes.
summary: Ur-Energy reported Q2 FY2026 production of 141,000 pounds at Lost Creek and initial capture of 10,634 pounds at Shirley Basin, resulting in $14.4 million in sales revenue from contracted deliveries totaling 215,000 pounds. Management proactively deferred 300,000 pounds of 2026 deliveries to later years to manage ramp-up risk and maintain flexibility rather than providing specific volume guidance for the remainder of the year. While operational execution improved with sand filtration installation increasing flow rates at Lost Creek, the company explicitly stated it is not interested in spot sales and will prioritize inventory protection.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin contracted to 32.2% (down from 35.2% YoY) due to geographical mix and cost pressures.
Full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance was lowered, with margins expected between 5%-6% versus a previous midpoint of 6.5%-7.5%.
Supply chain challenges regarding component availability are expected to persist through the remainder of FY2026.
positive_highlights: India bookings reached $120 million year-to-date, representing the highest level since Q1 FY2024.
North America revenue from a key Tier 1 carrier exceeded initial expectations despite some shipment timing shifts.
Record private network bookings were secured in North America with diverse use cases.
summary: Ceragon reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $93.9 million (up 14% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.02, driven by strong bookings in India ($120M YTD). Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance but lowered the gross margin outlook to a range of 33.5%-34.5% (from previously implied higher levels) and operating income guidance due to persistent supply chain cost pressures.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it expects its first commercial revenue in 2027, indicating no current or near-term sales
Management declined to disclose the size of the drone order due to customer confidentiality concerns
No GAAP financial results (revenue/EPS) were reported as this is an inaugural call for a newly public company
positive_highlights: Achieved the first commercial battery order from a separate leading U.S. drone manufacturer
Demonstrated >30% increase in flight range for customer drones using solid-state technology before engineering optimization
Reached an automotive integration milestone with Stellantis, becoming the first solid-state battery maker to achieve successful vehicle integration with two top 10 global OEMs
summary: Factorial Energy reported Q2 FY2026 operating expenses of $13 million and non-GAAP operating expenses of $14.5 million for the six months ended June 30, which were in line with expectations; capital expenditures totaled $0.6 million for the half-year against a full-year expectation of approximately $13 million. The company announced its first commercial battery order from a U.S. drone manufacturer and achieved an automotive integration milestone with Stellantis, but explicitly stated that it expects to generate its first commercial revenue in 2027.

negative_highlights: Piceance segment adjusted EBITDA decreased $0.9M quarter-over-quarter due to a 5.7% decline in volume throughput from temporary shut-ins.
Full-year guidance was tightened (narrowed) despite strong first-half performance, reflecting uncertainty on second-half commodity pricing assumptions.
Piceance segment expects cash flow step-down starting Q4 as roughly $4M/quarter of shortfall payments expire.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 12% quarter-over-quarter to $60.7 million driven by volume growth in Rockies ($30.4M) and Mid-Con ($21.4M).
Realized crude oil prices rose approximately 30% quarter-over-quarter, benefiting percentage-of-proceeds contracts.
Secured two new gathering agreements in Divide County adding visibility to ~30 new well connections not previously contemplated.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $60.7 million (a 12% increase vs Q1), driven by volume growth in Rockies and Mid-Con segments alongside a ~30% quarter-over-quarter rise in realized crude oil prices. Management tightened full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $235-$255 million while raising capital expenditure guidance to $100-$120 million, citing new well connections and Double E expansion projects.

negative_highlights: Consolidated occupancy growth (82.4%) came in slightly below expectations with only an 110 bps increase on a same-community basis.
Revenue declined 8.7% YoY due to a 15.7% reduction in average units from portfolio optimization activities, partially offset by higher RevPAR.
Other facility operating expenses were elevated during the quarter due to variability including repairs and maintenance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $122.1 million beat consensus estimates and grew 4.3% year-over-year.
RevPAR growth of 8.2% met the full-year guidance target, with RevPOR increasing 5.2% YoY as price concessions from last year are lapped.
Labor expense declined to 45.2% of revenue on a same-community basis, improving 90 bps YoY due to operational focus and hiring discipline.
summary: Brookdale Senior Living reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $122.1 million (up 4.3% YoY) and RevPAR growth of 8.2%, meeting the full-year guidance range but missing occupancy expectations which grew only 230 bps to 82.4%. Management reaffirmed its annual guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($502M-$516M) and RevPAR (8%-9%), noting that Q3 growth will be similar to Q2 before accelerating in Q4 due to disposition timing, while acknowledging a slight occupancy shortfall driven by move-outs.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was substantial at $596.5 million, primarily due to one-time IPO-related costs including a catch-up stock-based compensation expense of roughly $447.5 million.
Adjusted EBITDA remained in the red with a non-GAAP net loss of $73 million for the quarter compared to a prior year loss of $43.5 million.
R&D expenses were elevated at $367 million, including significant stock-based compensation related to IPO triggers.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 279% year-over-year driven by significant growth in the cloud business, reaching $8 million for Q2 FY26.
Year-to-date bookings reached approximately $81 million, with management expecting full-year 2026 revenue between $28-$32 million.
Achieved a major technical milestone on Sol system components via Honeywell Aerospace validation without showstoppers and demonstrated near five-nines logical fidelities on Helios.
summary: Quantinuum reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $8 million (up 279% YoY) and bookings of $4.3 million, with year-to-date bookings reaching approximately $81 million against a full-year guidance range of $28-$32 million for 2026. The company highlighted significant progress on its Sol system roadmap via Honeywell Aerospace validation and secured major strategic partnerships including an LOI from the U.S. Department of Commerce, agreements with Oracle and HPE, and new manufacturing alliances to scale supply chains. Management expressed high confidence in their technology leadership and commercial momentum despite acknowledging that quarterly results may remain volatile as they transition into a public company.

negative_highlights: Management characterized Q2 growth as 'modest' rather than a strong beat.
Retail channel take-up remains poor with limited visibility into refill dynamics outside the e-pharmacy segment.
Net loss of $31.9 million and no positive EPS reported.
positive_highlights: July script volume increased over 45% month-over-month following the launch of telehealth and national TV campaigns.
60% of e-pharmacy patients have purchased more than one monthly pack, indicating strong early refill behavior compared to competitors like VUITY (10-12%).
Over 75% of prescribing physicians (>13,000) are repeat prescribers.
summary: LENZ reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $5.5 million ($1.7M product revenue) and a net loss per share of $1.02 on a net loss of $31.9 million, with no GAAP or adjusted EPS provided in the text. Management highlighted an over 45% month-over-month increase in July prescriptions driven by new telehealth initiatives and national TV advertising, but explicitly stated that Q2 results were 'modest' growth rather than a significant beat. Guidance for H2 remains focused on assessing patient persistence data to align capital allocation with demonstrated performance.

negative_highlights: Asset quality is 'slightly below plan' with nonaccruals comprising 8.5% of total cost and 26% of the portfolio marked at investment category three or below.
Other income was lower than historical levels due to reduced cash balances available for sweep, rather than operational issues.
Dividend payments exceeded earnings by $0.08 per share as management distributed remaining spillover income from prior periods.
positive_highlights: Portfolio received five full repayments totaling $38.7 million plus $10 million in other par repayments during the quarter.
Realized and unrealized gains contributed $0.30 per share, driven by specific company performance improvements and a reversal of prior realized losses.
External advisor Stellus Capital Management officially joined Ridgepost Capital platform to leverage broader sponsor relationships.

summary: Astronics reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $260 million (up 27% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 19.8%, driven by volume leverage and a one-time tariff refund. The company highlighted strong momentum in aerospace bookings ($306 million) and significant progress on margin improvement levers including pricing adjustments and workforce stability.

Significant margin gap exists between top-performing and lowest-performing market centers

Full-year free cash flow guidance raised by $40 million, now expecting range of $160M-$170M
summary: Vestis reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $662 million (down 1.8% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $81 million (up 23% YoY), driven by a return to positive Revenue Per Pound growth for the first time as a public company despite volume declines from exiting low-quality linen business. CARVYKTI global sales grew 50% year-over-year to $657 million, driven by strong ex-U.S. growth of 128% and accelerating adoption in earlier lines (now >70% volume).

summary: Legend Biotech reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $341 million (implied from context) with total revenue growing 52% year-over-year to reach a new milestone in profitability. The company achieved its first quarter of company-wide profitability on both IFRS and adjusted bases.

Production costs at Ying remained below annual guidance range of $88-$90 per ton despite currency headwinds.

Management explicitly stated that full-year guidance is premature given the temporary shutdowns affecting Ying and GC mines, with current output running at only 40-50% of target for Q2.

Labor costs rose 30 basis points YoY due to incremental wage investments in team members.

Same-restaurant sales recovered from flat-to-positive levels to mid-single digits as Cyclospora consumer concerns eased during the quarter's final weeks.
New restaurant openings continued to outperform expectations, reinforcing brand portability in markets like Indiana and Ohio.
summary: CAVA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365.4 million (up 31.3% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $54.7 million (up 30%), driven by a 9% same-restaurant sales increase on 5.3% traffic growth, though food costs rose 50 bps due to salmon launch input prices. Management reiterated full-year guidance for 75-77 net new openings and mid-single-digit SSS, explicitly incorporating the lingering impact of Cyclospora outbreak concerns which caused same-store sales to dip before recovering sequentially in July.

negative_highlights: iGaming revenue was essentially flat year-over-year to $17 million, impacted by a significant increase in the U.K. gambling tax rate.
Average monthly revenue per payer declined from $286 to $218 due to the inclusion of WHOW Games metrics and market dynamics.
Operating expenses increased 10% year-over-year primarily due to the acquisition integration costs for WHOW Games.

Direct-to-consumer (DTC) contribution in social casino surged from ~15% last year to 52% this quarter, significantly improving margin dynamics.

Management maintained its strategic focus on operational excellence and DTC migration while noting sequential flatness in iGaming due to U.K. tax adjustments.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses increased compared to Q2 FY2025 driven by clinical operations and development costs

FORTIFI-FLEX alternative dosing study was successfully initiated to support a streamlined regimen

Management highlighted strong momentum from recent ASCO data but noted that operating expenses are expected to increase quarter-over-quarter through year-end as they prepare for potential commercialization.

negative_highlights: Natural gas production averaged 37.3 MMcm per day, down 6% year-over-year due to the exit from conventional fields.
CapEx increased by 16% interannually and 37% sequentially compared to prior periods.

The company also increased its CapEx forecast range to $5.8-$6.2 billion and expects net leverage to decline significantly to nearly 1x.

negative_highlights: Input costs for soybean oil remain elevated, partially offsetting favorable pricing in the biofuels segment.
Biofuel capacity utilization was only 56%, with production expected to ramp higher in Q3 following a three-week outage earlier in the period.
positive_highlights: Total revenue surged 120% YoY to $78.7 million driven by volume increases of 40% and price realizations up 80%.

Management highlighted improved plant reliability, regulatory clarity on biofuels mandates, and elevated input costs as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $5 million to $6.6 million due to increased R&D ($3.9M) and G&A expenses.

U.S. beef industry faces tight supplies and historically high costs, though margins are stabilizing.

summary: Imunon reported Q2 FY2026 results with R&D expenses of $1.5 million and G&A expenses down approximately 20% to $1.3 million due to cost containment initiatives. The company highlighted strong enrollment momentum in the pivotal OVATION 3 study, currently enrolling at 0.5 patients per site per month versus a plan assumption of 0.3, exceeding industry benchmarks for ovarian cancer trials. Management confirmed no guidance updates were provided but expressed high confidence that execution remains on track with their target timeline.

negative_highlights: Q2 results impacted by approximately $30/barrel discount composed of sulfur, demurrage, and transportation costs.
Platform Hondo restoration required about 50% more work than originally anticipated due to the platform being in bad need of structural repair.
Production constrained by pump capacity at Heritage and lack of gas lift compressors running on Harmony/Heritage.
positive_highlights: Completed refinancing of $675 million Senior Secured Term Loan B and issued $345 million convertible notes to retire the restrictive ExxonMobil seller note, lowering weighted average cost of debt.
Production ramped significantly with exit rate oil sales reaching 40,000 bpd in Q2 FY2026.
Implemented commodity hedging program starting July 2026 providing floor protection at $65/bbl for a significant portion of production.
summary: Sable Offshore Corp reported Q2 FY2026 results where production ramped to 40,000 bpd but faced significant marketing constraints and a $30/bbl discount due to sulfur content and demurrage charges. Management completed the refinancing of the senior secured term note in July 2026 to retire seller financing, providing more flexibility despite not raising guidance for the back half of the year which includes elevated deducts. The company expects production constraints to alleviate by Q4 2026 with Platform Hondo coming online and a full 3P reserve report expected in Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Oil and gas revenue declined 8.2% YoY ($8.5M) primarily due to customer program exits in 2025 and deferred maintenance activity amid elevated commodity prices.
Management anticipates oil & gas will remain flat-to-down through H2, contributing headwinds despite growth elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 4.2% YoY driven by strategic end markets which were up 28% in aggregate, specifically Aerospace & Defense (+13.2%) and Infrastructure (+76.5%).
Record Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million achieved with a gross margin expansion of 10 basis points.
Free cash flow improved significantly by $23.9 million quarter-over-quarter due to working capital dynamics.
summary: Mistras Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $193 million (up 4.2% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million ($25.8m vs prior year). Gross margin expanded by 10 basis points to a non-GAAP level implied around 73-74%, while operating income surged 53.6%. Management raised full-year guidance ranges for revenue (up to $740-$755M) and adjusted EBITDA (up to $92-$95M), citing strength in aerospace/defense and infrastructure offsetting a flat-to-down outlook for oil & gas.

negative_highlights: Adjusted segment EBITDA margin in production solutions decreased by 229 basis points quarter-over-quarter due to revenue mix shifts and higher operating expenses.
Natural Gas Systems segment saw both revenue and Adjusted Segment EBITDA decline sequentially, primarily driven by lower vapor recovery system sales offsetting rental growth.
Management lowered Q3 guidance range to $92 million-$98 million citing continued cost pressures from lube oil prices tied to high crack spreads and elevated O&M expenses.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 13% sequentially driven by growth in production solutions, specifically downhole components including the recently acquired Valiant business.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% quarter-over-quarter to approximately $94 million while maintaining top-quartile margins of roughly 40% despite cost headwinds.
Free cash flow generation remained strong at approximately $50 million, supporting a conservative balance sheet with leverage reduced below one times.
summary: Flowco reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $236 million (up 13% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $94 million ($93.9m GAAP), maintaining roughly 40% margins despite a 229 bps margin contraction in production solutions due to Valiant integration costs and higher O&M expenses including lube oil and fuel. Management stated results were within original guidance but explicitly noted that cost pressures will continue into Q3, leading them to reflect these headwinds by lowering their third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA guidance range from the prior $92m-$105m (implied) down to a new range of $92 million-$98 million. The company generated $50 million in free cash flow and declared a one-time special dividend alongside its regular quarterly payout.

negative_highlights: NeuroStar total revenue declined slightly by 2.7% due to double-digit drop in treatment session revenue
Full-year guidance narrowed from a range of $160M-$166M down to $160M-$164M
positive_highlights: Greenbrook revenue grew 17% YoY to $26.9M driven by provider growth and pricing improvements
Gross margin expanded significantly from 46.6% in the prior year to 61.1%
Cash burn reduced substantially with cash used for operations/investing falling to $1.4 million
summary: Total revenue was $41.6 million, up 9% year-over-year driven by a 17% increase in Greenbrook to $26.9 million and double-digit growth in NeuroStar capital sales offsetting session declines. Gross margin expanded significantly to 61.1%, while the company reduced its cash burn from operations and investing to just $1.4 million compared to $3.8 million last year. Management narrowed full-year revenue guidance slightly but raised gross margin expectations, reflecting improved operational discipline.

negative_highlights: Same-store NOI on legacy Holiday properties declined 6.3% year-over-year due to move-outs and unit offline pressures.
General and administrative expenses increased significantly by 44% YoY driven by CFO transition costs and ramping SHOP personnel.
Full-year same-store guidance remains at the lower end of expectations (1%-3%) with H2 growth expected only after addressing occupancy pressure from a specific building.
positive_highlights: Completed sale of NHC portfolio for $560 million cash, reducing leverage and providing significant liquidity to pursue future investments.
Same-store SHOP NOI increased sequentially by 18.9% from Q2 FY2025 to Q2 FY2026 as the company ramps its private pay senior housing platform.
Board declared a quarterly dividend increase of $0.02 per share, raising it to $0.94.
summary: NHI reported Q2 FY2026 results in line with expectations following the sale of its NHC portfolio for $560 million and a gain on property dispositions totaling approximately $137 million ($98.5M proceeds + $22M gain). While net income per share beat due to these one-time gains, core FFO metrics were flat or slightly down compared to the prior year period. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite same-store SHOP NOI growth being below the midpoint of their 1%-3% range in H1.

negative_highlights: Absorbed approximately $55 million of net cash hedge losses during the quarter, though management views this as a prudent risk management step.
Oil cut dropped to 64% from guided 67-68% due to accelerated completions stimulating high-oil wells and workovers on older gas-heavy assets.
positive_highlights: Production averaged 45,500 BOE/d during H1 FY26, exceeding the high end of guidance range.
