Unit LOE came in approximately 13% below full-year guided levels at $7.56/BOE due to operational improvements and electrification.
Accelerated completion schedule allowed capital deployment against productive work while capturing favorable service costs.
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q2 FY26 production of approximately 45,500 BOE/d, exceeding the high end of guidance despite accelerating completions which caused some frac-impacted volumes. The company generated $281 million in EBITDAX for H1 and absorbed roughly $55 million in net cash hedge losses while maintaining disciplined capital execution with first-half spending at 60%+ of budget. Management expects meaningful declines in second-half capital spend, positioning the business to generate stronger free cash flow as production remains supported by strong well performance.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA guidance explicitly excludes incremental revenue from the Intrepid Ranch acquisition announced post-quarter end.
General and administrative expenses were noted as 'a little bit light' in H1 relative to normalized public company costs, suggesting potential for higher spend later.
positive_highlights: Normalized revenue grew ~32% quarter-over-quarter to $46.8M, exceeding internal forecasts across all metrics.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 77.5%, demonstrating the benefit of high-margin surface use royalties and low operating costs.
Free cash flow conversion improved to approximately 96% after adjusting for interest expense on the predecessor credit facility.
summary: EagleRock reported Q2 FY2026 normalized revenue of $46.8 million (up ~32% vs Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $36.2 million (up ~32%), driven by strong brackish water sales, surface use royalties, and resource sales. The company initiated full-year 2026 guidance for normalized adjusted EBITDA between $129M-$133M, which is above original expectations but explicitly excludes the recently announced Intrepid Ranch acquisition. Management highlighted a robust balance sheet with $261.8 million in available liquidity and high free cash flow conversion of approximately 96% after adjusting for interest expense.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $53 million due to non-cash revaluation impacts on financial instruments, financing costs from the recapitalization, and increased pre-development expenses.

Cash used in operating activities surged to $50 million for the quarter compared to $11 million last year, driven by inventory buildup at third-party processing facilities and higher exploration outflows.
Drilling progress was slower than planned at Archimedes and Mineral Point due to drill rig availability issues and contractor staffing constraints.
positive_highlights: Gold production increased to approximately 8,600 ounces in Q2 compared to the prior year period as Granite Creek ramps up.
Gross profit expanded significantly due to a realized gold price of nearly $4,800/oz and higher sales volume from ramp-up activities.
Balance sheet strengthened with cash ending at approximately $465 million following recapitalization proceeds and restricted cash release.
summary: i-80 Gold reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $24 million and a net loss of $53 million ($0.06/share), driven by higher non-cash accounting impacts from financial instrument revaluations, financing costs, and increased pre-development expenses despite gross profit rising to $9 million due to gold price increases and production ramp-up at Granite Creek (8,600 ounces). Management reiterated 2026 guidance for annual output of 30,000-40,000 ounces but noted that growth capital expenditures will be below the prior range due to timing on Lone Tree refurbishment accruals and lower exploration spend. The company remains focused on executing its development plan with a strong balance sheet ($465M cash) while acknowledging moderate delays in drilling campaigns at Archimedes and Mineral Point.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted by 130 basis points to 20.3% due to specific FORGE hardware purchases for a government program.
Free cash flow outflow widened from $78.9 million in Q1 to $106.3 million in Q2, primarily driven by the final SciTec acquisition payment of approximately $24 million.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue crossing the $100 million threshold for the first time in company history.
Backlog grew sequentially by approximately $200 million to a record high of $1.5 billion, indicating strong order conversion.
Non-GAAP net loss per share improved from $0.46 to $0.42 as revenue scale increased.
summary: Firefly reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $117.7 million (up 46% sequentially and 659% YoY) driven by five parallel lunar missions and strong spacecraft demand. The company closed the quarter with a historic backlog of $1.5 billion, up from $1.3 billion previously. GAAP gross margin declined slightly to 20.3% due to specific government program hardware purchases, while non-GAAP operating loss narrowed significantly as revenue scaled.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income was impacted by significant unrealized losses on bunker fuel hedges in Q2
Total G&A expenses increased 25% YoY due to incentive compensation and added headcount
Charter-in costs rose 24% YoY as market rates for chartered vessels increased
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew nearly $20M YoY to $35M driven by robust market rates
TCE rates averaged a premium of 10% over the prevailing Panamax, Supramax, and Handysize indices
Unrestricted cash balance reached $105 million following vessel sales
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA of $35 million (up nearly $20M YoY) driven by a 50% increase in TCE rates to an average of $18,153/day. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.10 per share and ended the quarter with unrestricted cash of $105 million following asset sales. Management maintains a positive outlook for H2 2026 citing seasonal tailwinds from Arctic trades and continued demand momentum.

negative_highlights: Net loss from continuing operations was $11.9M, though improved from prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$1.9M despite a significant improvement.
The AVCAD program revenue has been excluded from core full-year guidance pending government next steps.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 23% YoY to $16.1M driven by handheld product revenue up 24%.
Adjusted gross margin expanded approximately 85 basis points to 57% due to volume and channel mix improvements.
Secured a specific $6 million ProtectIR order for corrections agencies in the Asia-Pacific region.
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.1 million (up 23% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 57%. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance range to $68-$70 million, citing strong execution on FTIR modernization, the new NIRLab acquisition integration, and a specific $6 million ProtectIR order. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by over half year-over-year.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased significantly due to $200 million upfront royalty payment to Tanabe Pharma Corporation
R&D expenses rose from $38.3M in Q2 FY25 to $221.4M in Q2 FY26 primarily due to the one-time payment and headcount growth
positive_highlights: $500 million committed senior secured term loan facility entered into in June 2026
$150 million equity offering completed to expand capital access
Post hoc analysis of Launch-HTN trial showed statistically and clinically meaningful blood pressure reductions comparable to broader population despite severe hypertension
summary: Mineralys Therapeutics reported a net loss of $241.1 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $43.3 million in the prior year quarter, driven by a one-time $200 million upfront payment to Tanabe Pharma Corporation and increased R&D expenses totaling $221.4 million. The company ended the period with cash equivalents and investments of $661.4 million, sufficient to fund operations through 2028 while awaiting FDA approval for lorundrostat expected by December PDUFA date.

negative_highlights: Third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered by 30 bps to reflect tougher comparisons and timing of end-market recoveries in the back half.
Recreational marine market remains soft with interest rates suppressing growth for financed products.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat high-end of outlook by $0.05 per share driven by strong volume growth and operational leverage.
Gross margins expanded 280 bps to 34.6%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of expansion.
Order intake grew double-digits for a fourth straight quarter, signaling robust demand visibility.
summary: Helios Technologies reported Q2 FY26 sales of $232 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.88, which exceeded the high-end of its prior guidance by $0.05 per share. Gross margin expanded 280 bps to 34.6%, driven by volume growth, mix shifts, operational initiatives, and a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Management raised full-year sales guidance to an implied range of $880-$900 million (up from the prior midpoint) and increased adjusted EBITDA margin expectations for the year.

negative_highlights: Industry growth is expected to moderate relative to historical norms as job growth slows despite stable unemployment rates.
Canadian tax season performance was not great due to regulatory changes with the CRA, though Australia performed well.
$8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027 related to transitioning from a seasonal office leadership model to a year-round structure.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 4.9% with a healthy balance of volume, price (up ~3%), and mix (up 1%) in the assisted category.
Conversion improved 200 basis points, marking the largest single-year improvement in recorded history due to customer journey refinements.
Wave small business services delivered its second consecutive year of double-digit revenue growth driven by paid pro tier subscriptions.
summary: H&R Block reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $3.95 billion (up 4.9%) and adjusted EPS of $5.31 (up 13.9%), driven by higher net average charge, volume growth in assisted tax preparation, and momentum from Wave small business services. Management raised the full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to a range of $4.11 billion-$4.16 billion while maintaining adjusted EBITDA between $1.11 billion-$1.14 billion and raising the quarterly dividend by 10% to $0.46 per share.

negative_highlights: Gross margin faces near-term pressure from a higher mix of purchase subscriptions (60% vs prior guidance) and costs associated with redeploying Gen1 units.
Component and supply chain costs are running modestly higher than anticipated, creating approximately half a point of gross margin headwind.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34% year-over-year driven by new customer wins (70 added) and expansion within existing customers.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10.1%, up from 6.5% in the prior year quarter, demonstrating operating leverage despite investments.
Net revenue retention remained above 100% with ARR growing 20% YoY to $132.7 million.
summary: Evolv Technology reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.8 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 10.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $180-$185 million from the prior forecast of $175-$180 million, citing strong demand for Gen2 upgrades and multi-product adoption.

negative_highlights: FDA communication regarding IGE PMA supplement was not approvable in its current form, requiring additional clinical evidence and an amendment process via the SIR.
Service revenue declined significantly to $0.3 million from $0.9 million a year ago due to discontinued operations with DIXI Medical.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 17% year-over-year driven by a 21.3% increase in RNS System revenue ($22.5M).
Full-year total revenue guidance was raised to $99.5 million-$101.5 million, up from the previous range of $99 million-$101 million.
Adjusted gross margin remained strong at 83.4% despite a slight year-over-year decline.
summary: NeuroPace reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $22.8 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted gross margin of 83.4%, slightly down from the prior year due to material costs but supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $99.5M-$101.5M, reflecting improved visibility into service revenue which is now expected at approximately $1 million for the full year versus a previous expectation of $500k. However, the company disclosed that its PMA supplement expansion into idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE) was not approvable in its current form due to FDA requests for additional clinical evidence regarding specific patient subgroups.

negative_highlights: Net income was heavily skewed by an $82.8 million unrealized gain; operating performance is obscured by volatile fair value accounting.
Full run-rate cost savings of approximately $4-5 million from legacy operations will not be realized until Q4 due to transition costs and lingering obligations.
Management explicitly stated they do not assume current staking yields (approx. 17% annualized) can continue indefinitely as the network matures.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue increased significantly year-over-year (implied) driven by higher staking rewards of approximately $15 million compared to Q1's $3 million.
Gross profit margin remained strong at 95% with gross earnings of $14.3 million on total revenue.
Operating income turned positive at approximately $0.5 million, a turnaround from the first quarter loss despite recognizing non-cash charges.
summary: Q2 revenue was $15 million and GAAP net income was approximately $83.5 million, driven by a non-cash fair value gain of $82.8 million on Gram holdings rather than operational earnings power. Management raised the full run-rate OpEx savings from legacy Verb wind-downs to Q4 2026 due to transition costs and noted that staking yields are expected to evolve as the network matures, explicitly avoiding assumptions about indefinite current economics.

negative_highlights: Recognized a non-cash loss of approximately $32 million associated with changes in fair value of derivative and warrants liability.
Net loss for the quarter was approximately $33.8 million after offsetting gains on debt extinguishment.
Ongoing investment in MetCom Japan faces unmet considerations regarding Japanese government spectrum positioning agreements, delaying warrant access.
positive_highlights: Company became debt-free and increased available liquidity to approximately $300 million (comprised of roughly $230M cash equivalents/securities plus warrant proceeds).
Announced a strategic partnership with Safran Electronics & Defense to validate interoperability between NextNav's 5G PNT network and navigation receivers.
Demonstrated ~20 ns timing accuracy over the operational 5G PNT network in real-world environments, exceeding critical infrastructure requirements.
summary: NextNav reported a net loss of approximately $33.8 million for Q2 FY2026 due to a non-cash derivative liability loss of roughly $32 million and warrant exercise proceeds offset by debt extinguishment gains, resulting in no GAAP or adjusted EPS beat against implied breakeven expectations from the prior period's transformational narrative. Management provided no specific revenue guidance but highlighted significant financial restructuring including becoming debt-free with approximately $300 million in liquidity as of June 30th and converting all outstanding warrants to shares. The company emphasized steady progress on FCC regulatory milestones, a new partnership with Safran Electronics & Defense for terrestrial 5G PNT validation, and technical achievements like demonstrating ~20 ns timing accuracy.

negative_highlights: Substantial doubt remains regarding the company's ability to continue as a going concern, with cash declining from $4.1M at year-end to $3.6M despite financing activities.
Net loss widened to $2.7 million (from $2.3M prior year) due to increased operating expenses and heavy working capital investment in inventory ($2.3M).
Management explicitly warned that Q2 margin expansion should not be assumed to repeat, citing sensitivity to product mix, pricing, and manufacturing efficiency.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 199% year-over-year driven by product sales growth of 347%. Gross margins expanded significantly from 38% to approximately 62% due to favorable mix and pricing on OEM products. The company received purchase orders exceeding $3.2 million for industrial manufacturing components.
The SINAPTIC Foot and Ankle Osteotomy Wedge System achieved FDA clearance in late 2025 and recognized initial commercial revenue following its first clinical use in March 2026.
summary: SINTX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $452,000 (up 199% YoY) and gross margins expanding to approximately 62%, driven by a shift from grant/contract work to product sales. However, the company incurred a net loss of $2.7 million with cash declining to $3.6 million due to significant working capital investment in inventory ($2.3M). Management provided Q3 guidance of $900k-$1.1M revenue but explicitly reiterated substantial doubt regarding its ability to continue as a going concern.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 44.2% from 44.4% YoY, primarily due to revenue mix shifts and Ximalaya amortization.
Subscription growth moderated in the core music business excluding Ximalaya consolidation effects.
Advertising business faces headwinds despite actions to improve ad exposure and eCPM.
positive_highlights: IP-related consumption services delivered strong double-digit year-over-year growth driven by live events and merchandise sales.
SVIP user base saw highest growth in ARPPU, time spent, retention, and conversion of premium ancillary experiences.
Completed $400 million share buyback in Q2 under the existing program while preparing for a new round.
summary: TME reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 8.9 billion (up 6% YoY) and net profit attributable to equity holders of RMB 2.5 billion (up from RMB 2.4 billion in the prior year). The quarter included approximately RMB 0.4 billion of revenues from Ximalaya consolidation, while gross margin declined slightly to 44.2% due to revenue mix shifts toward offline services and amortization impacts.

negative_highlights: Pharma revenue growth is expected to normalize from outsized levels in FY26, incorporating headwinds from annualizing IRA price changes.
GMPD segment reported a 2% decline due to customer payables related to the tariff refund and lower distribution volumes.
positive_highlights: Enterprise operating earnings grew 30% to $935 million, with Pharma profit up 21% driven by brand/specialty growth offsetting IRA headwinds.
Adjusted free cash flow reached a record $5 billion for the fiscal year while maintaining strong liquidity and low leverage.
GMPD segment profitability improved significantly due to operational simplification initiatives and a one-time tariff refund benefit.
summary: Cardinal Health reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $63.7 billion (up 6%) and adjusted EPS growth of 40% to $2.91, driven by strong Pharmaceutical volume demand and a one-time $100 million IEEPA tariff refund benefit in the GMPD segment. Management raised fiscal 2027 guidance for enterprise-wide non-GAAP EPS growth to 13%-15%, projecting full-year earnings between $12.40 and $12.60, while reconfirming long-term organic EPS growth of 12%-14%. The company generated $5 billion in adjusted free cash flow for the year and authorized a new $4 billion revolver facility alongside an increased share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Net non-operating income declined to $66 million from $83 million in the prior year quarter.
Income tax expense increased significantly to $451 million compared to $144 million last year, impacting net income growth.
positive_highlights: Shopee adjusted EBITDA reached $255 million (up 12% YoY) with ad revenue up more than 70% YoY.
Monee loan book grew to $11.1 billion (+62% YoY) while maintaining a stable NPL ratio of 1.0%.
Garena bookings increased 15% YoY, driven by Free Fire's continued scale and new IP launches like Palworld Online.
summary: Sea reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.8 billion (up 48% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of over $917 million (up 11% YoY). Management reaffirmed full-year GMV growth guidance at around 25%, citing strong momentum in Shopee, Monee, and Garena across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Brazil, and other markets. The company highlighted significant unit economics improvements, particularly in logistics fulfillment and advertising take rates.

negative_highlights: Consolidated sales decreased 2.3% year-over-year as volume declines in fresh pork (down 5.5%) offset price increases.
Fresh pork segment operating profit dropped significantly due to $37 million of industry market spread compression, resulting in a low 0.7% margin.
Full-year outlook lowered for both total company adjusted operating profit and sales range reflecting persistent inflationary inputs and softer demand.
positive_highlights: Record second quarter adjusted operating profit of $300 million with margin expansion to 8.1% despite industry headwinds.
Packaged meats segment delivered strong profitability at an 13.1% adjusted operating margin, up from the prior year's lower base due to cost pressures.
Hog production achieved six consecutive quarters of profitability driven by higher note prices and operational efficiency savings.
summary: Smithfield Foods reported record second quarter adjusted operating profit of $300 million and diluted EPS of $0.62, though consolidated sales declined 2.3% year-over-year to $3.7 billion due to volume pressure in fresh pork and packaged meats. Management updated its full-year outlook downward for total company adjusted operating profit (now expected between $1.225B-$1.375B) and sales guidance, citing softer commodity market assumptions and a cautious consumer environment.

negative_highlights: Commercial sheet door revenues declined significantly due to headwinds in pre-engineered metal buildings
North America organic self-storage revenue expected to be down high single digits for the full year
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by approximately 430 basis points compared to the prior year
positive_highlights: Nokē Smart Entry platform surpassed the milestone of 500,000 installed units
International segment grew by 9.5% driven by new construction and market share gains
R3 business showed growth in door replacements and redevelopment activity
summary: Second quarter revenue of $233.5 million beat consensus estimates but adjusted EBITDA missed at $40.2 million due to a decline in commercial sheet door demand and lower margins driven by product mix. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting organic North America self-storage revenues down high single digits and adjusting Kiwi II Construction revenue expectations to reflect project delays.

negative_highlights: Supply constraints across wafers, packaging, substrates, and testing limit second-half revenue potential despite strong demand
Non-GAAP net loss of $1.8M with OpEx rising to ~$24-25M in Q3 due to IP purchases for new product development
positive_highlights: Net sales grew ~90% YoY with revenue outside top three customers surging 143% YoY
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 450 bps to 47.2%, driven by favorable mix and manufacturing efficiencies
Apollo5 sales more than doubled year-over-year while Apollo3/Apollo4 maintained double-digit growth
summary: Ambiq reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $33.9 million (up ~90% YoY) and non-GAAP gross profit more than doubling to $16M on a margin expansion to 47.2%. Management raised full-year guidance to approximately $135M despite supply constraints, citing accelerating demand for edge AI that exceeds initial forecasts.

negative_highlights: Assets under administration declined 5% year-over-year in July due to lower crypto pricing.
Crypto net contribution fell YoY, reflecting a cyclical shift of users toward equities rather than structural decline.
July trading activity was impacted by seasonality and a correction in popular stocks.
positive_highlights: Net contribution increased 9% year-over-year to $229 million driven by strong equity trading volume.
Funded accounts grew 18% year-over-year to 4.28 million, supported by marketing investment and retention improvements.
Announced acquisition of TradeZero for up to $230-231 million to accelerate U.S. expansion with futures and options capabilities.
summary: eToro reported Q2 FY26 net contribution of $229 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $78 million (up 9% YoY), with funded accounts growing 18% to 4.28 million despite a sequential dip in assets under administration due to crypto price declines. The company announced the planned acquisition of TradeZero for up to $230-231 million, which is expected to close in H1 FY27 and strengthen its U.S. presence with futures and options capabilities. Management noted that July KPIs showed a sequential pullback in AUA but expressed confidence that activity will recover as markets stabilize.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from 22.4% in Q1 FY2025 to 21.4% due to a $5.9 million increase in G&A expenses driven by public company costs and stock-based compensation.
Routine scan volumes showed some weakness compared to the strong performance of advanced imaging, though mammography volumes improved after a slower start.
Stock-based compensation expense increased significantly from $8.3M to $12.7M due to one-time resetting of legacy equity plans post-IPO.
positive_highlights: Advanced modalities grew 6.3% system-wide, reaching a record high of 37.4% of total volume and driving higher reimbursement rates.
Free cash flow converted to $23.1 million in Q2, marking a record for the company with roughly 41% conversion of adjusted EBITDA.
Successfully opened two de novo centers this year against an annual goal of eight to ten, including new partnerships with UPMC and Hospital for Special Surgery.
summary: Consolidated revenues reached $264.2 million in Q2 FY2026, representing a 5.1% year-over-year increase driven by advanced modality volumes growing 6.3%. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $56.4 million compared to the prior year quarter due to incremental public company costs and stock-based compensation increases offsetting strong underlying volume growth. Management narrowed its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance range from $234M-$242M to $235M-$241M while maintaining revenue guidance at $1.045B-$1.097B.

negative_highlights: OEM security revenue is expected to be $40M-$50M lower in the second half due to a large customer pursuing vertical integration.
Input costs (memory, metals, PCBs) are increasing at a pace greater than originally expected for Q3 and Q4.
Cash flow from operations decreased YoY by ~$52M primarily due to $45M in payments for non-recurring business separation activities.
positive_highlights: Total adjusted EBITDA grew 19% year-over-year driven by volume increases and favorable manufacturing variances.
Products & Solutions achieved gross margin expansion for the 13th consecutive quarter, reaching 43.6% (up 70 bps YoY).
New product adoption remains strong ahead of expectations in smoke/CO detectors and Honeywell Home ElitePRO thermostats.
summary: Resideo reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of just under $2 billion (up ~2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $249 million (up 19% YoY), exceeding the high end of prior guidance. Management provided a standalone full-year 2026 outlook with revenue between $2.9B-$2.95B, which represents a lower growth rate than previously implied for the combined entity due to the ADI spin-off and specific headwinds in the OEM security channel.

negative_highlights: No specific financial figures (revenue or EPS) were disclosed in the transcript; results are referenced only as 'second-quarter financial results' without quantitative detail.
The Q4 disclosure of whether the month 15 primary endpoint was met will be determined by an independent Data Monitoring Committee, with full data remaining masked until that decision is made.
positive_highlights: ARCHER II trial execution exceeded targets with patient discontinuation rate under 10% and dosing compliance over 95%. The company added a month 24 endpoint using 'found money' from strong enrollment (30 patients above target) without weakening the primary study.

Initial FORWARD cohort data for GBS showed rapid improvement in all 10 treated patients, with four bed-bound patients regaining ability to walk within eight days and one patient weaned from a ventilator in four days.
Annexon secured $200 million in non-dilutive capital via a credit facility with Oxford Finance, extending its cash runway into 2028.
summary: Annexon reported Q2 FY2026 financial results and announced a strategic expansion of its ARCHER II phase III trial for vonaprument in geographic atrophy by adding an independent month 24 dual primary endpoint alongside the existing month 15 readout. Management expressed strong confidence that the study will meet or exceed targets at both time points, citing robust patient retention (discontinuation rate <10%) and dosing compliance (>95%). The company also confirmed it is on track to submit a BLA for its GBS drug candidate tanruprubart in Q4 2026 following positive initial FORWARD study data.

negative_highlights: Q2 adjusted EBITDA decreased $44.7 million sequentially due to startup delays and transition costs.
Recognized a one-time credit loss provision of $10.8 million related to a former West African customer, leaving net zero receivables from that entity.
Odin contract preparations took longer than anticipated with regulatory approvals received only in mid-July.
positive_highlights: Secured eight new contract commitments representing over 2,100 days of additional work across Asia, West Africa, North Sea, and Americas.
Galar and Gersemi contracts in Mexico extended by two years each into 2030.
Successfully refinanced debt to extend maturities significantly while reducing financing costs.
summary: Q2 adjusted EBITDA declined $44.7 million to $43.8 million due to startup costs for the Odin rig ($11.1M increase), higher fuel/insurance expenses from Middle East conflict ($7.3M increase), and a credit loss provision of $10.8 million, resulting in a net loss of $241.4 million. Management expects Q3 adjusted EBITDA to improve significantly as six transitioning rigs resume operations alongside the Odin commencing work, targeting an average fleet size of 23 active rigs for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Repairable claims volumes were estimated to be flat to down 2% year over year, indicating limited demand recovery compared to prior declines.
Net earnings of $1.3 million missed the adjusted net earnings growth narrative due to higher amortization and depreciation costs related to new location acquisitions.
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history with a 30% year-over-year increase.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 140 basis points to 13.4%, driven by Project 360 cost savings and Joe Hudson's synergies.
Same-store sales growth of 2.9% confirmed continued market share gains despite a flat-to-down claims volume environment.
summary: Boyd Group Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1 billion (up 30% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 45%, driven by a new location footprint expansion and same-store sales growth of 2.9%. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 13.4%, reflecting accelerated synergy realization from the Joe Hudson's acquisition, leading management to raise their full-year synergy target to $35 million.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.8M (vs $7M prior period) due to higher R&D spend on the ChoICE Study ($4.3M vs $3.4M).
Gross margin expansion was dampened by foreign exchange fluctuations rather than pure operational leverage.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 45% year-over-year to $1.8M driven by system sales and probe utilization growth.
summary: IceCure Medical reported first-half FY2026 revenue of $1.8 million, representing a 45% year-over-year increase driven by higher sales of ProSense systems and disposable probes. Gross margin expanded to 30%, though this was partially offset by foreign exchange fluctuations compared to the prior period's 28%. The company ended with approximately $12 million in cash following financing activities.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $154 million due to $110M in accelerated share-based compensation expense
Consolidated gross margin compressed to 22.2% YoY, though management notes this is a typical note weakness in learning curve for new programs
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $167.3 million driven across all three end markets
Contract backlog grew to a record over $1.1 billion, providing strong visibility into 2027
Net leverage reduced pro forma to 2.7x following IPO debt repayment
summary: Applied Aerospace & Defense reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $167.3 million (up 47% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $36.4 million following its IPO. Management raised full-year guidance to a range of $670-$690M in revenue, citing strong backlog conversion and second-half volume ramps. The quarter was impacted by one-time share-based compensation from the accelerated vesting at IPO.

negative_highlights: FID delayed until later in the year compared to earlier hopes for Q2 end
$800k investment loss from joint ventures increased slightly vs prior period
Remains dependent on finalizing offtake agreements before FID
positive_highlights: Completed federal environmental review with FONSI from DOE
Signed primary construction contracts with Wood Group and S&B Engineers
Net loss narrowed $1.9 million YoY due to FX gains of $2.7M
summary: Standard Lithium reported a net loss of $3.1 million for Q2 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $5 million loss driven by higher cash balances and FX gains. The company successfully completed two major pre-FID milestones: securing construction contracts with Wood Group and S&B Engineers, and receiving a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) on its NEPA review for the Southwest Arkansas project. Management maintains an unchanged expectation to achieve Final Investment Decision later in 2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $15 million due to higher depreciation, interest expense, and a one-time customer termination.
Revenue included approximately $12.3 million associated with a previously disclosed customer termination.
NC-1 ramp was affected by delivering and commissioning issues involving switchgear equipment before resolution.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 54% YoY to $28.8 million, with cloud services revenue growing from $16.6M to $23.8M.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $5.5 million compared to a prior period of $3.3 million.
Signed new multi-year agreements representing over $270 million in aggregate contract value with Baseten and Prime Intellect.
summary: WhiteFiber reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $28.8 million, a 54% year-over-year increase driven by cloud services growth to $23.8 million and colocation ramping at MTL-3. The company achieved positive Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million despite a net loss of $15 million due to higher depreciation on infrastructure expansion. Management highlighted significant progress in securing long-term contracts, including new multi-year agreements with Baseten ($165M value) and Prime Intellect ($108M value), while noting that the NC-1 site has commenced initial billing for its first tranche of capacity.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 30 basis points in Q2, with a specific headwind of roughly 100 basis points expected for the third quarter due to produce pressure.
Basket size declined approximately 2.1% year-over-year despite traffic growth and sequential improvement from Q1.
GAAP effective tax rate increased significantly to 38.8% compared with 20.3% last year, impacting net income.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA and diluted adjusted EPS exceeded management's outlook due to disciplined cost management and reduced liquidation activity.
Opportunistic comp accelerated meaningfully in Q2, improving by over 500 basis points relative to the start of the year.
Gross margin improved sequentially by 60 basis points from Q1 as promotional spending tapered.
summary: Revenue increased 1% to $1.19 billion while comparable store sales declined 30 basis points due to Easter timing and a Cyclospora outbreak headwind expected in Q3. Adjusted EPS of $0.20 beat the outlook, driven by gross margin expansion to 30.2% from lower promotional spending despite flat gross profit dollars. Management raised full-year net sales guidance slightly but maintained comparable store sales expectations near zero.

negative_highlights: Total revenue missed expectations with a 15% year-over-year decline to $7.3 million due to discontinued partner programs and timing of instrument placements.
Gross margin contracted to 77%, impacted by product mix shifts toward lower-margin instruments and inventory provisions.
Processing assembly (PA) revenue fell 20% YoY as the largest customer completed its inventory drawdown, creating a difficult comparison.
positive_highlights: Announced a significant multi-platform technology license partnership with Genentech covering research through commercial manufacturing, diversifying beyond traditional SPLs.
SPL program-related revenue grew to $0.8 million (vs $0.3M prior year) driven by CASGEVY royalties and Vertex's strong uptake in the U.K., Italy, and Middle East.
Operating expenses decreased 25% YoY as restructuring actions from 2025 are fully realized.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.3 million (down 15% YoY) and core revenue of $6.5 million (down 21% YoY), driven by lower license revenue from discontinued programs and a difficult comparison to accelerated PA purchases in the prior year quarter. Gross margin contracted to 77%, while operating expenses decreased significantly due to restructuring benefits, resulting in an improved net loss despite the top-line miss. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $30M-$32M total revenue with low single-digit growth expected for H2.

negative_highlights: Finance expenses were $1.3 million due to the strengthening Israeli shekel against the USD
IturanMOB in the U.S. remains in a low mode with very few monetized customers so far
UBI segment growth is limited primarily to Israel and Argentina with low ARPU
positive_highlights: Record revenue growth of 21% year-over-year to $104.8 million
Recurring subscription revenue grew by 25% YoY, now representing 76% of total revenues
Net income increased 29% YoY with operating leverage shining through
summary: Ituran reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $104.8 million (up 21% YoY) and net income of $17.3 million (up 29% YoY), driven by a recurring subscription base growing to $80 million. The company added 41,000 net new subscribers for a total of 2.711 million and generated record cash flow from operations of $32.2 million. Management declared a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share ($10M) and executed $3M in buybacks.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $68.3 million from $66.1 million in the prior year quarter
note, general, and administrative expenses increased significantly to $31.8 million compared to $25.2 million last year
positive_highlights: KOMZIFTI captured majority share of new patient starts in relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutated AML menin inhibitor market within only the second full quarter on the market
New patient starts grew approximately 35% sequentially, while total prescriptions (TRx) growth was about 60%
Clinical data from KOMET-007 showed an overall response rate of 87% in venetoclax-naive patients and a median overall survival not reached at almost 11 months follow-up
summary: Kura Oncology reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $9.1 million from KOMZIFTI and collaboration revenue of $11.8 million versus a prior year period with no product sales; the company achieved majority share of new patient starts in its second full quarter despite being second to market, driven by 35% sequential growth in new patients and strong clinical data supporting combination strategies.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $22.9M due to a one-time debt extinguishment charge of $11.7 million.

note, general, and administrative expenses increased quarter-over-quarter by approximately $1.4 million (from $12.7M to $14.1M) primarily due to higher legal fees ($2.1M), severance costs ($1.4M), and personnel costs.
Management explicitly stated the resubmission will be a standard six-month review, indicating no acceleration in approval timeline despite positive data.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased to $13.8M YoY (38% growth) driven by Suboxone supply revenue increases.
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to a $5.2 million quarterly loss from a prior year loss of $9.3 million.
Human factors and PK studies for Anaphylm showed statistically significant improvements in packaging usability and comparable efficacy to manual IM administration even with misadministration.
summary: Aquestive reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $13.8 million (up from $10M in the prior year quarter) and a net loss of $22.9 million ($0.18/share), driven by an $11.7 million one-time debt extinguishment charge on its 13.5% notes. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of $46-$50 million but reiterated that the Anaphylm resubmission will be a standard six-month review, with no specific date raised despite positive human factors and PK data supporting the filing in Q3.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was 46%, down from prior periods due to mix shifts including lower-margin ticketing activity and ramp-up of new merchants.
GAAP net loss widened slightly year-over-year to a $9.1 million loss, impacted by foreign currency fluctuations.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% YoY to $98.7 million, marking the strongest year-over-year growth in over four years.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 84% to $3.9 million as cost discipline and scaling efficiency improved margins.
Digital Finance category accelerated with approximately 180% YoY growth driven by new merchant onboarding.
summary: Riskified reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $98.7 million (up 22% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.9 million (an 84% increase). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($405M midpoint, up from prior range) and adjusted EBITDA ($36M midpoint), citing accelerated growth driven by Digital Finance expansion and live sports events.

negative_highlights: GMV growth slowed due to supply disruptions in phones/electronics categories, specifically entry-level smartphones.
Ivory Coast physical goods GMV declined 1% YoY driven by a nearly 60% drop in cocoa farm gate prices reducing purchasing power.
Management lowered the full-year GMV guidance range from prior expectations to account for persistent supply chain volatility.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by 36% year-over-year while absorbing significant supply chain disruptions.
Gross profit expanded 28% YoY as higher take rates on non-electronic categories offset lower GMV from electronics shortages.
Fulfillment cost per order decreased 7% YoY to $2.04 despite temporary fuel surcharges and one-time termination costs.
summary: Jumia reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $52 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $8.7 million from a prior year loss of $13.6 million, driven by strong growth in lower-margin categories like fashion and home goods that offset supply disruptions in phones/electronics. Management maintained its full-year profitability guidance despite lowering the GMV outlook due to external headwinds including memory chip shortages, fuel surcharges, and demand pressure from falling cocoa prices in Ivory Coast.

negative_highlights: Sugar/ethanol segment adjusted EBITDA declined year-over-year driven by lower sugar prices and volumes sold as well as a strategic shift toward ethanol inventory building.
Production costs were negatively impacted in the quarter due to the appreciation of the Brazilian Real, though excluding FX effects local currency costs remained flat.
Ethanol sales volumes decreased as part of commercial strategy to build inventories following sharp declines in domestic prices caused by higher market supply.
positive_highlights: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA set new records at $173 million in Q2, up from prior periods despite mixed portfolio dynamics.
Fertilizer segment delivered strong performance with urea production increasing 22% year-over-year and margins expanding significantly due to higher international prices captured during the quarter.
Sugarcane plantation conditions are excellent with yields recovering thanks to normalized weather following El Niño, driving crushing volume growth.
summary: Adecoagro reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $173 million and gross sales of $535 million; while the fertilizer segment drove record earnings with higher volumes and prices, results in sugar/ethanol were softer due to lower sugar prices/volumes and a strategic decision to hold ethanol inventories. Management raised full-year guidance for fertilizers above initial projections but maintained caution on other segments citing inventory strategies and market volatility.

negative_highlights: Theater bookings are currently pacing behind goals for September and December quarters, though management expects to narrow the gap.
Family show category faces a tough year-over-year comparison due to the absence of Cirque du Soleil's holiday run at the Infosys Theater.
positive_highlights: Revenues increased 27% year-over-year to $196.3M driven by concert volume and Knicks championship share revenue ($7.4M increase).
Adjusted operating income turned positive at $18.6 million, a swing of nearly $20M from the prior quarter's loss.
Christmas Spectacular attendance hit 1.2 million tickets (highest in 25 years) with sales for 230 shows.
summary: Fiscal Q4 FY26 revenues were $196.3 million, up 27% year-over-year driven by a more than doubling of concerts at The Garden and shared revenue from the Knicks' NBA championship run (a $7.4M increase in quarter). Adjusted operating income swung to an $18.6 million profit from a loss in the prior period. Management raised fiscal 2027 guidance expectations, citing strong demand momentum for events across venues.

negative_highlights: Retail Point of Sale (POS) remained relatively flat or cautious due to conservative inventory management among major retail partners.
Helly Hansen reported a $0.06 per share loss for the quarter, though well ahead of expectations and historical performance.
Full-year SG&A expenses are expected to increase approximately 23% YoY as Helly Hansen operates on a full year basis.
positive_highlights: Helly Hansen revenue grew 6% in Q2 on a pro forma basis, exceeding expectations with strong performance across sport and workwear categories.
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 53.8%, up 710 bps YoY due to Project Genius savings and favorable mix/pricing.
Wrangler gained market share for the 17th consecutive quarter in bottoms business, supported by double-digit growth in female and Western categories.
summary: Kontoor Brands reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.2 billion (high end of outlook) and adjusted EPS of $2.12 (36% YoY increase), driven by strong Helly Hansen performance (+19% pro forma growth in first half). Management raised the full-year 2026 guidance for both operating income ($413M-$420M vs prior $411M-$418M) and EPS ($5.25-$5.35 vs prior $5.15-$5.25), citing mid-single-digit growth expectations for the second half despite conservative retail inventory levels.

negative_highlights: Total cash cost guidance was raised due to increased royalties from strong gold prices, higher diesel costs, and elevated explosive expenses.
Non-sustaining capital expenditure guidance for the year was revised upward by $9 million following the acceleration of heap leach pad construction into Q2 2026.
positive_highlights: Gold production surged 30% quarter-over-quarter to 16,379 oz driven by record mining rates.
Operating cash flow increased 40% year-over-year to $22.8 million as the mine transitions into higher output phases.
Updated life-of-mine plan extends active mine life to eight years and increases annual production profile.
summary: Integra Resources reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $70.8 million and adjusted EPS of $0.06 per share, representing a beat on the prior year's earnings while maintaining full-year production guidance at 70k-75k oz despite higher costs. The company maintained its AISC guidance range but raised total cash cost guidance to reflect increased royalties from strong gold prices and higher fuel/explosive expenses. Management highlighted record throughput of 87,867 tons per day and a significant increase in ore placed on heap leach pads.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 38% YoY due to the cancellation of the WildFireSat contract for convenience.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$8.6 million, with breakeven expected by late 2026 or early 2027.
positive_highlights: Core revenue expanded sequentially by 19% YoY, marking the strongest core quarter since divestiture.
Over 85% of full-year guidance is under contract as of end-July, up from 76% in May.
Secured awards from four new international RFGL customers and signed a $5M+ NOAA HyMS data extension.
summary: Spire reported Q2 FY26 core revenue of $18 million, representing a 16% year-over-year increase and a 19% sequential gain driven by space services data delivery and increased RFGL purchases. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $75-$85 million (midpoint ~$80M), noting that over 85% of the midpoint is already under contract as of late July, despite a one-time gross margin contraction to 38% caused by the cancellation of the WildFireSat contract. The company highlighted progress on NOAA negotiations for an eight-figure microwave sounding opportunity and expects its Radio Occultation (RO) follow-on award in September to exceed last year's $11.2M annual value.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses surged $8.4 million YoY to $13.8 million due to R&D investments and integration costs
Net loss widened significantly to $14.1 million ($0.79/share) compared to a prior year net loss of $6.3 million
No specific revenue or EPS guidance was provided for the next quarter, relying instead on qualitative forward statements
positive_highlights: Revenue hit a new quarterly record of $9 million, up >200% YoY
Gross margin expanded to positive territory at ~7%, driven by acquisition synergies and maturing machines
Client base grew to 434 clients across 42 states with strong retention in the acquired Security Force portfolio
summary: Second quarter revenue reached a record $9 million, representing more than 200% year-over-year growth driven by the Security Force acquisition and core subscriptions. Gross margin turned positive at approximately 7%, marking the second consecutive quarter of profitability following an accretive acquisition integration. Management reiterated that every subsequent quarter will be better than the last while noting no specific numerical guidance was provided for future periods.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell sharply by 33% year-over-year to $11.8 million due to deferred deployments in private cloud/on-premises segments.
Operating loss widened to negative $2.2 million (or -18.5% of revenue) from a prior operating income, driven by lower sales and increased R&D spending.
Net loss per diluted share was $0.09 compared to net income of $0.25 in the same quarter last year.
positive_highlights: Secured three new contracts post-quarter-end with CETIN Networks, a Tier 1 operator in Asia Pacific, and an existing European customer for network visibility.
Gross margin remained resilient at 76.3% despite the revenue decline.
Company maintains strong balance sheet with $109.7 million cash equivalent and no debt.
summary: RADCOM reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $11.8 million, a decline of 33% year-over-year compared to $17.7 million in the prior period, driven by customer deployment delays due to rising server infrastructure costs rather than demand weakness or competitive loss. Management reaffirmed its revised full-year 2026 guidance range of $57-$63 million (midpoint $60M) and announced a new share repurchase program of $20-25 million, while noting that deployment activity is expected to normalize in Q1 FY27.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $54.7 million in H1 and $28.6 million in Q2 due to launch-related SG&A increases
Q2 revenue was suppressed by low coverage levels resulting in high denial conversion rates where scripts were effectively given away at zero net price
Average note prices remain depressed until co-pay mitigation decreases as commercial coverage reaches critical mass
positive_highlights: Commercial coverage expanded from ~25% at quarter-end to over 50% of commercially insured lives driven by UnitedHealthcare/Express Scripts decisions
Unique prescribers grew significantly from ~200 in Q1 to >600 in Q2, totaling >800 for the first half
Phase III AFib-RVR trial (ReVeRA-301) lead clinical sites are now active with patient enrollment expected shortly
summary: Milestone Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY26 product revenue of $0.6 million and a net loss of $28.6 million ($0.21/share), driven by significant increases in SG&A expenses to $22.6 million due to commercial launch costs, while R&D decreased slightly to $3.5 million. Management highlighted that Q2 coverage was only 25% but noted meaningful progress post-quarter close pushing total covered lives past the 50% threshold for commercially insured patients. The company expects revenue per script and prescription volume to improve in H2 as co-pay mitigation decreases with broader formulary access.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from a prior quarter's -$17.2M to -$67.7M due to one-time charges of $48.8M related to convertible note conversions and term loan repayment.
Adjusted EBITDA declined slightly to negative $14 million compared to the first quarter, as revenue recognition was impacted by timing shifts in project deliveries rather than a lack of demand.
Ongoing services revenue decreased 15% sequentially due to non-recurring campaign work performed in Q1 that did not repeat in this period.
positive_highlights: Backlog surged to a record $1.7 billion, representing a 10x year-over-year increase fueled by large-scale orders including a new agreement with Anthropic for 470 MW of generation capacity.
Gross margin expanded sequentially to an adjusted gross margin of 22.2% as the company delivered more generators and installation work compared to Q1.
The IPO raised approximately $400 million in proceeds, leaving the balance sheet with strong liquidity including $627 million in unrestricted cash and no outstanding debt.
summary: ERock reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $39.9 million (up 26% sequentially) and a net loss of $67.7 million driven by non-recurring IPO-related debt extinguishment losses totaling $48.8 million, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA miss relative to the prior quarter's -$12.4M as guidance was not yet issued at that time but implied positive H2 2026. Management provided full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $435-$465 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3-$9 million, projecting a return to profitability in the second half driven by backlog conversion.

negative_highlights: North America revenue share jumped disproportionately high (31%) due to large Tera III product deals rather than pure organic growth in that region.
Gross margin declined slightly YoY from 73.4% to 71.8%, primarily reflecting a shift toward higher-margin product sales versus recurring services.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year with Security-as-a-Service revenue surging 47% YoY to $9.4 million.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded significantly from 5% in the prior year quarter to 9.9% this quarter.
Operating cash flow strengthened materially, reaching $8.5 million compared to $4 million a year ago.
summary: Allot reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $27.7 million (up 15% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.09, driven by a 47% increase in Security-as-a-Service revenue to $9.4 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from the previous range of $113M-$117M to $115M-$118M and narrowed it due to accelerating order momentum, particularly in North America where recurring revenues now represent two-thirds of total sales.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance implies a sequential slowdown (approx. flat growth) as model breakthroughs realized in Q2 are now embedded, reducing near-term upside.
The company expects an adverse impact on margins in Q3 due to the timing of certain expenses that benefited Q2.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 35% year-over-year to $220 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 60%, representing a sequential expansion of approximately 2 percentage points.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to the range of $870M-$880M, implying roughly 4% higher growth than prior expectations due to model breakthroughs monetizing sooner than expected.
Free cash flow generation improved significantly to $50 million in Q2 compared to $15 million in the same period last year.
summary: Liftoff reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $220 million (up 35% YoY and 7% QoQ) with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 60%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue between $870M-$880M ($27-28% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $510M-$518M. The strong performance was driven by market expansion, Cortex self-learning, model breakthroughs, and specific demand from the FIFA World Cup.

negative_highlights: First commercial spaceflight delayed from original schedule due to note of small installation tasks requiring more time than estimated.
Capital expenditures expected to temporarily increase in Q3 and Q4 before resuming a downward trend later in FY2026.
No revenue recognized for the quarter as commercial operations are not yet active, with cash inflows starting only upon customer signing conditions of carriage prior to flights.
positive_highlights: Over $50 million added to expected future revenue due to oversubscription on the recent tranche at the $750,000 price point.
The company raised $134 million via its ATM program and reduced principal debt payments by $93 million in Q2.
Free cash flow improved 20% year-over-year to -$91 million despite increased labor intensity on the first ship.
summary: Virgin Galactic reported Q2 FY2026 with operating expenses of $65 million and capital expenditures of $41 million, resulting in free cash flow of -$91 million. Management raised the first commercial spaceflight to February 2027 due to modest time extensions on installation tasks but noted that a new tranche at higher price points was oversubscribed by over $50 million. The company expects quarterly positive cash flow within 2027 and projects adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1 billion annually with two fully utilized space ports.

negative_highlights: Power sales volume decreased by 0.6% YoY driven by an economic slowdown in industrial demand.
Nuclear power capacity factor declined for four consecutive quarters due to prolonged preventive maintenance.
Fuel costs increased significantly by 8.8%, with SMP rising from KRW 121/kWh (July '25) to KRW 133-151/kWh in H1 FY26.
positive_highlights: Other revenue increased by 16.7% YoY to KRW 2,353 billion due to overseas business growth.
Interest expense decreased by KRW 132.2 billion YoY to KRW 2,790 million.
summary: KEPCO reported H1 FY26 revenue of KRW 46,317 billion (up 0.3% YoY) and net income of KRW 2,796.5 billion, driven by a 16.7% increase in other revenue but offset by power sales declining 0.4%. Management noted that while full-year nuclear contribution is expected to slightly rise due to Saeul Unit 3 additions, H1 capacity factors were weak and fuel costs rose 8.8%, leading to cautious guidance on tariff hikes for the remainder of the year.

negative_highlights: Policy acquisition expenses increased substantially to $17.4 million compared to $6.3 million in the prior year period.
New construction volumes in Florida have plateaued, though management notes diversification into other states is offsetting this slowdown.
positive_highlights: Income before taxes hit an all-time quarterly record of $46.4 million, up 93% YoY driven by voluntary production and quota share reduction benefits.
Tri-County new business policies surged to over 7,600 in the quarter compared to fewer than 200 a year ago, representing a 40x increase.
Combined ratio improved significantly to 63.4% from 72.9% YoY due to lower ceded premiums and reduced acquisition expenses.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported record Q2 FY2026 results with gross premiums written increasing 13.8% to $327 million and income before taxes reaching a company-record $46.4 million. The quarter featured significant growth in voluntary new business, particularly in Tri-County (up 40x YoY) and middle-aged homes segments, alongside successful reinsurance renewal economics with rate reductions of 15%-20%. Management raised the outlook for investment income following a post-quarter deployment of $200 million into fixed-income securities.

negative_highlights: H2 Adjusted EBITDA guidance ($6M-$10M) represents a step-down from the Q2 actual of $11.4M, though management attributes this to conservative forecasting rather than expected deterioration.
Subscription revenue remained flat at roughly equivalent levels compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $23.2M driven by licensing revenue up 48% YoY to $14.1M.
Gross margin expanded significantly from 53% in the prior year quarter to 73% due to high-value licensing mix and minimal incremental distribution costs.
Total operating expenses declined 24% year-over-year as cost rationalization efforts took effect.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $23.2 million (up 22% YoY) and record Adjusted EBITDA of $11.4 million with a gross margin expansion to 73%. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $77-$82 million and H2 adjusted EBITDA between $6-$10 million, noting the latter reflects a conservative approach rather than anticipated headwinds.

negative_highlights: Card Issuing revenue faced headwinds with flat card loads and slight transaction declines, though purchase volume rebounded.
RTP transactions generate higher margins but weigh modestly on top-line revenue compared to PINless debit shifts.
Operating cash flow was lower in the first half of 2026 compared to last year due to timing of annual outlays.
positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to ~19% in Q2, excluding interest income which approached 20%.
PayFac business revenue surged 43% year-over-year driven by ISV onboarding flywheel.
Management raised full-year guidance from 10%-12% to 14%-16% following strong H1 performance.
summary: Usio reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of approximately 19% (excluding interest income approaching 20%), with total payment dollars and transactions up 27%. The company met or beat analyst expectations on the top line while generating positive GAAP net income for the second consecutive quarter. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of 14%-16%, upgrading from prior guidance of 10%-12%.

negative_highlights: Cash balance decreased from $58.5 million at year-end to $36.7 million as of June 30, indicating significant cash burn.
Management explicitly stated they cannot comment on FDA's preliminary conclusion regarding accelerated approval eligibility during the informal meeting.
Company is still awaiting FDA comments on confirmatory trial design which could impact launch timing.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased significantly from $23.5 million to $6 million due to a non-cash gain of $13.9 million on warrant liabilities.
Operating expenses dropped by 19% year-over-year, falling from $23.1 million in Q2 FY2025 to $18.6 million in Q2 FY2026.
FDA completed all scheduled pre-licensure inspections with only one reported observation that the company believes has been appropriately addressed.
summary: Inovio reported a net loss of $6 million ($0.07 per share) for Q2 FY2026 compared to a prior year loss of $23.5 million, driven by non-cash warrant liability gains rather than operational performance issues. The company raised approximately $18.3 million in July 2026 via an equity offering and expects its cash runway to extend into late Q1 FY2027 through the anticipated PDUFA date of October 30 for INO-3107. Management confirmed that FDA inspections are complete with only one observation addressed, but noted they cannot comment on accelerated approval eligibility until after label negotiations begin in September.

negative_highlights: Volumes on key exchanges reduced meaningfully, down 17% compared with the first quarter.
Net interest income decreased by $5 million QoQ as higher interest expense from new debt issuances offset growth in interest income.
Energy revenues were lower than an exceptionally strong prior year comparator.
positive_highlights: Adjusted profit before tax increased 56% YoY to $166 million with margins expanding to 24%.
Clearing client balances grew significantly, driving a 31% increase in clearing net interest income despite lower rates.
Market making revenue surged 106% YoY to $118 million due to broad-based performance across metals and securities.
summary: Marex reported Q2 FY26 revenues of $696 million (up 39% YoY) and adjusted profit before tax of $166 million (up 56% YoY), driven by strong growth across clearing, agency/execution, market making, solutions, and NII. Management highlighted a diversified platform with structural growth offsetting cyclical volume declines in key exchanges, resulting in an expanded adjusted PBT margin to 24%. The company reaffirmed its ability to grow earnings resiliently through organic expansion and disciplined M&A.

negative_highlights: Franchise level margin decreased year-over-year due to lower same-store sales, fewer restaurants in the system, and higher bad debt expense
Elevated beef costs increased food cost percentage by 70 basis points with expectations of high costs persisting into Q4
Closures have occurred slower than anticipated but are expected to accelerate through 2028 due to franchisee profitability pressures
positive_highlights: Philly Cheesesteak platform launched early in Q4 generated strong customer interest with a higher associated average check
Q4-to-date same-store sales are positive in the low single-digit range following menu pivot
Completed refinancing reduced total debt outstanding to $1.5 billion and lowered net leverage ratio from 6.9x to 6.3x
summary: Q3 same-store sales decreased 1.1% driven by a decline in transactions and polarizing Hot Ones promotion performance, partially offset by menu price increases. Restaurant level margin contracted to 17.6%, pressured by elevated beef costs (commodity inflation of 5.4%) and lower franchise revenue due to closures. Management lowered full-year guidance for restaurant count to approximately 2,100 units and adjusted franchise-level margin expectations downward.

negative_highlights: Total sales declined 8.4% year-over-year to $458.5 million, with comparable stores down 6.2%.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped from $81.6 million a year ago to $55.7 million due to volume and margin pressures.
Gross profit margin contracted to 36.5%, down from 39.6% in the prior-year period.
positive_highlights: Achieved positive comparable sales on leslies.com despite overall declines in physical store traffic.
summary: Third quarter sales declined 8.4% year-over-year to $458.5 million due to softer demand and the closure of 80 stores, while adjusted EBITDA fell significantly from $81.6 million in Q3 FY2025 to $55.7 million. Gross margin contracted by roughly 3 percentage points (from 39.6% to 36.5%) driven by product mix shifts and higher distribution costs. Management withdrew previously issued full-year guidance for sales and adjusted EBITDA, citing lower-than-anticipated customer traffic during the peak season.

negative_highlights: Company remains unprofitable with a net loss of RMB 401 million for the quarter.
R&D expenses increased by 36% year-over-year to support AI infrastructure investments, though growth was slower than revenue.
Overseas expansion faces potential geopolitical tensions and regulatory hurdles in new markets.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 103% quarter-over-quarter to RMB 232 million driven by asset-light overseas expansion.
Gross margin expanded nearly 10 percentage points to a record high of 37.5%, reflecting the shift toward higher-margin AI service revenue.
L4 Robotaxi fleet doubled in Q2 with new commercial launches in Spain, Switzerland, Denmark, and expanded operations in Abu Dhabi/Dubai.
summary: WeRide reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 232 million, representing an 82% year-over-year increase and a 103% quarter-over-quarter surge driven by rapid scaling in overseas Robotaxi operations (up 47%) and L2+/L3 ADAS deployments. Gross margins expanded significantly to 37.5%, up from 28.1% last year, while operating leverage emerged as R&D expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue. Management raised guidance for cumulative vehicle installations in the L2++/L3 business, projecting over 100,000 units by year-end and exceeding 500,000 cumulatively next year.

negative_highlights: Silver equivalent production declined from Q1 due to the strategic decision to mine lower-grade surface material at Avino Mine which yielded fewer ounces.
Margins were negatively impacted by provisional pricing adjustments of $5 million and a weakened U.S. dollar against the Mexican peso averaging 12-15% stronger than in Q2 last year.
positive_highlights: Achieved a transformational milestone with the announcement of an inaugural mineral reserve estimate totaling 127M silver-equivalent ounces across three assets.
Record cash position of $144 million and working capital of $141 million provide a strong balance sheet for growth execution.
La Preciosa development production increased significantly by 59% quarter-over-quarter, contributing over 100k silver-equivalent ounces.
summary: Avino reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $26.8 million and net income of $10.9 million ($0.06/share), beating the prior year's EPS but missing on silver production due to a strategic decision to mine lower-grade surface material at Avino Mine which reduced ounces sold by approximately 5,000 oz compared to Q1. Management highlighted an inaugural mineral reserve estimate of 127M silver-equivalent ounces and record cash balances of $144 million, while noting that current costs are elevated due to processing development ore rather than production-grade material.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow for the full year ($1.3 billion) came $200 million below the outlook range due to Middle East conflict working capital impacts.
Healthcare volumes were down due to a mix shift toward lower-margin subcategories, though profit expansion is expected from higher-margin pharma products.
Higher interest and tax expenses partially offset operating performance improvements in the transition period.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.23 increased 23% year-over-year, landing at the high end of the outlook range.
Full fiscal year synergies reached $285 million, which is approximately 10% ahead of initial year-one expectations.
Volume growth was broad-based across core and non-core businesses with sequential improvement in both Flexibles and Rigid segments.
summary: Amcor reported Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS of $1.23 (up 23% YoY) and revenue of $6.4 billion, with full-year synergies reaching $285 million ahead of initial targets. Management provided a transition period outlook for the six months ending December 31st expecting adjusted EPS between $1.80-$1.90 per share. The company highlighted broad-based volume growth and successful integration progress despite macroeconomic headwinds.

negative_highlights: Revenues from note goods were partially offset by lower sales volumes to Pfizer compared to the prior year period.
Cost of revenues increased significantly to $7.8 million due to higher sales volumes and associated costs.
positive_highlights: Elfabrio revenues increased $4.4 million sequentially and were driven by continued global penetration of Elfabrio through Chiesi.
The company recognized a previously reported $25 million milestone payment in Q1 2026, contributing to the profitable quarter.
Cash equivalents and note weakness in-term bank deposits totaled $40.7 million as of June 30, 2026.
summary: Protalix reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $19.9 million and net income of $3.8 million ($0.05 per share), driven by a $4.4 million increase in Elfabrio sales to Chiesi partially offset by lower Pfizer sales. Management stated that positive revenue trends keep the company firmly on track with its full year 2026 guidance, which remains unchanged from prior periods.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for Q3 or beyond, citing a need to understand prescribing trends
Non-GAAP adjusted net income was an $1.8 million loss due to non-cash mark-to-market adjustments on convertible notes
European regulatory application received negative opinion from CHMP requiring re-examination before approval
positive_highlights: YARTEMLEA generated $32.2M in gross sales and $4.1M positive cash flow in the first full quarter of commercialization
Adult patient utilization grew at more than twice the rate of pediatric, representing ~75% of sales as mix shifts toward historical norms
Company strengthened capital structure by repurchasing 843k shares and retiring $30.5M principal amount of convertible notes
summary: Omeros reported Q2 FY26 results driven by its first full quarter of YARTEMLEA sales, generating $32.2 million in gross revenue and $4.1 million in positive operating cash flow while repurchasing shares and convertible notes to strengthen capital structure. Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance for the third quarter or beyond due to a need to gain additional experience with prescribing trends and market dynamics following the launch. The company noted that reported GAAP net income was significantly impacted by non-cash mark-to-market adjustments on its 2029 convertible notes, which excluded from adjusted results showing an $1.8 million loss.

negative_highlights: Q3 net loss increased from $7.6 million prior year quarter due to higher G&A, R&D, and OpEx scaling costs
No commercial revenue guidance provided; business remains pre-revenue dependent on future licensing approvals
Management explicitly stated no definitive timeline for BaRupOn licensing application or construction start
positive_highlights: NRC formally accepted Construction Permit Application for UIUC project, initiating review with environmental assessment projected in Q1 2027
Completed acquisition of STS (nuclear logistics) which generated $3.9M revenue H1 and provides profitable fuel cycle capabilities
Advanced feasibility study with BaRupOn evaluating up to 1 GW phased deployment potential
summary: NANO Nuclear reported a Q3 net loss of $10.1 million compared to $7.6 million in the prior year quarter and a YTD net loss of $25.8 million versus $32 million last year, driven by higher operating expenses as it scales engineering and regulatory workstreams for its UIUC project. The company ended with approximately $580 million in liquidity after raising roughly $26 million via ATM proceeds, though no revenue guidance was provided given the pre-revenue nature of the business. Management highlighted substantial progress on NRC licensing milestones (environmental assessment expected Q1 2027) and strategic partnerships but offered no specific commercial deployment timelines or financial targets.

negative_highlights: Automotive gross margin declined from Q1 (46.2% to 41.5%) driven by one-time testing facility expenses
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly compared to prior quarter expectations ($4.9M-$4.4M vs actual $4.2M)
Inventory increased to $12.5 million from Q1 levels
positive_highlights: Revenue beat exceeded top end of guidance at $18.1M
Full-year guidance raised by $3M due to strong AV adoption and automotive program progress
Barco design win for wired ClickShare extension validates demand for high-performance connectivity
summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.1 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($17.2M-$17.6M) and beating prior quarter results. GAAP gross margin was 61.5%, within the guided range but down from Q1 due to automotive testing expenses which are expected to stabilize in future quarters. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $78 million - $81 million, up from the previous range of $75 million-$77 million.

negative_highlights: Net loss for the quarter was $69.0 million, driven by unrealized losses on digital assets of $49.8 million.
SG&A expenses increased to $7.4 million from $1.9 million in the prior year period due to strategy launch costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew significantly from $2.5 million in the prior year period to $10.8 million driven by staking revenue.
Gross margin expanded substantially to 62.2% compared to -24.9% in the prior year period.
SOL per share increased sequentially to 0.0730 (June) and 0.0754 (August), representing a 36% annualized growth rate.
summary: Forward Industries reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $10.8 million (up from $2.5M prior year) and a gross margin expansion to 62.2%, though the quarter included significant unrealized losses on digital assets totaling $49.8 million resulting in a net loss of $69.0 million ($0.8/share). Management highlighted strong operational execution with SOL per share growing 36% annualized, index inclusion into Russell indices, and successful deployment of capital via ATM issuances and buybacks to accrete value.

negative_highlights: Net advertising revenues declined slightly to RMB 146.9 million compared to RMB 153.3 million in the prior year
Total operating expenses increased sharply by 30.4% year-over-year due to higher sales and marketing spend for digital reading services
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 15.8% year-over-year to RMB 216.7 million
Paid services revenue surged 106.5% year-over-year to RMB 69.8 million driven by digital reading Mini Programs
Gross margin expanded significantly from 49.2% to 57.3%
summary: Phoenix New Media reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 216.7 million, a 15.8% year-over-year increase driven by paid services growth (RMB 69.8 million) and net advertising revenues of RMB 146.9 million. Gross margin expanded significantly to 57.3%, while operating expenses rose 30.4% due to digital reading initiatives, resulting in a narrow loss from operations but an improved net income attributable to the company compared to the prior year's loss. Management provided Q3 guidance of RMB 220.9 million to RMB 235.9 million total revenue and noted that while advertising demand was mixed due to contract timing issues, they see a structural shift toward content-driven monetization.

negative_highlights: Q2 net loss of $6.2 million compared to a prior year loss of $2.7 million, primarily due to costs incurred for delayed waste processing.
