Higher education delivered $200 million in revenue (up 10%) driven by a mix of ~4% enrollment growth, price realization (~2%), and share gains; trailing 12-month market share increased 140 bps to above 30%. Recurring HE revenue grew 14%.
New ELA programs Emerge!, Summit!, and Soar! are exceeding expectations with early cumulative capture rates already surpassing the 25%-30% target range in open territory districts.
summary: McGraw Hill reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $550 million (up 2.6% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $207 million with a margin expansion to 37.7%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing strong momentum in K-12 ELA adoption driven by the science-of-reading mandates and higher education share gains despite awaiting final enrollment data for H2 visibility.

negative_highlights: $86 million in non-operating charges including a $28.8M loss on digital assets and $46M impairment of liquid staked ETH
Ethereum price declined for the third consecutive quarter, reducing staking revenue to $0.9M from $2.3M prior quarter
Company trades at significant discount (up to 43%) to NAV despite active strategy
positive_highlights: Cloud services revenue grew 42% sequentially driven by new contracts entering service
WhiteFiber secured $50M liquidity via related party bridge facility avoiding equity dilution while preserving Ethereum position
Contract liabilities nearly doubled to $143.1 million, indicating strong future visibility
summary: Bit Digital reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $32.1 million (up 15% sequentially) and a net loss attributable to shareholders of $107.2 million ($0.31 EPS), driven by an $86 million non-operating charge from digital asset revaluation, impairment on liquid staked ETH for financing collateralization, interest expense, and derivative losses. Management highlighted strong operating cash flow growth but noted the market continues to value the company as a passive treasury despite active capital allocation strategies like WhiteFiber expansion and bridge financing.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents declined from $18M to $13.6M due to working capital investments
Operating expenses are expected to trend higher as the company normalizes spending post-merger termination
Q3 procedure volume is historically lower in various regions, creating a seasonal headwind
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA reached $3.6M, marking the strongest quarterly performance to date
Recurring revenue grew 20% YoY to $13.7M, representing 83% of total revenue
Installed base expanded by placing 10 ALLY systems in Q2 for a total global count of ~445
summary: LENSAR reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.5 million (up 18% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million, its strongest quarterly performance to date driven by recurring revenue growth to $13.7 million and a one-time tariff refund benefit. The company raised guidance implicitly through strong execution despite noting that operating expenses will normalize higher in future quarters as commercial investments resume following the terminated merger with Alcon.

negative_highlights: Industrial Mobility Solutions revenue declined 3% due to lower material handling volumes, though transportation orders nearly doubled.
IMS adjusted operating margin contracted by 70 basis points to 9.3%, as price mix gains were offset by loss of leverage on reduced volume.
positive_highlights: Q1 net sales grew 5% year-over-year to $936 million, with Precision Power Solutions revenue surging 24% driven by aerospace and defense demand.
Free cash flow conversion reached an exceptional 187%, generating $218 million in the quarter versus a loss of $32 million in Q1 FY2026.
Data center orders expanded over 80% year-over-year, providing strong visibility into project-based demand for lead-acid and upcoming lithium offerings.
summary: EnerSys reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $936 million (up 5% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.20 per share (excluding one-time tariff refunds), driven by strong growth in Network Infrastructure Solutions (+9%) and Precision Power Solutions (+24%). Management raised second-quarter guidance, expecting revenue between $955-$995 million and excluding-45X adjusted EPS up 21% YoY at the midpoint. The company highlighted record free cash flow of $218 million and secured a DOE grant for a new defense-focused lithium manufacturing facility.

negative_highlights: Trading volumes moderated as Bitcoin prices fell to ~$60k and volatility declined.
Full-year SSNO guidance was narrowed (lowered) from previous expectations due to the current market environment.
Q2 adjusted operating expenses were elevated by $2.5 million in one-time compensation costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted revenue grew 62% year-over-year despite a soft crypto market.
Subscription, Services & Other revenue reached a record $62.7 million driven by new institutional partnerships (e.g., SoFi, BitGo Prime).
CoinDesk media metrics showed strong growth with page views up 38% YoY and unique visitors up 83%.
summary: Bullish reported Q2 FY26 adjusted revenue of $92.6 million (up 62% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 32%, though trading volumes moderated with the broader crypto market decline. Management narrowed its full-year SSNO guidance to a range of $225-$245 million due to increased visibility into the softer price environment, while maintaining optimism about long-term tokenization opportunities post-acquisition closing in January 2027.

negative_highlights: Gold production at Jacobina expected to be ~10,000 ounces below original annual guidance due to seismic mitigation measures reducing rates in high-grade areas.
El Peñón gold production forecasted ~10,000 ounces below the low end of guidance as mining shifted from lower continuity secondary structures to higher silver/low gold veins.
Q2 effective tax rate spiked to 37% due to true-ups on prior year profitability and repatriation withholding taxes.
positive_highlights: Attributable silver production hit the high end of guidance at 6.5M ounces driven by La Colorada expansion progress (first cut of 588 decline).
Returned a record $300 million to shareholders in Q2, exceeding initial capital return targets.
Full-year all-in sustaining costs for silver remained below the low end of guidance despite higher cost inventory drawdowns.
summary: Q2 attributable silver production of 6.5 million ounces met the high end of guidance driven by La Colorada and Juanicipio, while gold production missed outlook due to seismic mitigation at Jacobina and continuity issues at El Peñón. Management reaffirmed full-year operating ranges but lowered Q3 gold expectations and noted higher tax expenses ($179M) impacting net earnings compared to consensus estimates. The company returned a record $300 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, maintaining strong liquidity of approximately $3.2 billion.

negative_highlights: U.S. organic growth was flat for the quarter due to project timing delays, though management expects acceleration in H2.
DSO increased slightly to 75 days at quarter-end, sitting at the higher end of internal targets but within guidance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record high of 18.7% with an increase of 90 basis points year-over-year.
Contract backlog reached a new record of CAD 9.2 billion, representing approximately 13 months of work and up 17.5% YoY.
Global region delivered over 18% net revenue growth driven by double-digit organic expansion in water (over 20%) and energy/resources.
summary: Stantec reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of CAD 1.8 billion (up ~12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to a record 18.7%. Management raised the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 17.8%-18.3%, citing strong backlog growth, particularly in water and global regions, while noting Q2 U.S. organic growth was impacted by timing issues rather than demand weakness.

negative_highlights: Total revenues missed expectations significantly due to product sales dropping -18% YoY on constant currency basis, primarily from IXIARO (EUR 44M vs EUR 54.7M) and DUKORAL (EUR 14.7M vs EUR 17.4M).
First half operating loss widened to EUR 49.9 million compared to a EUR 16.8 million loss last year, exacerbated by non-cash inventory impairment of EUR 4.5 million and cancellation fees.
Third-party product revenue collapsed from EUR 11.4 million in H1 2025 to just EUR 1 million as distribution agreements expired without renewal.
positive_highlights: Pfizer remains positive on Lyme disease vaccine prospects with an expectation of regulatory decisions within the next 12 months following a strong point efficacy greater than 70%.
IXCHIQ locally manufactured vaccine approved by Brazil's health authorities and expected to be incorporated into the public system in the near future after vaccinating over 50,000 people.
Company generated EUR 121.5 million cash at period end following a recent offering and disciplined management.
summary: Valneva reported a significant miss in the first half of FY2026 with total revenues of EUR 65.8 million versus EUR 97.6 million last year and product sales declining to EUR 64 million from EUR 91 million, driven by distributor transitions for IXIARO/DUKORAL and contract phasing for the U.S. Department of Defense. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance despite these headwinds but noted that operating loss widened to EUR 49.9 million due to one-off restructuring costs (EUR 3.2M) and non-recurring inventory/write-down impacts totaling over EUR 10 million in the first half.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses surged from $1.5 million in Q2 FY2025 (pre-public) to $5.7 million in the current quarter due to public company costs and growth investments.
Net loss widened to $1.8 million compared to net income of $0.8 million in the prior year period, primarily driven by higher G&A expenses.
Ammunition demand remained soft despite core business strength.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded approximately 290 basis points to 13.5% driven by favorable mix and AI-driven pricing optimization.
PEW Logistics processed over $1.9 million in gross merchandise value with the addition of a third manufacturer, Backwoods Suppressors.
Mobile engagement increased to 71% of traffic, accounting for 67.5% of revenue.
summary: Second quarter net revenue increased 9% year-over-year to $23 million, driven by an 8% increase in firearm sales and a shift toward higher price-point products. Gross margin expanded significantly from 10.6% to approximately 13.5%, while operating expenses rose sharply due to incremental costs associated with becoming a public company and scaling PEW Logistics. The quarter ended the transition period for like-for-like expense comparisons, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million compared to prior year income.

negative_highlights: Gross profit declined sequentially in Mexico due to pricing power erosion, where cost structure rose slightly while revenue grew.
Africa and Asia segments saw sequential gross profit declines driven by lower share of high-spread markets like Mozambique and Vietnam.
Full-year operating profit guidance was maintained rather than raised despite strong execution because FX headwinds and a $4.4M prior year tax item were not adjusted out.
positive_highlights: TPV growth accelerated to 92% year-over-year, exceeding prior expectations with volume surpassing all of 2023.
Gross profit reached a record $127 million in Q2, up 29% YoY and 7% sequentially.
Operating leverage improved significantly with operating profit as a percentage of gross profit rising to 50%, up 6 points from Q1.
summary: DLocal reported Q2 FY26 TPV of $17.7 billion (up 92% YoY) and gross profit of $127 million (up 29% YoY), driven by record performance in Brazil ($40M GP) and Argentina ($20M GP). Management raised full-year guidance for TPV growth to 60%-70% and gross profit growth to 25%-30%, while maintaining operating profit growth at 27.5%-32.5%. The company highlighted strong net revenue retention of 153% and a sequential improvement in operating leverage, though it noted some FX headwinds and one-off tax impacts affecting the full-year outlook.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $2.1 million fell significantly below expectations and was down year-over-year
Gross loss for the quarter due to delayed shipments caused by supply chain bottlenecks
Bitcoin mark-to-market change contributed approximately $31.4 million to a first half net loss
positive_highlights: SG&A spending declined approximately 9% year-over-year in Q2 reflecting cost discipline
First half R&D expense was about 3% lower than the prior period
Secured initial defense drone battery orders from a U.S. maker participating in Drone Dominance exceeding $5 million
summary: Q2 revenue was $2.1 million and down significantly from the prior year due to supply chain delays and a new Texas facility not yet contributing; gross margins resulted in a loss for the quarter as planned shipments were delayed. Management exited Bitcoin mining, repaid its credit facility using proceeds from watching 333 Bitcoin, and simplified operations by terminating mining agreements while focusing resources on KULR ONE.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $7.8 million to $22.6 million due to heavy non-cash expenses ($9.4M SBC), interest costs, and debt extinguishment fees
Gross profit compressed 35% year-over-year as new site capital expenditures outpaced revenue contribution in early ramp-up phases
Proprietary Bitcoin mining segment declined $1.1 million due to a 40% drop in hash prices
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 145% year-over-year with five consecutive quarters of sequential growth
Operating capacity expected to increase from 192 MW to 206 MW by end of summer following Kati 1 Phase 3 energization
Raised $183M in capital (ATM, debt, warrants) and retired Series B preferred stock to simplify the balance sheet
summary: Soluna reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $15.1 million (up 145% YoY) and a net loss of $22.6 million compared to $7.8 million in the prior year, driven by non-cash stock-based compensation ($9.4M), interest expense increases, and debt extinguishment losses following capital raises totaling ~$183M. Management raised guidance for operating capacity from 192 MW at quarter-end to an expected 206 MW by summer end due to the energization of Kati 1 Phase 3. The company acquired a $53M wind farm and consolidated ownership of Project Dorothy, while advancing two major AI campuses (Kati 2 and Dorothy 3) toward construction.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 58.3% as costs rose significantly, including ~BRL 28 million in inflationary pressure on chemicals and investments in customer service channels.
Water production fell 4.3% YoY due to milder weather conditions (average temperatures down 1.1%) and the application of night pressure management rules.
Allowance for doubtful accounts increased from a historical low of 1.4% to 2.5%, reflecting seasonality in Q2 collection patterns.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net revenue grew 9.4% YoY driven by a price contribution of 8.7% from the January 2026 tariff cycle and volume expansion.
Underlying EBITDA would have grown close to 20% year-over-year excluding one-time items like legal reversals, ERP timing effects, and extraordinary inflation costs.
CapEx execution remains strong with BRL 7.5 billion invested YTD and a contracted backlog of over BRL 40 billion through 2029.
summary: SABESP reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net revenue growth of 9.4% year-over-year driven by tariff increases and customer expansion, while Adjusted EBITDA declined 3.2% to BRL 3.5 billion due to higher costs from inflationary pressures (chemicals), investments in commercial initiatives (~BRL 800 million annualized spend), and ERP timing effects. Management provided a cautious outlook on underlying cost normalization for the second half of the year, noting that roughly 75-80% of current elevated OpEx is expected to be recovered through future tariff cycles or productivity gains by 2027.

negative_highlights: Gross margin compressed to ~62% due to note weakness in-dated product reserves, manufacturing inefficiencies at scale, and ex-U.S. launch costs
SG&A expenses were $77.6 million in Q2 before a planned >40% reduction for H2 2026
Phase II-B trial interim readout delayed to Q1 2027 due to patient enrollment design requirements

Field sales expansion fully deployed targeting high-volume prescribers representing 44% of opportunity
90% commercial coverage achieved with 57% without prior authorization
summary: ARS Pharma reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $26.2 million and total operating expenses of $95.1 million with gross margins at approximately 62%. Management announced a significant strategic pivot to reduce SG&A by over 40% in the second half, projecting cash-flow breakeven by end-2027 rather than raising near-term revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Q2 unit deliveries of 30 missed internal expectations due to customer delays and acceptance issues shifting orders into subsequent quarters.
Revenue declined sequentially from Q1 as the mix shifted away from higher-volume step van chassis toward lower-margin powertrain kits in that specific quarter.
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered, with management explicitly stating deliveries will be lighter than planned for H2.
positive_highlights: H1 GAAP gross margin reached a historic high of 31% driven by favorable product mix toward higher-margin Hubs and powertrains.
Non-GAAP operating loss for the first half narrowed to $8.8 million from $14.9 million in the prior year period, demonstrating operational leverage.
Cash position strengthened with cash on hand rising 35% quarter-over-quarter following capital raises.
summary: Xos reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.7 million on 30 units delivered, a decline from the prior year quarter due to order deferrals and customer acceptance delays. GAAP gross margin was 12.1% for the quarter but improved significantly in H1 with a record 31%, while operating loss narrowed sequentially despite lower volumes. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting revenue between $35 million and $43 million.

negative_highlights: Take rate came in at 3.6% (low end of guidance) due to higher interest rates reducing gain on sale and faster-than-anticipated migration of large partners directly to lower-take-rate Figure Connect.
First lien volume grew 3x year-over-year, which typically carries a lower take rate than HELOCs, creating a modest structural headwind for the metric.
positive_highlights: Consumer loan marketplace volume surged to $4.3 billion, up 132% year-over-year, beating the top end of prior guidance by 4%.
Figure Connect adoption accelerated significantly, growing from 56% share last quarter to 65% this quarter as partners migrate directly to the capital-light platform.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 55%, reflecting strong operating leverage and a shift toward fee-based economics with ecosystem fees now being the largest revenue contributor.
summary: Figure reported Q2 FY26 consumer loan marketplace volume of $4.3 billion (up 132% YoY), beating the top end of guidance by 4%. Adjusted net revenue reached $218 million with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 55%, driven largely by Figure Connect now representing 65% of total volume and ecosystem fees becoming the largest P&L line item. Management raised Q3 volume guidance expectations, citing strong July performance ($1.7B) and a confident outlook for August/September.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, though improved YoY
No repurchases made under the authorized share buyback program due to blackout period
EMJX figures are hypothetical model results and do not represent actual trading returns yet
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 27% year-over-year to $3.4 million
Supply chain fill rate recovery reached 98%
New-to-brand consumers for Halo increased 13% year-over-year
summary: Net sales for the fiscal third quarter totaled $3.4 million, representing a 27% year-over-year increase driven by Halo's operational improvements and supply chain recovery reaching 98%. GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, an improvement of 40% year-over-year to a smaller absolute loss compared to the prior period. Management highlighted a debt-free balance sheet with no repurchases made under the newly authorized program due to blackout periods.

negative_highlights: Revenue was not recognized for two treatments due to one low-yield batch and one out-of-specification batch.
Two scheduled biopsies were cancelled last-minute in Q2 due to patient health deterioration.
Manufacturing yields remain variable with a rare event of an out-of-spec test failure requiring FDA specification review.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 31% QoQ to $11.4 million driven by five treated patients.
Expanded qualified treatment center (QTC) network now includes seven activated centers nationwide with CHOP completing its first treatment shortly after activation in May.
Achieved CMS New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP) status effective October 2026, providing supplemental reimbursement for Medicare beneficiaries.
summary: Abeona Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $11.4 million, a 31% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by five patient treatments, though one low-yield batch and one out-of-specification batch resulted in no revenue recognition for those specific cases despite patients receiving treatment. R&D expenses decreased to $5 million from Q1's $9.6 million due to the exclusion of a one-time licensing cost incurred earlier in the year. Management highlighted operational bottlenecks including scheduling disruptions, patient health deterioration leading to cancellations, and manufacturing yield variability as key headwinds.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined 2.9% YoY, with electronics and home appliances revenue moderated by a high trading base and upstream price increases.
General merchandise growth was impacted by the same high comparison base effects seen in other categories during Q2.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income surged 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion driven by robust profitability and loss reduction in new businesses.
JD Retail gross margin expanded 130 bps YoY to a record high of 18.5%, marking the 17th consecutive quarter of expansion.
JD Food Delivery narrowed total losses by over 50% YoY while maintaining healthy order volume momentum.
summary: JD.com reported Q2 FY26 total revenues of RMB 346 billion, a slight year-on-year decline of 2.9% due to high comparison bases in electronics and home appliances. Non-GAAP net income surged by 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion as JD Retail gross margin expanded to 18.5% and JD Food Delivery losses narrowed significantly. Management raised the outlook for H2, expecting top-line growth re-acceleration in electronics/home appliances once base effects normalize.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened from income in prior year due to structural margin compression and legal provisions.
Net other loss of $230.8 million caused fair value volatility on Arashi Vision Inc., wiping out core business profitability.
No specific full-year guidance provided despite strong top-line growth.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 38.9% YoY to $102.7M driven by strong overseas audio live streaming growth of 54.8%.
summary: Xunlei reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $102.7 million, up 38.9% year-over-year, driven by a 22.6% increase in subscription services and a 54.8% surge in overseas audio live streaming. However, the company posted an operating loss of $4.8 million due to higher costs associated with revenue mix shifts (lower-margin live streaming) and legal provisions, resulting in a net other loss of $230.8 million primarily from fair value volatility on investments. Management announced a new $20 million share repurchase program initiated July 1st but provided no specific guidance for the full year.

negative_highlights: Proteus launch delayed by approximately six months from late 2026 to Q2 FY2027 due to manufacturing repeatability concerns.
Revenue declined significantly year-over-year, dropping $591k in the prior period to just $344k this quarter.
Company is executing a reduction in force representing approximately 20% of total headcount.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly to $23.5 million compared to a net loss of $28.8 million in the prior year quarter.
Adjusted operating expenses decreased sequentially and YoY, with GAAP OpEx falling from $30.5M to $25.8M due to cost actions.
Management confirmed sufficient capital runway extending into Q4 2028 following the reduction in force.
summary: QSI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $344,000 (down from $591,000 in the prior year) and a net loss of $23.5 million, while maintaining full-year guidance for approximately $1M revenue despite announcing significant cost-cutting measures including a 20% reduction in force. Management delayed the Proteus launch timeline to Q2 FY2027 from late 2026 following internal testing that revealed manufacturing repeatability risks requiring an additional design cycle before production.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide formal financial guidance for the upcoming quarter citing macro uncertainty.
Total operating expenses increased year-over-year by approximately 26% due to stock-based compensation and commissions, despite sequential improvement.
The proposed merger with TYTL Corp remains non-binding and subject to shareholder approval, a fairness opinion, and valuation analysis.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 57% year-over-year driven by a strategic shift toward higher-margin non-QM products like bank statement loans.
July operating margins reached the highest level in company history, reflecting improved product mix and cost discipline.
Sequential cash burn decreased to $1.7 million from Q1 levels as working capital timing normalized.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 57% year-over-year to $2.6 million while net loss declined by 24% from the prior quarter and cash burn decreased to $1.7 million. Management highlighted a shift toward higher-margin non-QM products, resulting in July margins reaching company records and sequential improvements across operating expenses and adjusted EBITDA. However, management explicitly stated they are not providing formal financial guidance for Q3 due to market uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Engineering and design revenues declined 4%, primarily due to soft demand in sustainability consulting for mixed-use clients.
Consolidated gross margin was impacted by a revenue mix shift toward lower-margin installation services following the Bowers acquisition.
Sustainability consulting business experienced softer market conditions reflecting broader commercial real estate challenges.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth was nearly 60%, with total revenue more than doubling when including acquisitions.
Full-year 2026 guidance raised significantly on both top-line ($4.7B-$4.8B) and bottom-line (~$565M-$585M).
Backlog reached a record $5.7 billion, up 105% year-over-year.
summary: Legence reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 111% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 114%, driven by organic expansion in data centers/technology and the Bowers acquisition. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($4.7B-$4.8B, up ~13%) and adjusted EBITDA (~$565M-$585M, up ~20%), citing strong backlog growth of $5.7 billion (up 105% YoY) and accelerating project execution speeds.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined year-over-year, with the GEO segment down 26% due to non-renewals and lower capacity renewals.
Two legacy satellites (Anik F4 and Telstar 14R) were retired during the quarter, creating a headwind for cash flow visibility.
Net loss widened significantly to CAD 559 million compared to prior periods.
positive_highlights: Secured the first contract in the ESCP-P program, adding significant backlog and funding for Lightspeed acceleration.
GEO segment backlog increased to CAD 900 million due to a five-year extension of a broadcast video contract.
FCC report confirmed eligibility for $189 million in incentive payments related to C-band spectrum repurposing.
summary: Telesat reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of CAD 79 million and a net loss of CAD 559 million, driven by lower GEO segment revenue (down 26% YoY) due to contract expirations and satellite retirements. Management reiterated its guidance for the legacy GEO business but raised full-year investment guidance for Lightspeed from CAD 1-1.2 billion to CAD 1.3-1.5 billion following a decision to accelerate constellation expansion to 225 satellites funded by new government contracts.

negative_highlights: Inflation proved more persistent than anticipated at over 32%, impacting macroeconomic conditions and FX dynamics.
Net income was impacted by increased depreciation associated with the commercial launch of 5G assets.
Paycell margins faced volatility due to erosive POS transaction profitability, though total revenue grew 22%.
positive_highlights: Group revenue achieved genuine real growth of 2.5% YoY in an environment where inflation exceeded 30%.
Digital Business Services delivered outstanding performance with revenue up 33% to TRY 8.7 billion, supported by a system integration backlog of TRY 16 billion.
Turkcell crossed the historic milestone of 40 million mobile subscribers for the first time in company history.
summary: Turkcell reported Q2 FY2026 group revenue of TRY 71.8 billion (up 2.5% YoY) and net income of TRY 5.2 billion, driven by real growth despite inflation exceeding 30%. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged after revising year-end inflation expectations to around 28%, citing disciplined pricing and strong momentum in Digital Business Services (+33%) and FWA (+64k subscribers). The company crossed the 40 million mobile subscriber milestone with a postpaid base of 32.5 million, while EBITDA margin remained steady at 41.8%.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide quantitative guidance on YUVIWEL patient starts or sales ranges, citing insufficient time in market for analytical trends.
SG&A expenses increased significantly from EUR 145 million in Q1 to EUR 173 million in Q2 due to investments accelerating global launches.
positive_highlights: Total product revenue more than doubled year-over-year, with YORVIPATH reaching blockbuster status on a run-rate basis in its second launch year.
YUVIWEL enrollment accelerated rapidly to over 220 unique patients by end of July, capturing >65% reimbursement approval rate and demonstrating strong market expansion beyond switches.
COACH trial data showed unprecedented arm span improvements (+9.4 cm) with combination therapy compared to limb lengthening surgery.
summary: Ascendis Pharma reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of EUR 339 million (up from EUR 145m in the prior quarter), driven by YORVIPATH sales of EUR 252 million and SKYTROFA at EUR 55 million. The company achieved a significant non-product milestone gain of EUR 17 million related to TransCon CNP, resulting in net profit of EUR 207 million. Management raised full-year cash flow guidance expectations from greater than EUR 300m (implied prior) to greater than EUR 500 million for the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose sequentially to $806 million as timing effects reversed from Q1 and international expansion investments accelerated.
Overall NPLs deteriorated slightly by 40 basis points due to portfolio mix shifts rather than fundamental credit quality issues in core segments.
positive_highlights: Net income reached a milestone $1.1 billion, up 49% year-over-year and marking the first time exceeding $1B.
Risk-adjusted net interest margin expanded to a record 12.4%, driven by lending growth and disciplined risk expansion rather than portfolio deterioration.
Mexico banking license approved with deposits at $5.7 billion, demonstrating successful transformation into a full-scale digital bank.
summary: Nu Holdings reported a historic quarter with net income exceeding $1 billion for the first time ($1.1B), driven by gross revenue of nearly $5.9 billion and record risk-adjusted NIM expanding to 12.4%. The company achieved this while maintaining an efficiency ratio near its long-term target of 20% despite sequential operating expense increases due to international expansion investments.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to the end of Menarini's reimbursement ($6.5M impact)
Phase III XPORT-EC-042 study failed to achieve statistical significance in endometrial cancer, leading to a strategic pivot away from that program
Cash runway extends only to September 2026 without additional financing or lender waivers
positive_highlights: U.S. XPOVIO net product revenue of $30.8M showed consistent underlying demand despite competition
Strong clinical momentum for selinexor in myelofibrosis with FDA feedback supporting SVR35 as a surrogate endpoint
Planned sNDA submission remains on track for August 2026
summary: Karyopharm reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $33.4 million (down from $37.9M prior year) and a net loss of $67 million due to the conclusion of Menarini's reimbursement, though underlying operating performance improved with disciplined expense reductions. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $130-$150 million but highlighted an urgent liquidity constraint requiring financing or strategic alternatives by September 10th to avoid a default on their term loan.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted 130 bps year-over-year due to a combined 280 bps drag from FX and U.S. tariffs.
Net leverage increased to 1.8x following the accelerated share repurchase (ASR) and debt refinancing activities.
Middle East conflicts continue to impact demand in key markets like the UAE, though mitigated by strength elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% in constant currency, hitting the high end of guidance with double-digit growth across Americas (14%), EMEA (15%), and APAC (23%).
D2C channel accelerated to 16% growth while retail revenue surged 50%, driven by new store openings.
Full price realization remained strong at 93% in Europe, demonstrating brand resilience against promotional pressure.
summary: Birkenstock reported Q3 FY26 revenue of EUR 720 million (up 15% in constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR 242 million. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to the high end of its range at 15% and increased the minimum adjusted EBITDA target to at least EUR 710 million, citing strong momentum across all regions despite FX headwinds and tariffs.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased by $0.9 million YoY due to investments in clinical development for PTSD and alcohol use disorder research.
G&A expenses rose approximately $0.7 million driven by higher professional fees and administrative costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 35% YoY to $17.1 million driven by a 42% increase in system shipments (125 units).
Operating income surged over 300% year-over-year, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of profitability.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 11% to 20%, reflecting strong operating leverage.
summary: BrainsWay reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.1 million (up 35% YoY) and operating income increasing over 300% to $2.4 million. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance from a range of $66M-$68M to $68M-$70M, citing strong demand for the SWIFT protocol and growing remaining performance obligations of $80.4 million.

negative_highlights: NAND growth is expected to be slower next year as the market focuses primarily on upgrades rather than wafer capacity additions.
Q1 FY27 will be a 14-week quarter, which may result in higher-than-average step-up in operating expenses compared to standard quarters.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 revenue of $9.1 billion driven by double-digit sequential growth across all segments.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to a record 50.4% (up 40 bps sequentially) and operating margin hit a record 34%.
DRAM revenue grew 52% YoY, while Applied Global Services delivered record $1.8 billion in revenue.
summary: Applied Materials reported record Q3 FY26 revenue of $9.1 billion (up 15% sequentially and 25% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 (up 41% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, citing strengthened demand visibility from customers providing eight-quarter rolling forecasts through to 2030. The company expects particularly strong growth in DRAM and leading-edge foundry logic for the second half of calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $51 million as the company front-loaded investments in operating expenses.
Cash operating expenses were elevated at ~$93 million due to integration costs and growth investments, though management expects moderation later in the year.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $83.8 million representing more than 13-fold growth versus the prior year period.
Pro forma organic revenue grew approximately 85% year-over-year, validating underlying business execution beyond acquisition impacts.
Backlog increased approximately 33% sequentially to roughly $757 million with a two-year strategic pipeline exceeding $1.4 billion.
summary: Ondas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.8 million (up >13x YoY) and adjusted gross margin stable at 50.4%. Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $525-$550 million, citing strong organic growth drivers including Sentrycs (+298% pro forma), Airobotics (+112%), and 4M (+258%). The company ended with approximately $1.4 billion in cash equivalents after deploying capital for new acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Public sector revenue declined YoY due to temporary budgetary shifts in late Q2 driven by conflict spending priorities.
VDR deal timing remains uncertain, causing some large hyperscaler transactions to be under active review rather than fully processed.
Fiscal 2026 guidance was lowered from prior expectations with a new range of $100-$150 million.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially by 20% to $24.3M driven by VDR and licensing services which were up 40% QoQ.
Executed approximately $11.3 million in annualized cost reductions, with a target of reaching $15-$20 million total savings by end of FY26.
Secured major public sector wins including multi-year renewals with the Pac-12 Conference and CHP for document redaction.
summary: Veritone reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million (up 20% sequentially and 5% YoY), but missed expectations due to delayed public sector budget shifts related to the conflict in Iran and timing issues with hyperscaler VDR deals. Management lowered fiscal 2026 full-year guidance to a range of $100-$150 million, citing reduced visibility on government contracts and specific VDR deal closures. The company executed significant cost reductions totaling approximately $11.3 million annually as of June 30, positioning for potential breakeven in the first half of fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth implies ~28% in H2 against an exceptionally strong prior year of ~36%, indicating a conservative outlook.
Rental segment margins faced an approximate 50 basis point headwind from increased fuel costs, though partially offset by pricing power.
positive_highlights: Rental segment revenue surged >39% YoY driven by fleet absorption ahead of plan on large-scale mega projects.
Adjusted core EBITDA reached $531 million, reflecting a robust margin mix between rental and sales segments.
Management raised OWN program contribution guidance for the full year by approximately $11M due to strong institutional demand.
summary: EquipmentShare reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion (up 26% YoY) and rental segment revenue of $908 million (up >39% YoY). Adjusted core EBITDA grew to $531 million, representing a beat on the prior period's implied growth trajectory despite management noting that full-year guidance remains conservative for the back half. Management raised specific OWN program contribution guidance by approximately $11M and highlighted strong demand visibility in mega projects.

negative_highlights: Telco core income declined 2% YoY to PHP 16.6 billion, primarily due to a 6% increase in depreciation and amortization.
Home revenues dropped 1% to PHP 30 billion as the business continues to lag from Q1 installation constraints carried into H1.
Maya's contribution to core income was lower than expected for the quarter due to one-time accounting adjustments, though underlying growth remains strong.
positive_highlights: Enterprise revenues grew 5% to PHP 24.8 billion, driven by ICT revenue expansion of 22%.
Wireless top-ups turned positive in June (+1%) and improved further in July (+3%), indicating a recovery trend after Q1 constraints.
Home fiber net adds accelerated significantly in the second quarter with postpaid churn improving to 1.4%.
summary: PLDT reported first-half FY26 service revenues of PHP 108.7 billion (up 2% YoY) and EBITDA of PHP 56.1 billion at a stable 52% margin, though Telco core income declined 2% to PHP 16.6 billion due to higher depreciation. Wireless revenue was broadly flat while Home revenues fell 1% following Q1 installation constraints that are now recovering in the second quarter with positive net adds starting in May. Enterprise remained a strong growth driver up 5%, and management reiterated full-year CapEx guidance of mid-PHP 50 billion despite elevated depreciation from network upgrades.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss widened year-over-year from $3.9M to $4.3M driven by increased costs for Coosa permitting, stock-based compensation, and product development.
Graphite flake input prices remain at historic lows ($500-$600/ton), which management notes is suboptimal compared to the higher price environment desired when Coosa comes online in 2028-2029.
positive_highlights: Received formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan to support Kellyton Phase I development, representing non-dilutive capital with single-digit cost of capital expectations versus mid-teens private market rates.
summary: Westwater Resources reported a Q2 FY2026 consolidated net loss of $4.3 million ($0.03/share), an increase from the prior year's loss of $3.9 million due to higher permitting costs, stock-based compensation, and product development expenses. The company received a significant non-dilutive milestone in the form of a formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan dedicated exclusively to advancing Phase I construction at the Kellyton Graphite Plant. Management maintains a target timeline for commercial production starting as soon as next year (late 2026/early 2027), contingent on securing remaining capital and closing documentation.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly by 46% YoY due to higher court costs and stock-based compensation from the IPO.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance on deployments or earnings, limiting forward visibility.
Cash efficiency ratio excluding Bluestem/Conn's portfolios was lower at 67.8%, reflecting one-time portfolio impacts.
positive_highlights: Record deployments in July of $185 million across the spectrum including new auto finance portfolios.
Strong growth in legal channel collections, up 54% YoY to $64 million.
Forward flow commitments reached a record $480.7 million as of June 30th.
summary: Jefferson Capital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $178 million (up 16% YoY) and collections of $301 million (up 18% YoY), driven by strong deployments including a record July figure. Adjusted EPS was $0.77, with cash efficiency at 72.2%. The company raised its estimated remaining collections to $3.4 billion (+18%) but did not provide specific forward guidance for revenue or earnings.

negative_highlights: Revenue from Remini declined, attributed partly to market saturation rather than AI disruption.
Splice revenue also contributed negatively to the overall portfolio growth rate.
Organic growth of 3% was lower than Q1's 6%, reflecting a blended impact from low single-digit growth in newer acquisitions like AOL and Vimeo.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 126% YoY with organic revenue growth of 3%, exceeding internal expectations.
AOL Advertising performance was better than anticipated following price experiments and infrastructure upgrades.
Management successfully closed the acquisition of Tractive ($759M EV) and reached an agreement to acquire Airtable for $1.29 billion.
summary: Bending Spoons reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $704 million (up 126% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $381 million (up 150%), driven by strong performance in AOL Advertising, WeTransfer, and Tractive. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $2.78 billion-$2.82 billion and adjusted operating income between $1.46 billion-$1.51 billion, which excludes the pending Airtable acquisition expected to close later this year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $78.9 million compared to a prior year loss of $45.3 million.
SG&A expenses surged by $27.4 million quarter-over-quarter, primarily due to hiring for the commercial function and pre-launch activities.
No revenue reported in Q2 as product shipments are not expected until late third quarter 2026.
positive_highlights: FDA approved REVTORPYK for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without PIK3CA mutation following progression on endocrine therapy.
NCCN updated guidelines recommending gedatolisib regimens as preferred Category 1 options in the second-line setting.
Positive efficacy data from VIKTORIA-1 showed median PFS of 11.1 months for the triplet regimen versus 5.6 months with alpelisib.
summary: Celcuity reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $78.9 million ($1.44/share) and an adjusted net loss of $58.7 million ($1.07/share), representing significant year-over-year deterioration in profitability driven by a $35 million increase in SG&A expenses to support commercial launch preparations. While the company achieved major regulatory milestones including FDA approval for REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) and positive Phase III data, it has not yet generated any revenue from product sales as shipments are expected only late in Q3 2026.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 20% due to a significant pullback in procurement services, which dropped 45% compared to the prior-year quarter.
Net income per diluted share decreased from $0.06 to $0.05 primarily because of higher tax expenses following the full release of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.
Systems integration revenue was slightly below recent quarterly averages, with management noting a downturn in mainstream business demand.
positive_highlights: Systems integration revenue increased 46% year-over-year to $13.9 million as the business mix shifts toward higher-margin offerings.
Facilities management revenue surged 84% to $2.7 million, offsetting declines in maintenance agreements with discrete project work.
Blended gross margin expanded significantly from 16.4% last year to 22.8%, reflecting the structural improvement in earnings quality.
summary: Total revenue declined 20% year-over-year to $35.1 million due to a sharp drop in procurement services ($18.2M vs $33M prior year), though higher-margin systems integration grew 46%. Gross profit increased 11% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 12%, driven by the shift toward high-margin segments, but net income fell slightly to $0.05 per share due to a one-time tax valuation allowance release in Q4 FY2025 affecting comparability.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not reaffirming prior revenue guidance and declined to provide specific numbers due to deployment timing uncertainty.
Operating loss widened significantly in Q2 compared to the same period last year as expenses rose sharply ahead of commercialization.
Sequential gross margin contracted from 48% in Q1 to approximately 28% in Q2, attributed to product mix and pre-revenue engineering investments.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth accelerated by approximately 51%, reaching $8.1 million.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year from roughly 7.8% to 27.9% due to a shift away from lower-margin acquired product sales.
Series A rights exercise generated net proceeds of approximately $20.12 million, strengthening the balance sheet for larger customer engagements.
summary: AmpliTech Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $8.1 million (up 51% sequentially but down year-over-year) and a net loss of roughly $3.09 million driven by elevated investments in R&D, marketing, supply chain readiness, and cybersecurity to support larger customers. Gross margin improved significantly from the prior year period due to product mix changes following an asset acquisition, rising from 7.8% YoY but declining sequentially from Q1's 48%. Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or provide specific revenue guidance for the remainder of FY2026, citing timing uncertainties in large telecom deployments.

negative_highlights: Pulp sales volumes were lower compared to Q2 FY25 due to concentrated maintenance downtimes at Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas mills.
EBITDA from Brazilian operations declined 20% year-over-year driven by lower prices, export volume contraction, and unfavorable FX effects.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow remained strong despite volatile geopolitical conditions.
summary: Suzano reported Q2 FY26 results with solid free cash flow and the successful closing of the Arbex acquisition on July 1st, though paperboard volumes were impacted by customer inventory build-up ahead of price increases. Pulp sales reached 2.9 million tons driven by higher export prices to $601/ton despite constrained production from maintenance downtimes in Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas. Management reiterated a focus on deleveraging the business following Arbex consolidation, with cash costs expected to decline below BRL 800/ton in H2 due to reduced downtime and wood consumption.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened due to an incremental operating loss of $1.4M and unfavorable FX impact of $400k, alongside non-cash warrant charges
Discontinued operations revenue declined 34% year-over-year as the company winds down ESWL and distribution businesses
positive_highlights: HIFU capital system sales reached an all-time high of 13 units globally with U.S. volumes growing 47% year-over-year
Gross margin expanded significantly to 55.6%, up from 51.1% in the prior period, driven by pricing and cost reductions
Management secured a $40 million equity offering to fortify balance sheet for growth initiatives
summary: FocalTherics reported Q2 FY26 HIFU revenue of $13.2 million, a 39% year-over-year increase driven by 13 capital system sales and strong procedure volume growth in the U.S. Gross margin expanded to 55.6%, while operating expenses rose due to strategic investments and non-cash warrant charges. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for core HIFU revenue between $50 million-$54 million, maintaining their previously announced targets despite a change in financial reporting classification.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margins contracted from 43.6% to 41.2%, impacted by a $1.0 million non-cash stock-based compensation charge related to the accelerated vesting of the 2025 annual bonus.
EPS decreased year-over-year despite net income growth due to an increase in weighted shares outstanding from April's rights offering.
Management expects gross margins to contract slightly further in H2 FY2026 as new programs ramp up, with a realistic range of 41.5%-43.5%.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 13.8% YoY to $15.1 million driven by strong aerospace and defense program shipments.
Backlog grew significantly, increasing 37.2% year-over-year to $84 million with three consecutive quarters of book-to-bill ratios well above one.
Company received heavy order volume in counter-drone areas for phased array radar systems used in military and border control applications.
summary: M-tron reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $15.1 million (up 13.8% YoY) and net income of $1.9 million ($0.43 diluted EPS), though GAAP gross margins contracted to 41.2% from 43.6%. Management noted a one-time non-cash stock-based compensation charge in the current quarter but expects guidance for H2 FY2026 gross margins between 41.5%-44%, citing margin pressure as new programs ramp up.

negative_highlights: Accelsius removed DarkNX from its 2026 forecast due to a site becoming unavailable, likely related to power envelope constraints.
Management explicitly suspended revenue targets and guidance for Accelius until structural market constraints ease or foundational KPIs are met.
Cash balance decreased quarter-over-quarter as the company used $59.5 million in operating cash flow while raising only $13 million via equity draws.
positive_highlights: AeroFlexx commercial pipeline grew close to $35 million (up 9% QoQ) with new partnerships in Latin America and Europe.
Accelsius completed a major third-party benchmark showing NeuCool cold plates running GPUs 9-14 degrees cooler than single-phase systems, validating the technology for high-density AI workloads.

The FDA Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted against approval for the cardiomyopathy indication (3-9), though management plans to resubmit an amended BLA focusing on upper limb skeletal muscle efficacy supported by HOPE-3 data published in The Lancet. Commercial readiness activities are being paced until regulatory clarity is achieved.

Crème de la Crème summer camp enrollment increased approximately 26% compared to last year, signaling repositioning traction
Marketing initiatives successfully drove a week-over-week increase in inquiries across the portfolio
summary: KinderCare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $698 million, down slightly from the prior year's $700 million and missing expectations due to a 4% decline in total enrollment driven by footprint optimization. Adjusted EPS was $0.08 compared to $0.22 last year, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $63 million as management updated full-year guidance downward to reflect the impact of closing approximately 80-85 centers and a reduced tuition contribution assumption from state subsidies.

negative_highlights: Ipiranga expects margins in Q3 to decline from current levels as they normalize toward first-quarter figures due to Middle East conflict impacts.
Ultragaz volume decreased by 3% YoY, with a specific drop of 4% in the bottled segment and 2% in bulk segments.
Hidrovias adjusted EBITDA fell 8% compared to Q2 FY2025 primarily due to the sale of its coastal navigation operation.
positive_highlights: Net income reached a historic high of BRL 1,677 million, representing a 46% increase compared to Q2 FY2025.
Operating cash flow generation hit an all-time record of BRL 4.8 billion due to strong operations and working capital release at Ipiranga.
Leverage ratio improved significantly to 0.9x, the lowest level since 2008.
summary: Ultrapar reported record net income of BRL 1,677 million (up 46% YoY) and recurring adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3,657 million for Q2 FY2026. The company achieved a significant working capital release at Ipiranga driven by diesel imports amid Middle East volatility, resulting in record operating cash flow generation of BRL 4.8 billion. Management anticipates margins will normalize to first-quarter levels due to the offsetting effects of fighting illegal practices and ongoing supply disruptions.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue/EBITDA growth is capped at a modest implied rate of 6.5% due to pro-forma adjustments.
Same-Quarter Revenue (MSR) forecasted to decline by approximately 3% in Q4 FY26 compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Achieved a record first-half booking total of 470 MW, with Q2 alone contributing 260 MW.
Secured an additional 600 MW in reservations from customers for future capacity needs.
Raised full-year sales target to 1 GW and CapEx guidance to RMB 10 billion reflecting strong demand.
summary: GDS Holdings reported a record first-half of FY26 with 470 MW in new bookings and secured an additional 600 MW in reservations for future needs. Management raised its full-year sales target to 1 GW from the prior guidance, alongside raising CapEx paid guidance from RMB 9 billion to RMB 10 billion. Pro forma adjusted EBITDA growth is now implied at 6.5% for FY26 following pro-forma adjustments that deduct one-time items and restructured recurring income.

negative_highlights: Platform revenue decreased approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million.
Total platform expenses increased by approximately 11% to $5.9 million, primarily due to bad debt charges on uncollectible development fees.
positive_highlights: Platform Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $0.3 million, an improvement of roughly $0.4 million from the prior year quarter's loss.
Completed first fund tokenization for PURE Pickleball & Padel and launched a second offering (Steamboat Springs Hyatt Studios) with an initial slate targeting ~$100 million in managed assets.
summary: Q2 platform revenue declined approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million due to timing of project financings and lower development fees, while total expenses rose by roughly 11% to $5.9 million driven by bad debt charges. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly from a loss in the prior period but remained below guidance targets as management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $18-$22 million without raising it.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year ROAE guidance expectations from ~9.5-10% to 9.25%, citing second-half margin pressures.
NIM on investments is being built conservatively at 2% for the remainder of the year due to potential rate hikes and derivative offsets.
Concerns expressed regarding a new local tax project in Bogotá that could add COP 500 billion to operational expenses.
positive_highlights: Attributed net income reached COP 577 billion, up 17% compared to the prior year quarter.
ROAE expanded significantly to 12.7%, reflecting strong profitability despite macro headwinds.
Loan growth accelerated with total loans increasing 2.1% over the quarter and deposits growing 3.8%.
summary: Grupo Aval reported Q2 FY26 attributed net income of COP 577 billion (up 17% YoY) and ROAE of 12.7%, driven by loan/deposit growth and strong investment portfolio contributions. Management maintained full-year ROAE guidance at 9.25% despite a first-half performance near 10%, citing caution regarding second-half NIM pressures from further rate hikes, earthquake impacts on asset quality, and potential local tax increases in Bogotá.

negative_highlights: Total net revenues decreased by 1.3% year-over-year to $56.5 million due to a lower average number of vessels owned and operated.
First half revenue declined slightly, indicating that recent strong market rates have not yet fully offset the impact of fleet size reduction.
positive_highlights: Charter coverage stands at 96% for 2026 with highly attractive average daily rates of approximately $30,900 per day.
Fleet utilization remains remarkably tight with idle capacity just 200,000 TEU or 6% of the global fleet as of early July.
Newbuilding prices moved higher up approximately 2% quarter-over-quarter reflecting robust demand across the sector.
summary: Euroseas reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $56.5 million and EPS of $4.74 per diluted share, representing a slight miss against the prior year's revenue growth despite higher charter rates driven by supply tightness. Management noted that while current market conditions are strong with high utilization, they anticipate potential moderation in demand towards the end of 2026 as geopolitical disruptions may ease and new vessel deliveries increase.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$14M due to IM-4 estimated complete adjustment of $14.7M and acquisition-related costs
Gross profit margin pressure from one-off adjustments on the IM-4 mission
positive_highlights: $206 million revenue delivered, more than four times the prior year
Record $1.8 billion backlog with diversification across civil (37%), commercial (49%), and national security (14%) segments
Won three GEO communication satellites valued at over $600 million for a 30-month term
summary: Intuitive Machines reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $206 million (up from a loss in the prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of -$14 million (improving from -$25 million). The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for revenue between $900M-$1B and positive adjusted EBITDA, citing record backlog growth to $1.8 billion driven by diversification into commercial GEO satellites ($600M award) and national security programs (SDA Tranche 3/AMDT3). Management noted that near-term cash usage remains elevated due to strategic inventory investments but expects free cash flow improvement in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $5 million driven largely by one-time leadership transition costs ($0.9M) and stock-based compensation
No revenue guidance provided as the company is still in a learning stage with initial commercial launch only just beginning
FDA pivotal trial timeline remains uncertain pending review, though management expects to start before year-end
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment of ALIGN-ACS pilot study with 134 patients ahead of schedule, results accepted at TCT conference
Initial commercial orders shipped and first patients onboarded in concierge practices across four target geographies
Operating cash outflow decreased by 7% QoQ due to cost efficiencies and pausing non-key projects
summary: HeartBeam reported a net loss of $5 million for Q2 FY2026, which included approximately $1 million in one-time items related to leadership transition and severance; excluding these, the underlying operating cash outflow decreased by roughly 7% quarter-over-quarter. Management confirmed that initial commercial orders have shipped with patients being onboarded at concierge practices across four U.S. geographies (New York, Dallas, South Florida, Southern California), though specific revenue figures were not disclosed as the business remains in a learning stage. The company submitted its pre-submission to the FDA today for heart attack detection indication via the 510(k) pathway.

negative_highlights: Exploration and evaluation expenses surged $45.6 million year-over-year, primarily due to a one-time charge of $37.5M owed to Allseas
Cash used in operating activities increased to $20.1 million from $10.7 million in the prior period (excluding tax timing differences)
Management clarified that no investment decision has been made for the Brownsville processing site and future capital commitments remain contingent on U.S. government support
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $60.1 million from a net loss of $74.3 million in Q2 FY2025
NOAA certification for USA-A application expected imminently, with permanent grant anticipated by October 2026 despite administrative delays
New Master Services Agreement signed with Eco Minerals to provide vessel charter and AUV equipment
summary: TMC reported a net loss of $60.1 million in Q2 FY2026 compared to $74.3 million in the prior year period, driven by exploration and evaluation expenses increasing significantly due to charges owed to Allseas ($37.5M) related to their development agreement signed in May. While management highlighted steady progress on U.S. permitting milestones for USA-A and USA-B applications and confirmed that cash reserves are sufficient for at least 12 months, they explicitly stated no investment decision has been made regarding the Brownsville processing site yet.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened by $9.7 million year-over-year due to pre-development acceleration
Cash used in operating activities increased from $7.2M (H1 '25) to $22.8M (H1 '26)
Management explicitly stated they cannot provide specific spending guidance until feasibility studies conclude
positive_highlights: Successfully completed IPO raising $310 million, bolstering liquidity significantly
Treasury cash balance increased robustly from $31M to $288.7M in six months
Completed approximately 1,200m of underground development and commissioned a replacement hoist
summary: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining reported a net loss of $16.7 million ($0.13 per share) for Q2 FY2026, an increase from the prior year's loss due to accelerated development activities and IPO-related costs. The company raised approximately $310 million in its recent IPO, bringing cash on hand to $288.7 million at quarter-end with no long-term debt. Management provided a clear path toward production targeted for late 2028 but declined to provide specific financial guidance or updated spending forecasts beyond noting that G&A will taper off starting Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Q2 Revenue declined from Q1 due to the elimination of $1.8 million in staking revenue following the sale of Ethereum holdings.
General and administrative expenses increased to $10.3M, including a one-time cash charge of $1.8M for an early termination fee on an asset manager agreement.
Management explicitly stated that AI compute deployment is contingent on closing specific deals in Q4 rather than being fully operational.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly from $77.5 million in Q1 to $12.4 million in Q2 as the business transitioned away from digital asset volatility.
Acquired two additional commercial aircraft engines already generating contracted lease revenue with targeted double-digit annual returns.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance remains intact at $18-$22M despite capital deployment into buybacks and new assets.
summary: Forum Markets reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.4 million and a net loss narrowing to $12.4 million from the prior quarter's $77.5 million loss due to asset sales and buybacks rather than operational growth. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $18-$22 million, driven by aircraft lease income ($5-6M in H2) and a pending AI compute deal expected to contribute ~$8-12M in Q4. The company executed significant share repurchases (7.1M shares), reducing outstanding equity by 35%.

negative_highlights: Q2 combined ratio spiked to 99.5%, significantly above H1 average of 93.1%, due to $162 million in catastrophe and large losses.
Management explicitly stated they do not expect Q3 growth to match the quarter's pace, citing seasonality where more premium is earned in Q4 for wind perils.
Reinsurance acquisition expense ratio was higher than anticipated as new partner business earns through without Fidelis Partnership commissions.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written grew by over 6% in both the quarter and year-to-date, driven by new underwriting partners.
Book value per diluted common share increased 23% YoY to $26.56 due to strong capital returns including a $73 million return (buybacks + dividends).
War-related lines have run at a sub-20% loss ratio since the Russia-Ukraine conflict, demonstrating profitable deployment in geopolitical risk.
summary: Pelagos Insurance Capital reported Q2 FY26 gross premiums written of $1.3 billion (up 6% YoY) and operating net income of $29 million ($0.34 diluted EPS). The quarter's combined ratio was elevated at 99.5%, driven by large loss events totaling $162 million, including specific losses from the Middle East conflict and a gas plant explosion in Qatar; however, management views this as random timing variability rather than an underlying trend deterioration. Management maintained its full-year guidance for mid-single-digit growth and ROAE targets of 13%-15%, citing that H1 results are broadly on plan with Q3/Q4 expected to normalize the combined ratio.

negative_highlights: The company remains at an operating loss, reporting a non-GAAP net loss of $5.8 million ($0.07 per share) compared to a larger loss last year.
Management noted that autonomous processing and Plaque Tracker are expected to drive further margin expansion in 2027 rather than the current fiscal year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $64.1 million, marking the fastest growth rate in eight quarters.
Plaque revenue reached $7.8 million, beating expectations by approximately $3-4 million and driving significant gross margin expansion of 770 bps quarter-over-quarter.
New account additions hit a record cohort of 340 accounts added during the prior year (2025), ramping in line with or ahead of expectations.
summary: HeartFlow reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $64.1 million, up 48% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, driven by accelerating plaque adoption and durable FF-CT utilization. Management raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to a range of $246-$250 million (representing 40%-42% growth) and increased the non-GAAP gross margin outlook to approximately 82%. The company highlighted record new account additions in Q2, with plaque activations ahead of plan and coverage reaching roughly 78%.

negative_highlights: Research and development expenses increased by 9.8% due to AI investment
AI BOX was integrated into existing suites rather than growing as a separate line item
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased by 6% year-over-year to CNY 162.1 million
Gross margin expanded five percentage points to reach 70.1%
Net loss narrowed significantly from CNY 73.9 million to CNY 14.4 million
summary: In the first half of FY2026, YXT reported total revenues of CNY 162.1 million, a 6% year-over-year increase driven by AI product adoption and large enterprise focus. Gross margin expanded significantly to 70.1%, up five percentage points from the prior period, while net loss narrowed substantially to CNY 14.4 million. Management expressed confidence in further gross margin expansion for H2 due to continued operational efficiencies.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined from 24.5% to 23% driven by $7 million incremental marketing/IT investment in Q2.
Digital Wallet segment adjusted EBITDA fell 9% YoY and revenue per active user decreased 5% due to regional mix shifts including weaker rest-of-world markets.
Merchant Solutions volume growth of only 5% reflects a slowdown in same-store sales for existing customers despite strong iGaming volumes.
positive_highlights: Resolution of major inherited SPAC-era legal overhang via settlement in principle with Farzad litigation removes significant restructuring expense drain on cash flow and P&L.
Completion of debt refinancing extending maturity profile to 2030, upsizing the revolver, and reducing net leverage ratio from 5.5x at Q4 end to a projected year-end range of 5.1-5.2x.
Strong double-digit user growth in Latin America for digital wallets and successful launch of PaysafeWallet in Poland expanding consumer reach.
summary: Paysafe reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $447.4 million (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $102.8 million (down 2%), resulting in an EPS miss due to increased marketing/IT investments and interest expenses despite the resolution of legacy litigation matters. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue and adjusted EBITDA while updating adjusted EPS expectations, citing a strong first-half growth rate of 7% that met prior outlooks.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased approximately 87% year-over-year to $34.2 million due to Melinta integration and new personnel.
note and marketing expense surged 95% to $12.4 million reflecting a larger product portfolio rather than organic growth efficiency gains.
New LDO pilot is not included in current guidance, with visibility into its impact expected only by late year or early next year.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat prior year by more than doubling from $22.4M to $58.7M driven by Melinta portfolio contribution and DefenCath growth.
Signed a multi-year commercial supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization (LDO), securing agreements with all five top U.S. dialysis providers.
Positive Phase III ReSPECT data for REZZAYO met primary endpoint of fungal-free survival at day 90, positioning the product for sNDA submission in Q3.
summary: CorMedix reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of $101.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $58.7 million, significantly beating the prior year period which included no Melinta contribution. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance at $325-$345 million while raising full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a new range of $125-$140 million following a multi-year commercial supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization.

negative_highlights: Low unit volume sales (9 consoles) failed to match revenue growth despite margin expansion.
Operating expenses increased YoY by $800k due to investments in commercial and product development initiatives.
Net loss widened from $12.6M prior year quarter, though this included a one-time warrant valuation charge of ~$1.7M.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14% YoY to $1.97M driven by a 5% increase in circuit ASP and favorable product mix.
Gross margin expanded significantly from 56% to 76% due to pricing power and transition to contract manufacturing.
Installed base growth accelerated with nine consoles sold in Q2, bringing the first-half total to 24 units.
summary: Nuwellis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.97 million (up 14% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 76%, driven by pricing adjustments and product mix shifts rather than volume growth, which remained low with only nine consoles sold in the quarter compared to three last year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $4.8 million, including roughly $1.7 million in warrant valuation expense from recent financing activities that strengthened cash reserves but did not provide formal financial guidance for future periods.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 20 basis points due to a significant LIFO expense of $6.4 million compared to $2.9 million in the prior-year quarter.
Flow control operations experienced muted sales growth, partially offsetting gains from other segments within Engineered Solutions.
Fiscal 2027 guidance assumes more difficult comparisons and potentially lower market growth rates in the second half of the year.
positive_highlights: Organic sales growth accelerated to 10%, driven by double-digit volume increases in automation (over 20%) and fluid power operations.
EBITDA margin expanded more than 60 basis points year-over-year, leveraging strong top-line momentum into higher returns.
Free cash flow increased 16% YoY to $461 million for the full fiscal year, supported by working capital optimization.
summary: Applied Industrial Technologies reported a solid finish to fiscal Q4 FY26 with record sales of $1.3 billion (up 10% YoY) and EPS of $3.17 (up 13%). EBITDA margins expanded by over 60 bps to 13%, driven by volume growth in automation and fluid power, though gross margin was slightly down due to LIFO expense. Management raised intermediate financial targets for fiscal 2028-2029, increasing the sales objective to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and EBITDA margins to 14%.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses spiked sharply to ~$7.5 million due to public company costs, legal fees, and one-time equipment purchases.
Net loss widened materially to approximately $7.2 million compared to a prior year net loss of roughly $1.6 million.
Management declined to provide specific visibility on converting the MOU with Powers into a full contract.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew YoY to approximately $216,000 despite accounting deferrals on the SkyKnight program.
Gross profit increased significantly to roughly $184,000 compared to $82,000 in Q2 FY25.
Cash position strengthened with total cash and equivalents at June 30 reaching approximately $25.3 million.
summary: Swarmer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $216,000 compared to $138,000 in the prior year period, driven by a commercial deal where only ~$200k was recognized due to accounting treatment. Gross profit rose to roughly $184,000 from $82,000 primarily reflecting this revenue recognition mechanics rather than margin expansion on scale. Operating expenses surged to approximately $7.5 million (up from $855,000) driven by public company costs and one-time equipment purchases, resulting in a net loss of ~$7.2 million versus a prior year loss of ~$1.6 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell sharply to 19.5% due to elevated milk prices, resin costs, and oil-related transportation expenses.
Management expects input cost pressures to persist into the third quarter before conditions normalize.
Net income was minimal at $0.1 million ($0.01 per share) despite record sales volume.
positive_highlights: Net sales reached $66.9 million, marking the highest quarterly figure in company history and up 24.1% year-over-year.
The quarter extended a streak of growth to 27 consecutive quarters with nearly seven years of uninterrupted performance.
Distribution expanded significantly for Muscle Mates (nearly 800 Walmart locations) and Farmer Cheese (nationwide at Walmart, coming soon to Target).
summary: Lifeway Foods reported record quarterly net sales of $66.9 million in Q2 FY2026, representing a 24.1% year-over-year increase and extending its streak to 27 consecutive quarters of growth. However, gross margin contracted significantly to 19.5%, primarily due to elevated milk prices, packaging resin costs, and transportation pressures related to the Middle East conflict. Management noted that while SG&A decreased as a percentage of sales (operating leverage), near-term profitability remains under pressure from these input cost headwinds.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 19.1%, with total operating expenses rising 19.4% primarily driven by $129.6 million of stock compensation from the IPO.
Revenue was negatively impacted by a payer mix shift due to ACA exchange subsidy expiration, resulting in approximately $16 million lower revenue compared to expectations.
Net loss widened to $28.3 million as reported earnings were significantly offset by one-time IPO-related expenses and No Surprises Act comparability issues.
positive_highlights: Same-market revenue increased by $53.1 million (3.8% YoY) driven by emergent transport growth and new market starts totaling over $43 million in incremental annualized revenue.
911 Nurse Navigation calls grew significantly to nearly 29,000, representing a 50% year-over-year increase as the company expands this non-emergent solution.
Air medical volumes increased 6.9% YoY due to strong demand and improved capture rates in weather-constrained markets.
summary: GMR Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.49 billion (3.3% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $285 million, which was down 11.8% YoY due to a lack of favorable No Surprises Act estimate adjustments compared to the prior year. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $5.89B-$6.18B and adjusted EBITDA between $1.135B-$1.195B, noting that underlying performance remains strong despite headwinds from ACA subsidy expiration impacts of approximately $16 million per quarter.

negative_highlights: Management declined to provide specific numerical guidance for fiscal 2027, noting that results will reflect higher team compensation and luxury tax expenses.
SG&A expenses increased by $2.9 million related to the proposed spin-off transaction costs.
