NHL revenue sharing expense is expected to increase in FY27 due to changes under the new collective bargaining agreement.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 36% year-over-year driven by a Knicks championship run that generated $182 million in playoff-related revenues versus $115.2 million the prior year.
Adjusted operating income swung from an adjusted loss of $16.8 million to a profit of $39.6 million, reflecting robust demand and record per-game gate revenues during the postseason.
Sponsorship revenues more than doubled year-over-year during the championship run due to heightened partner activation opportunities.
summary: For fiscal Q4 FY26, MSG Sports reported total revenues of $278.7 million and adjusted operating income (AOI) of $39.6 million, representing a significant beat against the prior year's revenue of $204 million and AOI loss of -$16.8 million driven by Knicks championship playoffs. Management raised full-year FY26 guidance to approximately $59 million in AOI from an implied lower range based on Q4 results but declined to provide specific numerical guidance for fiscal 2027, citing higher team compensation and revenue sharing expenses as headwinds.

negative_highlights: Sweaty Betty revenue declined 3% in the quarter due to an ongoing strategic reset of its U.S. business.
Work Group revenue fell 2%, though this was noted as modestly ahead of expectations amidst varying progress across brands.
Gross margin decreased 70 basis points YoY, primarily pressured by a ~310 bps unmitigated tariff headwind and elevated oil prices.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.40 beat the high end of prior guidance ($0.35-$0.38) driven by strong revenue growth and disciplined cost management.
Merrell delivered double-digit revenue growth (10%) with triple-digit basis point market share gains in the U.S. hike category.
Saucony achieved 9% quarterly growth on top of a massive 40% YoY increase last year, raising its full-year outlook to mid-teens.
summary: Wolverine World Wide reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $506 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.40 (up 14%), both exceeding expectations with the latter beating the upper end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.98B-$2.0B from $1.965B-$1.985B and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55-$1.65 from $1.43-$1.58, citing strong H1 execution by Merrell (up 10%) and Saucony (up 9%). The company also raised its full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 46.9%.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from $2,508M midpoint to $2,462M due to new market deterioration and travel volatility.
Adjusted operating margin of 13.2% missed the guided range driven by dollar weakness in Colombia and utilization below targets.
North America region experienced a 2.4% revenue contraction while new markets saw an 17.7% decrease.
positive_highlights: AI Pods adoption accelerated with revenue growing roughly 60% quarter-over-quarter, now comprising ~45 of top client projects.
Top 20 clients grew by 6.6% year-over-year while new market segment dragged growth down significantly.
Free cash flow for the first half reached a record $48.7 million.
summary: Globant reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $614.4 million, which was within the prior guided range but represented a slight year-over-year decline and sequential growth of only 1.2%. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance downward to a range of $2.43B-$2.46B from the previous $2.46B-$2.51B, citing geopolitical pressures in new markets (specifically Middle East) and travel sector slowdowns due to oil prices. Adjusted operating margin slipped below expectations to 13.2% as FX headwinds impacted Colombia and utilization targets were missed.

negative_highlights: Market share recovery is expected to take more time than anticipated due to prior retail disruptions.
Share buybacks have been suspended to prioritize debt paydown, indicating a shift away from aggressive capital return.
Management declined to provide specific leverage ratio targets or timelines for deleveraging.
positive_highlights: Category remains robust with value up ~3.4% and volume up ~1.6% in the frozen segment year-to-date.
summary: Management stated that retail disruptions in Germany and France are largely resolved but warned it will take time to return market share to neutral levels despite strong category growth of roughly 3% year-to-date. The company suspended share buybacks to focus on deleveraging while maintaining dividends, with a EUR 200 million productivity program remaining on track.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $113 million represents a significant decline from $215.4 million in Q2 FY2025 due to legacy adjustments
Gross loss widened significantly to $71 million compared to gross profit of $13 million last year, primarily driven by non-cash catch-up adjustments
Net loss attributable to stockholders was $84.3 million ($1.55 per diluted share) versus a net loss of only $10.3 million in the prior period
positive_highlights: Surety partners advanced approximately $71 million during Q2, bringing total advances to $210 million
Debt service relief estimated at approximately $27 million over the next 12 months via interest capitalization and suspended amortization
$190 million contract value secured for Phase Three Winnipeg North End Sewage Treatment Plant award
summary: Second quarter revenue was $113 million compared to a prior year of $215 million, driven by unfavorable legacy dispute adjustments totaling approximately $102 million in revenue reversals and $94 million impacting gross loss. Gross loss for the quarter reached $71 million versus a profit of $13 million last year due to these non-cash catch-up adjustments on derecognized claim positions. Management finalized strategic agreements with sureties providing financing support, restructuring debt terms including interest capitalization, and expects bidding activity to increase in the back half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Billable service fees decreased due to partial DHS shutdown in February 2026
Reselling and other services declined $2.1M YoY as non-recurring revenues from prior period normalized away
CWMS 3.0 full ramp-up depends on GAO protest resolution by October 7, 2026
positive_highlights: Secured $3.1 billion, 10-year CWMS 3.0 contract with DHS
Awarded prime status on the $60 billion NASA SEWP VI contract
Expanded scope of ATV carrier contract expected to go live by year-end
summary: WidePoint reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $38 million (up from $37.3M YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $66k ($0.01 EPS) compared to a prior year loss of $618k, driven by growth in carrier services but offset by lower billable fees due to partial DHS shutdowns. Management highlighted the awarding of CWMS 3.0 and SEWP VI contracts as major wins for future scale while noting that Q2 results were impacted by non-recurring items and a temporary government shutdown.

negative_highlights: Gross-to-net margins were only 29.6%, below the expected mid-30% steady state due to pending payer contract additions.

Net loss widened slightly from $25.1 million in Q1 to $23.4 million (improvement) but cash burn remains high at -$8.7M adjusted EBITDA equivalent before one-time items, though the text reports a net loss of $23.4m vs prior quarter's $25.1m.
A $0.9 million write-off occurred for commercial API inventory identified through quality control processes.
positive_highlights: Net product revenue grew 45% quarter-over-quarter to $15.4 million driven by a 48% increase in prescribed units.
Units dispensed increased 81.3% within one major PBM contract, while prescribers rose 68%.
Refill rates surged with an 82% quarter-over-quarter increase and repeat writer counts hitting all-time highs.
summary: Pelthos Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net product revenue of $15.4 million, a 45% increase from the prior quarter and driven by a 48% rise in prescribed units to 11,925. Gross-to-net margins were favorable at 29.6%, slightly up from Q1 but below management's mid-30% long-term target due to ongoing payer contract negotiations. The company restated its Q1 financials regarding convertible debt fair value accounting, which impacted reported net loss and adjusted EBITDA figures for the period.

negative_highlights: Middle East/Africa region (less than 2% of revenue) saw a temporary pause in demand due to conflict and higher energy costs
International markets were flat overall, masking strength in Asia-Pacific but including softness in Europe and the Middle East
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% YoY with pricing contributing slightly more than half of the increase
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 28.1%, up 135 bps from the prior year, excluding one-time items
Net leverage reduced significantly to 2.4x adjusted EBITDA at quarter-end after paying down $50 million in debt
summary: Alliance Laundry reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 7% YoY and adjusted EBITDA growth of 12%, driven by pricing power that offset inflationary pressures including tariffs. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to an 8%-10% range while maintaining the prior revenue outlook, citing strong first-half performance and visibility into H2 demand despite minor regional lumps in Middle East/Africa.

negative_highlights: Management noted temporary pressure on gross margins due to unexpected supply chain challenges and material cost inflation requiring safety stock investments through early 2027.
Leverage target for year-end 2026 was slightly revised from '2x or below' to '2x or above' due to the aforementioned temporary working capital measures.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew by 22% year-over-year to $42 million, significantly outpacing revenue growth.
Order backlog increased nearly 20% YoY to approximately $1.3 billion, providing strong visibility for future quarters.
North America secured a landmark seven-year, $96 million frame contract with a strategic U.S. customer.
summary: Aebi Schmidt reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $496 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $42 million (up 22% YoY), driven by a backlog increase to ~$1.3 billion and strong performance in North America and Europe. Management confirmed full-year guidance for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA, noting that realized synergies are accelerating toward the updated target of over $40M annually while acknowledging temporary supply chain investments impacting leverage targets slightly into 2027.

negative_highlights: Automotive sales declined for a second straight year with successive drops in Q3 and Q4 suggesting stabilization rather than immediate recovery.
Industrial segment fell 5% sequentially driven by lower HVAC demand, partially offset only by smart meter recoveries in Europe.
Gross margin expansion of 90 bps was constrained by incremental costs associated with the Indianapolis facility ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income was better than estimates at a 4.9% margin rate despite lower sales volume.
Medical business completed the fiscal year with growth in all four quarters and exceeded 10% normalized organic growth versus FY25.
Cash from operations remained robust at $42.4 million, marking the 10th consecutive quarter of positive cash flow.
summary: Kimball Electronics reported Q4 FY26 net sales of $371.6 million, a 2% year-over-year decline and a sequential increase, with adjusted operating income at $18.1 million (4.9% margin). The company raised full fiscal 2027 guidance to organic revenue growth of 3%-5%, projecting total FY27 sales between $1.535 billion and $1.56 billion driven by medical segment expansion, while acknowledging automotive will likely be flattish due to EV demand softness.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue was minimal ($0.2M) because the primary new product launch occurred after quarter-end, excluding Q2 performance from results.
note, general and administrative expenses increased to $2.6 million due to a non-cash write-down of previously deferred offering costs.
No specific financial guidance or revenue targets were provided for FY27.
positive_highlights: Flora Sync LF5 launched successfully with sales beginning July, marking the company's first direct commercialization milestone.
DARE to PLAY sildenafil cream received healthy prescription activity from both office providers and telehealth channels prior to dispensing start.
Net loss narrowed significantly year-over-year due to non-dilutive funding offsets in R&D.
summary: Total revenue for Q2 FY26 was approximately $0.2 million compared to negative $21k in the prior year period due to a one-time accounting adjustment and delayed product launch timing (Flora Sync LF5 sales began July). Net loss improved from $4M to $3M, driven by lower R&D expenses offset by non-cash write-downs of deferred offering costs. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated revenue recognition for DARE to PLAY will begin in Q3 and DARE to RECLAIM is targeted for 2027.

negative_highlights: Avionics revenue remained flat quarter-over-quarter as demand stayed stable but did not grow.
Training segment performance was below expectations due to task orders outside AIRO's strengths; management is evaluating strategic alternatives for this capital-intensive unit by year-end.
Second half revenue expected to be in line with or modestly above H1, implying Q3 sequential decline before a stronger Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a ~76% year-over-year increase driven by drone segment outperformance.
Gross margins expanded sequentially and YoY to 64%, aided by product mix shift toward drones and lower development costs for JC250/JX250 variants running low double-digits below internal estimates.
RQ-35 achieved Blue UAS certification, opening access to DoW federal procurement channels.
summary: AIRO reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.2 million (up ~76% YoY) and swung to a small operating profit of $1.7M from a prior year loss, driven by drone segment outperformance where gross margins expanded to 64%. Management reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of 15%-25%, noting that H1 represented roughly half of current annual expectations due to timing shifts in major deliveries and anticipated FX headwinds.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses surged 156% YoY to $164.6 million, driven by a one-time non-cash equity-based compensation charge of $33.5 million related to the IPO.
Other income/expense included a significant non-cash mark-to-market loss of $5.6 million on an exercised warrant liability.
Operating cash flow used was $97.3 million, up from $20 million in Q2 2025, reflecting higher activity and prepayments to vendors.
positive_highlights: DOE cooperative agreement increased to up to $2.115 billion total cost share contribution, signaling strong government support for the ARDP program.
TRISO-X fuel facility (TX-1) vertical construction is approximately 80% complete on schedule.
summary: X-Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $54.6 million (up 154% YoY) and operating expenses of $164.6 million due to higher ARDP work and a one-time equity comp charge, resulting in an implied loss per share as the company is newly public post-IPO. Management highlighted significant progress on supply chain de-risking with binding HALEU agreements and graphite capacity expansions, alongside a major DOE funding increase for their demonstration program. Forward guidance remains qualitative regarding project timelines (Dow permit expected late 2026) rather than quantitative financial targets.

negative_highlights: Mining net revenue dropped due to the impact of a 15-day operational shutdown in May/June, offsetting strong sales volume.
Consolidated EBITDA growth was partially neutralized by higher logistics costs and foreign exchange appreciation affecting iron ore revenues.
High interest rates continue to pressure cash generation despite deleveraging efforts via asset sales (cement binding offers received).
positive_highlights: Cement segment delivered a second consecutive record EBITDA exceeding BRL 420 million with margins above 30% despite maintenance shutdowns.
Logistics achieved the second-best EBITDA in company history with a margin of 45%, driven by dry weather seasonality and efficiency gains.
Steel segment returned to double-digit profitability (10.5%) following anti-dumping measures that reduced import penetration.
summary: CSN reported a consolidated EBITDA increase of 5% year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter to BRL 6 billion for Q2 FY2026, driven by record performance in cement (EBITDA >BRL 420 million) and logistics. However, the mining segment saw net revenue decline due to a 15-day shutdown and foreign exchange impacts, while steel margins recovered but remain under pressure from raw material costs. Management highlighted significant working capital releases of approximately BRL 900-1 billion projected by year-end as key drivers for cash flow.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $4.5M ($0.16/share) was driven by approximately $12.9M in one-time equity-based compensation costs from IPO award vesting.
Operating expenses spiked 251% YoY to $24.2 million, largely due to the aforementioned stock-based comp and new public company compliance costs.
Gross margins were temporarily pressured by operational challenges at EMP factories producing high-margin AD&G components.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 35% YoY to $66.4 million driven by strong demand across Aerospace & Defense (AD&G) end markets.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 57% year-over-year to $8.9 million, reflecting improved operational execution and productivity gains in the CMC division.
Open order backlog surged 55% YoY to a record $131.5 million, with AD&G backlog specifically up over 100%.
summary: Revenue grew 35% year-over-year to $66.4 million driven by a net demand increase and raw material pricing impacts on tungsten and molybdenum. Adjusted EBITDA rose 57% to $8.9 million, though GAAP reported a loss of $0.16 per share due to significant one-time equity-based compensation costs associated with the IPO vesting ($12.9M). Management noted that while backlog grew significantly in defense and aerospace segments, margins were pressured by operational challenges at EMP factories dealing with high-margin AD&G products.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income declined slightly on an annual basis despite EPS growth driven by buybacks.
Cost of risk remained elevated at 21.5% due to portfolio expansion and roll-forward effects from late 2025/early 2026 vintages.
Management explicitly stated the operating backdrop is 'considerably more challenging' than anticipated, citing higher-for-longer interest rates.
positive_highlights: TPV growth re-accelerated to 4%, signaling early success in new merchant retention initiatives.
Retail deposits grew significantly, reaching BRL 10.8 billion up more than 20% year-over-year.
Credit portfolio doubled its level from a year ago to reach BRL 3.8 billion.
summary: StoneCo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of BRL 3.6 billion and adjusted gross profit that was broadly stable year-over-year at BRL 1.6 billion due to higher revenues offset by provision expenses from credit portfolio growth. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted gross profits (BRL 6.6-7bn) but noted the backdrop is more challenging than anticipated, with a focus on delivering toward the lower end of ranges given elevated interest rates and macro headwinds. TPV growth accelerated to 4% annually as retention initiatives began showing traction.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly to approximately $58.4 million, driven by non-cash warrant fair value changes and one-time combination charges
Management explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for the remainder of FY2026 or full year 2027
Adjusted EBITDA remained in a loss position at $27.8 million despite reported progress on milestones
positive_highlights: Completed Critical Design Review (CDR) with lead customer USSOCOM on the C-130J program
Achieved Stage of Involvement (SOI) 3 certification milestone with Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand for AI autonomy
Balance sheet strengthened to $183.9 million in cash equivalents and note weakness in-term investments with no debt
summary: Merlin reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $2.2 million (up from $1M in Q1) and a GAAP net loss of $58.4 million, which improved by $32M compared to the prior quarter due to non-cash financing items; adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $27.8 million versus a loss of $23.3 million previously as engineering investment continued. Management highlighted significant technical milestones including CDR completion on the C-130J and SOI 3 certification with New Zealand, but explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for FY2026 or beyond, citing reliance on future contract expansions.

negative_highlights: Private Duty Services cost of revenue increased $2.06/hour (up 7.8%) due to wage adjustments and caregiver retention efforts.
Family First acquisition integration remains in early stages with back office transitions expected through late Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 13.7% YoY with all three segments posting double-digit growth (Home Health & Hospice +14.8%, Private Duty Services +14.0%).
Achieved full-year goal of 50 preferred payer agreements in Home Health, now accounting for approximately 64% of total MCO volumes.
Secured a significant rate increase for California pediatric private duty nursing effective January 2027 after four years of advocacy.
summary: Aveanna Healthcare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $670 million (up 13.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $95.4 million (up 8% YoY), driven by volume growth across all segments including a 14.8% increase in Home Health & Hospice. Management raised full-year guidance to revenue greater than $2.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA greater than $365 million, citing improved rate environments and successful preferred payer execution.

negative_highlights: Management admitted to a 'slight delay' in releasing the beta product for QSM IP due to security concerns arising from new AI-based cryptanalysis threats.
No revenue was generated by core commercial products (QSSN, Bitcoin Quantum) during this quarter as contracts are still being negotiated and mainnet launches are scheduled for H2 2026.
The company relies heavily on non-dilutive European grants to fund the QPerfect division rather than immediate product sales.
positive_highlights: QSM architecture taped out inside a root of trust with preliminary performance figures showing record low gate counts for ML-KEM, SHA-3, and AES-256 algorithms running on the same block.
QSSN mainnet transactions exceeded 100,000 with settlement times reduced to under 4 seconds (down from 35 seconds earlier in the year) and zero fallback rate.
MIMIQ quantum simulator went live with SDT partner QUREKA in Korea and is expanding cloud distribution via OVHcloud and upcoming partnerships.
summary: BTQ reported Q2 FY2026 with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted product milestones including a CAD$150M ATM launch and over $9.73 million cash on hand, but explicitly stated that commercial contracts for key products like QSSN are still under negotiation with expected monetization only starting in H2 2026. The company acknowledged significant delays to IP release timelines due to new AI-driven cryptographic threats requiring additional security analysis, and noted the recent integration of QPerfect is self-funding via grants rather than immediate revenue generation.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings generated as the asset is in early exploration and development stage prior to production target of 2031.
Don Diego remains outside current resource estimates, though it could link Caracol and Agaves deposits upon further confirmation.
positive_highlights: IPO and concurrent placement secured $331 million in total gross proceeds with strong investor demand.
Phase One drilling completed successfully on schedule with over 61,000m drilled using a fleet of up to 18 rigs.
Don Diego corridor showing high-grade mineralization including intercepts grading approximately 727 g per ton silver equivalent.
summary: Sinda reported its first quarter as a public company following the successful IPO which secured $331 million in gross proceeds and strategic investments from Fresnillo and Franco-Nevada. The Company completed Phase One surface drilling of nearly 61,000 meters across Caracol, Agaves, and Don Diego targets without any revenue or EPS to report as it remains a pre-production exploration stage asset. Management raised guidance for total annualized drilling by year-end from the initial plan of ~128,000m (based on Phase 1 + planned Phase 2) to nearly 135,000 meters after accelerating Phase Two plans.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $14.4 million for the quarter due to depreciation and non-cash items
Company is still in debt financing discussions rather than having secured funding yet
GPU revenue recognized was limited to five weeks of income from a new fleet
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $3.3 million compared to Q2 2025
Cash and cash equivalents increased significantly from $1.7M last year to approximately $150M today
Total assets grew dramatically from $37M a year ago to $279M
summary: Digi Power X reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $6.6 million and a net loss of $14.4 million, driven by the transition to AI compute revenue which began in May with only five weeks of income from GPU rentals. While adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $3.3 million (up $3.2m YoY), management highlighted significant balance sheet improvements including cash rising to ~$150M and total assets reaching $279M, but explicitly stated that the company is still in debt financing discussions rather than having secured a facility yet.

negative_highlights: Gross profit remained flat year-over-year despite top-line growth, indicating that cost of goods sold stayed elevated and profitability per unit has not yet improved.
Cash available for operations was constrained to approximately $0.7 million due to roughly $10 million being held in a restricted account for the Iowa facility.
positive_highlights: Cut herb sales increased more than 42%, driven by growth with existing customers and new programs with major retailers including Kroger, Target, and Weis.
SG&A expenses declined approximately $0.9 million (or 21.5%) to $3.1 million as the company improved operating efficiency.
Edible Garden secured a significant distribution win at Target's largest fresh cut herb center in Iowa amidst industry consolidation.
summary: Revenue grew 12.8% year-over-year to $3.6 million in Q2 FY2026, driven by a 42% increase in cut herb sales and expanded relationships with major retailers like Target and Kroger. SG&A expenses declined significantly by approximately $0.9 million (21.5%) compared to the prior year period as management focused on operational efficiency. The company made significant progress on its Prairie Hills manufacturing platform, completing prototype production at Tetra Pak's facility while securing pre-sold commitments for 100% of future capacity.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell by $557,000 in the first half of FY2026 compared to the prior year period.
Third-party revenue decreased by approximately 8% (from $852k to $781k) due to lower activity levels and reduced contract material/labor costs.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened in Q2 from a loss of $3.9 million to $5.1 million, indicating underlying operational deterioration.
positive_highlights: Company raised a total of $258.5 million in gross proceeds during Q2 via two registered direct offerings ($58.5M in April and $100M in May), significantly strengthening the balance sheet to $166.5 million.
The next LizzieSat successfully completed vibration testing, clearing a key environmental qualification milestone for launch readiness.
Fortis VPX Maxima is advancing toward Technology Readiness Level 9 following successful flight heritage integration.
summary: Sidus Space reported a significant revenue miss for the second quarter of FY2026 with total Q2 revenue declining to approximately $583,000 from $1.3 million in the prior year period (a decrease of 54%). While net loss narrowed due to non-operating factors like loan repayment and higher interest income, operating performance deteriorated as gross profit before depreciation declined by approximately $117,000 and cash operating expenses increased by roughly $1 million.

negative_highlights: El Niño-related provisions increased the cost of risk by 27 basis points, with potential impacts expected in Q1 2027.
Insurance underwriting results decreased due to a base effect from provision reversals recorded in the prior year's second quarter.
Primary GDP contracted nearly 5% year-over-year due to disruptions in fishing and agriculture sectors.
positive_highlights: ROE reached 20.3%, exceeding prior medium-term expectations of 19.5% which were set conservatively during a political cycle.
Loan growth accelerated to 13.1% year-over-year, driven by retail and wholesale banking at BCP and Mibanco.
NPL ratio declined to 4.1%, supported by improved origination quality and enhanced collections capabilities.
summary: Credicorp reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with a 20.3% ROE and accelerated loan growth of 13.1%, driven by retail banking at BCP and Mibanco despite El Niño-related provisions adding 27 bps to the cost of risk. Management raised its medium-term ROE expectation from 19.5% to approximately 22% citing structural improvements, while reaffirming full-year loan growth guidance around 12%. The company remains confident in Peru's economic outlook and expects fee income to grow into the high teens.

negative_highlights: Continued lack of commercial revenue as the company remains pre-launch with a reported net loss.
European unit sales growth was offset by significant pricing pressure and regulatory barriers, particularly in Germany where compounding is standard care.
Management explicitly stated that Europe will likely contribute less than 25% of total peak opportunity compared to the U.S.
positive_highlights: Secured FDA approval for LYTENAVA, becoming the only FDA-approved ophthalmic formulation of bevacizumab for wet AMD in the U.S.
summary: For Q3 FY2026, Outlook Therapeutics reported an adjusted net loss of $10.9 million ($0.09/share), a significant improvement from the prior year's $15.8 million loss and last quarter's unit sales decline in Europe which saw a 46% increase but remains below breakeven territory overall. Management provided forward guidance for total U.S. net revenue of $50-$75 million over the first 12 months following launch, with SG&A expenses expected to double by end-2026 and R&D remaining steady as they prepare for a commercial launch later this year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly due to a $3 million unrealized loss on Bitcoin holdings as prices fell from Q1 levels.
The new debt facility has a note weakness in-dated nature (revolving 30-day term) and is subject to renewal risk despite lower rates.
AI/HPC revenue generation remains in the proof-of-concept stage with no material contribution yet.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year by 9.8% driven by an increase in active miners (27.9 BTC mined vs 18.4 BTC prior YoY).
Mining margin expanded to 29% from 24.1% sequentially, supported by $145,000 in curtailment and energy sales.
Successfully refinanced debt facilities with Arch Lending at a lower blended rate (approx 2%) compared to the prior ~13%, reducing interest expense.
summary: Total revenue was $2.1 million in Q2 FY26, essentially flat sequentially and up 9.8% year-over-year to $1.9 million in the prior period quarter. The company reported a net loss of approximately $4.6 million driven by a $3 million fair value loss on digital assets against an average Bitcoin price decline from ~$75,700 to ~$72,000. Management clarified that previously cited revenue potential figures are illustrative estimates only and not guidance.

negative_highlights: Trading company posted -BRL 180 million recurring EBITDA due to position settlements in the South sub-market.
Gasmig results declined with a reduction of distributed volume by 17% and migration of clients to the free market.
Financial expenses increased significantly, impacting net income despite strong operational performance.
positive_highlights: Recurring EBITDA grew 9.3% YoY and net income up 15.6%, driven by Cemig D (EBITDA +21%) and Cemig GT (Net Income +3.6%).
Operating cash flow in H1 was close to BRL 4 billion, supporting the investment program.
Quality indicators improved with DEC at 8.43 and FEC at 4.86, both below regulatory limits.
summary: Cemig reported Q2 FY26 operating performance of BRL 2.5 billion and recurring EBITDA growth of 9.3% YoY, though net income was impacted by higher financial expenses from funding investments for the program totaling BRL 4.6 billion in the quarter. The company is executing its investment plan with BRL 1.8 billion CapEx (BRL 2.6 billion in distribution) and expects a tariff review impact of +6.5% average starting May 2028, while acknowledging trading losses of -BRL 180 million due to position settlements that were expected but offset by generation results.

negative_highlights: Q2 Revenue declined 27% YoY to $2.3 million due to non-recurring revenue trailing off
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened from a profit of $0.9M in Q1 FY25 to a loss of $1.7M in Q2 FY26
Year-to-date revenue is down 24% compared to the same period last year
positive_highlights: Net dollar retention rate reached a new all-time high of 91% for core customers
Stockholders' equity hit an all-time high of $12.2M following debt paydown and cost actions
Management expects significant revenue growth in H2 driven by ConnectAndSell contribution ($6.5M) and legacy product improvements
summary: Parabolic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.3 million, a decrease from the prior year quarter and down significantly due to non-recurring revenue trailing off in legacy products. The company acquired ConnectAndSell which will contribute approximately $15M annually starting later this year but is not reflected in current results. Net loss improved 41% YoY to $5 million driven by cost reductions, though the business remains unprofitable with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million.

negative_highlights: Net loss narrowed to only marginally from $13.4M last year but margins collapsed to -14.5% excluding grants due to a specific $1.2 million write-down.
The company was delisted from NASDAQ and is now trading on the OTCQB tier after failing continued listing standards for bid price, stockholders' equity, and filing requirements.
Cash balance decreased by $1.4M quarter-over-quarter to approximately $0.5 million due to operating cash burn of $3.6 million.
positive_highlights: Total revenue surged 268% year-over-year to $1.23 million driven by V2G school bus business deliveries and Japan interconnection agreements.
Megawatts under management increased 16.8% compared to the prior year quarter, reaching 29.9 MW with a growing backlog of $5.3 million.
Management is executing on three core geographies (Japan, Europe via Omnia partnership, and New Mexico) while rebuilding the balance sheet.
summary: Nuvve reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.23 million, a 268% year-over-year increase driven by V2G school bus charging station deliveries and Japan interconnection services. However, margins contracted significantly to -14.5% excluding grants due to a $1.2 million Troy project write-down and higher warranty costs on DC chargers. The company is trading on the OTCQB following NASDAQ delisting for failing listing standards but maintains an immediate priority to return to a senior market within months.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $37.1 million from a net profit in Q2 FY2025 due to one-time de-SPAC charges
Cash used in operating activities was approximately $19.6 million driven by elevated SG&A and acquisition-related costs
Weather conditions negatively impacted volumes specifically in Texas, Oklahoma, and North Texas markets
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew approximately 9% YoY despite unusually wet weather across much of the footprint
Completed five acquisitions adding six states across the Sun Belt platform including Texas and Louisiana
Oklahoma City acquisition is already achieving margins consistent with historic standards ahead of schedule
summary: Suncrete reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $97.2 million (up 146% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million, but recorded a net loss of $37.1 million due to a $26.9 million non-cash de-SPAC charge. Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue ($420M-$480M), income (net loss of $4M to net income of $20M), and adjusted EBITDA ($68M-$93M). The strong organic growth was achieved despite wet weather conditions in Texas and Oklahoma, with management noting that missed volume is expected to shift into the stronger third quarter.

negative_highlights: Second quarter revenue was flat year-on-year, failing to build on the strong Q1 growth.
Net loss increased from $6.3 million in Q2 FY2025 to $7.3 million in Q2 FY2026 due to non-cash accounting charges of approximately $3 million.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses reduced by 32% year-over-year following a cost program that cut headcount by 27%.
summary: Second quarter revenue was approximately $0.4 million, flat year-over-year compared to Q1's growth but lower than the prior period due to timing in services and deferred recognition from a vet agreement. Operating expenses decreased by 32% YoY following headcount reductions, yet net loss widened slightly to $7.3 million driven by non-cash charges on convertible notes. Management explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for FY2026 citing the lumpy nature of project delivery and deferred revenue recognition.

negative_highlights: Exchange revenue fell 38% YoY and transaction revenue dropped 15% due to a 66% decline in spot trading volumes
Credit card receivables remained flat while provision for expected credit losses spiked from $3.6m to $20.1m driven by fraud-related delinquency maturation
Assets on platform declined significantly to $8.4 billion from $18.2 billion in Q2 2025 due to crypto price declines and net outflows
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 37% YoY to $45.5 million despite a weak crypto trading environment
Services revenue and interest income surged 117% YoY to $26 million, now representing 59% of net revenue
Prediction markets volume reached new monthly highs in July with strong engagement in Bitcoin contracts
summary: Total revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $45.5 million driven by services and OTC growth, while exchange revenue declined 38% due to soft crypto volumes. Net loss narrowed slightly to $107.7 million from a prior quarter's adjusted EBITDA deterioration of roughly $26M compared to Q1, primarily reflecting non-cash mark-to-market losses on Bitcoin holdings following the May strategic investment. Management provided no formal revenue guidance for 2H but expects technology and G&A expenses between $155m-$170m full year.

negative_highlights: Second-quarter net revenues moderated sequentially due to trade inventory normalization following first-quarter shipment adjustments.
Management expects Mainland China sales for the full year to be broadly flat year-over-year amid tightening domestic regulations and conservative approval timelines.
Gross margin expansion is partially attributed to temporary product mix shifts, with expectations that margins will settle back to a healthy range as flows normalize.
positive_highlights: Top-line grew 14.8% year-over-year driven by international expansion and an acquired entity completed in May 2025.
Gross margin expanded sequentially to 35.4%, up 790 basis points year-over-year due to supply chain optimization and mix shifts.
Non-GAAP operating profit reached RMB 149.6 million, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of positive non-GAAP income from operations.
summary: RLX Technology reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 1.01 billion (up 14.8% YoY) and gross profit of RMB 357.8 million with a margin expansion to 35.4%. Management noted that sequential revenue moderation was due to trade inventory normalization following Q1 regulatory-driven shipments rather than demand softening, while highlighting the upcoming consolidation of a Western European acquisition in Q3 which will boost reported growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $5 million from a prior year adjusted loss, though this reflects one-time settlement costs.
Galena Q2 production was suppressed by phase 2 shaft upgrades and waste development activities designed for H2 ramp-up.
A minor fire at Galena displaced some high-grade ore in the specific scope mined during Q2.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 71% YoY to $46.3 million driven by higher realized silver prices ($67/oz vs $34/oz).
Cosalá production rose 26% YoY to ~337k oz supported by improved recoveries and entering the high-grade EC120 zone.
Settlement of Sprott and Royal Gold obligations removed >$76M in variable debt service with only 3.3% dilution.
summary: Americas Gold and Silver reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $46.3 million (up 71% YoY) driven by a silver price increase to $67/oz, while consolidated production reached ~800k silver equivalent ounces with Cosalá output up 26%. The company settled remaining variable delivery obligations for Sprott and Royal Gold, removing over $76 million in future debt service. Management reiterated full-year guidance of 3.2-3.6M oz despite Q2 being a trough quarter due to infrastructure spending at Galena.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined sequentially and YoY to 63.7% due to product mix shift as Conversational AI products remain at a subscale stage.
Operating cash flow turned negative at -$2.1 million compared to -$0.4M in the prior year quarter, primarily driven by annual bonus payments and share repurchases.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance at $40.4 million, marking third consecutive quarter of accelerating top-line growth.
GAAP net profit surged to $2.2 million (up 50% YoY) driven by improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management in G&A.
Dollar-based net retention rate improved significantly to 104%, moving back above the 100% threshold from 94% last year.
summary: Total revenue for Q2 FY26 reached $40.4 million, beating the high end of guidance and growing 18% year-over-year to a third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth. GAAP net profit was $2.2 million (up 50%), though gross margin contracted slightly to 63.7% due to product mix changes as Conversational AI usage grew at a subscale stage. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance expectations, projecting between $41M and $42M with growth of 15.8%-18.6%, while reaffirming the goal of achieving GAAP operating profitability by year-end.

negative_highlights: Skillz revenue declined sequentially by ~3% excluding one-time items, driven by an 8% drop in paying monthly active users
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $13.6 million from a normalized loss of $2.7 million due to elevated litigation costs near the Papaya trial conclusion
Skillz user acquisition spend decreased significantly as management paused spending to repair operational funnels
positive_highlights: RZR exceeded $10 million in quarterly revenue for the first time, growing 6% QoQ and 75% YoY
RZR delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability with sequential growth each period
Company secured a unanimous jury verdict awarding approximately $730 million against Papaya Gaming
summary: Firy reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $31 million (up 23% YoY), but the company posted a net loss of $24.5 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $13.6 million, including approximately $11 million in litigation expenses. While RZR achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability with strong growth, Skillz revenue declined sequentially due to operational headwinds and reduced user acquisition spend aimed at fixing funnel issues. Management highlighted a recent court victory awarding ~$730 million against Papaya Gaming but noted that proceeds are not yet realized in financial statements.

negative_highlights: Sales of resins and major chemicals decreased in the Brazilian market by 2% and 4%, respectively.
Polyethylene sales fell 11% in Mexico due to lower availability from reduced utilization rates at Braskem Idesa.
Management warned that global petrochemical fundamentals remain under pressure with overcapacity, suggesting Q2 results were a tactical capture of value rather than structural improvement.
positive_highlights: Consolidated recurring EBITDA reached $1.043 billion, representing an increase compared to the previous quarter.
International spreads for resins and main chemicals expanded significantly in Brazil (82%) and Mexico (73%).
Green polyethylene sales increased by 49% due to commercial opportunities in Europe.
summary: Braskem reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated recurring EBITDA of $1.043 billion with a margin of 24%, driven by significant international spread increases (up to 73% in Mexico) and PIS/COFINS credits, partially offset by lower Brazilian sales volumes and currency appreciation. Management noted that the strong quarter was largely tactical due to Middle East conflict-induced supply shocks rather than structural demand growth, with spreads expected to normalize toward pre-conflict levels in Q3. The company emphasized a focus on capital structure restructuring and operational discipline as it navigates global overcapacity.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $75 million due to one-time non-cash items totaling $64.4M (tax charge and stock-based comp).
Operating costs were high at $44 million with depreciation rising to $18.1 million during the rapid deployment phase.
No specific guidance on future profitability or margin expansion was provided for this transitional quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~270% YoY driven by lease revenue from GPU rental fleet deployment and bespoke assets for customers.
Total Contract Value (TCV) stands at $1.9 billion with an average duration of approximately three years.
Management secured a strategic procurement agreement worth $4B-$5B in compute hardware with multiple OEMs, including Dell.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $31.1 million (up ~270% YoY), but the company reported a GAAP net loss of $75 million and an operating loss of $12.9 million, heavily impacted by one-time non-cash items including a $55.7M tax charge from transitioning to C-Corp status and $64.4M in other transaction-related adjustments. Management reaffirmed guidance for approximately $400 million annualized recurring revenue at year-end 2026 but provided no specific EPS or margin targets due to the one-time nature of the quarter's results.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 27% year-over-year as one-time non-recurring revenue from CreateStudio in Q1 trails off
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $1.7 million despite lower operating expenses due to the revenue miss
Gross profit decreased compared to the prior year quarter
positive_highlights: Net dollar retention rate reached an all-time high of 91% for the core customer segment
Stockholders' equity hit a new record of $12.2 million following debt paydowns
Cost reduction actions reduced operating expenses by $1.7M compared to Q1
summary: Parabolic reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.3 million, a decrease of approximately 16% from the prior quarter and 27% year-over-year due to non-recurring revenue trailing off in legacy products. Net loss narrowed by 41% compared to Q1 driven by cost reductions totaling $1.7M versus Q1, while adjusted EBITDA remained at a loss of $1.7 million. Management raised full-year guidance expectations citing significant second-half growth from ConnectAndSell ($6.5M contribution) and legacy product improvements.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide full-year guidance for 2026, citing parabolic volatility in fuel prices that makes forward-looking statements unreliable.
CASK increased significantly year-over-year due to a 61.8% rise in fuel costs and temporary deleveraging of fixed costs over reduced capacity.
Recurring free cash flow was nearly breakeven (negative BRL 80 million) hindered by non-recurring restructuring payments totaling approximately BRL 794 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a record 10.2%, recapturing approximately BRL 448 million of the fuel headwind through disciplined capacity management and pricing actions.
Operating revenue reached a quarterly record, supported by RASK growth of 12.7% YoY despite significant volume reductions.
NPS increased 26 points since December 2025 as operational reliability improved to make Azul the most on-time airline in Latin America.
summary: Azul reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of BRL 5 billion (up 0.7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 510 million in a seasonally weak quarter impacted by fuel prices up 61%. Management declined to provide full-year guidance due to extreme volatility in the fuel curve, noting that capacity was reduced proactively by 10.6% to protect liquidity while maintaining record RASK.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $12.8M for the quarter and Adjusted EBITDA was -$3.2M due to merger-related stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) and legacy business wind-down costs.
Material weaknesses in internal controls remain unremediated with a multi-step remediation plan underway involving an external accounting firm.
positive_highlights: Contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached $22 million as of August 4th, inclusive of new Blackwell cluster deliveries announced last week.
summary: Corvex reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.8 million entirely from its newly integrated AI platform business following a March merger with Corvex Legacy Holdings; the legacy healthcare segment was fully wound down and transferred to lenders, resulting in no meaningful year-over-year comparisons. Management highlighted that contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached approximately $22 million as of August 4th, driven by new cluster deliveries including Blackwell expansion funded via debt financing and customer prepayments. The quarter included significant non-cash stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) related to merger equity awards and disclosed unremediated material weaknesses in internal controls.

negative_highlights: Revenue was constrained by a temporary suspension of mining and processing operations due to TAC negotiations in Brazil.
Not all produced material (low-grade fines) could be sold within Q2, resulting in lower revenue than production volume might suggest for the period.
Operational timeline pushed forward by three months regarding full capacity ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Production volume increased significantly by 52% quarter-over-quarter to deliver 35,400 tons of lithium oxide concentrate.
Company maintained high gross margins at 60% and achieved record EBITDA margin of 47%. All-in sustaining costs decreased over 30% year-over-year to $668/ton.
Deleveraged balance sheet significantly, repaying 43% of total debt over the last two years.
summary: Sigma Lithium reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $55 million and generated approximately $30-32 million in cash flow from operations for the quarter. While production volumes increased by 52% to 35,400 tons due to a ramp-up that surpassed guidance, revenue was impacted by lower sales volume compared to total production as low-grade material produced but not sold during the quarter is being monetized later. Management adjusted its full-year cost guidance downward based on executed costs of $668/ton and pushed forward certain operational timelines by three months due to a temporary suspension related to TAC negotiations.

negative_highlights: Average note price for Zgounder was $68.29/oz, which is below the quarter's average due to a precipitous drop in June prices.
positive_highlights: Production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), representing a 61% year-over-year increase driven by record mining rates at Zgounder.
Cash flow generation reached $48 million, up 522% from the prior year quarter, with total H1 operating cash flow hitting $119 million.
Discovery of a new high-grade zone parallel to the main structure at Boumadine (intercept of 51m @ 890 g/t silver equivalent) and completion of Phase 2 tailings facility.
summary: Aya reported Q2 FY2026 production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), a 61% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter rise, driven by record performance at the Zgounder mine where mining rates reached 4,900 tonnes per day against a plant nameplate capacity of 2,700 tonnes. Revenue surged to $97 million (up 151% YoY) and net income hit $35 million due to strong cash costs ($17.69/oz at Zgounder) despite silver prices averaging below the quarter's low-water mark. Management confirmed full alignment with H1 guidance for production, cash cost, and CapEx while highlighting a successful Nasdaq listing as a major catalyst.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue decreased 19% YoY due to a specific large order delay that prevented meeting proposed expectations for the quarter.
Service revenue declined 28% YoY as non-recurring customization revenues and recurring service renewals lagged timing assumptions.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded sharply to 87% from 73%, driven by high-margin license revenue mix and inventory liquidation.
Net loss improved 51% YoY to $0.56 per share, with cash position strengthened to over $4.5 million following warrant exercises.
Significant pipeline growth identified in EMEA (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Portugal) and new opportunities in AI agent governance.
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to $1.92 million driven by a 53% increase in license fees, but the quarter missed proposed expectations due to a delayed hardware shipment shifting into H2. Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, while net loss improved 51% to $0.56 per share on an adjusted basis of shares post-reverse split. Management targets profitability for the second half of 2026, citing strong pipeline growth in EMEA and new AI governance opportunities.

negative_highlights: Full-year cash spend guidance increased slightly to $27-$28 million reflecting accelerated commercialization activities.
Net loss of $8.5 million includes significant non-cash charges related to earn-out shares and vesting liabilities.
Modest pay deployment revenue expected for the JV in 2026, with more meaningful commercial revenue anticipated only beginning in 2027.
positive_highlights: Signed an exclusive sales agreement with Kubota Corporation to deploy AirJoule systems in water-constrained regions of Texas and California.
First full-scale Prime system commissioned in Newark is operating outdoors at high uptime and tracking toward the expectation of 2,000 liters per day.
Awarded one of the UAE's first Expo City green licenses, providing access to business missions and a seat in the Green Majlis Leadership Forum.
summary: AirJoule Technologies reported a net loss of $8.5 million for Q2 FY26, driven by non-cash losses on earn-out shares and an increase in full-year cash spend guidance to approximately $27-$28 million from the prior expectation. Management highlighted significant commercial milestones including an exclusive partnership with Kubota Corporation for residential development in Texas and California, a deployment at GE Vernova's Frontier Campus, and regulatory validation via UAE green licenses.
